audits.jarvis_gap: Today the trigger→spawn→act loop is economically sophisticated and cognitively blind. The pre-spawn gate chain in `src/butlers/core/spawner.py:1275-1760` is genuinely good engineering — catalog resolution with a folded quota probe, spend routing rules, permissions, monthly ceiling (prefetched concurrently), per-call cost cap, evidence-scored tie-breaking, a dispatch-outcome breaker, capability hard-fit via `DispatchIntent`, speculative adapter prewarm. Every one of those answers "may this dispatch run and on which model". Nothing in the loop answers "what does this session need to know, and what should happen when it turns out to need more". A session's entire spawn-time perception is four static layers (`spawner_context.py:116-146`): CLAUDE.md, a timezone sentence, active context-bus signals, and a prompt-similarity memory slice. It cannot see whether its own connectors are stale, what the same scheduled task produced yesterday (`scheduled_tasks.last_result` is written at `scheduler.py:2297` and read by nothing), whether an approval it filed is still open, or how long the owner is willing to wait. Once running it has no upward door: complexity is frozen at `trigger()` (`spawner.py:619`) and the spec's only failure mode is "default to workhorse" (`openspec/specs/complexity-classification`, Classification failure scenario). Once terminated by a guardrail it loses everything it produced — `result_text` is in hand at `spawner.py:2554` and thrown away at `spawner.py:2975` with `output=None`, episode never stored. And the one field that already classifies risk, `Consequence` (`dispatch_intent.py:57-67`), is consumed at exactly one line in the whole repo (`dispatch_intent.py:299`) to tolerate an unknown capability. The result is a fleet that ran 22,879 sessions and 3.3B input tokens in a week (live `/api/sessions/aggregate?period=week`) at an 88.3% success rate, where the 11.7% that fail leave no salvageable work, the cheap tier cannot ask for help, and no butler is structurally prevented from narrating a stale source as current fact.
audits.live_verification: Live (READ-only, http://127.0.0.1:42200): `/api/sessions/aggregate?period=week` → 22,879 sessions, 20,211 success / 2,668 failed (88.3%), 3,316,883,757 input tokens, `by_trigger_source: []`; `/api/spend?period=7d` → $45.16 / 864 priced sessions, by_model shows the enabled fleet (gpt-5.6-sol, gpt-5.6-luna, opencode-go/qwen3.7-plus, mimo-v2.5, kimi-k2.6, ollama/qwen3.5:9b), `divergence_source_error: true`; `/api/settings/models` → full catalog with priorities/enabled/routing_score (only 4 entries have ≥5 samples; cheap-tier top-priority enabled entries are gpt-5.6-luna pri 31 and opencode-go/mimo-v2.5 pri 30, while `gpt-5.4-mini` sits at pri 25); `/api/sessions?limit=1` → a live row confirming `trigger_source` and `complexity` are stored per session. Everything else is source-confirmed by reading the decisive mechanism: spawner._run's gate chain and guardrail raise/discard path, spawner_context._compose_system_prompt's four layers, dispatch_intent's `_TRIGGER_PROFILES` and single `consequence` consumer, scheduler's write-only `last_result`, and exhaustive greps for callers of `max_tool_calls` / `timeout_override` / `expected_signals` / any verifier concept (none). Stack fully reachable; no write was issued.
audits.ideal: A JARVIS-grade loop treats a dispatch as a negotiated contract, not a fire-and-forget. At spawn the daemon hands the session a typed, deterministic perception pack it could not cheaply assemble itself: what this same task concluded and promised last time, what its own sources currently cannot see (with the reason and the clock that judged it), what obligations are open in its domain, and what the owner's latency and cost budget is for this particular trigger class — every element stamped with provenance and freshness so the session's language is honest by construction rather than by prompt discipline. During the session, capability is elastic in one direction only and always on the record: a cheap-tier session that finds itself out of depth calls `request_escalation` and the deterministic daemon re-dispatches exactly once at the next tier, carrying the cheap session's findings forward, so cheap-first becomes a safe default rather than a gamble. At termination, nothing paid for is discarded: a guardrail or deadline stop persists the partial output and tool trace as a handoff that either continues once or surfaces as an honest partial. And where the dispatch's product leaves the system — `Consequence.EXTERNAL` on an irreversible act — a bounded independent verifier checks the proposed act against the evidence the session actually gathered before it goes out, routing a mismatch to the approvals spine instead of to the owner's inbox. The owner sees all of it as one spine: a session detail that shows what the session was told, what budget it was given, whether it escalated, what it carried forward, and who verified the act — a door at every consequential clause, with no aggregate that denominates nothing and no gate that is only metadata.

findings.title: Guardrail termination discards the model's completed output and its episode after the owner paid for every token
findings.evidence: src/butlers/core/spawner.py:2554-2568 (guardrail raise happens with result_text already in hand), src/butlers/core/spawner.py:2971-2977 (outer handler calls session_complete with output=None), src/butlers/core/spawner.py:2751 (store_session_episode is on the success path only, never reached), src/butlers/core/failover_classifier.py:269-270 (retry explicitly suppressed)
findings.detail: On the post-invocation success path the adapter has already returned `result_text`, `tool_calls` and `usage`; token counts are captured into the ledger vars at spawner.py:2537-2543. If `_check_degenerate_tool_loop` / `_check_tool_call_budget` / `_check_token_budget` returns a reason, a bare `RuntimeError` is raised at spawner.py:2568. The outer `except Exception` handler preserves the tool-call list but writes `output=None` (spawner.py:2975) and never reaches `store_session_episode`. So the owner is billed for the full session, memory learns nothing from it, and the session row shows an error with no work product — for a condition (degenerate loop) that means the session was noisy, not that its conclusion was wrong. The failover classifier then suppresses any retry, so the work is unrecoverable by design.
findings.taxonomy_shape: computed-then-discarded truth

findings.title: classification_timeout bucketing keys off a model-name substring that matches no enabled model in the live catalog
findings.evidence: src/butlers/core/sessions.py:729-741 (`_ERROR_MARKER_CASE_SQL`: `model ILIKE '%mini%'` plus `error ILIKE '%butler=switchboard%'`), live GET /api/settings/models (cheap-tier enabled top priorities: gpt-5.6-luna pri 31, opencode-go/mimo-v2.5 pri 30; gpt-5.4-mini only pri 25), live GET /api/sessions?limit=1 (row carries `trigger_source` and `complexity` columns)
findings.detail: The comment above the SQL states the intent honestly — 'classification sessions specifically use a mini model with a <=60s cap' — but that was a fact about a retired catalog. Against the live catalog the cheap tier resolves to `gpt-5.6-luna` or `opencode-go/mimo-v2.5` (neither matches `%mini%`; 'mimo' is not 'mini'), so every genuine switchboard classification timeout is bucketed as `'other'`. The heuristic reaches for a provider's model naming convention when the session row already stores the two decisive facts: `trigger_source='classification'` (set by modules/pipeline.py per openspec/specs/complexity-classification) and `complexity='cheap'`. A writer's naming convention is standing in for a stored fact, and the resulting failure-taxonomy aggregate under-counts the fleet's single most frequent cheap-tier failure mode to zero.

findings.title: DispatchIntent's three economic fields are structurally dead on every owner-facing dispatch
findings.evidence: src/butlers/core/spawner.py:1293-1295 (`derive_dispatch_intent(trigger_source, complexity, deadline_s=timeout_override)` — min_context_tokens and max_cost_usd_per_call never supplied), src/butlers/core/healing/dispatch.py:670 and src/butlers/core/qa/dispatch.py:1720,3079 (the only callers that set timeout_override), src/butlers/core/dispatch_intent.py:137-150 + 206-219 (FitCode.DEADLINE_EXCEEDED / COST_EXCEEDS_BUDGET / CONTEXT_WINDOW_TOO_SMALL)
findings.detail: `DispatchIntent` declares a deadline, a context floor and a per-call cost cap, and `evaluate_fit` implements exclusion codes for all three. In production none of the three is ever populated on a butler dispatch: `min_context_tokens` and `max_cost_usd_per_call` have zero call sites, and `deadline_s` is set only by the healing and QA dispatchers — whose own trigger profiles are `Consequence.REVERSIBLE`/`OBSERVE`, i.e. the two classes where nobody is waiting. The `route` and `dashboard` classes, the only ones with an owner actually waiting, always pass `deadline_s=None`, so `FitCode.DEADLINE_EXCEEDED` can never fire for them and a candidate whose evidence proves it overruns is never excluded from an interactive dispatch. The fit machinery is real; the requirement side that would make it bite is unwired.
findings.taxonomy_shape: gates as metadata not enforcement

findings.title: The max_tool_calls guardrail has no caller and no control plane, yet three downstream taxonomies carry a branch for it
findings.evidence: src/butlers/core/spawner.py:200 (`_DEFAULT_MAX_TOOL_CALLS = 0`, 0 disables), src/butlers/core/spawner.py:624,1213 (only default-valued parameters; grep for `max_tool_calls=` finds no non-passthrough caller in src/), src/butlers/core/sessions.py:732, src/butlers/core/failover_classifier.py:269, src/butlers/core/qa/sources/session_records.py:74
findings.detail: Unlike `max_token_budget`, which reaches `Spawner.trigger` from `ScheduleConfig` (config.py:500,515 → daemon.py:1086 → background.py:184), `max_tool_calls` is exposed nowhere: no TOML field, no `runtime_config` key, no API. The default of 0 disables the check, so `_check_tool_call_budget` can never return non-None in production. The spec is honest about the default (openspec/specs/core-spawner/spec.md:587,609) but omits that there is no way to turn it on. Meanwhile the session error taxonomy, the failover classifier's suppression list, and the QA discovery source all reserve a bucket for `tool_call_budget_exceeded` that is guaranteed empty — a runaway-tool-call runaway is the exact failure the fleet's 3.3B weekly input tokens make expensive, and the only defense against it is the 6-consecutive-identical-call degenerate-loop check.
findings.taxonomy_shape: gates as metadata not enforcement

findings.title: Consequence is derived for every dispatch and changes exactly one boolean in the entire repository
findings.evidence: src/butlers/core/dispatch_intent.py:57-67 (Consequence enum), :86-100 (_TRIGGER_PROFILES assigns it per trigger class), :299 (`tolerate_unknown = intent.consequence is Consequence.OBSERVE`); grep for `consequence` across src/ finds no other functional consumer
findings.detail: The loop already computes, deterministically and prompt-free, whether a dispatch's product lands in an internal artifact (OBSERVE), on revisable butler state (REVERSIBLE), or outside the system (EXTERNAL). That classification is then used only to decide whether an UNKNOWN model capability disqualifies a candidate. An EXTERNAL dispatch that will send mail or actuate a light and a REVERSIBLE tick that will update a cache get identical model requirements, identical retry policy, identical verification (none), and identical budget treatment. The risk classification the system already owns is inert everywhere it would matter.
findings.taxonomy_shape: NEW: a declared risk classification that changes nothing downstream

findings.title: scheduled_tasks.last_result is a write-only column: the scheduler records every run's product and never reads it back
findings.evidence: src/butlers/core/scheduler.py:2286-2300 (`SET last_run_at = $2, last_result = $3`), src/butlers/core_tools/_scheduling.py:301,322 (same write from the MCP path); grep for `last_result` across src/ finds only writes plus a docstring at scheduler.py:1973 and a comment at modules/memory/ann_observability.py:13
findings.detail: Every prompt-mode scheduled dispatch serializes its SpawnerResult into `last_result` (`_result_to_jsonb`), and no code path — prompt assembly, the `prompt_hooks` map, any API router, any butler tool — ever reads it. The next run of the same task therefore starts with no knowledge of what the previous run concluded, promised, or failed to see. The only general-purpose prompt-time extension seam, `_prepare_scheduled_prompt` (scheduler.py:55-64), is fed a hard-coded single-entry map built for the chronicler day-close task in daemon.py:1116-1157; there is no general continuity layer, and `sessions` carries no parent/continuation column (session_create, sessions.py:115-180).
findings.taxonomy_shape: computed-then-discarded truth

moves.title: Session escalation door: request_escalation core tool + exactly one bounded re-dispatch at the next tier
moves.why: openspec/specs/complexity-classification fixes complexity at spawn and its only named failure mode is 'Classification failure defaults to workhorse' — there is no upward path in the entire loop (spawner.py:619 freezes `complexity` at trigger time; no verifier or escalation concept exists anywhere in src/). Today cheap-first is a gamble: a cheap-tier classification session that finds a message genuinely ambiguous can only guess, and the owner pays for the misroute downstream. With an escalation door the owner can push far more traffic to the cheap tier because the loop self-corrects upward on evidence rather than on a pre-spawn guess. Owner-visible within a week: fewer misroutes on ambiguous inbound messages, and a session detail that says 'this started cheap, asked for help, and finished on workhorse — here is why', which is exactly the unbroken signal→session→evidence spine the north star demands. Serves architecture.md § The Core Loop (the daemon stays deterministic: the SESSION requests, the DAEMON decides and re-dispatches) and the Switchboard MANIFESTO's 'Message classification' responsibility.
moves.integration_points: New core tool module src/butlers/core_tools/_escalation.py registering `request_escalation(reason, findings, confidence)` in a new `escalation` core group (gated via runtime_config core_groups, per vision non-negotiable #5); new table public.session_escalations (alembic core chain: from_session_id, logical_session_id, from_tier, to_tier, reason, findings JSONB, to_session_id, decided_at, decision) ; Spawner.trigger gains an `escalated_from` seed parameter and _run threads it into session_create (new `escalated_from_session_id` column on sessions, sessions.py:115-180); derive_dispatch_intent unchanged (same trigger class, higher complexity_tier) so the existing hard-fit machinery covers the new tier; _write_dispatch_attempt gains an `escalation` outcome so the attempt trail shows the tier hop; openspec/specs/complexity-classification MODIFIED (new requirement: Upward Escalation) and openspec/specs/core-spawner MODIFIED; GET /api/sessions/{session_id} surfaces the escalation chain; Concierge MANIFESTO amendment to let the fleet read-model answer 'which sessions escalated and why'.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: cheap session calls request_escalation with its findings; the tool returns a terminal marker; the session ends cleanly with success=true and an `escalated` outcome (NOT a failure); the daemon re-dispatches once at the next tier with the original prompt plus the typed findings block, seeded escalated_from. Failure: escalation requested at the top tier (reasoning) → tool returns refusal with the reason 'no higher tier'; session continues and must answer at its own tier. Concurrency: the escalation row is inserted under the logical_session_id with a unique (logical_session_id, from_session_id) constraint, so a session that calls the tool twice gets the first decision back — the daemon never spawns two continuations. Idempotence: the re-dispatch carries the same logical_session_id (effective_request_id) so spend, dispatch attempts and the ledger all roll up to one logical unit; a replayed escalation row is a no-op. Rollback: an escalation budget (max 1 hop per logical session, enforced by the unique constraint plus a depth check) means the worst case is exactly 2x cost, never a loop; disabling the `escalation` core group in runtime_config removes the tool and the loop reverts byte-for-byte to today's behavior.
moves.verification: (1) A spawner integration test at the real seam: dispatch a fake cheap-tier runtime whose scripted tool call is request_escalation, assert exactly one follow-up Spawner._run at the next tier, assert both sessions share logical_session_id, assert the second session's prompt contains the findings block. (2) A depth test asserting a second escalation from the continuation is refused and no third dispatch occurs. (3) A concurrency test firing request_escalation twice from one session and asserting one public.session_escalations row and one continuation. (4) A cost test asserting the two attempts appear as two rows in public.model_dispatch_attempts under one logical_session_id so /api/spend does not double-count the logical unit. (5) An openspec verify run against the MODIFIED complexity-classification requirement.
moves.slice_plan: Slice 1: migration + public.session_escalations + sessions.escalated_from_session_id, no behavior change. Slice 2: request_escalation core tool behind the `escalation` core group, returning a decision but with re-dispatch disabled (records intent only) — ship and observe how often the cheap tier would have asked. Slice 3: enable the bounded re-dispatch for `classification` trigger class only (lowest blast radius, highest volume: 7,266 switchboard sessions/week live). Slice 4: extend to `schedule`/`route`, add the session-detail escalation chain and the Concierge read model.
moves.manifesto: roster/switchboard/MANIFESTO.md § Responsibilities (Message classification) — escalation is classification quality, which is Switchboard's contract; plus a Concierge MANIFESTO amendment to add escalation evidence to its fleet-telemetry jurisdiction (it already owns 'which sessions failed').

moves.title: Blind-spot preamble: tell every session, at spawn, what it currently cannot see
moves.why: The north star says failure must never impersonate health and staleness must never wear current-data authority — but the loop's only enforcement of that is prompt discipline inside each butler's CLAUDE.md. A session's entire spawn-time perception is four layers (spawner_context.py:116-146): base prompt, timezone sentence, context-bus signals, prompt-similarity memory. None of them is source health. The honest-absence machinery shipped in run 11 (src/butlers/core/expected_signals.py, PRESENT/ABSENT/UNMEASURABLE) is consumed by exactly one butler — grep finds readers only under roster/relationship/tools/. So Health can narrate a nine-hour-stale Google Health feed as today's data, and Finance can say 'nothing unusual' when the ingestion connector never heartbeated. Owner-visible within a week: butlers start saying 'I cannot see your inbox right now — Gmail last heartbeat 9h ago' instead of 'your inbox is clear'. Serves architecture.md § The Core Loop step 5, which already sanctions enriching the act step with shared awareness (RFC 0009) without changing the loop's shape.
moves.integration_points: New `fetch_blind_spot_preamble(pool, butler_name, modules, connectors)` in src/butlers/core/spawner_context.py, wired as a fifth layer in `_compose_system_prompt` (spawner_context.py:116-146) between context_preamble and memory_ctx (memory stays last for prefix-cache stability); reads public.expected_signals via the existing evaluator in core/expected_signals.py plus public.v_qa_connector_state and the ha_source_health guard; a per-butler declaration of which signals it depends on, sourced from the butler's module/connector list in roster/{butler}/config.toml rather than invented; openspec/specs/expected-signals MODIFIED (new requirement: Session-Facing Projection); openspec/specs/core-spawner MODIFIED (fifth composition layer); GET /api/butlers/{name} surfaces the same projection so the dashboard and the session agree.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: all declared signals PRESENT → no preamble emitted, prompt is byte-identical to today (prefix cache preserved). Degraded: one or more signals ABSENT or UNMEASURABLE → a typed block naming each signal, its producer, its last_observed_at and the evaluator's own clock, with the instruction that any claim depending on it must be stated as unmeasured. Failure — and this is the deliberate inversion: unlike the other four layers, this one does NOT fail open. If the blind-spot query itself errors, the preamble emits 'source health could not be evaluated at <ts>; treat every source-dependent claim as unverified' rather than silently omitting the layer, because a silent omission is indistinguishable from all-clear. Concurrency: read-only, no locks, evaluated per spawn against now(); two concurrent spawns may see different states, which is correct. Idempotence: pure function of (butler, declared signals, clock). Rollback: the layer is additive and gated by a runtime_config flag; clearing the flag restores today's four-layer composition exactly.
moves.verification: (1) A composition test asserting `_compose_system_prompt` is byte-identical to today's output when every declared signal is PRESENT. (2) A fail-closed test: make the expected_signals query raise and assert the preamble is emitted with the unevaluable wording (the inverse of the fail-open tests that guard the other four fetchers). (3) A per-butler declaration test asserting a butler with no email module gets no Gmail blind-spot line — the projection must be scoped by declared dependencies, not by the whole fleet. (4) An end-to-end spawner test with a stubbed stale connector asserting the string reaches `invoke_kwargs['system_prompt']` at spawner.py:2033-2040. (5) A cross-surface consistency test asserting GET /api/butlers/{name} and the injected preamble derive from the same evaluator call, so the dashboard and the session cannot disagree.
moves.slice_plan: Slice 1: generalize core/expected_signals.py from a Relationship-only helper into a per-butler evaluator with a declared-dependency input; no injection yet. Slice 2: inject for one butler (health — highest staleness stakes, Google Health cadence is already modeled) behind a runtime_config flag, and diff its outputs. Slice 3: roll to all domain butlers; add the fail-closed unevaluable path. Slice 4: expose the same projection on GET /api/butlers/{name} and reference it from the butler detail page.
moves.manifesto: Every domain manifesto's honesty clause is served, but the binding one is roster/health/MANIFESTO.md (a health butler that reports stale vitals as current is the sharpest violation). Implies a small amendment to openspec/specs/expected-signals adding the session-facing projection as a first-class consumer alongside the API readers.

moves.title: Task continuity ledger: a scheduled task that remembers what it concluded, promised and could not see last time
moves.why: scheduled_tasks.last_result is written on every dispatch (scheduler.py:2286-2300) and read by nothing — grep finds only writes. The only prompt-time continuity seam, `_prepare_scheduled_prompt` (scheduler.py:55-64), is fed a hard-coded single-entry map built for the chronicler day-close task (daemon.py:1116-1157). So the morning briefing has no idea what yesterday's briefing said, the finance check has no idea it already flagged the same anomaly three days running, and the only thing standing between the owner and daily repetition is a semantic memory search over the prompt (spawner_context.py:182-202) that was never designed for task self-continuity. Owner-visible on day 2: briefings stop repeating themselves and start closing loops — 'yesterday I said I would chase the refund; the merchant replied, here is where it stands' — which is the single most JARVIS-shaped thing a recurring session can do. Serves vision.md § What Success Looks Like ('the amount of mental labor the system reliably absorbs') and architecture.md § The Core Loop step 6 (Log) by making the log load-bearing instead of archival.
moves.integration_points: New table public.task_continuity (butler_name, task_name, run_at, session_id, carry_forward JSONB {did, deferred, expect_next, could_not_see}, superseded_at) with a partial unique index on the live row per (butler_name, task_name); a new core tool `carry_forward(...)` in src/butlers/core_tools/_scheduling.py registered in the existing scheduling core group; scheduler.py's `_prepare_scheduled_prompt` generalized from the chronicler-specific `prompt_hooks` map into a continuity layer that injects the live carry_forward row for the task about to run; sessions gains `continuation_of_session_id` so the chain is walkable; openspec/specs/core-scheduler and openspec/specs/core-spawner MODIFIED; the Chronicler day-close hook (core_tools/_chronicler.py:117) is refactored onto the general layer rather than remaining a special case.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: task runs, calls carry_forward once before finishing, row supersedes the previous live row; next run's prompt carries the block with an explicit age ('recorded 24h ago at <ts>'). Failure: session ends without calling carry_forward → the previous row is NOT superseded and the next run is told 'the last run (<ts>) recorded no carry-forward' — an honest gap, never a silently stale block presented as fresh. Concurrency: the scheduler already claims an occurrence atomically (scheduler.py:2183-2212); the continuity write is guarded by the same claim plus the partial unique index, so two ticks cannot both supersede. Idempotence: carry_forward is upsert-by-(butler, task, session_id); a retried tool call overwrites its own row, never appends a second. Rollback: the injection layer is per-task opt-in via a `continuity = true` field on ScheduleConfig (config.py parse_schedule); a task without it behaves exactly as today. Staleness guard: a carry_forward older than N cadence periods is injected as historical with its age, never as current.
moves.verification: (1) A scheduler test at the real dispatch seam asserting run N+1's `dispatched_prompt` contains run N's carry_forward block and its recorded timestamp. (2) A gap test: run N ends without calling carry_forward; assert run N+1's prompt names the gap rather than replaying run N-1's block as current. (3) A concurrency test firing two ticks for the same task against the existing atomic claim and asserting exactly one live continuity row. (4) An idempotence test calling carry_forward twice in one session and asserting one row. (5) A chronicler regression test asserting the day-close prompt produced by the general layer is equivalent to today's hard-coded hook output, so the refactor is provably behavior-preserving.
moves.slice_plan: Slice 1: migration + public.task_continuity + sessions.continuation_of_session_id; write-only, nothing reads it. Slice 2: carry_forward core tool; observe which recurring tasks actually record something. Slice 3: injection for two high-value recurring tasks (a briefing and a finance check) behind the per-task opt-in, with the age stamp and the gap wording. Slice 4: migrate the chronicler day-close hook onto the general layer and delete the bespoke prompt_hooks map; extend opt-in across the roster.
moves.manifesto: roster/chronicler/MANIFESTO.md (day-close continuity is already its concern and its bespoke hook becomes the first citizen of the general layer) plus roster/general/MANIFESTO.md and roster/finance/MANIFESTO.md for recurring briefings. No amendment needed — this is the mechanism those manifestos already assume exists.

moves.title: Consequence-gated verification lane: an independent check before an irreversible act leaves the system
moves.why: `Consequence` (dispatch_intent.py:57-67) is derived deterministically for every single dispatch and consumed at exactly one line in the whole repository (dispatch_intent.py:299) to tolerate an unknown model capability. An EXTERNAL dispatch about to send mail or actuate a light and a REVERSIBLE tick updating a cache receive identical treatment everywhere else, and grep confirms no verifier, second-opinion or ensemble concept exists anywhere in src/. The run-11 physical-consequence gate (RFC 0028) proved the owner wants a door on actuation; this puts a *reasoning* check behind that door rather than only an approval prompt, so the owner is not the only verifier in the loop. Owner-visible within a week: outbound acts carry a verdict — 'verified against 3 evidence items' or 'verifier disagreed, held for you' — and a mismatch routes to the approvals spine instead of to the recipient. Serves the north star clause that every consequential clause is a door on an unbroken signal-to-session-to-evidence spine.
moves.integration_points: New table public.act_verifications (session_id, act_tool_call_ref, consequence, verifier_session_id, verdict, disagreement_reason, evidence_refs JSONB, decided_at); a post-invoke hook in spawner._run's success path (after the tool-call merge at spawner.py:2500-2545, before session_complete) that fires only when `dispatch_intent.consequence is Consequence.EXTERNAL` AND the merged tool_calls contain a registered irreversible verb; a bounded cheap-tier verifier dispatch (trigger_source 'verification', a new entry in `_TRIGGER_PROFILES` with Consequence.OBSERVE and no MCP wiring beyond a read-only evidence tool) that sees the act payload and the session's own tool-call trace, never the raw prompt; integration with modules/approvals so a disagreement produces an approval rather than an egress; openspec/specs/module-approvals and openspec/specs/core-spawner MODIFIED; the irreversible-verb registry reuses the RFC 0028 risk map rather than inventing a second one.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: an EXTERNAL session proposes an irreversible act; the verifier agrees; the act proceeds and the receipt carries the verdict and the verifier's session id. Disagreement: the act is held and an approval is created naming the disagreement reason — the owner sees a door, not a silent block. Failure: the verifier session itself fails, times out, or is quota-denied → the act is held with verdict `unverifiable` (fail-closed for irreversible acts; a verifier that cannot run must never read as agreement). Concurrency: verification is keyed on (session_id, act_tool_call_ref) with a unique constraint, so a replayed hook cannot double-verify or double-approve; the verifier itself carries the parent's logical_session_id so spend rolls up to one unit. Idempotence: re-running the hook for an already-verified act returns the stored verdict. Rollback: gated per irreversible verb in the RFC 0028 risk map — an empty map means zero verifications and the loop is unchanged; the ceiling and per-call gates already apply to the verifier dispatch, so it cannot escape the budget spine.
moves.verification: (1) A spawner test asserting the hook fires for consequence=EXTERNAL plus a registered verb and does NOT fire for the same verb at REVERSIBLE, proving the enum is finally load-bearing. (2) A fail-closed test: verifier raises → assert verdict `unverifiable`, act held, approval created, and no egress tool call executed. (3) An idempotence test replaying the hook and asserting one public.act_verifications row and one approval. (4) A cost test asserting the verifier attempt appears under the parent's logical_session_id so /api/spend attributes it to the act, not to a phantom session. (5) An approvals integration test asserting a disagreement lands in the existing approval spine with the disagreement reason as its dossier, not as a new bespoke surface.
moves.slice_plan: Slice 1: the irreversible-verb registry, sourced from the shipped RFC 0028 risk map, plus public.act_verifications — shadow mode only, recording what WOULD have been verified. Slice 2: run the verifier and record verdicts without holding anything; measure the disagreement rate before granting it authority. Slice 3: grant holding authority for one verb class the owner picks (home actuation is the natural first, given RFC 0028 already gates it). Slice 4: extend to outbound message egress via the Messenger contract; surface the verdict on the act receipt.
moves.manifesto: roster/messenger/MANIFESTO.md needs an amendment: Messenger owns outbound delivery, so a pre-egress verification verdict becomes part of its delivery contract (what it will and will not deliver unverified). roster/home/MANIFESTO.md and RFC 0028 already carry the actuation half. If the owner prefers not to amend Messenger, the alternative is a new 'Auditor' staffer whose infrastructure contract is exactly this lane — but amending Messenger is the smaller, more honest change.

moves.title: Owner-settable dispatch SLOs with a degrade door: make the intent envelope's dead fields real
moves.why: DispatchIntent declares a deadline, a context floor and a per-call cost cap, and evaluate_fit implements exclusion codes for all three — yet on the production path min_context_tokens and max_cost_usd_per_call have zero call sites and deadline_s is supplied only by healing and QA (spawner.py:1293; healing/dispatch.py:670; qa/dispatch.py:1720,3079), the two classes where nobody is waiting. The interactive route and dashboard classes always pass None, so DEADLINE_EXCEEDED can never fire for the dispatches the owner is actually sitting in front of. Separately, max_tool_calls has no control plane at all (spawner.py:200). Owner-visible within a week: for the first time the owner can say 'answer me within 15 seconds or tell me you cannot' and get an honest partial or a named refusal instead of a spinner — and can cap what a single dashboard turn is allowed to cost. Serves architecture.md § Why Connectors Are the Computational Cost Boundary by extending the same 'gate before the expensive thing' principle to the dispatch itself, and the north star's 'earned calm'.
moves.integration_points: New table public.dispatch_slo keyed (butler_name, trigger_class, complexity) with deadline_s, max_cost_usd_per_call, min_context_tokens, max_tool_calls, degrade_mode ('partial' | 'refuse'); read in spawner._run immediately before `derive_dispatch_intent` (spawner.py:1293) and passed as the caller-supplied bounds the function already accepts; max_tool_calls threaded to the existing but unreachable `_check_tool_call_budget` (spawner_guardrails.py:101-128); the resolution receipt records which SLO row applied and which FitCode excluded whom; Settings surface alongside the Models/Spend tabs (GET/PUT /api/settings/dispatch-slo, following docs/api_and_protocols/response-conventions.md); openspec/specs/core-spawner and openspec/specs/model-catalog MODIFIED. Deliberate boundary with the sibling economics work: this move supplies owner POLICY into the existing fit evaluation; it does not split a dispatch into phases or change candidate ranking.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: an SLO row exists; its bounds populate the intent; unfit candidates are excluded by the already-implemented FitCodes and the receipt names the exclusion. Nothing fits: degrade_mode='refuse' → the dispatch is denied with a named reason on a quota_skip-shaped attempt row (the existing denial vocabulary, not a new one) and the owner sees 'no model can meet your 15s budget for this trigger'; degrade_mode='partial' → the dispatch runs with the deadline forwarded as the session timeout and its result is marked partial-within-budget rather than presented as complete. No SLO row: behavior is byte-for-byte today's. Failure: the SLO read errors → fail open to today's unbounded behavior and record the read failure on the receipt, because an unreadable policy must not silently tighten or loosen a budget. Concurrency: policy rows are read per spawn; an edit mid-flight affects the next dispatch only, and the receipt pins the row version that applied. Idempotence: pure read. Rollback: deleting a row restores unbounded behavior for that (butler, trigger_class, complexity) immediately.
moves.verification: (1) A resolution test asserting that with a 15s deadline row, a candidate whose recent evidence proves p95 > 15s is excluded with FitCode.DEADLINE_EXCEEDED — the code path that today can never execute for route/dashboard. (2) A degrade test for both modes asserting refuse produces a named denial with no invocation, and partial marks the result honestly rather than reporting success. (3) A guardrail-reachability test asserting a non-zero max_tool_calls from the SLO row actually produces a tool_call_budget_exceeded termination, closing the unreachable-guardrail finding. (4) A fail-open test asserting an SLO read error leaves the dispatch unbounded AND records the failure on the receipt. (5) A receipt test asserting the applied SLO row version is persisted, so a past dispatch can be read against the policy that produced it (mirroring DISPATCH_POLICY_VERSION at dispatch_intent.py:54).
moves.slice_plan: Slice 1: migration + public.dispatch_slo + read-only API, no enforcement — the owner can author policy and see which dispatches would have been affected. Slice 2: wire deadline_s and max_cost_usd_per_call into derive_dispatch_intent with degrade_mode='refuse' for the `dashboard` trigger class only (smallest blast radius, owner is present to see the refusal). Slice 3: wire max_tool_calls to the existing guardrail and add the partial degrade mode. Slice 4: Settings UI and the receipt's applied-policy row.
moves.manifesto: No butler owns the dispatch loop, so this lands on core doctrine: vision.md non-negotiable #5 (operational tuning lives in the database, edited via the dashboard) is exactly the shape of this table, and architecture.md § The Core Loop keeps the decision deterministic in the daemon. It implies a Concierge MANIFESTO amendment so the fleet read model can answer 'which dispatches missed your SLO and why' — Concierge already owns session and spend telemetry.

moves.title: Forced continuation on guardrail and deadline termination: stop throwing away work the owner paid for
moves.why: When a guardrail trips, the adapter has already returned result_text (spawner.py:2554) and the tokens are already billed (captured into the ledger vars at spawner.py:2537-2543), yet the outer handler writes output=None (spawner.py:2975), store_session_episode (spawner.py:2751) is never reached, and the failover classifier explicitly suppresses any retry (failover_classifier.py:269-270). The same is true of a deadline stop. Against 2,668 failed sessions in the live week, that is a standing policy of paying for reasoning and discarding it. Owner-visible within a week: long jobs stop vanishing — the session detail shows the partial answer and 'continued as <session>' instead of a bare error, and the fleet's failure rate stops overstating how much was actually lost. Serves the north star's 'nothing fabricated, failure never impersonates health' from the other direction: a session that produced something must not be recorded as having produced nothing.
moves.integration_points: New table public.session_handoffs (session_id, logical_session_id, termination_reason, partial_output, tool_call_digest JSONB, continuation_session_id, created_at) with a unique key on (logical_session_id, session_id); spawner._run's guardrail branch (spawner.py:2559-2568) persists the partial before raising, and the outer handler (spawner.py:2971-2977) writes session_complete with the partial output plus the termination error rather than output=None; one bounded continuation dispatch for Consequence.REVERSIBLE trigger classes only, seeded with the handoff; sessions.continuation_of_session_id shared with the task-continuity move; openspec/specs/core-spawner MODIFIED (Guardrail Termination requirement gains an output-preservation clause); the session detail API and page render the handoff and the chain. Shares the escalation move's substrate: both are 'one bounded re-dispatch under the same logical_session_id', and they should be built as one mechanism with two entry doors.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path (preservation only): guardrail trips; partial output and the tool digest are persisted; the session row is honestly failed WITH its output; the episode is stored marked partial. Continuation: for a REVERSIBLE trigger class, exactly one continuation dispatch is seeded with the handoff and the same logical_session_id. No continuation for EXTERNAL consequence — a half-finished outward act must not be resumed automatically; it becomes an owner-visible partial instead. Failure: the handoff write itself fails → the original error path is preserved unchanged (best-effort, never blocks the terminal outcome), matching how _write_dispatch_attempt and session_process_log_write already behave. Concurrency: the unique (logical_session_id, session_id) key means a retried handler cannot write two handoffs or spawn two continuations. Idempotence: continuation is keyed on the handoff row; replaying returns the existing continuation_session_id. Rollback: continuation is gated by a runtime_config flag; with it off, only the preservation half ships, which is pure honesty and has no cost implication.
moves.verification: (1) A spawner test tripping the degenerate-loop guardrail with a non-empty result_text and asserting session_complete receives that text — the exact inversion of today's output=None, and the direct regression test for the finding. (2) An episode test asserting the partial reaches store_session_episode marked partial rather than being silently skipped. (3) A consequence test asserting an EXTERNAL-consequence guardrail termination produces a handoff but NO continuation. (4) An idempotence test replaying the termination handler and asserting one handoff row and one continuation. (5) A cost-attribution test asserting the continuation shares logical_session_id so the pair reads as one logical unit in /api/spend rather than as two independent failures plus a success.
moves.slice_plan: Slice 1 (ship alone, S): preservation only — persist partial output and the tool digest, write session_complete with the output, store the partial episode. No new dispatch, no cost change, pure honesty repair. Slice 2: public.session_handoffs + session-detail rendering of the partial and the termination reason. Slice 3: the bounded continuation for REVERSIBLE trigger classes, built on the escalation move's re-dispatch mechanism so there is one path, not two. Slice 4: reachable max_tool_calls (from the SLO move) makes the guardrail fireable, at which point continuation is what keeps that guardrail safe to enable.
moves.manifesto: Core doctrine rather than a butler contract: architecture.md § The Core Loop step 6 (Log: 'records the session: trigger source, tools called, tokens consumed, duration, and outcome') is violated when the outcome is recorded as nothing while tokens are recorded as spent. No amendment required; this is a repair to an existing obligation, and openspec/specs/core-spawner's Guardrail Termination requirement is the spec that changes.

findings.title: Every fact is born with confidence = 1.0; the credence numeral the fleet renders everywhere denominates nothing but time-since-confirmation
findings.detail: `_insert_fact` passes a literal `1.0` for the `confidence` column (src/butlers/modules/memory/storage.py:1343) and `store_fact` exposes no `confidence` parameter at all (signature at storage.py:1366-1393), so no writer — session, consolidation, or connector — can express uncertainty. The catalog projection hardcodes the same value (`confidence=1.0`, storage.py:2029). The composite retrieval score reserves a 0.1 weight for confidence (search.py:342-348, 409) but with base credence constant that term collapses to `exp(-decay_rate * days_since_confirmed)` — it ranks staleness, not belief. The retrieval floor `min_confidence=0.2` (search.py:468, 541-547) is therefore a staleness cutoff misnamed as a confidence filter. Downstream this is presented as calibrated belief: `_format_fact_line` writes `(confidence: 0.94)` into every butler's system prompt (tools/context.py:150-155) and the dashboard's FactsRegister renders it as the row's 'belief numeral' with confidence-as-ink dimming (frontend/src/components/memory/FactsRegister.tsx:68-71, 84-90, 143-145, 255). Net effect: a fact the owner stated in person, a fact scraped from an ambiguous email, and a fact an LLM guessed during consolidation all assert identical authority to every reader.
findings.evidence: src/butlers/modules/memory/storage.py:1343; src/butlers/modules/memory/storage.py:1366-1393; src/butlers/modules/memory/storage.py:2029; src/butlers/modules/memory/search.py:342-348,409,541-547; src/butlers/modules/memory/tools/context.py:150-155; frontend/src/components/memory/FactsRegister.tsx:68-71,143-145; src/butlers/modules/memory/migrations/001_memory_schema.py:114; live: GET /api/memory/facts?limit=200 -> 200/200 rows confidence=1.0 of 6303 total
findings.taxonomy_shape: aggregate that denominates nothing (a scoring term and a rendered numeral computed from a constant, presented as calibrated credence)

findings.title: Local memory reads have no sensitivity ceiling while the cross-butler catalog has a server-held one — confidential owner facts enter every butler's system prompt unfiltered
findings.detail: Catalog reads resolve a server-held ceiling from `runtime_config.catalog_read_sensitivity` and filter with `COALESCE(sensitivity,'normal') = ANY(...)`, failing closed to `['normal']` on an unknown ceiling (search.py:817-860, 885, 927 — core_209 read authority). The same module's *local* pool reads have no equivalent: `_apply_filters` treats `sensitivity` as a caller-supplied equality selector (search.py:659-661), so omitting it returns `pii` and `confidential` rows, and passing `normal` wrongly excludes nothing above it by ceiling semantics but by exact match. `memory_context`'s Profile Facts query filters only on tenant, validity and the owner role — no sensitivity predicate at all (tools/context.py:52-63) — and the assembled block is injected into the spawned session's system prompt. So the fleet governs what one butler may learn *about another butler's* knowledge, but not what any butler may be told about the owner's most sensitive facts. There is also no withheld count, so a caller cannot tell that anything was (or was not) omitted — the opposite of the honesty RFC 0031 built into its withheld-stub design.
findings.evidence: src/butlers/modules/memory/search.py:659-661; src/butlers/modules/memory/search.py:817-860,885,927; src/butlers/modules/memory/tools/context.py:52-63; about/legends-and-lore/rfcs/0031-public-entity-graph-projection.md (Withheld Stub Edges)
findings.taxonomy_shape: gate that is metadata (sensitivity is stored on every row and enforced on exactly one of two read paths)

findings.title: Profile Facts — 30% of every butler's memory context — degenerates into a receipt feed and bypasses the retrieval floor
findings.detail: `_fetch_profile_facts` selects owner-entity facts `ORDER BY importance DESC, created_at DESC, id ASC` with no predicate or knowledge-class filter (tools/context.py:47-70). `importance` defaults to 5.0 (001_memory_schema.py:113) and is 5.0 on 108 of 200 sampled live rows, so the ordering degenerates to 'most recent owner facts'. Live, the owner entity's newest facts are `transaction_debit` ('SODENG AMOY 284.16 SGD') and `tomorrow_prep_briefing_sent` ('The specialist briefing payload was empty…') — operational receipts, not profile knowledge. Separately, this section applies no confidence floor: `recall` discards rows below `min_confidence=0.2` (search.py:541-547) but Profile Facts is a raw SQL fetch, and `_effective_confidence` returns exactly 0.0 whenever `last_confirmed_at IS NULL` with a non-zero decay rate (tools/context.py:135-146), so a fact can be injected into the system prompt rendered as `(confidence: 0.00)`. The highest-privilege slice of every butler's context is therefore both mis-selected and un-floored.
findings.evidence: src/butlers/modules/memory/tools/context.py:47-70,135-146,150-155; src/butlers/modules/memory/migrations/001_memory_schema.py:113; src/butlers/modules/memory/search.py:541-547; live: GET /api/memory/entities/c64f5aed-9b1f-492e-bab2-86c986c31ebd -> recent_facts[0].predicate=transaction_debit, fact_count=2531; GET /api/memory/facts?limit=200 -> importance 5.0 on 108/200
findings.taxonomy_shape: NEW: privileged context slice selected by a proxy that no longer discriminates (default-valued sort key collapses a semantic ranking into recency)

findings.title: memory_entity_neighbors presents one butler's private slice as 'the entity graph', with no coverage statement
findings.detail: `entity_neighbors` runs its recursive CTE over the *calling butler's own* `facts` table (`FROM facts f WHERE f.entity_id = $1 …`, tools/entities.py:709-745), so Health's answer to 'who is connected to Chloe' contains only edges Health itself wrote. The tool is documented fleet-wide as 'Get graph neighbors of an entity' (docs/modules/memory.md:94) and returns a bare neighbour list with no source-scope or coverage field, so a partial view is indistinguishable from a complete one. RFC 0031 exists precisely because this cross-butler union has no home (about/legends-and-lore/rfcs/0031-public-entity-graph-projection.md, Motivation), but until its writers land the existing tool keeps answering the graph question with a schema-local answer that never says so.
findings.evidence: src/butlers/modules/memory/tools/entities.py:658-745 (esp. 709-745); docs/modules/memory.md:94; about/legends-and-lore/rfcs/0031-public-entity-graph-projection.md (Motivation)
findings.taxonomy_shape: NEW: partial-scope read wearing whole-graph authority (no coverage clause on a deliberately narrowed traversal)

findings.title: memory_context section budgets sum to 110% of the declared hard token budget, and the fifth section is undocumented
findings.detail: The five section fractions are 0.30 + 0.35 + 0.20 + 0.15 + 0.10 = 1.10 (tools/context.py:33-38), and each section receives an independent `int(total_chars * frac)` slice of the same `token_budget * 4` (tools/context.py:254-258) with no shared remaining-budget accounting in `_fill_section` (tools/context.py:181-215). With `include_fleet_knowledge=True` the assembled block can therefore exceed the budget the docstring calls a hard cap by 10%. docs/modules/memory.md:116 still states 'a hard token budget. Four sections in fixed order' — the Fleet Knowledge section (tools/context.py:99-133) is absent from the documented contract.
findings.evidence: src/butlers/modules/memory/tools/context.py:33-38,181-215,254-258; docs/modules/memory.md:116
findings.taxonomy_shape: NEW: budget declared hard, allocated per-section from the same pool (sum > 1) so the cap is advisory

findings.title: Structured search filters silently ignore unrecognized keys, so a mistyped or unsupported filter returns unfiltered results
findings.detail: `_apply_filters` documents and implements exactly eight keys and states 'Unrecognized filter keys are silently ignored per spec' (search.py:580-608). A caller passing `validity`, `permanence`, `tags`, or a typo receives the full result set with no error and no echoed effective-filter set, so a narrowing intent silently becomes a widening one. The dashboard's own facts endpoint supports `validity` and `permanence` filters (api/routers/memory.py:860-916), so the MCP and HTTP filter vocabularies diverge without either side declaring it.
findings.evidence: src/butlers/modules/memory/search.py:580-608,659-661; src/butlers/api/routers/memory.py:860-916
findings.taxonomy_shape: gate that is metadata (a filter argument accepted, recorded nowhere, applied never)

audits.ideal: A JARVIS-grade knowledge graph is one the owner can interrogate in plain language and be told the truth about, including the truth about its own blind spots. Every belief carries a calibrated credence and an evidence class (you told me / a connector observed it / a session inferred it / it was derived), so an inference can never quietly overwrite an assertion and no reader mistakes a guess for a statement. Every belief is one hop from the artefact that caused it — the email, the message, the session — and when that trail is broken the system says exactly where it broke rather than showing a plausible-looking chain. Reads are governed by one sensitivity ceiling with an honest withheld count, so the owner can mark something confidential and know it will not be pasted into the Home butler's prompt, and can see that something was withheld without seeing what. The graph is the substrate for spawn-time context: each butler starts with the owner's actual profile knowledge plus the named people and things in the current trigger resolved to entities and their one-hop neighbourhood — never a recency feed of transaction receipts. It knows what a complete picture of a person looks like and reports the gaps as first-class absence (never known / stale / no butler owns this), which turns the graph from a store into a conversation partner that can ask the owner the one question that would most improve it. And the owner can correct it from any channel with one verb, getting a receipt, with corrections structurally dominant over inference forever after.
audits.jarvis_gap: The substrate is genuinely strong and genuinely live: 6,303 facts across the fleet with 2,531 anchored to the owner entity, entity anchoring on both edge ends, a predicate registry that already encodes `is_edge`/`is_temporal`/`inverse_of`/`is_symmetric` with automatic inverse-fact closure inside the write transaction (storage.py:1839-1900), a server-held catalog read ceiling (core_209), and now `public.entity_graph_edges` with a schema-enforced withheld-stub invariant (core_215/RFC 0031). What is missing is the entire trust and consumption layer above it. Credence is a constant 1.0 on every row ever written, yet is rendered as a two-decimal 'belief numeral' in the dashboard and injected into every butler's system prompt — the one number the owner would use to calibrate trust is fabricated. Sensitivity is enforced on cross-butler catalog reads and on nothing else, so the most sensitive owner facts flow unfiltered into every spawned session. The spawn-time context pack spends 30% of its budget on the owner's most recent facts, which live are HSBC transaction alerts and 'briefing sent' receipts. `memory_entity_neighbors` answers the graph question with one butler's private slice and never says so. Nothing anywhere resolves a name in the trigger prompt to an entity before retrieving, so recall is embedding luck. And the owner cannot ask the graph anything: `dashboard_read` is system-plane only by Concierge's own manifesto (roster/concierge/MANIFESTO.md: 'It never answers a domain question'), so 'who is Chloe to me', 'what don't you know about my inner circle', and 'why do you believe that' have no answering authority in the fleet at all.
audits.live_verification: Dev stack up and read-only queries only (no POST/PATCH/PUT/DELETE issued). Live-confirmed via http://127.0.0.1:42200: GET /api/butlers (12 agents, chronicler/concierge ok); GET /api/memory/entities?limit=3 (owner entity c64f5aed… 'Tze How Lee', roles=[owner], fact_count 2526→2531 during the audit, 7 aliases; 'Lee Hui Min' dunbar_tier 5 score 43.04; 'Chloe Wong' 470 facts); GET /api/memory/entities/{owner} (recent_facts[0] predicate=transaction_debit content='SODENG AMOY 284.16 SGD' confidence=1.0 source_episode_id set; recent_facts[1] predicate=tomorrow_prep_briefing_sent confidence=1.0 source_episode_id=null session_id=null); GET /api/memory/facts?limit=200 over 6,303 total — confidence=1.0 on 200/200, importance 5.0 on 108/200, predicate histogram led by device_issue (62), listening_session (21), measurement_weight (15). Statically confirmed (source read, not executed): the hardcoded 1.0 at storage.py:1343 and 2029; the missing `confidence` parameter on store_fact; the sensitivity equality-filter vs catalog ceiling asymmetry; the 1.10 budget sum; `_fetch_profile_facts` having no sensitivity or class predicate; `entity_neighbors` traversing the local `facts` table. Also confirmed statically: `public.entity_graph_edges` has zero writers anywhere in src/ or roster/ (grep over *.py returns only the migration and docs), consistent with RFC 0031 Slice 1 being the only landed slice — so every proposal below that touches the public graph is written to compose with S2 writers rather than assume them.

moves.title: Expected knowledge: per-entity completeness against a declared profile expectation (honest absence for what you know about people)
moves.why: vision.md 'What Success Looks Like' promises the owner's relationship context is maintained without manual entry, and Relationship's manifesto binds the butler to 'a complete picture of the people in your life' under the Dunbar model (roster/relationship/MANIFESTO.md, 'Richness' + 'The Dunbar Model'). Today the graph can only report what it has; it cannot report what a complete picture would require, so silence about a person is indistinguishable from knowing nothing. This applies the exact pattern the fleet already accepted for signals — public.expected_signals with unmeasurable semantics (RFC 0029) — to knowledge. Owner-visible payoff in week one: a single view saying, for the ~15 people in the inner Dunbar tiers, exactly which high-value facts have never been known, which have gone stale past their expectation window, and which no butler is even capable of learning — every row a door to one question worth asking.
moves.manifesto: roster/relationship/MANIFESTO.md ('a complete picture of the people in your life', Dunbar model). No amendment needed; the expectation table is the machine-readable form of a promise the manifesto already makes.
moves.integration_points: New `public.expected_knowledge` (core migration, shaped after core_210/211 expected_signals): rows keyed (entity_type, dunbar_tier_max, predicate) with `expectation_window_days`, `owning_butler`, `value_tier`, plus `unmeasurable_reason` for predicates no butler owns. New zero-LLM core tool `entity_knowledge_gaps(entity_id, tiers?)` in a `graph` core tool group (mirrors the group RFC 0031 S3 reserves) reading `public.entities` (roles, dunbar_tier — live-confirmed on GET /api/memory/entities) joined against the per-pool `facts` fan-out already implemented in src/butlers/api/routers/memory.py:1636-1792 and the entity-anchored columns on public.memory_catalog (core_009/core_024). New `GET /api/memory/entities/{id}/gaps` and `GET /api/memory/gaps?tier<=N` using the existing DegradedSources envelope (src/butlers/api/routers/memory.py:860-963) so an unreachable pool yields `unknown`, never `never_known`. Spec: new capability in openspec/specs/memory-discovery-catalog or a sibling `memory-expected-knowledge`; frontend consumer on EntityDetailPage (frontend/src/pages/EntityDetailPage.tsx:2193 already hosts a per-fact confidence/staleness inspector).
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy: expectation row exists, a matching active fact exists inside its window -> `satisfied` with the fact id and last_confirmed_at. Gap kinds: no matching fact -> `never_known`; matching fact whose last_confirmed_at is older than expectation_window_days -> `stale` (with the fact id, so it is a confirm door not a re-ask); expectation row carrying unmeasurable_reason -> `unmeasurable` with the reason, never counted as a gap the owner can close. Failure: one memory pool unreachable -> that pool's predicates return `unknown` with null fact ids and the response carries meta.pools_failed; a completed subset is explicitly lower-bound evidence, never a fleet all-clear (same contract as openspec/specs/memory-graph-health REQ-002). Concurrency: read-only, no locks; a fact written mid-read simply lands in the next read. Idempotence: pure read, no writes, no reference_count bump. Rollback: drop the tool + endpoints; the expectation table is inert data with no readers.
moves.verification: pytest at the module seam, not the HTTP shell: a test that seeds one satisfied / one never_known / one stale / one unmeasurable expectation and asserts the four distinct verdicts with no zero-filling; a test that a predicate whose owning_butler pool raises is reported `unknown` with null metrics and named in pools_failed (asserting the exact DegradedSources behavior, not a mocked envelope); a test that `unmeasurable` rows never enter the closable-gap count denominator; a determinism test that the same fixture yields byte-identical ordering.
moves.slice_plan: S1: migration + expectation seed for the person/inner-tier predicate set Relationship's manifesto already names (birthday, how-we-met, employer, relation-to-owner, last-interaction). S2: `entity_knowledge_gaps` core tool with the four verdicts and the degraded contract. S3: the two API routes on the existing fan-out. S4: EntityDetailPage gap panel + a fleet 'blind spots' lens keyed to Dunbar tier. S5: each gap row becomes an ask-me door once the correction verb (move 7) exists.

moves.title: Entity-grounded recall: names in the trigger prompt become graph anchors before embeddings get a vote
moves.why: architecture.md's daemon-deterministic doctrine says the deterministic layer should do the deterministic work; today the only path from 'Hui Min mentioned her new job' to what the fleet knows about Hui Min is MiniLM cosine similarity over a scope-filtered fact set (src/butlers/modules/memory/search.py:468-570), even though `memory_entity_resolve` and a 2,531-fact entity anchor already exist. The graph's most valuable property — that facts are keyed to stable identities — is invisible to retrieval. Owner-visible payoff in week one: mention a person, place, or thing by name in any channel and the butler's answer reliably reflects what it actually knows about that entity, instead of whatever the embedding happened to rank in the top 30.
moves.manifesto: roster/relationship/MANIFESTO.md ('You're not scrambling to recall context') and roster/general/MANIFESTO.md ('Find what you need… Discover connections you'd forgotten about'). No amendment needed.
moves.integration_points: `src/butlers/modules/memory/search.py:recall` (:468-570) gains a deterministic anchor pass; `src/butlers/modules/memory/tools/entities.py:entity_resolve` supplies name->entity candidates (its alias/trigram path already exists); `src/butlers/modules/memory/tools/context.py` Task-Relevant Facts section (:246-268) reserves a sub-quota for anchored facts; `predicate_registry.is_edge` (001_memory_schema.py:406-430) selects the 1-hop edge facts to include; `public.entities.aliases` (live: 7 aliases on the owner) is the match surface. Spec: amend openspec/specs/module-memory's retrieval requirement to state that entity-anchored candidates are unioned deterministically, with the composite score used only to order within the union.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy: prompt contains a resolvable name -> its entity-anchored active/fading facts plus its 1-hop edge facts are unioned into the candidate set under a reserved sub-quota, then ordered by the existing composite score; a fact that would have missed the similarity cutoff is now present with an `anchor_reason` field naming the resolved entity. Failure: name resolves to multiple candidates above threshold -> anchor on none, emit an `ambiguous_anchor` marker listing the candidates (never silently pick the highest-scoring 'Chloe'); resolver raises -> degrade to today's pure similarity path and record that the anchor pass was skipped, so the caller can tell. Concurrency: read-only; the existing reference_count bump (search.py:567-568) applies to anchored rows exactly once per result, same as similarity rows. Idempotence: identical inputs produce identical output (the module's stated determinism contract). Rollback: a runtime_config flag disables the anchor pass and retrieval returns to the current behavior with no schema change to undo.
moves.verification: A test that seeds a target entity whose facts are deliberately embedded far from the query wording and asserts they appear in recall output with `anchor_reason` set — i.e. the test fails under the current similarity-only path. A test that two entities sharing an alias produce `ambiguous_anchor` and zero anchored facts. A test that a raising resolver degrades rather than fails and marks the skip. A determinism test over the fused ordering. An assertion that reference_count is incremented once, not twice, for a fact that both anchors and matches.
moves.slice_plan: S1: anchor resolution helper with the ambiguity rule and a typed AnchorOutcome. S2: union into `recall` behind a runtime_config flag, sub-quota'd. S3: wire into memory_context's task section and render `anchor_reason` in the fact line so a session can cite why a fact was surfaced. S4: extend from person entities to place/org entity_types once the gap read (move 1) shows which types carry enough facts to matter.

moves.title: Why do you believe that: a deterministic fact provenance chain with named breakage
moves.why: Chronicler's manifesto binds it to 'preserve source provenance on every row… and let you correct me when I am wrong' (roster/chronicler/MANIFESTO.md); the fact store makes the same implicit promise and cannot keep it. A fact carries `source_episode_id` (nullable), a `metadata.source` free-text string ('HSBC credit card transaction alert email' — live-confirmed) that no reader can resolve to an artefact, and a `supersedes_id` link. Nothing joins those into a chain, and the dashboard already exposes an unresolved-provenance state it cannot explain (frontend/src/components/memory/FactsRegister.tsx:87-90 renders source_episode_status 'unresolved'). Owner-visible payoff in week one: click any belief and see the actual message, session, and ingestion event that produced it — or be told exactly which hop is missing, instead of a plausible-looking blank.
moves.manifesto: roster/chronicler/MANIFESTO.md (provenance-on-every-row, correction-friendly) applied to the shared memory module. Implies a small amendment to openspec/specs/module-memory: provenance resolution is a required read surface of the memory module, not a Chronicler-only property.
moves.integration_points: New core tool `memory_fact_provenance(fact_id)` + `GET /api/memory/facts/{id}/provenance`. Joins: `facts.source_episode_id` -> `episodes` (and `episode_tombstones`, already joined by `_with_source_episode_status`, src/butlers/api/routers/memory.py:1033-1049) -> `episodes.session_id` -> the sessions read model used by src/butlers/api/routers/sessions.py -> `facts.request_id` -> `switchboard.ingestion_events` (src/butlers/api/routers/ingestion_events.py) -> the connector message reference; plus `memory_links` relation='supersedes' (written at storage.py:1826-1834) for revision lineage. Reuses the existing per-butler fan-out and DegradedSources envelope. Frontend: FactDetailPage (frontend/src/pages/FactDetailPage.tsx) provenance panel.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy: full chain fact -> episode -> session -> ingestion event -> connector message, each hop a typed node with its own id and as_of, and each an existing dashboard route. Terminal states, all explicit and distinguishable: `owner_asserted` (no upstream expected — pairs with move 4's evidence class); `episode_tombstoned` (the episode existed and was reaped; the tombstone is the evidence); `chain_broken_at=<stage>` when a hop's key is null (live-confirmed case: a general-butler fact with source_episode_id, session_id and source_episode_status all null); `cross_schema_unreadable` when the upstream row lives in a schema the caller's role cannot read — reported as unreadable, never as absent. Failure: an upstream pool unreachable -> that hop is `unknown` with the pool named in meta.pools_failed. Concurrency: read-only; a concurrently-reaped episode surfaces as tombstoned on the next read, not as a fabricated hop. Idempotence: pure read. Rollback: remove tool + route; no schema change.
moves.verification: One test per terminal state, each asserting the *stage name* rather than a generic failure: full chain; source_episode_id null -> chain_broken_at='episode'; episode tombstoned -> episode_tombstoned with the tombstone id; session row absent -> chain_broken_at='session'; role denied on the upstream schema -> cross_schema_unreadable. A test that no hop is ever synthesized from `metadata.source` free text. A test that the supersedes lineage is returned in write order and terminates.
moves.slice_plan: S1: the join + typed node/terminal model as a pure function over rows, with the five terminal states. S2: core tool in the `graph` group. S3: the API route on the existing fan-out with the degraded envelope. S4: FactDetailPage panel where every hop is a link to its existing route. S5: expose the same chain from the dashboard chat's citation contract so a chat answer can cite the artefact, not the fact id.

moves.title: Calibrated credence and evidence class on every fact, with owner assertions structurally dominant over inference
moves.why: This is the load-bearing fix under every other graph consumer: while base confidence is a hardcoded 1.0 (storage.py:1343, 2029 — live-confirmed on 200/200 sampled rows of 6,303), the 0.1 confidence weight in the composite score, the 0.2 retrieval floor, the '(confidence: 0.94)' line injected into every butler's system prompt, and the dashboard's confidence-as-ink dimming all encode staleness while claiming belief. vision.md's non-negotiable framing of a system 'trusted with real decisions' and General's promise 'Once you tell us something, it's safe' both require that what the owner said outrank what a session guessed. Owner-visible payoff in week one: guesses stop asserting certainty, and a correction can no longer be silently overwritten by the next inference.
moves.manifesto: roster/general/MANIFESTO.md ('Reliability. Once you tell us something, it's safe.') and roster/relationship/MANIFESTO.md (thoughtfulness rests on accurate recall). No amendment needed; this makes an existing promise enforceable.
moves.integration_points: Memory-module migration adding `credence DOUBLE PRECISION` (semantically distinct from the decayed `confidence` column, or repurpose `confidence` as base credence and rename the decayed value at read time) and `evidence_class TEXT CHECK (evidence_class IN ('owner_asserted','connector_observed','llm_inferred','derived'))` on `facts`, plus the same pair on `public.memory_catalog` (core_009/core_209 vocabulary). `store_fact` signature (src/butlers/modules/memory/storage.py:1366-1393) gains both as required arguments; `_insert_fact` stops passing the literal 1.0 (:1343); `_upsert_catalog` carries the real value (:2029). `memory_store_fact` tool schema in src/butlers/modules/memory/tools/writing.py requires them; `src/butlers/modules/memory/consolidation_parser.py` must emit them per extracted fact and default to a class-specific floor rather than 1.0 when the model omits one. `search.py:342-348,409` scores real credence; `tools/context.py:150-155` prints class + credence; frontend/src/components/memory/FactsRegister.tsx:68-71,143-145 renders class alongside the numeral. Spec: amend openspec/specs/module-memory (fact write contract) and openspec/specs/memory-catalog-schema (enrichment fields).
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy: a writer supplies credence + evidence_class; both persist to the fact and its catalog row; the retrieval score and the rendered line reflect them. Precedence: an `llm_inferred` write against an existing `owner_asserted` fact on the same (entity_id, object_entity_id, scope, predicate) key is REJECTED with a typed error naming the incumbent fact id — the session must ask the owner or store nothing; it may not supersede. `connector_observed` may supersede `llm_inferred` but not `owner_asserted`. Failure: a writer omitting the fields is rejected at the tool boundary (no silent 1.0 default); a legacy row with NULL evidence_class reads as `unknown_provenance` and is scored at the `llm_inferred` floor, never at 1.0. Concurrency: precedence is evaluated inside the existing store_fact transaction that already holds the supersession lookup (storage.py:1733-1900), so two concurrent inferences cannot both win; the inverse-fact mirror (storage.py:1839-1900) inherits the parent's class and credence. Idempotence: unchanged — the temporal idempotency key path is untouched; a re-store with identical class/credence is a no-op confirm. Rollback: the migration is additive; reverting the writers leaves the columns populated and readers fall back to the `unknown_provenance` floor.
moves.verification: A test that `_insert_fact` persists the supplied credence and that the catalog row carries the same value (asserting against the real upsert, which is where the second hardcoded 1.0 lives). A test that an `llm_inferred` store against an `owner_asserted` incumbent raises a typed error naming the incumbent id and leaves the incumbent's validity untouched. A test that `connector_observed` supersedes `llm_inferred`. A test that a NULL-class legacy row scores at the inferred floor, not 1.0. A test that the inverse mirrored fact carries the parent's class. A context-assembly test asserting the rendered fact line names the class.
moves.slice_plan: S1: additive migration + `unknown_provenance` read semantics for the 6,303 existing rows (no backfill guess). S2: required arguments on store_fact and the MCP tool, with the class-floor default in consolidation_parser. S3: precedence rule inside the existing store transaction. S4: scoring + context line + FactsRegister render. S5: catalog projection carries both, unlocking a credence-aware cross-butler read.

moves.title: Knowledge-class the predicate registry and rebuild the spawn-time profile pack around it
moves.why: 30% of every spawned session's memory budget is the Profile Facts section, and live it is filled with HSBC transaction alerts and 'tomorrow-prep briefing sent' receipts, because the section orders owner facts by an importance column that is 5.0 on the majority of rows and then by recency (tools/context.py:47-70; importance default at 001_memory_schema.py:113). The predicate registry already exists with `is_edge`, `is_temporal`, `scope` and `status` — it is one column short of being able to say which predicates are *identity* knowledge versus operational exhaust. Owner-visible payoff in week one: butlers start every session knowing who you are and who the people around you are, instead of what you bought yesterday.
moves.manifesto: roster/general/MANIFESTO.md ('Once you tell us something, it's safe… waiting patiently for whenever you need it') and roster/relationship/MANIFESTO.md. No amendment needed. Deliberately not a fleet ontology — one enum column on an existing registry, not a taxonomy project.
moves.integration_points: Memory-module migration adding `knowledge_class TEXT CHECK (knowledge_class IN ('identity','preference','state','episodic','receipt'))` to `predicate_registry` (001_memory_schema.py:406-430), seeded across src/butlers/modules/memory/migrations/002_seed_predicates.py (the live offenders — transaction_debit, tomorrow_prep_briefing_sent, listening_session, measurement_* — classify as receipt/episodic/state). `tools/context.py:_fetch_profile_facts` (:47-70) joins the registry and restricts to identity+preference, adds the missing confidence floor, and adds the sensitivity ceiling from move 6. `_PROFILE_FACTS_FRAC` (:33) reallocates the reclaimed budget to the anchored task facts of move 2. docs/modules/memory.md:116 updated to the real five-section contract with the corrected fractions.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy: Profile Facts contains only identity/preference-class owner facts, ordered by credence (move 4) then importance then created_at, deterministic ties as today. Empty: if the owner has no identity-class facts, the section is omitted entirely (existing `_fill_section` contract) rather than backfilled with receipts — honest absence, and the gap read of move 1 is where that absence is reported. Failure: a predicate absent from the registry is treated as unclassified and excluded from Profile Facts (fail closed) while remaining fully available to task-relevant recall, so nothing is lost from retrieval. Concurrency/idempotence: pure read, deterministic for identical inputs. Rollback: revert the join; the enum column is inert.
moves.verification: A test that a receipt-class fact with the highest importance and newest created_at is absent from Profile Facts while still returned by recall. A test that a fact with `last_confirmed_at IS NULL` and non-zero decay is excluded rather than rendered as `(confidence: 0.00)` — the current bug at tools/context.py:135-146. A test that an unregistered predicate is excluded from Profile Facts but present in task facts. A test asserting the five section fractions sum to <= 1.0 and that a maximally-filled block with all opt-ins never exceeds token_budget * 4 characters (the current 1.10 sum, tools/context.py:33-38).
moves.slice_plan: S1: column + seed classification, no reader change (pure metadata, observable via memory_predicate_list). S2: Profile Facts join + confidence floor + section-fraction correction and the budget-sum assertion. S3: doc contract update. S4: expose knowledge_class in memory_predicate_list/search so a session can see why a predicate is or is not profile knowledge.

moves.title: One memory read ceiling: sensitivity governance on local recall and context, with an honest withheld count
moves.why: The fleet already decided that reads over knowledge must be governed: core_209 gave the cross-butler catalog a server-held sensitivity ceiling that fails closed to 'normal' (search.py:817-860, 885, 927), and RFC 0031 made 'a withheld thing still counts, its content never leaks' a schema-enforced invariant. Neither applies to a butler reading its own pool: sensitivity is a caller-supplied equality selector (search.py:659-661) and the Profile Facts query has no sensitivity predicate at all (tools/context.py:52-63), so the owner's confidential facts are pasted into every spawned session's system prompt. Owner-visible payoff in week one: marking something confidential actually restricts where it can appear, and the context block says 'N withheld' so the restriction is visible without being revealing.
moves.manifesto: vision.md non-negotiable 1 (full sovereignty over one's own data) and non-negotiable 3's spirit — governed boundaries are structural, not aspirational. Implies an amendment to openspec/specs/module-memory: the read ceiling is a property of every memory read path, not of the catalog alone.
moves.integration_points: Generalize `runtime_config.catalog_read_sensitivity` to a memory read ceiling (or add `memory_read_sensitivity` alongside it) and reuse `resolve_allowed_sensitivities` / `load_catalog_read_policy` verbatim (src/butlers/modules/memory/search.py:817-860). Apply in `search.py:search` and `recall` (:468-570, :691-780) as a SQL-level ceiling predicate — not a post-fetch selector — and in `tools/context.py:_fetch_profile_facts` (:52-63), `_fetch_recent_episodes` (:73-96) and the task-facts path. Add a withheld count to the returned envelope and a `_fill_section` footer line mirroring RFC 0031's coverage statement.
