Keep `_apply_filters`' sensitivity key as an additional narrowing filter and make an above-ceiling value an error rather than a silent widening (search.py:580-608, which today documents that unrecognized keys are ignored).
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy: reads return only rows at or below the ceiling; the result envelope and the context block both carry `withheld: {count, by_tier}` with no content. Failure: ceiling missing or unrecognized -> fail closed to ['normal'] (the existing catalog behavior, search.py:852-860) and mark the policy as defaulted so the caller can see it was not configured; runtime_config unreadable -> fail closed, never open. Filter interaction: a caller requesting `sensitivity='confidential'` above its ceiling gets a typed authorization error, not an empty list that reads as 'nothing sensitive exists'. Concurrency: the policy is read once per assembly so a mid-assembly config change cannot produce a half-governed context block. Idempotence: pure read. Rollback: set the ceiling to the highest tier and behavior matches today exactly, with the withheld count reading zero.
moves.verification: A test that a `confidential` owner fact is absent from memory_context output under a `normal` ceiling AND that the block reports `withheld: 1` — both halves, since a silent drop is the failure this move exists to prevent. A test that an unknown ceiling value yields ['normal'] and a `policy_defaulted` marker. A test that the ceiling is applied in SQL (asserting the query text or, better, that a pool containing only above-ceiling rows returns zero rows without the post-fetch filter path running). A test that an above-ceiling explicit filter raises rather than returning []. A test that recall and Profile Facts agree on the same ceiling within one assembly.
moves.slice_plan: S1: generalize the policy loader and thread it through search/recall behind the existing catalog default. S2: apply to memory_context's three fetches with the withheld footer. S3: the explicit-filter authorization error and the search.py:580-608 'silently ignored keys' repair. S4: surface the effective ceiling on the memory console so the owner can see what the fleet is allowed to read.

moves.title: One correction verb, any channel: 'no, that's wrong' as a door with a receipt
moves.why: Chronicler's manifesto promises 'I let you correct me when I am wrong', and the memory module's own doctrine treats confirmation as first-class (memory_confirm resets the decay clock). But the only correction doors that exist are `POST /api/memory/facts/{id}/confirm` and `/retract` (src/butlers/api/routers/memory.py:1050, 1132) — dashboard-only, fact-id-keyed, and reachable only by an owner who already found the row. The owner reading a wrong claim in a Telegram briefing has no verb. This is the last-hop-has-no-door pattern applied to belief. Owner-visible payoff in week one: reply 'wrong — Hui Min is my sister, not a colleague' to any butler message and the belief changes, with a receipt naming exactly which fact was retired and which replaced it.
moves.manifesto: roster/chronicler/MANIFESTO.md ('let you correct me when I am wrong') generalized to the shared fact store; roster/relationship/MANIFESTO.md for the entity-relation case. Deliberately NOT the belief-revision ledger — this builds the door and the receipt only, and records the change through the existing `memory_links` relation='supersedes' edge (storage.py:1826-1834) rather than a new ledger table.
moves.integration_points: New core tool `memory_correct(fact_id | (entity_id, predicate), new_content, reason)` writing through the existing `store_fact` supersession path with `evidence_class='owner_asserted'` and full credence (move 4), so the precedence rule makes the correction permanently dominant over later inference. Gated on the existing approval spine (src/butlers/modules/approvals) exactly as `memory_reclassify` is for Relationship (docs/modules/memory.md, tool table). Reachable from: the dashboard chat action lane (openspec/specs/dashboard-chat-ui, propose-then-act), Telegram via the existing notify()/inline-confirm boundary, and `POST /api/memory/facts/{id}/correct`. Receipt delivered through the same notify.v1 boundary the unknown-sender notice uses (docs/concepts/identity-model.md), pointing at the new fact's detail route.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy: the incumbent fact moves to validity='superseded' with invalid_at set and the replacement lands as owner_asserted in the same transaction (the exact path storage.py:1733-1900 already implements), a memory_links supersedes edge records the pair, and the owner receives a receipt naming both ids. Failure: the target fact is already superseded/retracted -> typed error naming the current head, so a stale correction cannot resurrect a dead branch; the (entity_id, predicate) form matching zero or multiple heads -> ambiguity error listing candidates, never a guess. Concurrency: two corrections racing the same head -> the second sees the first's supersession and errors with the new head id (optimistic, via the existing `expected_supersedes_id` parameter at storage.py:1386). Idempotence: an idempotency key on the correction makes a retried delivery a no-op returning the same receipt. Rollback: the supersedes edge is bidirectional evidence — re-correcting to the prior content is a normal correction, and the original row is never deleted.
moves.verification: A test that a correction supersedes the incumbent and the replacement carries evidence_class='owner_asserted' with the incumbent id on the memory_links edge. A test that a subsequent `llm_inferred` store against the corrected predicate is rejected (proving the correction is durable, which is the whole point). A test that a retried correction with the same idempotency key produces one supersession and one receipt. A test that a racing second correction errors with the new head id rather than double-superseding. A test that the correction is refused without an approval decision. A test that the ambiguous (entity_id, predicate) form lists candidates and writes nothing.
moves.slice_plan: S1: `memory_correct` over the existing supersession path with the expected_supersedes_id optimistic guard and the approval gate. S2: the receipt through notify.v1 with both fact ids. S3: the dashboard-chat action-lane verb and the REST route. S4: the Telegram inline-confirm entry. S5: wire the gap rows from move 1 and the provenance panel from move 3 as correction entry points, so every wrong belief the owner can see is one keystroke from being fixed.

findings.title: Trip end_date is read and discarded: the context bus can never say when travel ends
findings.evidence: src/butlers/jobs/context_producers.py:329-355 (SELECT ... end_date ... then set_context with no expires_at and metadata={"source","status"} only); src/butlers/context_bus.py:98 (_TTL_CONFIG traveling default 24h)
findings.taxonomy_shape: computed-then-discarded truth (run 09 theme) — a writer's-clock TTL substituted for a known world horizon
findings.detail: run_travel_context_producer selects start_date/end_date to decide whether a trip is underway, then writes `traveling` with the default 24h TTL as an explicit "crash backstop" and puts neither date in metadata. The trip's real end is in hand at write time and is thrown away, so every downstream consumer (Home away-mode, Relationship scheduling, Finance renewal timing, insight quiet-hours anchoring) can only learn "traveling, believed for 24h" and never "away through the 19th". The bus's expires_at is therefore doing double duty as belief expiry and situation duration, and only the weaker meaning survives.

findings.title: Three of five domain-event contracts are undeliverable by construction (permitted_subscribers = [])
findings.evidence: roster/finance/domain_events.toml:19, roster/health/domain_events.toml:18, roster/home/domain_events.toml:18 (permitted_subscribers = []); src/butlers/core/domain_event_contracts.py:353-366 (check_subscription refuses any subscriber not in the list, empty renders as "(none)"); live http://127.0.0.1:42200/api/domain-events/contracts (5 contracts) vs /api/domain-events/subscriptions (2 rows: finance<-travel.trip_booked, health<-travel.trip_active)
findings.taxonomy_shape: a gate that closes everything — publication with a structurally empty audience; the fleet-wide collaboration graph is 2 edges over 12 agents
findings.detail: finance.budget_pressure, health.recovery_state and home.actuation_executed each declare an empty permitted-subscriber list, and check_subscription fails closed on it. Those three publishers pay the write, the payload-minimization work and the retention cost for events no butler can ever subscribe to. Nothing at contract-load time flags a zero-audience contract, so the honest reading of the live fleet is: five contracts, two possible collaborations, three write-only channels. home.actuation_executed carries `attention_required` — a field whose only purpose is to make someone else act — into a channel with no permitted listener.

findings.title: A 'routed' delegation has no terminal state and no reconciliation sweep; one has been stuck 19 days live
findings.evidence: live GET http://127.0.0.1:42200/api/delegation/ledger?limit=5 — single row, relationship->finance birthday-gift budget question, asked_at 2026-08-17T23:06:41Z, status=routed, answer=null, wake_state=not_applicable; src/butlers/core/delegation_ledger.py:64 (VALID_STATUSES has no unanswered/stalled); src/butlers/api/routers/delegation.py:72 (wake_stuck filters only callback_failed/task_conflict); contrast src/butlers/core/domain_event_reactions.py:26-34 (`unreported` is the honest verdict about silence) and src/butlers/core/domain_events.py:33-48 (run_domain_event_reactions/reconciliation sweep re-drives stuck deliveries)
findings.taxonomy_shape: acceptance impersonating completion (run 09 theme) — `routed` means "the target scheduled itself", is returned to the asker as success, and never expires
findings.detail: The only cross-butler question the fleet has ever asked is unanswered after 19 days and nothing anywhere says so. dispatch_delegated_ask marks `routed` on route acknowledgment (src/butlers/core_tools/_delegation.py:225-249) and returns it to the asker as the success shape. There is no sweep over stale `routed` rows (grep across src/butlers/jobs and roster/*/butler.toml finds no delegation sweep or schedule), no `unanswered` terminal, and the API's stuck-row filter cannot see it. The domain-event bus solved exactly this problem with a terminal `unreported` plus a reconciliation sweep; delegation has neither, so the asking butler's session ends believing the answer is coming and the owner never learns their gift-budget question died.

findings.title: delegate_receive's answering wake has a two-minute liveness window and no retry
findings.evidence: src/butlers/core_tools/_delegation.py:404-420 — target_time = now + 1min, cron built from that single minute, until_at = target_time + 1min, then _schedule_create
findings.taxonomy_shape: the last hop has no door (run 11 theme) — a one-shot wake with a 2-minute expiry and no evidence recorded when it never fires
findings.detail: The answering task is a one-shot cron pinned to a single minute with until_at one minute later. A target butler that is restarting, at its concurrency ceiling, or has its scheduler paused during those two minutes loses the wake permanently. Nothing records that the task expired without running: the ledger row keeps status='routed' forever (see the live stuck row), so an expired wake and a wake that ran but produced no answer are indistinguishable, and neither is retryable.

findings.title: fleet_case_evidence.contributor is self-asserted, not attested to the writing role
findings.evidence: alembic/versions/core/core_217_fleet_case_file.py:152-176 (contributor TEXT NOT NULL, only a non-empty CHECK; every runtime role granted SELECT,INSERT with no RLS) vs alembic/versions/core/core_210_expected_signals.py:67-68 (producer TEXT NOT NULL, producer_role TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT current_user)
findings.taxonomy_shape: NEW: identity-in-a-string — a shared ledger keys idempotence and provenance on a free-text actor name the database never binds to the writing role
findings.detail: RFC 0032 fences fleet_cases and fleet_case_links to butler_switchboard_rw with RLS keyed on current_user, then deliberately leaves fleet_case_evidence open to every role — correctly, since any butler contributes. But `contributor` is an unconstrained string with no `contributor_role DEFAULT current_user` companion, so butler_health_rw can insert evidence attributed to 'finance', and the UNIQUE(case_id, contributor, kind, ref) idempotence key is only as trustworthy as the string. The sibling ledger written three revisions earlier (expected_signals) already has the exact pattern that fixes this. Every consumer of a case's contributor roster — completeness meters, narrator selection, 'who has not weighed in' — inherits an unattested denominator.

findings.title: Delegation targets are resolved from memory-row ownership, and catalog_score is recorded but never gates
findings.evidence: src/butlers/core/delegation_ledger.py:585-607 (top hybrid catalog hit's source_butler/source_schema becomes the target; score returned); src/butlers/core_tools/_delegation.py:307-352 (score passed only to record_ask, never compared to a threshold); openspec/specs/cross-butler-delegation/spec.md "Domain Resolution Via Shared Catalog"
findings.taxonomy_shape: a gate that is metadata (run 09/11 theme) — a relevance score is persisted for display and never used as an admission decision
findings.detail: "Whose domain covers this question" is answered by whichever schema happens to own the single top-scoring memory row for the question text — a proxy for topical mention, not for answerability. A health note mentioning a budget routes a finance question to health. The rrf_score that would let the resolver refuse a weak match is computed, returned, and written to the ledger, but no code path ever compares it to a floor: any non-empty hit routes. There is also no notion of what a butler can actually answer, so the target has no way to reply "not my domain" other than free prose, and no way to distinguish "I have no data" from "no".

audits.ideal: A JARVIS-grade Butlers ecosystem treats a life situation as a first-class object every specialist can see, contribute to, and be measured against. The owner says once — in chat, on Telegram, or by a butler inferring it — "I'm in Tokyo the 12th to the 19th", "Dad's in hospital", "we're moving in November", and a case opens under a named archetype whose git-declared contract says exactly which butlers a situation of that kind needs, what each is expected to contribute, when the situation is complete, and who speaks for it. Each specialist then does what only it can: Travel owns the window, Finance the envelope and the renewals that land inside it, Health the medication supply and the fitness question, Home the away plan and the empty-house energy, Relationship the people who need telling and the dinner that must not be booked on landing night. They coordinate over the substrate the repo already has — the Switchboard as the sole channel, the domain-event bus for standing facts, the delegation ledger for questions, the case file for shared situation state — but with three things it lacks: a forward horizon so context is answerable for a future date and not only for now, typed and machine-consumable answers with an explicit basis (measured / derived / absent / unmeasurable) so a butler can program against a sibling's reply instead of parsing prose, and one narrator per situation so the owner receives one coherent paragraph rather than five independent pings. Every collaboration leaves a receipt: an unanswered question becomes an honest `unanswered`, an absent contribution shows as absent against a named denominator, and a case card tells the owner in five seconds what the fleet has handled about the situation and precisely what it has not.
audits.jarvis_gap: The substrate is well built and almost entirely unused. Live, this fleet has 12 agents, 5 declared domain-event contracts, exactly 2 active subscription edges (finance<-travel.trip_booked, health<-travel.trip_active), 3 contracts that no butler can ever subscribe to because they declare `permitted_subscribers = []` against a fail-closed gate, exactly 1 delegated question in the ledger's entire history — relationship asking finance for birthday-gift budget guidance — stuck in `routed` for 19 days with no sweep, no terminal state, and no surface that can see it, and 0 fleet cases with no reader at all (`/api/fleet/cases` and `/api/cases` both 404). The pieces that would let butlers genuinely collaborate exist as excellent primitives (contracts with payload minimization and reaction receipts; a delegation wake protocol with immutable digests; a case file with RLS-fenced arbitration); what is missing is the shared vocabulary that would make them fire. There is no situation taxonomy, so a trip and an illness are indistinguishable free-text correlation keys and no butler knows it is expected to contribute. There is no owner authorship anywhere — `_WRITE_PERMISSIONS` in the context bus lists only butler names and fleet_cases writes are switchboard-only, so the fleet can only recognise situations it inferred and can never be told one. There is no forward horizon: the bus is now-with-a-TTL, and the travel producer literally reads the trip's `end_date` and discards it. Answers are prose, so the one question ever asked could not have been consumed by a job even if it had been answered. The result is a fleet of excellent specialists who each see one facet of the owner's week and have no way to act as one hand.
audits.live_verification: Live (read-only, http://127.0.0.1:42200): GET /api/butlers — 12 agents, all status ok (chronicler, concierge, education, finance, general, health, home, lifestyle, messenger, qa, relationship, switchboard, travel). GET /api/domain-events/contracts — 5 contracts; travel.trip_active (permitted: health), travel.trip_booked (permitted: finance), finance.budget_pressure / health.recovery_state / home.actuation_executed (permitted: []). GET /api/domain-events/subscriptions — 2 rows, both created 2026-07-26, no new edge in 6 weeks. GET /api/delegation/ledger?limit=5 — total 1; relationship->finance, asked 2026-08-17T23:06:41Z, status routed, answer null, wake_state not_applicable, catalog_match_id null (seeded by the deterministic briefing job, not by catalog resolution). GET /api/fleet/cases and /api/cases — both 404 (no case reader exists). No POST/PATCH/PUT/DELETE issued. Statically confirmed by reading the decisive mechanism: src/butlers/context_bus.py (_WRITE_PERMISSIONS, _TTL_CONFIG, set_context), src/butlers/jobs/context_producers.py (travel/home/calendar/sleep producers), src/butlers/core/domain_event_contracts.py (check_publish/check_subscription fail-closed), src/butlers/core/domain_event_reactions.py (EVIDENCE_KINDS, `unreported`), src/butlers/core/delegation_ledger.py, src/butlers/core_tools/_delegation.py, alembic/versions/core/core_217_fleet_case_file.py, core_210_expected_signals.py, core_206_domain_event_contracts_and_reactions.py, roster/*/domain_events.toml, roster/*/MANIFESTO.md, roster/switchboard/tools/insight/broker.py, about/legends-and-lore/rfcs/0032-fleet-case-file.md, and openspec/specs/{context-bus,cross-butler-delegation,cross-butler-briefing-aggregation,conversation-decomposition,calendar-event-proposals,calendar-conflict-overcommitment-radar,seasonal-awareness}. Also checked openspec/changes/{commitment-lifecycle,consolidate-owner-attention-policy} to keep Moves 2 and 5 clear of in-flight work.

moves.title: Situation archetypes: a git-declared taxonomy of recognisable life events, with an expected-contribution roster per case
moves.why: RFC 0032 gives the fleet a durable situation object whose `correlation_key` is deliberately readable free text and whose contributor set is whoever happened to file evidence. Nothing declares what a situation of a given kind *needs*, so no butler knows it is expected, and the owner cannot be told what is unhandled. vision.md §What Success Looks Like measures the system by 'the amount of mental labor the system reliably absorbs'; a case that cannot say what it is missing absorbs none of the worry. This is the shared vocabulary the whole lens is short of: today a Tokyo trip and a respiratory illness are the same shape of row. Owner-visible payoff within a week: a case card that reads 'Trip · Tokyo · 12-19 Oct — 4 of 6 expected contributions. Health has not confirmed medication supply through the 19th. Home has no away plan.' Honest absence at the situation level, reusing the shipped `present | absent | unmeasurable` vocabulary rather than inventing a fourth freshness dialect.
moves.manifesto: Serves every domain manifesto's central promise at the seam where each alone fails (travel.MANIFESTO 'a single, coherent view of every booking, every change, and every deadline'; health 'it holds the context so you don't have to'; home 'we notice and fix it, before you have to ask'). Implies a Switchboard MANIFESTO amendment: roster/switchboard/MANIFESTO.md lists only ingress, classification, routing, buffer, agent registry, connector registry and butler-to-staffer routing under Responsibilities — RFC 0032 already made it the sole arbiter of case existence, state, posture and bindings with no corresponding contract line, SLA, or failure mode. Add 'Situation arbitration' as a Responsibility with an archetype-projection SLA and a failure mode row (archetype registry unloadable -> cases open with archetype=null and completeness reported unmeasurable, never complete).
moves.integration_points: New git declaration `roster/<butler>/case_roles.toml` plus a fleet-level `about/heart-and-soul/case_archetypes.toml` (or `roster/switchboard/case_archetypes.toml`), loaded by a new `src/butlers/core/case_archetypes.py` that mirrors `src/butlers/core/domain_event_contracts.py:load_contract_registry` / `project_contracts` fail-closed loader-and-projector exactly. New migration `public.fleet_case_archetypes` (kind PK, summary, default_posture, narrator_butler, close_criteria, materialized_at) and `public.fleet_case_expected_contributions` (kind, butler, evidence_kind, cadence_seconds NULL, required BOOL) — switchboard-RLS-fenced on the core_217/core_210 pattern. `public.fleet_cases` gains `archetype TEXT REFERENCES fleet_case_archetypes(kind)` and `origin TEXT`. Read side: a `case_completeness` SQL function returning per-expected-contribution `present | absent | unmeasurable`, reusing the `measurability` vocabulary from `alembic/versions/core/core_210_expected_signals.py:72`. New spec `openspec/specs/fleet-case-archetypes/spec.md`. RFC 0032 amendment naming the archetype as the source of the contributor roster, the narrator, and the close criteria (its S3 tool list stays as-is and gains `archetype` on `open_case`).
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: switchboard boot projects archetypes from git (same delete-then-insert transaction shape as project_contracts); `open_case(correlation_key, archetype='trip')` writes the case; the completeness read joins expected contributions against fleet_case_evidence and reports 4/6 with the two absent butlers named. Failure: a malformed or missing archetype file fails the projection closed and leaves the previous projection intact; a case whose archetype row is absent reports completeness `unmeasurable` with reason 'archetype_unloaded' and never 'complete' (the honest-absence contract, not a silent 100%). An expected contribution from a butler that is down/quarantined reports `unmeasurable`, distinct from `absent`. Concurrency: two butlers racing to open the same situation still hit `uq_fleet_cases_active_correlation_key`; the loser re-reads and contributes. Idempotence: projection is keyed on `kind` PK and is rerun-safe; completeness is a pure read with no writes. Rollback: drop the two tables and the two columns; existing cases keep working with archetype null and completeness `unmeasurable` — no case is closed or reopened by the rollback.
moves.verification: tests/core/test_case_archetypes.py — malformed declaration fails closed and preserves the prior projection; an archetype naming an unknown butler is refused at load. tests/migrations/test_case_archetype_migration.py — RLS fences INSERT/UPDATE to butler_switchboard_rw (assert an INSERT as butler_health_rw raises), FK on fleet_cases.archetype, rerun-safe. tests/integration/test_case_completeness.py — with 4 of 6 evidence rows present the read names the two absent butlers; with the archetype row deleted the same case reports `unmeasurable`, not complete; with a contributor butler marked unreachable in public.butler_reachability_conditions the read reports `unmeasurable` for that slot only. All behavior-executing at the DB seam, no mock-only assertions.
moves.slice_plan: S1 loader + two tables + projection at switchboard startup, no fleet_cases change (the registry is readable and testable alone). S2 `fleet_cases.archetype` + `origin` columns and `open_case(archetype=...)`. S3 the `case_completeness` read plus its API projection onto the existing case read surface. S4 seed six archetypes (trip, illness, move, new_job, hosting, bereavement) from the manifestos of the butlers each names, one PR per archetype so the roster owner reviews each contributor list against its manifesto. S5 amend roster/switchboard/MANIFESTO.md and RFC 0032.

moves.title: Owner-declared situations: the fleet can be told, not only infer
moves.why: Every situation-recognition path in the repo is inference-only. `src/butlers/context_bus.py:73-85` authorizes only butler names to write any signal — there is no owner writer for `sick`, `away`, or anything else. `alembic/versions/core/core_217_fleet_case_file.py:130-142` fences case creation to butler_switchboard_rw. Insight candidates come from producers. So the highest-value situations — the ones the owner already knows and the fleet cannot possibly infer ('Dad's in hospital', 'we're moving Nov 14', 'guests until Sunday', 'money is tight this quarter') — cannot enter the system at all, and the owner instead re-explains them to five butlers one channel at a time. This is the single largest gap between this fleet and vision.md's 'The system is boring. It works. The owner stops thinking about it.' Distinct from openspec/changes/commitment-lifecycle, which lifecycles one owner-declared *obligation* ('I told Sam I'd send that book'); this declares a multi-butler *situation* that reframes six domains at once. Owner-visible payoff within a week: say it once in dashboard chat or Telegram, and Home, Finance, Relationship, Health, Travel and Calendar all adjust, each with a receipt saying what it did.
moves.manifesto: Serves the Switchboard contract's ingress ownership ('sole entry point for all inbound messages') extended from messages to situations, and the Concierge staffer's dashboard-read role as the owner's system-plane voice. Every domain manifesto is served by being told rather than guessing (health 'It exists to listen, remember'; relationship 'the friend who never forgets'; home 'We don't guess at what you want'). Implies the same Switchboard 'Situation arbitration' amendment as Move 1, plus one amendment to the context-bus spec: add an `owner` writer principal with authority over every signal type, since 'the owner may not correct their own state' is a defect the current permission table encodes.
moves.integration_points: New core tool `declare_situation(kind, name, window_start, window_end, note)` registered on the Switchboard (staffer-gated, the `ingest`/`notify` gating pattern in `_register_core_tools`), reachable from (a) the dashboard question/action lane already shipped in bu-0ynlk.2/.8, (b) Telegram via the normal route path, (c) `roster/concierge` as a propose-then-act confirm. Writes: `public.fleet_cases` with `origin='owner'` and `archetype` matched from Move 1's registry; a new `owner.situation_declared` contract in a fleet-level declaration with `permitted_subscribers` = the archetype's contributor roster, published through `publish_domain_event_once` (`src/butlers/core_tools/_domain_events.py`) so each contributor gets a standing-subscription wake and owes a `report_event_reaction` receipt (`src/butlers/core/domain_event_reactions.py`). Also writes the Move 3 horizon window when a date range is given. `public.fleet_cases` gains `declared_by` and `owner_close_only BOOL`. API: the case read surface must render origin.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: owner says 'I'm in Tokyo the 12th to 19th'; Concierge proposes, owner confirms, one case opens with origin=owner, the archetype roster is fanned out, five reaction receipts land (acted/ignored/deferred with evidence refs), and the case card shows who did what. Failure: a declaration whose kind matches no archetype opens a case with archetype=null and a named 'unclassified situation' state rather than being refused — the owner's words are never discarded; a fan-out route failure marks that delivery `failed`/`failed_permanent` per the existing bus semantics and the case shows that contributor as unreachable, not absent. Concurrency: the partial unique index on non-closed correlation_key makes a second declaration of the same situation an idempotent re-read; a butler-inferred case already open for the same key is *adopted* (origin upgraded to owner, declared_by set) rather than duplicated. Idempotence: declaration is keyed on (kind, window, name) hashed into the correlation_key, so repeating the sentence does not open a second case; the event publish uses publish_domain_event_once. Rollback: an owner-declared case can be withdrawn by the owner, which closes it with `outcome='withdrawn'`; the lapse sweep (RFC 0032 S5) must be forbidden from closing any `owner_close_only` case — only the owner closes what the owner declared.
moves.verification: tests/core_tools/test_declare_situation.py — an unmatched kind opens an unclassified case rather than erroring; a repeat declaration returns the same case id. tests/integration/test_owner_situation_fanout.py — declaration produces one delivery row per archetype contributor with UNIQUE(event_id, subscriber_butler) holding, and a subscriber lacking the domain_events core group yields `failed_permanent`, surfaced on the case, not silence. tests/core/test_fleet_case_lapse_sweep.py — the lapse sweep leaves an `owner_close_only` case untouched (assert state unchanged after a sweep past the lapse horizon). tests/api/test_fleet_cases_origin.py — owner-declared and inferred cases are distinguishable in the read payload.
moves.slice_plan: S1 the `origin`/`declared_by`/`owner_close_only` columns plus the declare tool writing a case and nothing else (the owner can already see their situation on the case surface). S2 the `owner.situation_declared` contract and archetype-roster fan-out with reaction receipts. S3 adoption of an already-open inferred case. S4 the Telegram and dashboard-chat entry points with propose-then-act confirmation. S5 the context-bus `owner` writer principal and the horizon write (depends on Move 3).

moves.title: Situational horizon: give the context bus a future, and stop the writer's clock from standing in for the world's
moves.why: Everything `public.user_context` carries is 'true now, believed for a TTL'. `src/butlers/jobs/context_producers.py:329-355` proves the cost: the travel producer reads the trip's `end_date`, uses it only in a WHERE clause, and writes `traveling` with the default 24h TTL as an admitted 'crash backstop' with neither date in metadata. So the fleet cannot answer 'what will be true on 14 Nov' — the question every forward-looking butler needs and none can ask. `seasonal_periods` (openspec/specs/seasonal-awareness) is per-butler and annually recurring, not a one-off window, and the RFC-0011 quiet-hours anchor logic already had to reconstruct a wake anchor by hand from active TTLs because no window object exists. Distinct from the deferred 'absence plans' idea, which is about autonomy authority while the owner is away; this is the substrate that would let any butler's deterministic job plan against a dated fact. Owner-visible payoff within a week: Home stops conditioning an empty house for the week you are away, Relationship stops proposing dinner on your landing night, Finance flags the renewal that lands mid-trip, and the sleep/DND anchor stops guessing.
moves.manifesto: Serves travel.MANIFESTO ('surface upcoming departures, connection times, and document expiry dates with enough lead time to act'), home.MANIFESTO ('We think ahead, reminding you to adjust things before discomfort sets in'), relationship.MANIFESTO ('Smart scheduling ... so you stay connected without thinking about it'). Implies an amendment to openspec/specs/context-bus/spec.md: the TTL Semantics requirement conflates belief expiry with situation duration and must be split — `expires_at` stays the writer's belief horizon, a new window carries the world's interval, and the spec's 'There SHALL be no indefinite signals' rule extends to windows (every window is bounded and evidence-backed).
moves.integration_points: New migration `public.context_windows` (id, signal_type FK-by-CHECK to the ContextSignal vocabulary, value, starts_at, ends_at, set_by_butler, set_at, confidence, provenance_kind, provenance_ref, case_id NULL REFERENCES public.fleet_cases, superseded_at) with the same per-signal write-permission table as `src/butlers/context_bus.py:_WRITE_PERMISSIONS`. New reads in `src/butlers/context_bus.py`: `set_context_window`, `get_context_at(pool, ts)`, `get_context_windows(pool, start, end)`; `format_context_preamble` gains a horizon line and `src/butlers/core/spawner_context.py:333-336` passes the target date when a task is planning for one. Producers: `run_travel_context_producer` writes the trip's real `[start_date, end_date)` window (the value it currently discards); Home writes away plans; Relationship writes confirmed calendar socialising; Health writes planned procedures and recovery horizons; Move 2's declare tool writes owner-declared windows. Consumers first: the RFC-0011 wake anchor in `roster/switchboard/tools/insight/broker.py:_get_suppressing_context_signal_detail` and `home` conditioning.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: travel writes a window for 12-19 Oct with provenance {kind:'trip', ref:trip_id}; `get_context_at('2026-11-14T09:00Z')` returns the signals true then, with source butler and confidence; the preamble for a task planning that date names them. Failure: a window with ends_at <= starts_at is refused at the CHECK constraint (never clamped silently); an unauthorized writer raises PermissionError as today; a window whose provenance ref no longer resolves is reported with provenance `stale` and never silently upgraded to current-data authority. Concurrency: windows are append-and-supersede, not upsert — two producers may hold overlapping windows for one signal and the read returns both with their writers named (no arbitration in the substrate; arbitration is the case's job). Idempotence: `UNIQUE(signal_type, set_by_butler, provenance_kind, provenance_ref) WHERE superseded_at IS NULL` makes re-running a 15-minute producer a no-op; a changed trip date supersedes rather than mutating, preserving the correction history. Rollback: drop the table and the three functions; `get_active_context` and every existing caller are untouched because the now-path is unchanged.
moves.verification: tests/core/test_context_windows.py — ends_at <= starts_at refused at the DB, not clamped; unauthorized writer refused; re-running the same producer inserts no second row; a date change supersedes and both rows remain readable. tests/jobs/test_travel_context_producer_window.py — the producer writes a window whose bounds equal the trip's start_date/end_date (the regression that pins finding #1), and clears/supersedes on trip end. tests/core/test_context_at.py — `get_context_at` for a future date returns only windows covering it and no now-signals. tests/integration/test_suppressing_wake_anchor_with_windows.py — the existing dnd/sleeping wake-anchor scenarios in openspec/specs/context-bus/spec.md still hold with windows present, and a window never shortens the anchor.
moves.slice_plan: S1 the table, the three read/write functions, and the permission/TTL split in the context-bus spec — no producer changes, so it can land and be tested alone. S2 the travel producer writes the trip window (this alone fixes finding #1 and is independently owner-visible via any window read). S3 `get_context_at` into `spawner_context` so a task planning for a date sees that date. S4 Home away-plan and Health procedure/recovery producers. S5 the insight-broker wake anchor reads windows. S6 case_id binding so an open case's windows travel with it.

moves.title: Answerable-question registry: typed cross-butler questions with a declared basis, so a butler can program against a sibling's answer
moves.why: The one delegated question in this fleet's history (live: relationship->finance, gift budget, 2026-08-17) could not have been consumed by a deterministic job even had it been answered, because `delegate_answer` takes free text. Worse, target resolution is not capability-based at all: `src/butlers/core/delegation_ledger.py:585-607` routes to whichever schema owns the top hybrid catalog hit for the question string, and the `rrf_score` that could refuse a weak match is stored and never compared to a floor (finding #6). And prose answers cannot distinguish 'no' from 'I have no data' — the exact honesty distinction the fleet already got right for expected_signals (`present | absent | unmeasurable`) and for reaction receipts (`ignored` vs `unreported`). This is the direct analogue of the domain-event contract pattern, applied to the pull path: `roster/<butler>/domain_events.toml` already proves that publisher-owned, git-declared, fail-closed contracts work. Owner-visible payoff within a week: the gift-budget question comes back as `{basis:'absent', reason:'no discretionary budget configured'}`, which Relationship turns into 'Set a gift budget?' — the owner sees the honest gap instead of 19 days of silence.
moves.manifesto: Serves finance.MANIFESTO ('Ask about your spending ... The answers come from your actual email history, not your memory' — extended so a sibling butler may ask too), health.MANIFESTO ('Your doctor asks, "How have you been feeling?" The Health Butler has the answer: not a vague memory, but the data'), relationship.MANIFESTO ('Financial clarity: track loans, shared expenses'). Implies an amendment to openspec/specs/cross-butler-delegation/spec.md: the 'Domain Resolution Via Shared Catalog' requirement currently mandates catalog similarity as the *only* resolution mechanism; it must admit a declared-capability lane for typed asks (catalog similarity stays the fallback for free-text asks) and must add a relevance floor for the free-text lane so a weak match is `unroutable`, not misrouted.
moves.integration_points: New git declaration `roster/<butler>/answerable.toml` (question_type, schema_version, summary, arg fields, answer fields, `basis` enum required in every answer, `as_of` required, permitted_askers, refusal vocabulary), loaded by `src/butlers/core/answerable_contracts.py` mirroring `src/butlers/core/domain_event_contracts.py` (fail-closed loader, `check_ask`/`check_answer` payload validation, `project_*` into a new switchboard-fenced `public.answerable_contracts`). New core tools `delegate_ask_typed(question_type, args)` and `delegate_answer_typed(ledger_id, answer)` in `src/butlers/core_tools/_delegation.py`, routing through the identical Switchboard `route()` path and the identical wake protocol (no new dispatch mechanism — the MCP-only doctrine and RFC-0026 wake contract are untouched). `public.delegation_ledger` gains `question_type`, `question_args JSONB`, `answer_payload JSONB`, `answer_basis`. Free-text lane gains a `catalog_score` floor in `resolve_target_via_catalog`.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: relationship calls `delegate_ask_typed('finance.discretionary_budget_for', {occasion_kind:'birthday'})`; the registry resolves finance deterministically with no LLM and no catalog search; the wake fires; finance returns a schema-valid `{amount, currency, basis:'derived', as_of}`; the asker's return task consumes it as data. Failure: an unknown question_type is `unroutable` with reason `no_declared_answerer` (never a catalog guess); an answer that violates the declared schema is refused at `delegate_answer_typed` and the row stays `routed` with the validation error in `reason` — never a fabricated success; an answer with `basis='absent'` is a first-class *success* that records what is missing. Concurrency: unchanged from RFC-0026 — the answer digest and wake key are computed over the canonicalized JSON payload, so the 'duplicate answer replays, changed answer is an integrity conflict' guarantee holds byte-for-byte. Idempotence: same digest -> same wake identity; the registry projection is keyed on question_type PK and rerun-safe. Rollback: drop the registry, the four columns and the two tools; the prose `delegate_ask`/`delegate_answer` path is unchanged and legacy rows stay discoverable and inert per the existing legacy-row rule.
moves.verification: tests/core/test_answerable_contracts.py — a declaration whose answer schema omits `basis` or `as_of` fails to load; a question_type namespace that does not match its declaring butler is refused; an ask from a butler outside permitted_askers is refused. tests/core_tools/test_delegate_ask_typed.py — unknown type is `unroutable/no_declared_answerer` with no catalog call (assert the catalog search is never invoked); a schema-invalid answer leaves status `routed` and records the validation error. tests/core/test_delegation_typed_wake_identity.py — digest over canonicalized JSON: a re-ordered but equal payload replays the same wake key; a changed value is an integrity conflict. tests/core/test_catalog_resolution_floor.py — a hit below the floor yields `unroutable`, closing finding #6. tests/integration/test_gift_budget_typed_roundtrip.py — the live-observed relationship->finance question end to end, asserting an `absent` basis when no budget is configured.
moves.slice_plan: S1 the loader plus `public.answerable_contracts` and the projection, with zero declarations — the registry ships testable and inert. S2 the ledger columns and `delegate_ask_typed`/`delegate_answer_typed` alongside the prose path. S3 the relevance floor on the free-text lane (independently valuable, closes finding #6). S4 seed the first four question types one PR at a time, each reviewed against its butler's manifesto: `finance.discretionary_budget_for`, `travel.away_window`, `health.medication_supply_through`, `home.away_ready`. S5 replace the deterministic briefing seed's prose ask with the typed one. S6 the free-text `delegate_ask` becomes the fallback lane in the spec.

moves.title: One voice per situation: the case narrator composes a single owner message from attributed contributions
moves.why: When five butlers each notice one facet of an illness, the owner gets five pings and must assemble the situation themselves — the exact labor vision.md says the system exists to absorb. RFC 0032's S4 dedupes the *quiet-hours bypass* per case (one urgent break instead of five), which is a rate concern; it does not touch authorship, so even inside quiet hours the owner still receives five separate paragraphs from five personalities. Adjacent to but distinct from the known 'one attention budget via the broker' (bu-7exe4.6): a budget decides *how many* messages, a narrator decides *who speaks and in whose words*. This is the clearest answer to the pursuit question — one coherent account of a situation is a thing no butler can produce alone, and it is exactly what a butler ecosystem is for. Owner-visible payoff within a week: instead of Health, Home, Relationship, Calendar and Finance each pinging, one paragraph: 'You've been unwell three days. Health: fever down, meds through Friday. Home: bedroom at 24C, humidifier on. Relationship: Sam's dinner Thursday still stands — move it? Finance: nothing due this week.'
moves.manifesto: Serves the Messenger contract (outbound channel delivery) and the Switchboard contract as the only sanctioned cross-butler channel, and honours each domain manifesto's voice by *attributing* every line rather than homogenizing it (home.MANIFESTO 'We tell you what matters and stay out of the way'; relationship 'attention shouldn't be a burden'; lifestyle 'stays in its lane'). Requires the Move 1 archetype to name the narrator, so specialist manifesto ownership is declared in git, not chosen by an LLM at delivery time. Implies a Messenger MANIFESTO amendment: a case-scoped composed delivery is a new delivery shape with its own failure mode (narrator unreachable -> degrade to per-butler delivery with a named notice), and an amendment to openspec/specs/insight-delivery for case-scoped composition.
moves.integration_points: New core tool `contribute_case_line(case_id, line, ask, urgency)` writing to a new `public.fleet_case_lines` table (case_id, contributor, contributor_role DEFAULT current_user, line, ask, urgency, contributed_at, delivered_in NULL) — RLS-open for INSERT like fleet_case_evidence but with the role attestation finding #5 says the evidence table is missing. Composition runs in `roster/switchboard/tools/insight/broker.py` at the existing `delivery_cycle` seam, reusing `_cluster_candidates`/`_synthesize_cluster_sentence` machinery but keyed on case rather than on cycle-scoped candidates and with the composed text *persisted* to `public.fleet_case_links` (link_kind='delivered_digest') instead of discarded — the discard RFC 0032's Context section names. Suppression: `notify()` (src/butlers/core/notify path) grows a `case_id` argument; a routine-priority notify naming an open case with a narrator is parked with an honest `suppressed_for_case` receipt on the existing attention ledger, never dropped. Delivery goes through Messenger unchanged.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: four contributors file lines against an active case; at the delivery window the Switchboard composes one attributed message, records it as a case link with the contributing line ids, marks each line `delivered_in`, and Messenger delivers once. Failure: the narrator butler is unreachable or the composition LLM call fails -> the cycle degrades to per-butler delivery of the undelivered lines with a named notice ('composed summary unavailable; showing contributions individually'), never silence and never a partial paragraph that omits a contributor without saying so. A contributor's line that arrives after composition is carried to the next window, not dropped. Urgent lines bypass composition and deliver immediately, then appear in the next composed message marked 'already sent'. Concurrency: composition takes a per-case advisory lock (the pattern `run_domain_event_reconciliation_sweep` already uses), so two overlapping cycles cannot double-deliver; `delivered_in` is the claim. Idempotence: a line is delivered at most once (partial unique index on `(id) WHERE delivered_in IS NULL` as the claim target); replaying a cycle with no undelivered lines composes and delivers nothing. Rollback: drop the table, the tool and the notify argument; every butler's own notify path is untouched, so rollback returns the fleet to five pings, never to zero.
moves.verification: tests/migrations/test_fleet_case_lines_migration.py — contributor_role defaults to current_user and a mismatched claimed contributor is detectable. tests/switchboard/test_case_composition.py — four lines compose to one message with every contributor attributed; a composition failure degrades to per-butler delivery of all four lines and emits the named notice (assert no line is silently dropped). tests/switchboard/test_case_composition_concurrency.py — two concurrent composition runs deliver each line exactly once (advisory lock + delivered_in claim). tests/core/test_notify_case_suppression.py — a routine notify naming an open narrated case yields a `suppressed_for_case` receipt on the attention ledger, and an urgent one is not suppressed. tests/switchboard/test_case_digest_persisted.py — the composed sentence lands in fleet_case_links and survives the cycle (the anti-discard regression).
moves.slice_plan: S1 `public.fleet_case_lines` + `contribute_case_line` with the role attestation, no composition — lines are already an owner-visible case detail. S2 composition and single delivery through Messenger, with the degrade lane. S3 the `notify(case_id=...)` suppression receipt. S4 persist the composed digest as a case link (closes the RFC 0032 discard). S5 urgency lane and the 'already sent' marking. S6 Messenger MANIFESTO and insight-delivery spec amendments.

moves.title: An unanswered question is an outcome: delegation stall reconciliation with a durable wake and an honest terminal
moves.why: Live proof that collaboration silently fails: the fleet's only delegated question has sat in `routed` for 19 days (GET /api/delegation/ledger). `dispatch_delegated_ask` returns `routed` to the asker as the success shape (src/butlers/core_tools/_delegation.py:225-249); the answering wake is a one-shot cron with a two-minute liveness window and no retry (:404-420); `VALID_STATUSES` has no unanswered terminal (src/butlers/core/delegation_ledger.py:64); and the API's stuck-row filter sees only `callback_failed`/`task_conflict` (src/butlers/api/routers/delegation.py:72). The domain-event bus solved this exact problem with `unreported` — 'the honest verdict about silence' — plus a reconciliation sweep with bounded retries and a `failed_permanent` terminal (src/butlers/core/domain_event_reactions.py:26-34, src/butlers/core/domain_events.py:33-48). Delegation, the older mechanism, has none of it. Owner-visible payoff within a week: the Overview attention list says 'Relationship asked Finance for your gift budget 19 days ago and never got an answer' — the owner learns the fleet is not collaborating instead of assuming it is, which is precisely the north star's 'failure never impersonates health'.
moves.manifesto: Serves the Switchboard contract's Failure Modes and Recovery table, which promises 'no message loss on restart' and an eligibility sweep that reinstates routes — a delegated question is a message the contract currently loses without saying so. Serves relationship.MANIFESTO's 'The one who follows through' and finance.MANIFESTO's 'We will not let overdue obligations pile up silently'. Implies an amendment to openspec/specs/cross-butler-delegation/spec.md: add an `unanswered` terminal, a durable answering wake with bounded retry, and the sweep's write authority (the sweep may only ever write `unanswered`, mirroring the reaction sweep's `unreported`-only rule — it must never promote a completed task into an answer).
moves.integration_points: `src/butlers/core/delegation_ledger.py` — add `unanswered` to `VALID_STATUSES`, an `answer_due_at` column on `public.delegation_ledger`, and `select_stale_routed_delegations` / `mark_unanswered` mirroring `select_stale_pending_deliveries` / `mark_delivery_failed` in `src/butlers/core/domain_events.py`. `src/butlers/core_tools/_delegation.py:404-420` — replace the two-minute one-shot cron with a durable wake record plus bounded retries (same shape as `delegation_wake_attempts`, which already exists for the callback direction and is the proof this asymmetry is accidental). New `delegation_stall_sweep` deterministic job on the Switchboard, registered in `_DETERMINISTIC_SCHEDULE_JOB_REGISTRY` and scheduled in `roster/switchboard/butler.toml` alongside `domain_event_reconciliation_sweep`. `src/butlers/api/routers/delegation.py` — extend the stuck filter to `unanswered` and stale `routed`. Surfacing reuses the Overview attention list the delegation spec already requires for stuck wake states.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: a routed row whose `answer_due_at` has passed is re-woken up to N times with backoff; on the first answer it proceeds through the unchanged answered->callback->return-task path. Failure: retries exhausted -> `status='unanswered'` with the attempt evidence and the last error, surfaced on the attention list; the question text and identities stay durable and the row stays discoverable. An `unanswered` row that later receives a genuine answer from its authoritative target is accepted and transitions to `answered` (silence was a verdict about the past, not a lock) — but the wake identity is minted then, exactly as for a late first answer. Concurrency: the sweep takes the same session advisory lock the reaction sweep uses and re-observes each row before acting, so a live answer landing mid-sweep is skipped rather than overwritten; a partial unique index guards the terminal so sweep and session cannot write contradictory outcomes. Idempotence: re-running the sweep over an already-`unanswered` row is a no-op; the retry counter is on the wake record, not recomputed from timestamps. Rollback: drop the column, the status, the sweep and the job schedule; existing rows keep their current statuses and the retry-less one-shot behavior returns — no row is mutated by the rollback.
moves.verification: tests/core/test_delegation_stall_sweep.py — a routed row past `answer_due_at` is re-woken, and after the retry bound becomes `unanswered` with attempt evidence; an already-answered row is never touched; two concurrent sweeps produce one terminal (assert the partial unique index rejects the second). tests/core_tools/test_delegate_receive_durable_wake.py — a target unavailable for the original window is still woken on a later retry (the regression that pins finding #4); the wake record survives a restart. tests/core/test_delegation_late_answer_after_unanswered.py — a genuine late answer from the authoritative target is accepted and mints the wake identity then. tests/api/test_delegation_stuck_filter.py — `unanswered` and stale `routed` rows are returned by the stuck filter. tests/integration/test_delegation_attention_surfacing.py — a stalled row appears on the Overview attention list with a deep link, and a failed fetch renders the named degraded notice rather than an all-clear.
moves.slice_plan: S1 the `unanswered` terminal, `answer_due_at`, and the sweep with sweep-only write authority — this alone makes the live stuck row honest and is independently shippable. S2 the durable answering wake with bounded retry replacing the two-minute one-shot (closes finding #4). S3 the API stuck filter and Overview attention surfacing. S4 the cross-butler-delegation spec amendment. S5 (folded in from finding #2) a startup validation that refuses to project a domain-event contract declaring `permitted_subscribers = []`, so a publisher can no longer ship a write-only channel — the same class of defect on the push path.

audits.live_verification: Live (read-only, http://127.0.0.1:42200): `GET /api/ingestion/connectors/available` returns exactly 13 connector types (gmail, telegram_bot, telegram_user_client, home_assistant, discord_user, spotify, owntracks, whatsapp_user_client, steam, google_calendar, google_drive, google_health, activitywatch) — live_listener is registered nowhere in that catalog. `GET /api/ingestion/connectors/summaries` live-confirms activitywatch:desktop `liveness=online, state=degraded, error="failed to list AW buckets: All connection attempts failed", today.messages_ingested=0`, first_seen 2026-07-05, and spotify:unconfigured `awaiting_credentials`; google_health is healthy with per-resource checkpoint children. `GET /api/relationship/entities?limit=200` returns 200 entities: 199 person, 1 organization, **0 place**. Everything else is source-confirmed by reading the decisive mechanism: the media-label substitution in telegram_bot/whatsapp, the base64-in-JSON return of get_attachment and its ATTACHMENTS prompt block, the closed ModelFeature vocabulary, the HA domain allowlist and actuation risk map, the live_listener speech-only pipeline, the OwnTracks payload dispatch with zero downstream consumers, and RFC 0018's deferral catalogue. No writes of any kind were issued.
audits.jarvis_gap: The connector *plumbing* is close to world-class — `ingest.v1` with idempotency keys, cursor checkpoints with an explicit `operational_role` split (src/butlers/connectors/registry_roles.py:1-60), filtered_events + replay drain as universal obligations (openspec/specs/connector-base-spec/spec.md:22-60), OAuth scope observation, heartbeat liveness — and RFC 0018 is an unusually disciplined scope record. What is narrow is the *senses*. Every one of the 13 live connectors delivers exactly one thing: a string. A photo the owner sends to Telegram is normalized to the literal text "Photo" (src/butlers/connectors/telegram_bot.py:133-181, :1470); WhatsApp images become "[image]" (whatsapp_user_client.py:387-389); the envelope's own `IngestAttachment` contract (roster/switchboard/tools/routing/contracts.py:220-254) is populated by exactly one connector (gmail.py:3046-3214), and the core tool meant to let a session *see* that blob hands the model base64 inside a JSON tool result (src/butlers/tools/attachments.py:78-92, core_tools/_media.py:24-43) while `ModelFeature` (core/model_capabilities.py:44-62) has no vision member to gate dispatch on — so "show me" is advertised in the prompt (core_tools/_routing.py:174-180) and physically impossible. Beyond vision: the microphones already in the house discard every non-speech sound (openspec/specs/connector-live-listener/spec.md:82-105; prefilter drops <3 words); the owner's *places* are a first-class entity_type in the schema (alembic/versions/core/core_002_identity.py:93-94) with zero rows while OwnTracks region transitions arrive as prose no code reads (owntracks.py:116, :647-662); the owner's own machines and self-hosted services are perceived only as noise to be filtered out of room comfort (src/butlers/jobs/home.py:872-891 explicitly excludes NAS/disk/CPU temperatures); and Home's manifesto promise of firmware/battery/offline device alerts (roster/home/MANIFESTO.md:30) has no mechanism because the `update` domain is not in the allowlist (connectors/home_assistant.py:122-142). A JARVIS perceives the world in the modalities the owner lives in — sight, sound, place, the state of his own machines, the room he is standing in — and can put a hand on the small levers (a list, a lever, a lamp). Today Butlers reads text and pulls one lever family (HA + Spotify + calendar/email).

findings.title: get_attachment advertises Claude vision input but returns base64 inside a JSON tool result — the model can never see the image, and the cost is paid anyway
findings.evidence: src/butlers/tools/attachments.py:3-4 ("as base64-encoded data suitable for Claude vision/PDF input"), :20 (MAX_ATTACHMENT_SIZE_BYTES = 5MB), :78-92 (b64encode → returns {"data_base64": ...}); src/butlers/core_tools/_media.py:24-43 (core tool returns that dict verbatim); src/butlers/core/model_capabilities.py:44-62 (ModelFeature closed vocabulary: TOOL_USE, STRUCTURED_OUTPUT, SESSION_RESUME — no vision member, so no dispatch can require or check it)
findings.taxonomy_shape: NEW: an advertised capability whose delivery channel cannot carry it — the value is computed and paid for (S3 GET, base64 expansion, tokens) but arrives in a form the consumer is structurally unable to interpret
findings.detail: FastMCP serializes a tool's dict return to JSON text. A base64 string in a JSON field is not an image content block: the model receives unreadable characters, not pixels. Worse, the 5MB cap permits ~6.8MB of base64 ≈ well over 1M tokens, so any real photo either blows the context window or is truncated into garbage. The gate that should have caught this — capability fit at dispatch (spawner.py:1295 comment, dispatch_intent) — cannot, because 'vision' is not expressible in the ModelFeature vocabulary. Net effect: the ATTACHMENTS prompt block instructs the session to call a tool that can only waste money.

findings.title: The ATTACHMENTS prompt promises on-demand retrieval for lazy attachments; no verb exists for a session to trigger it
findings.evidence: src/butlers/core_tools/_routing.py:174-180 ("Lazy-fetch attachments (no storage_ref) require on-demand retrieval."); src/butlers/connectors/gmail.py:3216 GmailConnector.fetch_attachment — zero callers outside the module (grep across src/, roster/, tests/ finds only its own log lines and a docstring reference at roster/switchboard/tools/routing/contracts.py:226)
findings.taxonomy_shape: the last hop has no door — the prompt names an action for which no tool, API route, or MCP surface exists
findings.detail: Large attachments (e.g. CSV/PDF above the eager cap) are recorded in the envelope with storage_ref=None and a status of pending_lazy_fetch. The connector has the materialization method; the butler session has no way to reach it (connectors talk to Switchboard, never the reverse). So the one class of attachment most likely to matter is permanently unreachable, and the prompt tells the model otherwise.

findings.title: Every chat connector drops image payloads and writes the word "Photo" as the message's normalized text, so the durable record asserts content that was never sent
findings.evidence: src/butlers/connectors/telegram_bot.py:133-139 (_MEDIA_TYPE_LABELS: "photo"→"Photo", "voice"→"Voice message", "document"→"Document"), :153-181 (tier cascade: text → caption → media-type descriptor), :1470 (text = msg.get("text") or msg.get("caption")); zero occurrences of `attachments`/`blob`/`getFile` in telegram_bot.py; src/butlers/connectors/whatsapp_user_client.py:366,387-389 (ImageMessage → caption or "[image]"); roster/switchboard/tools/routing/contracts.py:220-254 (IngestAttachment/payload.attachments exists and is unused by these connectors)
findings.taxonomy_shape: a placeholder promoted to a fact — a descriptor generated by the reader is stored in the field reserved for what the sender said
findings.detail: switchboard.inbox rows, conversation history, Dunbar interaction evidence and Chronicler episodes all read normalized_text. A month of photos from a family chat is indistinguishable in the record from a month of people literally typing the word "Photo". No `filtered_events` row is written either, because the message was not filtered — it was accepted with fabricated content.

findings.title: Home's manifesto promises firmware/battery/offline device alerts; the HA `update` domain is dropped at Layer 1 and no producer exists
findings.evidence: roster/home/MANIFESTO.md:30 ("get alerts when devices go offline, batteries run low, or firmware updates are available"); src/butlers/connectors/home_assistant.py:122-142 (_DEFAULT_DOMAIN_ALLOWLIST: light, switch, sensor, climate, lock, cover, binary_sensor, automation, script, person — no `update`); openspec/specs/connector-home-assistant/spec.md:126-127 (same default; non-allowlisted domains dropped as domain_excluded); no firmware/update producer in src/butlers/jobs/home.py or roster/home/
findings.taxonomy_shape: a binding manifesto clause with no mechanism — the promise is unmeetable by construction, not merely unimplemented
findings.detail: HA exposes pending firmware as `update.*` entities. Because the domain is excluded before significance filtering, no firmware event can ever reach a butler, and vision.md rule 6 makes the manifesto binding rather than aspirational. Battery level does arrive (sensor domain) but has no threshold producer either.

findings.title: `place` is a first-class entity_type with zero rows: the geography of the owner's life denominates nothing
findings.evidence: alembic/versions/core/core_002_identity.py:93-94 (CHECK entity_type IN ('person','organization','place','other')); src/butlers/modules/memory/tools/entities.py:20 and src/butlers/api/routers/memory.py:1957 (both accept 'place'); openspec/specs/predicate-taxonomy.md:25 (resolution cascade explicitly mints organization|place entities from ingestion); live: GET /api/relationship/entities?limit=200 → 199 person, 1 organization, 0 place
findings.taxonomy_shape: an aggregate/type that denominates nothing — a schema affordance with no producer, so every place-shaped question is unanswerable
findings.detail: OwnTracks already ingests `waypoints` (the owner's own named places) and `transition` enter/leave events with a human-readable `desc` (owntracks.py:116, :623-662), but no code in roster/ or src/butlers/jobs/ reads regions or waypoints — they land as inbox prose. So 'the gym', 'Mum's place', 'the office' exist in the owner's phone, pass through ingestion, and are never anchored to the entity graph that every butler shares.

findings.title: The HA actuation risk map cannot distinguish "unknown physical verb" from "not physical at all": every non-physical HA service defaults to PROTECTED
findings.evidence: roster/home/modules/actuation.py:23-50 (_RISK_MAP covers light/switch/fan/humidifier/climate/cover/scene/script/automation/lock/alarm_control_panel/homeassistant only), :79-81 (classify_actuation defaults to ActuationRisk.PROTECTED), :165 ("no deterministic post-condition is declared for {domain}.{service}")
findings.taxonomy_shape: a gate whose default is safe for one axis (physical consequence) and wrong for another (informational writes), so correct-by-default becomes unusable-by-default
findings.detail: Fail-closed is right for a physical unknown. But it means an informational HA verb (todo.add_item, notify.*, input_text.set_value) would demand an owner approval and a live post-condition receipt per call, with no post-condition declarable — which is exactly the friction that will kill any list/annotation capability built on the existing gate. The risk taxonomy needs a non-physical class whose receipt is the entity's own state read-back, not an approval.

findings.title: ActivityWatch has ingested nothing for two months while reporting liveness=online, and no expected-signal makes that absence visible
findings.evidence: live GET /api/ingestion/connectors/summaries → {connector_type: activitywatch, endpoint_identity: activitywatch:desktop, liveness: "online", state: "degraded", error_message: "failed to list AW buckets: All connection attempts failed", today.messages_ingested: 0, uptime_s: 14918, first_seen_at: 2026-07-05}; src/butlers/connectors/activitywatch.py:65,83 (source is a local/Tailscale-reachable AW host; trust boundary is localhost+Tailscale); expected_signals producers exist only for health/finance/relationship domain facts (roster/health/jobs/health_jobs.py:25, roster/finance/tools/pattern_recognition.py:19, roster/relationship/tools/stale_contacts.py:11) — none for connector source reachability
findings.taxonomy_shape: writer's clock impersonating the world's clock — the connector process's own liveness is reported as the source's liveness (new instance: activitywatch source-host unreachability)
findings.detail: The connector process is healthy and heartbeating, so the roster shows online; the *source* has been unreachable since at least the start of the day, and 'degraded' carries no attribution of which host, since when, or what the owner should do. Because no expected_signal declares that desktop-activity observations should be arriving at some cadence, the honest-absence machinery shipped in RFC 0029 cannot classify this as ABSENT — the silence is simply invisible to every downstream reader of screen-time and focus data.

moves.title: Make the butlers see: a real vision lane from chat transports through a content-block attachment tool
moves.why: vision.md "What Success Looks Like" measures mental labor absorbed, and the single largest unabsorbed class is 'look at this' — a rash, a parcel label, an error dialog, a meter reading, a handwritten note, a wine label, a boiler code. Doctrine already puts this in connector territory (vision.md rule 7: connectors normalize, butlers never know transport), and the envelope already has the contract (roster/switchboard/tools/routing/contracts.py:220-254). Today the capability is advertised to the model and cannot work (core_tools/_routing.py:174-180 vs src/butlers/tools/attachments.py:78-92). Owner-visible payoff in week one: photograph anything, send it to the butler on the channel he already uses, and get a grounded answer plus a durable, provenanced record — instead of a message whose text says "Photo".
moves.manifesto: Serves Health (roster/health — symptom and label evidence), Home (roster/home/MANIFESTO.md:30 device faults), Lifestyle, Relationship and General simultaneously; needs no manifesto amendment, but implies an amendment to openspec/specs/connector-base-spec (a Media Normalization Obligation: a connector that receives non-text content MUST materialize it as an IngestAttachment and MUST NOT synthesize a media-type descriptor into normalized_text) and to openspec/specs/connector-telegram-bot / connector-discord / the WhatsApp profile.
moves.integration_points: src/butlers/connectors/telegram_bot.py:133-181,1470 (delete _MEDIA_TYPE_LABELS text substitution; add getFile → blob_store.put → IngestAttachment); src/butlers/connectors/whatsapp_user_client.py:366-389 + the whatsmeow sidecar's media download; src/butlers/connectors/discord_user.py:134 (attachments already present in the payload, unused); shared media helper alongside src/butlers/connectors/gmail.py:3046-3214 (reuse its size caps, per-type policy and metrics at connectors/metrics.py:68-86); src/butlers/tools/attachments.py + src/butlers/core_tools/_media.py (return an MCP image/document content block, not data_base64; add a `describe` fallback for text-only models); src/butlers/core/model_capabilities.py:44-62 (add ModelFeature.VISION; declare it per model_catalog row) and src/butlers/core/dispatch_intent.py (require VISION when the trigger carries an image attachment, with UNKNOWN handled per its existing tri-state); src/butlers/core_tools/_routing.py:156-180 (ATTACHMENTS block becomes truthful — inline for vision-capable sessions, explicit 'this model cannot see images' otherwise); openspec/specs/s3-blob-storage (unchanged, already the store); a new `attachment_materialize` core tool that closes the lazy-fetch door via a Switchboard-mediated request rather than direct connector calls (MCP-only, vision.md rule 3).
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: owner sends a photo with caption 'is this mold?' → connector fetches bytes, puts one blob, emits IngestAttachment{media_type,storage_ref,size_bytes,width,height}, normalized_text = the caption (or empty, never 'Photo') → Switchboard persists attachments JSONB (ingest.py:841-867) → routing to Health → dispatch requires VISION → session calls attachment_view(storage_ref) → image content block → grounded answer citing the blob ref. Failure: getFile 404/expired file_id → attachment recorded with storage_ref=None and status=unavailable, normalized_text stays the caption, a filtered_events row with reason media_fetch_failed; blob store down → same, plus the ATTACHMENTS block says 'unavailable', never 'call get_attachment'; no vision-capable model in catalog → dispatch declares unmeetable capability and the reply says so instead of hallucinating a description. Concurrency: media fetch bounded by CONNECTOR_MAX_INFLIGHT; one blob per (endpoint_identity, external_message_id, media_id) via the existing idempotency key extended with a media suffix (mirrors owntracks.py:157-192 event_suffix). Idempotence: replay of the same update re-derives the same key; the pre-put existence check on (message_id, media_id) reuses the prior storage_ref rather than minting a second blob (the same lookup gmail.py:3251 already does). Rollback: revert the connector media branch and the tool's content-block return; blobs are orphaned but harmless (date-partitioned keys, existing retention); the envelope field is additive so no reader breaks.
moves.verification: tests/connectors/test_telegram_bot.py — a photo update yields normalized_text == caption (and empty, not 'Photo', when captionless) plus exactly one IngestAttachment with a resolvable storage_ref, asserted against a fake BlobStore; a second submission of the same update produces zero additional put() calls. tests/api or tests/core — get_attachment/attachment_view returns an MCP image content block for image/*, and for a >cap blob returns a typed refusal rather than a base64 payload; a contract test asserts no tool result anywhere contains a `data_base64` field over 64KB. tests/core/test_dispatch_intent — an image-bearing trigger against a catalog with no VISION model resolves to unmeetable, not to a text model. roster/switchboard/tests/test_ingest_api.py — attachments JSONB round-trips media_type/size/dimensions. E2E on the dev stack: ingest a fixture photo, then read GET /api/ingestion/events/{id}/payload and assert the stored text is the caption.
moves.slice_plan: S1 (trust, tiny): make the tool honest — content-block return + typed refusal above cap, ModelFeature.VISION, truthful ATTACHMENTS block; Gmail images become genuinely viewable with no connector work. S2: Telegram bot photos/documents → blobs (largest owner-visible win, one connector). S3: Discord (payload already has attachments) + WhatsApp sidecar media. S4: attachment_materialize for lazy blobs via Switchboard; retire GmailConnector.fetch_attachment's dead path. S5: base-spec + per-connector spec amendments and the no-synthesized-media-text contract test. Explicitly out of scope: voice-note STT (bu-r0dsz) and receipt/OCR finance extraction — this move carries pixels to a model, nothing more.

moves.title: Two-way household lists and device-update perception: promote the HA `todo` and `update` domains to first-class
moves.why: roster/home/MANIFESTO.md:15,30 promises device orchestration and firmware/battery/offline alerts; the second is unmeetable today (finding 4). And the highest-frequency household loop — the shared list — is invisible in both directions even though HA already hosts it as `todo.*` entities the owner edits from his phone. Doctrine fit is exact: HA is the sanctioned home surface (RFC 0018 'Home Assistant subsumes it'), the actuation gate already exists (RFC 0028, roster/home/modules/actuation.py), and this needs no new credential, sidecar, or paid API. Owner-visible in week one: he adds 'batteries' on his phone and the butler knows; the butler adds the thing he asked for and it appears on his phone in seconds; and 'the study lamp firmware is 3 versions behind, the front-door sensor battery is at 8%' becomes an actual alert instead of a manifesto sentence.
moves.manifesto: roster/home/MANIFESTO.md:15 (device orchestration), :30 (device health) — direct delivery of two existing promises; roster/lifestyle/MANIFESTO.md:15-19 consumes the same list as preference/pattern evidence. Requires amending openspec/specs/connector-home-assistant (default allowlist adds `todo`,`update`; significance semantics for non-numeric state) and openspec/specs/module-home-assistant (list verbs + a non-physical risk class).
moves.integration_points: src/butlers/connectors/home_assistant.py:122-142 (_DEFAULT_DOMAIN_ALLOWLIST += todo, update) and openspec/specs/connector-home-assistant/spec.md:123-132; src/butlers/connectors/home_assistant_filter.py (significance for `todo` item-count deltas and `update.installed_version` changes — these are not numeric-threshold sensors); src/butlers/connectors/home_assistant_pipeline.py:474 dispatcher (persist todo/update observations, today only `person` is persisted); roster/home/modules/actuation.py:23-50 + :79-81 (add ActuationRisk.INFORMATIONAL for todo.add_item/update_item/remove_item with the post-condition being an entity state read-back, not an approval; _EXPECTED_STATES/_INVERSE_SERVICES gain the item-level inverse) and roster/home/migrations/002_home_actuation_receipts.py (receipts already exist); roster/home/api/router.py + models.py for a list read surface; src/butlers/jobs/home.py (a device-health producer reconciling firmware-pending/battery-low snapshots into public.infra_conditions or owner_conditions via src/butlers/core/condition_ledger.py).
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path (perceive): owner adds 'batteries' in the HA to-do app → todo.* state change passes the allowlist, the filter classifies an item-added delta as significant, the dispatcher persists the item and ingests a low-priority envelope; Home/Lifestyle can read the list. Happy path (act): butler calls home_list_add(entity_id, item) → classified INFORMATIONAL → executed without an owner approval → receipt written only after re-reading the entity's item list and finding the item (post-condition authority, RFC 0028) → the item is on the owner's phone. Failure: HA unreachable → the call fails closed with no receipt and no 'done' claim; item added but read-back does not show it → receipt marked unverified and the tool returns failure, never success; `update` entity absent because the HA integration does not expose it → the device-health producer reports the check unmeasurable, never 'up to date'. Concurrency: the owner and the butler edit the same list at once → HA is the single writer of record; the butler always re-reads before claiming, and add is keyed on normalized item text so a double-add collapses. Idempotence: home_list_add is idempotent on (entity_id, normalized summary); the device-health producer uses condition_ledger fingerprints so a firmware-pending condition re-confirms rather than re-opens. Rollback: remove the two domains from the allowlist (config-level) and drop the list verbs; persisted observations and conditions remain readable; no schema removal needed.
moves.verification: tests/connectors/test_home_assistant_filter.py — a todo item-added event and an update.installed_version change are both classified significant, and a todo state change with an unchanged item list is dropped as insignificant (not merely allowlisted). tests/connectors/test_home_assistant_connector.py — a `todo.*` event is no longer recorded as domain_excluded in filtered_events. roster/home/tests — classify_actuation('todo','add_item') is INFORMATIONAL and requires no approval, while an unmapped ('todo','some_new_service') still defaults to PROTECTED; a receipt is written only when the post-read shows the item, and a read-back miss returns failure. A device-health job test asserting a firmware-pending snapshot opens exactly one condition and that a second identical snapshot confirms rather than duplicates. Live read-side check: after the allowlist change, GET /api/ingestion/connectors/{home_assistant}/{id}/events shows todo events instead of nothing.
moves.slice_plan: S1: allowlist + significance + dispatcher persistence for `todo` (perception only — the butler can answer 'what's on the list?'). S2: INFORMATIONAL risk class + home_list_add/complete/remove with read-back receipts (the two-way loop). S3: `update` domain + the device-health producer on the condition ledger, closing MANIFESTO.md:30. S4: spec amendments and a contract test that every promise sentence in Home's manifesto maps to a named producer.

moves.title: Steward: make the owner's own machines and self-hosted services a perceived domain
