moves.why: The instance is user-federated infrastructure (vision.md rule 1) running on the owner's own hardware over his own tailnet, and that substrate is load-bearing for the butlers themselves — the beads/Dolt backend, the dashboard boundary, the ActivityWatch host, the transcription service (src/butlers/api/middleware.py:27-29,216; connectors/activitywatch.py:65,83; jobs/decision_review.py:26). Today nothing perceives it: the only place a NAS appears in the codebase is a keyword list that filters disk temperatures *out* as non-ambient noise (src/butlers/jobs/home.py:872-891), and finding 7 is what that blindness costs — a connector silently dead for two months. Owner-visible in week one: 'your NAS array has a failing disk', 'the transcription box has been down since Tuesday, which is why the house has been quiet', 'a tailnet node key expires in 6 days and it is the one bd talks to' — the class of thing he currently discovers by accident.
moves.manifesto: No current manifesto owns the owner's infrastructure: roster/home/MANIFESTO.md:44-56 scopes Home to one residence's automation and explicitly refuses being an operator, and General (roster/general/MANIFESTO.md:11-15) is a freeform store. This implies a NEW butler — Steward, domain 'the owner's own compute' (hosts, self-hosted services, tailnet identity and key expiry, backup media, certificate and domain expiry) — or, if a new roster entry is unwanted, an explicit Home manifesto amendment adding a 'the machines that run your home' clause. Steward is a domain butler (it serves the owner, not the fleet), which keeps it out of the staffer archetype.
moves.integration_points: New connector src/butlers/connectors/homelab.py following openspec/specs/connector-base-spec (heartbeat, cursor_store checkpoints, filtered_events, replay drain) with three read-only probe families: Tailscale API (device list, last-seen, node/key expiry), HTTP/TCP service probes from a declared inventory, and host agent metrics already exposed to HA (disk health, SMART, free space) — plus src/butlers/connectors/registry_roles.py role registration and connectors/db_role.py grants; producer reconciling snapshots through src/butlers/core/condition_ledger.py into public.infra_conditions (src/butlers/core/infra_conditions.py:12-27 documents that the engine is already shared) for fleet-affecting hosts, and public.owner_conditions for owner-facing ones (expiring key, failing disk); roster/steward/{MANIFESTO.md,config,api/router.py,migrations}; docs/connectors/homelab.md; a new openspec/specs/connector-homelab + butler-steward.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: probe cycle enumerates the declared inventory, writes a complete snapshot, condition ledger opens 'transcription-service unreachable' at L0 and escalates on the existing schedule; a service that recovers is resolved by the *complete* snapshot, not by omission. Failure: the tailnet API itself is unreachable → the snapshot is marked incomplete and reconcile_snapshot(snapshot_complete=False) can confirm but never resolve, so nothing silently 'recovers'; a host outside the inventory is never reported as healthy. Concurrency: condition_ledger's source-scoped advisory lock serializes overlapping cycles; two Steward processes cannot double-open an episode. Idempotence: fingerprint identity per (host, check) means re-observing an outage confirms the open episode; the probe itself is read-only so retries are free. Rollback: stop the connector and archive its registry rows via the existing disconnect/archive routes; conditions remain as history; no other butler depends on it.
moves.verification: tests/connectors/test_homelab_connector.py — an unreachable service opens exactly one condition and a recovered snapshot resolves it, while an *incomplete* snapshot resolves nothing (the decisive semantic of condition_ledger); a key expiring inside the lead window opens an owner condition with the correct target date. tests/contracts — Steward declares an expected_signal per probed source so a probe that stops running reads UNMEASURABLE rather than PRESENT (the exact gap finding 7 exposes). Live read-side: GET /api/ingestion/connectors/summaries shows the new runtime_instance with checkpoints parented correctly (registry_roles.py:38-60 semantics), and the fleet roster does not list its cursors as offline connectors.
moves.slice_plan: S1: Steward manifesto + spec + the declared-inventory HTTP/TCP probe and condition producer (covers the whisper/AW/Dolt class of outage immediately). S2: Tailscale device inventory + key/cert/domain expiry as owner conditions with deadline lead times. S3: disk/SMART/free-space via the HA sensors already flowing (reuse, do not re-probe), and stop treating them as comfort noise. S4: an owner-facing Steward page or a Home page section; a briefing contribution.

moves.title: Hear the house, not just the talking: non-speech acoustic event perception on the microphones already installed
moves.why: The live-listener rig already runs mics, VAD and a discretion layer (openspec/specs/connector-live-listener/spec.md:4,82-105), and throws away every sound that is not a sentence — the prefilter drops anything under three words (src/butlers/connectors/live_listener/prefilter.py:29-40). Yet most of what a house tells you is not speech: the washer's end-of-cycle chime, a smoke alarm chirp, a dog barking for twenty minutes while the owner is out, glass, a running tap, a cough at 3am. This is new perception with zero new hardware, zero new credential, and no paid API — the cheapest large capability in the connector space. Owner-visible in week one: 'the laundry finished 40 minutes ago', 'your smoke alarm has been chirping since 14:10 — that is a battery, not a fire', 'the dog barked for 22 minutes after you left'.
moves.manifesto: roster/home/MANIFESTO.md:15,30 (comfort/appliance orchestration and device faults) and roster/health/MANIFESTO (night cough/snore as wellness evidence, delivered as observation not diagnosis); Home's 'not a voice assistant' clause (roster/home/MANIFESTO.md:47) is respected because this is perception, not command intake. Requires amending openspec/specs/connector-live-listener (its purpose sentence is speech-only) to add a non-speech event lane, and openspec/specs/connector-filtered-events for the new drop reasons.
moves.integration_points: src/butlers/connectors/live_listener/vad.py + audio.py:297-436 (tee the ring-buffer frames into a second consumer; VAD currently gates everything on speech probability); new live_listener/acoustic.py running a local deterministic classifier (YAMNet/PANNs-class, on-device, no LLM — keeps the cost boundary at zero marginal tokens per the architecture doctrine); live_listener/envelope.py (a distinct ingest.v1 event kind acoustic.v1 with label, confidence, mic, duration — never a transcript); live_listener/prefilter.py (a separate, non-word-count gate: label allowlist + per-label minimum duration + per-hour cap per mic); live_listener/filter_gate.py + connectors.filtered_events for suppressed labels; openspec/specs/connector-live-listener; the Home observation lane and, for wellness labels, roster/health ingestion policy.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: washer chime detected with confidence 0.86 for 3s on the kitchen mic → label-allowlisted, above duration floor, under the hourly cap → acoustic envelope submitted with no audio and no transcript → Home reports the finished cycle. Failure: classifier service/model unavailable → the speech lane is untouched (hard requirement: acoustic must never regress the sub-2s speech latency budget at spec:9-13) and the acoustic lane reports unmeasurable rather than silent; low-confidence label → dropped to filtered_events with reason acoustic_low_confidence so the owner can see what was heard and rejected. Concurrency: two mics hearing one event within a window collapse to a single event keyed by (label, coarse timestamp) so one alarm is not two; the acoustic consumer runs on its own task and back-pressures by dropping frames, never blocking the speech path. Idempotence: idempotency key acoustic:<endpoint>:<mic>:<label>:<bucketed unix_ms> — a replay re-submits the same key and Switchboard dedupes. Rollback: a single env flag disables the lane; no schema change beyond the envelope's event kind; the speech pipeline is byte-for-byte unchanged.
moves.verification: tests/connectors/live_listener/test_acoustic.py — a fixture WAV of an alarm chirp yields exactly one acoustic envelope with label and confidence and NO transcript field; a fixture of speech yields zero acoustic envelopes (the two lanes do not double-report); a below-floor 0.3s transient is dropped with reason acoustic_below_duration into filtered_events. A latency guard test asserting speech-offset-to-submission is unchanged with the acoustic consumer attached (spec:9-13 is the primary constraint). A privacy contract test asserting no acoustic envelope ever carries raw audio bytes or a storage_ref. Live read-side: the ingestion timeline shows acoustic events under the live_listener endpoint distinctly from utterances.
moves.slice_plan: S1: frame tee + on-device classifier + a deliberately tiny label allowlist (alarm/smoke chirp, appliance chime, glass break, running water) and the drop ledger. S2: Home consumption — appliance-cycle completion and alarm-chirp conditions with owner alerts. S3: opt-in wellness labels (cough, snore) gated by an explicit owner consent flag and Health-only routing. S4: spec amendment + per-label suppression UI on the existing connector filter surface. Never: speaker identification, or storing audio.

moves.title: Anchor the owner's places: a place registry from OwnTracks waypoints, with arrival as an evidence door
moves.why: Location is already ingested and already wasted (finding 5): region enter/leave and the owner's own named waypoints arrive as prose (src/butlers/connectors/owntracks.py:116,623-662) that no code in roster/ or jobs/ reads, while `place` sits in the entity_type CHECK with zero rows live. Anchoring places turns three separate butlers' questions into one substrate: Lifestyle can put an errand where it will actually be doable, Relationship gets in-person interaction evidence for the predicate that already exists (openspec/specs/predicate-taxonomy.md:180 interaction_meeting), Chronicler gets day texture with real toponyms instead of coordinates, and Finance can attach a merchant to a place. Owner-visible in week one: 'you are at the supermarket — two things on the list are here' and 'you spent 2h at Mum's on Sunday; last visit was 5 weeks ago'.
moves.manifesto: roster/relationship/MANIFESTO.md:15,59-65 (interaction history and Dunbar decay refreshed by real contact — an in-person visit is the strongest interaction there is, and today it is the only one the system cannot see); roster/lifestyle/MANIFESTO.md:15-19 (preferences and patterns); roster/chronicler (day narrative). No amendment needed for the place *registry*; the Relationship link needs an explicit owner-consent clause in that manifesto's philosophy section, since inferring a visit to a person from geography is a new inference class.
moves.integration_points: src/butlers/connectors/owntracks.py:116 (payload dispatch already supports `waypoints` and `transition`) — no connector change beyond keeping raw fields; a new deterministic producer that upserts public.entities rows with entity_type='place' from waypoint sync (openspec/specs/predicate-taxonomy.md:25 already prescribes the resolution cascade) and records enter/leave dwell as a place-visit observation; relationship.entity_facts for a place↔person association (has-address / lives-at style predicate, owner-confirmed only) and the shipped public entity graph edges (RFC 0031) for place↔person↔org; src/butlers/core/attention_ledger.py + the insight broker for arrival-triggered delivery (one attention budget, no second channel); composes with the HA `todo` list from the second move (an item tagged with a place becomes actionable on arrival); GET /api/relationship/entities?entity_type=place read surface.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: OwnTracks waypoint sync names 'Cold Storage' → one place entity minted with provenance source=owntracks; a later transition enter with the same desc opens a visit, leave closes it with a dwell duration; if any open list item is tagged to that place, the broker delivers one arrival nudge inside the existing budget. Failure: transition arrives with no matching waypoint (desc absent or renamed) → the visit is recorded against an unresolved place marked unidentified=true, never silently merged into a similarly named one; OwnTracks offline → no visit rows and an expected-signal that reads unmeasurable, never 'the owner went nowhere'. Concurrency: enter/leave for the same tst are disambiguated by the existing event_suffix idempotency key (owntracks.py:157-192); a duplicate enter without an intervening leave extends the open visit instead of opening a second. Idempotence: place upsert keyed on (canonical_name, entity_type) — the same index the entity table already carries (core_002_identity.py:125); visit rows keyed on (place, enter tst). Rollback: stop the producer; place entities are soft-deletable through the existing entity lifecycle (relationship migration 021) and nothing else depends on them. Privacy: arrival nudges and person-association inference are separately owner-gated; a place can be marked never-report.
moves.verification: tests for the producer — a waypoints payload mints exactly one place entity with provenance and a second identical sync mints none; an enter/leave pair produces one visit with the correct dwell, an enter/enter produces one; a transition whose desc matches no waypoint yields an unidentified place, not a fuzzy match. tests/relationship — a visit to a place associated with a person (owner-confirmed) produces one interaction_meeting fact with the visit as evidence, and an unassociated place produces none. Broker test: an arrival with three matching list items delivers one insight, and a second arrival inside the suppression window delivers none. Live read-side after the slice: GET /api/relationship/entities?limit=200 no longer returns zero places.
moves.slice_plan: S1: place registry from waypoints + visit ledger (pure perception, no delivery) — immediately answers 'where do I actually spend my time'. S2: arrival-triggered errand surfacing through the existing attention budget, composing with HA `todo`. S3: owner-confirmed place↔person association and interaction_meeting evidence for Dunbar. S4: Chronicler day-texture consumption and a place facet on the entity graph walk. Out of scope: transit/ETA and leave-by (already deferred), and any third-party geocoding — waypoint names come from the owner's own phone.

moves.title: Work is the missing half of the day: a Slack connector for commitments, colleagues and work rhythm
moves.why: Commitments are the one owner-condition class with no deterministic producer at all — src/butlers/core/commitments.py:12-16 states plainly that no scheduled job can survey the world for 'I told Sam I'd send him that book', so every commitment must be typed by hand. Most of the owner's promises are made at work, in threads, and the ecosystem ingests only personal channels (Telegram/WhatsApp/Discord). RFC 0018 deferred Slack (Messaging table, P2) on reach grounds — 'only valuable for Slack-using individuals' — which is a fleet-wide argument in a system whose first non-negotiable rule is one owner, one instance; and it concedes Socket Mode fits the tailnet-first model with no public ingress. For this owner the payoff is concrete: the promises, the people, and the hours that currently vanish. Owner-visible in week one: 'three things you said you'd do this week are still open', and a Dunbar picture that finally includes the people he actually talks to most.
moves.manifesto: roster/relationship/MANIFESTO.md:15,65 (interaction history and implicit tier placement — currently starved of the owner's highest-frequency channel), roster/general (obligations), roster/chronicler (day narrative), roster/messenger as transport-side staffer only. Requires an explicit RFC 0018 amendment recording that the Slack deferral rationale (reach) is not a valid criterion in a single-owner instance, plus a new openspec/specs/connector-slack.
moves.integration_points: New src/butlers/connectors/slack.py on Socket Mode (no public ingress, matching the WebSocket pattern of connectors/home_assistant.py and discord_user.py), endpoint identity from auth.test → slack:user:<team>:<user> (README 'Endpoint Identity' convention); openspec/specs/connector-base-spec obligations (cursor_store checkpoints, filtered_events, replay drain, heartbeat, source filters); src/butlers/connectors/registry_roles.py + db_role.py; src/butlers/connectors/discretion.py + filtered_event_buffer.py reuse for channel-scope discretion (the connector-base-spec:510-531 group-size discriminator applies directly — a 400-person #general is exactly the unbounded-token case it describes); identity via relationship.entity_facts has-handle triples prefixed slack:<id> (the pattern contacts-identity/spec.md documents for telegram:); src/butlers/core/commitments.py as the consumer for owner-authored promise candidates (created only through reconcile_snapshot(snapshot_complete=False), which is structurally unable to resolve what it did not see).
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: a DM or a channel message the owner is in arrives over Socket Mode → normalized to ingest.v1 with a stable idempotency key slack:<endpoint>:<channel>:<ts> → discretion + source filters applied → routed; the owner's own outbound messages feed passive interaction sync and commitment candidates. Failure: socket disconnect → exponential reconnect with the connector's last-seen ts as checkpoint; token revoked → the connector reports awaiting_credentials (the state spotify:unconfigured already models live) rather than online-with-zero-events; a channel the owner leaves stops producing without back-filling. Concurrency: Slack delivers duplicates on reconnect; the (channel, ts) key makes Switchboard dedupe exact. Idempotence: replays return the same canonical request_id per the base spec's at-least-once contract. Rollback: disconnect through the existing /api/ingestion/connectors/{type}/{id}/disconnect + archive routes; entity_facts handles remain (they are non-secret identifiers) and the schema addition is nil. Privacy: work content is high-sensitivity — default source filters exclude all channels until the owner opts each one in, the inverse of the personal-channel default.
moves.verification: tests/connectors/test_slack_connector.py — one message yields one envelope with the stable key; a reconnect replay yields no second submission; a non-opted-in channel is dropped with filter_reason channel_not_opted_in and appears in filtered_events; token revocation drives the registry state to awaiting_credentials, not online. tests/relationship — a slack: handle resolves to the same person entity as their email via the existing entity-graph cascade, and does not mint a duplicate. A commitment test: an owner-authored 'I'll send that by Friday' produces one candidate commitment through reconcile_snapshot(snapshot_complete=False) with evidence_opened pointing at the message, and a second identical run confirms rather than duplicating. Live read-side: the new connector appears in GET /api/ingestion/connectors/available and its checkpoints parent correctly in summaries.
moves.slice_plan: S1: RFC 0018 amendment + connector-slack spec + read-only Socket Mode ingestion of DMs only (highest signal, smallest privacy surface). S2: opt-in channel scope with group-size-aware discretion; interaction facts into Dunbar. S3: commitment candidates from the owner's own outbound messages, on the existing condition ledger. S4: work-rhythm perception (first/last message of day) into Chronicler; explicitly not a reply channel — Messenger owns egress and Slack stays read-only until the owner asks otherwise.

audits.jarvis_gap: Today Travel is a five-table filing cabinet (`travel.trips/legs/accommodations/reservations/documents`, `roster/travel/migrations/001_travel_tables.py`) with 7 MCP tools, 3 in-butler jobs, 3 core jobs (flight status, destination outlook, context producer), one bespoke dashboard tab (`frontend/src/components/butler-detail/ButlerTravelTripsTab.tsx`) and no route of its own — and against the live dev stack the filing cabinet is unreadable: every per-trip endpoint (`/api/travel/trips/{id}`, `/legs`, `/upcoming?within_days=90`) returns 400 because `travel.legs.metadata` was written double-encoded (jsonb_typeof = `string` on all four live legs) and `roster/travel/api/router.py:103` calls `dict()` on it. The same corruption makes `l.metadata ? 'flight_number'` false for every leg, so `src/butlers/jobs/flight_status.py:225` can never select a leg to poll — the entire "we alert you to delays before the airlines announce them" promise is structurally dead while `public.flight_status_feed_status` reports `legs_checked=0` with `last_error=NULL`. Beneath the corruption the data model has no notion of a journey (one round-trip PNR `DD94XR` became two separate 1-day trips, "Trip to PEK" and "Trip to SIN"), no notion of a travelling party (the same flight exists twice, once per passenger seat 47A/47C), no destination timezone anywhere, no passport type in the document CHECK, no layover/connection model despite the manifesto promising "connection times are verified for tight layovers", no cost or refundability field despite ingestion extracting `total_cost_sgd`/`cancellation_fee_sgd`/`change_fee_sgd` into the corrupted blob, no dreaming stage at all, and no observation of whether the owner actually went — `context_producer_travel` asserts `traveling` from calendar dates alone. The ideal is a journey spine that is booking-record-identified, party-aware, timezone-true, cost-and-refundability-honest, continuously reconciled against observed reality, and gated on entry requirements — with every consequential clause a door.
audits.live_verification: Live-confirmed READ-ONLY against the dev stack (JSON API http://127.0.0.1:42200 plus read-only SELECTs executed inside butlers-dev-dashboard-api-hotreload-1 via /app/.venv/bin/python + asyncpg against butlers-db-dev; no writes, no POST/PATCH/PUT/DELETE). Stack reachable and healthy: travel butler heartbeating active. Confirmed live: (a) GET /api/travel/trips?limit=5 → 200 with 4 planned trips; (b) GET /api/travel/upcoming (default 14d) → 200 empty, GET /api/travel/upcoming?within_days=60 and ?within_days=90 → 400 VALIDATION_ERROR "dictionary update sequence element #0 has length 1; 2 is required"; (c) GET /api/travel/trips/{id} and /legs → 400 for both live trips; (d) /accommodations, /reservations, /documents → 200; (e) SELECT jsonb_typeof(metadata) FROM travel.legs → 'string' for all 4 rows, and (metadata ? 'flight_number') → false for all 4; (f) travel.trips metadata written 2026-04 is jsonb 'object' (pre-codec) while legs written 2026-08 are 'string' (post-codec) — the JSONB codec landed 2026-05-01 in fae148e49 (#1324) and travel's json.dumps() call sites were never migrated; (g) all four legs share confirmation_number/pnr DD94XR yet sit in two different trips with start_date=end_date; (h) public.flight_status_feed_status → configured=false, legs_checked=0, last_error=NULL; (i) GET /api/travel/documents/expiring → {"documents":[]} despite two insurance documents (both expiry_date NULL). Static/source-confirmed: job-handler registration (src/butlers/scheduled_jobs.py:1910-1912 registers only flight_status_check/destination_outlook/context_producer_travel for travel — run_upcoming_travel_check and run_trip_document_expiry are referenced only from roster/travel/tests/test_jobs.py), the document type CHECK, and the frontend KPI wiring. No frontend browser render was performed; the KPI-zero claim is derived from the confirmed 400 plus the source at ButlerTravelTripsTab.tsx:646/669/173-240.
audits.ideal: A world-class travel butler treats a booking as an immutable provider record and a journey as the derived object: an order table keyed on (carrier, record_locator) with a traveller party, from which one trip container is reconstructed with true start/end, one leg per physical movement (not per passenger), destination-local timezones on every instant, and a connection graph that knows minimum connect times per airport and terminal. On that spine it perceives four things the owner cannot: fare economics with a refundability clock ("cancel free until 12 Oct 18:00 SGT; after that S$200 forfeit, changes S$70"), entry admissibility ("your passport expires 12 days inside China's 6-month rule"), connection integrity recomputed live from schedule deltas ("SQ800 is 40 min late — your PEK connection no longer holds; here are the two doors"), and execution truth from observed location and flight state ("you are wheels-up; trip is now active with evidence" / "the itinerary says in-transit and you are at home — this booking looks abandoned"). It speaks in destination-local time, closes trips itself with a receipt, and before booking exists it holds intentions — destination, target window, party, budget ceiling, feasibility against calendar and the party's availability — so the dreaming stage is a first-class ledger rather than a gap. Every consequential clause is a door on the approval spine, every aggregate is currency- and party-denominated, every absent signal is declared through `public.expected_signals` rather than rendered as a zero, and the owner's five-second glance shows a journey, its next irreversible deadline, and whether the system actually knows or is merely guessing from dates.

findings.title: Every per-trip Travel API endpoint returns 400 on real data: legs metadata is double-encoded jsonb and the row converter calls dict() on a str
findings.evidence: roster/travel/api/router.py:103 (metadata=dict(r["metadata"])); roster/travel/tools/bookings.py:231 (json.dumps(meta) into $13::jsonb); src/butlers/db.py:154-175 (register_jsonb_codec already json.dumps on write); git fae148e49 2026-05-01 (#1324); live: GET /api/travel/trips/d67e1ef2-32c6-4d77-9830-04765887c7f9 → 400, /legs → 400, /upcoming?within_days=90 → 400; SELECT jsonb_typeof(metadata) FROM travel.legs → 'string' ×4
findings.taxonomy_shape: NEW: writer bypasses a centrally-registered codec, so every row written after the codec landed is silently type-corrupted and only the reader that lacks a defensive fallback fails
findings.detail: The JSONB codec registered on all pools (src/butlers/db.py:169) encodes Python objects with json.dumps. roster/travel/tools/bookings.py passes an already-serialized str at lines 231, 282, 329, 361, 672 and 844, so the codec dumps it a second time and Postgres stores a jsonb *string*. travel.trips rows written before 2026-05-01 are objects (that is why /api/travel/trips still returns 200); every legs/accommodations/reservations row written since is a string. roster/travel/api/router.py:82,103,119,133,146 then calls dict() on that str and Pydantic raises, surfacing as a 400 VALIDATION_ERROR. Owner-visible effect: the trip detail drawer says "Trip data unavailable" and the Trips tab's week-ahead, checklist and KPI strip are all dead for every trip that actually has flights.

findings.title: The flight-status poll can never select a leg — its selection predicate is false for every row Travel writes, and the feed records the emptiness as success
findings.evidence: src/butlers/jobs/flight_status.py:225 (AND l.metadata ? 'flight_number'); flight_status.py:295 ((leg.get("metadata") or {}).get("flight_number")); flight_status.py:157-215 (_record_attempt writes legs_checked with last_error=NULL); live: SELECT (metadata ? 'flight_number') FROM travel.legs → false ×4; SELECT * FROM public.flight_status_feed_status → legs_checked=0, delays_detected=0, last_error=NULL
findings.taxonomy_shape: failure never impersonates health — violated: a structurally impossible query reports zero work with no error, so the feed reads as a healthy no-op
findings.detail: `?` on a jsonb scalar string is always false, so _fetch_upcoming_flight_legs returns zero rows even with a valid AVIATIONSTACK_API_KEY, and the fallback dict access at line 295 would also miss. The whole MANIFESTO promise "We will alert you to delays and gate changes before the airlines announce them" (roster/travel/MANIFESTO.md:21) is unreachable, and public.flight_status_feed_status will report configured=true, legs_checked=0, last_error=NULL — indistinguishable from "no upcoming flights".

findings.title: Travel KPI strip renders 0 active / 0 planned / 0 open actions and "—" next departure when its only data source 400s
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/butler-detail/ButlerTravelTripsTab.tsx:646 (useUpcomingTravel(90)); :669 (<KpiStrip upcoming={upcoming} isLoading={upcomingLoading}/> — no error prop); :168-196 (upcoming?.upcoming_trips ?? [], actions ?? []); live: /api/travel/upcoming?within_days=90 → 400
findings.taxonomy_shape: failure never impersonates health — the degraded envelope is rendered as authoritative zeros
findings.detail: The tab asks for a 90-day window, which is exactly the query that fails. WeekAheadSchedule and UpcomingChecklist do receive `error` and degrade honestly (:320, :381), but KpiStrip's props interface has no error field at all, so on failure it computes activeCount/plannedCount/actions.length from an empty array. The owner sees a confident "0 planned trips, 0 open actions" while four planned trips and a real 16-Oct departure exist in the database — two panels one row apart disagree, and the authoritative-looking one is the wrong one.

findings.title: One round-trip PNR became two separate one-day trips; trip duration is fiction, which silently disables the medication-prep gate
findings.evidence: roster/travel/tools/bookings.py:62-107 (_find_matching_trip matches on destination substring + date overlap only; never on pnr/confirmation_number); live: travel.trips → 'Trip to PEK' 2026-10-16..2026-10-16 and 'Trip to SIN' 2026-10-25..2026-10-25, both status=planned; travel.legs → all four legs share pnr='DD94XR'; roster/travel/jobs/travel_jobs.py:59,586-593 (_MEDICATION_PREP_MIN_TRIP_DAYS=3; `if (end_d - start_d).days <= 3: continue`)
findings.taxonomy_shape: NEW: the correlation key the domain already stores is excluded from identity resolution, so one real object is persisted as several
findings.detail: _create_trip_from_payload (bookings.py:109-172) derives start_date/end_date from the single leg's own dates, so a return leg 9 days later cannot overlap the outbound trip and no destination substring links PEK to SIN. Result: the owner's 10-day Beijing trip is two 1-day trips named after airport codes. Because end_date - start_date = 0, the medication-prep insight's `> 3 days` gate never fires; the destination-outlook and pre-trip windows key off the wrong dates; and the fleet's `traveling` context signal will assert for one day per leg rather than for the trip.

findings.title: No traveller party model: the same flight is stored once per passenger, double-counting departures — and the leg dedup key is both racy and wrong for multi-leg PNRs
findings.evidence: roster/travel/tools/bookings.py:181-191 (dedup SELECT on confirmation_number + trip_id, read-then-write, no unique index); roster/travel/migrations/001_travel_tables.py:74-83 (idx_legs_confirmation / idx_legs_pnr are plain indexes, not unique); src/butlers/jobs/briefing.py:1038-1041 ("{len(dep_rows)} departure(s) in next 48h"); roster/travel/tools/trips.py:241-252 (unseated-leg count); live: two legs SQ 800 seats 47A/47C, two legs SQ 807 seats 43A/43C, all confirmation_number='DD94XR'
findings.taxonomy_shape: NEW: an entity table conflates the movement with the ticket, so cardinality is per-passenger and every count downstream is multiplied by party size
findings.detail: Two consequences pull in opposite directions. (1) With no party model, a two-person booking writes two identical legs, so the daily briefing will announce "2 departure(s) in next 48h" for one flight and print two near-identical highlight lines, and _compute_trip_alerts counts unseated legs per passenger. (2) The dedup guard is simultaneously wrong the other way: a correctly-unified round trip has outbound AND return sharing confirmation_number DD94XR in the same trip, so the guard at bookings.py:181 would return the outbound's id and silently drop the return leg (created=False, deduped=True). Today the two bugs cancel — the return survived only because the trip-fragmentation bug put it in a different container. Fixing trip identity without fixing the dedup key would delete return legs.

findings.title: travel.documents cannot store a passport, the one document whose expiry gates travel, while the memory taxonomy and manifesto both promise passport tracking
findings.evidence: roster/travel/migrations/001_travel_tables.py:142 (CHECK (type IN ('boarding_pass','visa','insurance','receipt'))); openspec/specs/butler-travel/spec.md "Travel Memory Taxonomy" (predicate `passport_expiry`, permanence `stable`); roster/travel/MANIFESTO.md:24 ("Boarding passes, visas, insurance policies … tracked for expiry"); roster/travel/jobs/travel_jobs.py:33 (_EXPIRY_RELEVANT_TYPES = {"visa","insurance","boarding_pass"})
findings.taxonomy_shape: NEW: a domain's most consequential fact has no column, so the promise is met only in prose and in an LLM-side memory fact with no gate
findings.detail: The expiry scan's relevant-type set includes boarding_pass — whose expiry is meaningless — and excludes passport, which cannot even be inserted. Nothing anywhere compares a passport expiry to departure_date plus a destination's validity rule (typically 6 months), so the highest-stakes travel failure mode (denied boarding for insufficient passport validity) is entirely outside the system. Live corroboration of the resulting emptiness: /api/travel/documents/expiring returns {"documents":[]} while two insurance documents exist with expiry_date NULL.

findings.title: Two deterministic travel jobs are unreachable dead code kept alive only by their own tests, while the schedules that name them run as LLM prompts
findings.evidence: roster/travel/butler.toml (schedules `upcoming-travel-check` and `trip-document-expiry` both dispatch_mode = "prompt"); src/butlers/scheduled_jobs.py:1910-1912 (travel handler map registers only flight_status_check, destination_outlook, context_producer_travel); roster/travel/jobs/travel_jobs.py:79-230 (run_upcoming_travel_check), :232-330 (run_trip_document_expiry); roster/travel/tests/test_jobs.py:289-410 (the only callers)
findings.taxonomy_shape: built twice, unified never — a deterministic path and an LLM prompt path implement the same scan; only the prompt path runs, only the deterministic path is tested
findings.detail: ~250 lines re-implement upcoming_travel's alert logic and the document-expiry sweep with their own thresholds, and no scheduler dispatch can reach either. The test suite exercises them thoroughly, which manufactures confidence that the deterministic scan exists. Doctrine cuts the other way too: rule 4 (about/heart-and-soul/vision.md "the daemon is deterministic infrastructure") argues these two zero-reasoning scans should be the job path and the prompt should be retired, not the reverse.

findings.title: Fare economics are extracted at ingestion then discarded: cost, cancellation fee, change fee and miles live only inside the corrupted metadata blob with no column, no aggregate and no deadline door
findings.evidence: live travel.legs metadata payload: total_cost_sgd=1622.6, cancellation_fee_sgd=200, change_fee_sgd=70, krisflyer_miles=2790, payment_method, pps_club_valid_until=2026-10-31; roster/travel/migrations/001_travel_tables.py:52-72 (legs has no cost/currency/refundability column); roster/travel/AGENTS.md "Scope discipline" ("expense accounting is out of scope"); roster/travel/domain_events.toml:16-29 (travel.trip_booked carries trip ids and dates only)
findings.taxonomy_shape: computed-then-discarded truth
findings.detail: The ingestion session already parsed the exact numbers that make a trip a financial commitment, and stored them in an unqueryable, type-corrupted JSON string. Nothing can answer "what did Beijing cost", nothing knows the trip is S$1,622.60 committed, nothing knows S$200 is forfeit after a deadline, and travel.trip_booked hands Finance a trip id and dates with no amount — so Finance's pre-budget wake has to guess. AGENTS.md's scope-discipline clause is being read as "do not persist the price", which is a different and much weaker claim than "do not do expense accounting".

findings.title: The `traveling` fleet signal and `travel.trip_active` are asserted from calendar dates alone, never from observed reality, and the once-per-trip publish cannot be retracted
findings.evidence: src/butlers/jobs/context_producers.py:330-341 (WHERE status='active' OR (status IN ('planned','active') AND start_date <= current_date AND end_date >= current_date)); :347-355 (set_context confidence=1.0, metadata.source='travel_trip'); :369-383 (publish_domain_event_once memoized on trip id); no writer anywhere transitions travel.trips.status automatically (grep for UPDATE travel.trips SET status → only roster/travel/tools/bookings.py:679 via update_itinerary)
findings.taxonomy_shape: writer's clock impersonating world's clock (new instance: a booked date impersonating an observed location)
findings.detail: confidence=1.0 is asserted for "the owner is travelling" on the sole basis that today falls inside a date range typed from an email — with no OwnTracks corroboration, no flight-status corroboration, and no owner confirmation. A cancelled-but-not-updated booking makes the whole fleet believe the owner is in Beijing; Health's medication-prep wake fires on that belief, at-most-once, with no retraction path if the trip never happens. Because nothing auto-advances status, trips also never reach `completed`: all four live trips are `planned`, including two from April and July that are long past.

findings.title: The flight-status poll writes an estimated departure into metadata but never updates the leg's departure_at, its updated_at, or any downstream connection
findings.evidence: src/butlers/jobs/flight_status.py:240-256 (_write_leg_status merges metadata->'flight_status' only; no departure_at, no updated_at); flight_status.py:100-140 (parse_flight_status returns estimated_departure); no consumer of metadata->'flight_status' exists (grep 'flight_status' across roster/travel and frontend/src → none)
findings.taxonomy_shape: computed-then-discarded truth + last hop has no door
findings.detail: Even with the corruption fixed, a 90-minute delay would leave departure_at showing the original schedule everywhere the owner actually looks — trip_summary's timeline, the daily briefing's "in {hours_until}h", the calendar overlay, the check-in-window alert — because the delta lands in a metadata key nothing reads. updated_at is not touched either, so freshness reads as stale-but-current. And nothing recomputes whether the connection still holds or offers a rebooking door: the notification is terminal advice, not a decision.

findings.title: Two row-to-dict converters for the same tables, one defensive and one not, so the MCP tool path survives the corruption the API path dies on
findings.evidence: roster/travel/tools/_helpers.py:14-37 (_row_to_dict has an isinstance(val, str) and key == "metadata" json.loads fallback, documented as "defensive fallback for environments where the JSONB codec is not registered"); roster/travel/api/router.py:74-148 (five bare dict() converters with no fallback)
findings.taxonomy_shape: built twice, unified never
findings.detail: The tool layer's converter was hardened against exactly this failure and its docstring names it; the API layer's five converters, written later, were not. The consequence is that the same trip is readable via MCP and unreadable via HTTP, so an LLM session and the dashboard disagree about whether the owner has an itinerary.

findings.title: butler-travel spec's scheduled-task inventory omits three schedules the butler actually runs
findings.evidence: openspec/specs/butler-travel/spec.md "Scenario: Scheduled task inventory" (lists upcoming-travel-check, trip-document-expiry, insight-scan + 3 contribution jobs); roster/travel/butler.toml also declares flight-status-check (*/30 * * * *), destination-outlook (30 7 * * *) and context_producer_travel (*/15 * * * *)
findings.taxonomy_shape: NEW: an exhaustive-by-wording spec inventory that is not exhaustive, so spec-versus-code reconciliation reads clean while three jobs are ungoverned
findings.detail: The two most externally-coupled travel jobs — the only one that spends an external API budget and the only one that asserts a fleet-wide context signal — are absent from the capability spec that claims to enumerate the schedules, so neither has a stated degraded-mode requirement or cadence contract in openspec.

moves.title: Journey identity: a PNR-keyed booking record and a traveller party, from which the trip container is derived
moves.why: MANIFESTO.md:19 promises "your entire trip is already in one place: flights, hotels, reservations, and documents all connected to the right trip at the right time" — live, a single round-trip PNR (DD94XR) is two trips named 'Trip to PEK' and 'Trip to SIN', each one day long, each holding two copies of the same flight. Owner-visible within a day of shipping: the Trips tab reads 'Beijing · 16–25 Oct · 9 days · you + Chloe' with four legs, instead of two airport codes and four rows. This is the identity substrate every other move on this list stands on, and it is where the correctness clean-up (double-encoded metadata, racy dedup, per-passenger cardinality) belongs — vision.md rule 4 puts deterministic identity resolution in the daemon, not in a session's judgment.
moves.integration_points: New tables `travel.booking_records` (id, carrier, record_locator, source_message_id, issued_at, raw_ref, UNIQUE (carrier, record_locator)) and `travel.travellers` (id, entity_id → public.entities, display_name, is_owner) plus `travel.leg_passengers` (leg_id, traveller_id, seat, ticket_number, baggage, UNIQUE (leg_id, traveller_id)); `travel.legs` loses `seat` and gains `booking_record_id`, `segment_index`, and a UNIQUE (booking_record_id, segment_index); `travel.trips` gains `booking_record_ids uuid[]` and derived start/end. Migration roster/travel/migrations/002_journey_identity.py plus a backfill that json.loads every string-typed metadata blob. Writers: roster/travel/tools/bookings.py (_find_matching_trip resolves on (carrier, record_locator) first, then dates; every json.dumps at :231,:282,:329,:361,:672,:844 is dropped so the codec at src/butlers/db.py:169 owns encoding). Readers: roster/travel/api/router.py:74-148 (delete the five bare dict() converters, reuse roster/travel/tools/_helpers.py:_row_to_dict), roster/travel/tools/trips.py, src/butlers/jobs/briefing.py:953-985 (dedup by leg, list party), src/butlers/jobs/calendar_overlay.py:369-420, src/butlers/jobs/flight_status.py:225. Spec: openspec/specs/butler-travel/spec.md 'Trip Container Model' amended to a journey model; roster/travel/domain_events.toml travel.trip_booked schema_version → 2 with party_size and record_locator. Tool surface: record_booking accepts a full booking record with a segments[] array and a passengers[] array in one call.
moves.manifesto: roster/travel/MANIFESTO.md ("One view. All the details.", "every confirmation number, PNR, and reservation detail organized") — served, not amended. The party model touches roster/relationship/MANIFESTO.md's ownership of people: travellers link to public.entities by entity_id and Travel stores no relational facts of its own.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy: a two-passenger round-trip confirmation yields one booking_record, one trip 16–25 Oct, two legs (segment_index 0,1), four leg_passengers rows. Failure: a confirmation with no record locator falls back to today's date+destination matching and sets trips.metadata.identity_confidence='weak' so the UI can say so, never silently merging. Concurrency: the read-then-write dedup at bookings.py:181 is replaced by ON CONFLICT (booking_record_id, segment_index) DO UPDATE, so two sessions racing the same email converge instead of duplicating; leg_passengers has its own unique key so a second passenger is an insert, not a dedup hit. Idempotence: re-ingesting the same source_message_id is a no-op returning created=false with the same ids. Rollback: the backfill writes the pre-parse blob to legs.metadata.raw_pre_migration, and 002's downgrade restores seat onto legs from leg_passengers (owner-scoped party only) — the booking_records table is additive so a revert loses derivation, not data.
moves.verification: (1) A migration test asserting jsonb_typeof(metadata)='object' for all travel.legs rows after backfill and that raw_pre_migration round-trips. (2) roster/travel/tests/test_bookings.py: ingesting the real DD94XR fixture (two passengers × two segments, four record_booking-shaped payloads in any order) produces exactly 1 trip with start_date 2026-10-16/end_date 2026-10-25, 2 legs, 4 leg_passengers — asserted against the DB, not the return value. (3) A concurrency test firing the four payloads under asyncio.gather and asserting the same invariant. (4) A regression test that the return leg is NOT deduped away when both segments share confirmation_number. (5) Live seam: GET /api/travel/trips/{id} and /legs return 200 for the DD94XR trip (today both 400). (6) A test asserting src/butlers/jobs/flight_status.py:_fetch_upcoming_flight_legs selects both segments of the backfilled PNR.
moves.slice_plan: Slice 1 (unblocks everything, ship alone): drop the json.dumps call sites, backfill string-typed metadata to objects, replace router.py's five dict() converters with _row_to_dict, and add an API test that reads a leg with non-empty metadata — this alone restores the Trips tab and the flight-status poll's selectability. Slice 2: booking_records + segment identity + ON CONFLICT dedup + _find_matching_trip on record_locator, with the fragmentation backfill behind a dry-run report the owner reviews before it merges trips. Slice 3: travellers/leg_passengers + party-aware briefing and alert counts. Slice 4: spec amendment, domain-event schema_version 2, dashboard party chip.

moves.title: Connection integrity: a journey graph that knows whether the layover still holds, recomputed live from schedule deltas
moves.why: MANIFESTO.md:23 states flatly "Connection times are verified for tight layovers" and the upcoming-travel skill even scripts the output ('⚠️ Tight layover: 45 min at ORD') — but no code anywhere computes a layover; grep for layover/connection_time across src/ and roster/ returns only prose and skill text. This is the single largest gap between what Travel says and what Travel does. Owner-visible within a week: the pre-trip notice becomes 'PEK connection: 1h05 against a 90-minute minimum — this does not hold', and when the flight-status poll sees a 40-minute delay the owner is told the connection broke before the airline tells them, which is precisely the promise on MANIFESTO.md:21.
moves.integration_points: New `travel.connections` (id, trip_id, inbound_leg_id, outbound_leg_id, planned_minutes, minimum_minutes, terminal_change bool, verdict text CHECK (verdict IN ('holds','tight','broken','unknown')), evidence jsonb, computed_at) derived deterministically from adjacent legs of a booking_record; a small owner-editable `public.airport_minimum_connect` reference table (iata, domestic_minutes, international_minutes, source, note) seeded from owner input rather than a scraped feed, with verdict='unknown' and an honest absence row in public.expected_signals when an airport is unknown. Producer: extend src/butlers/jobs/flight_status.py:_write_leg_status to also write the observed estimated_departure onto the leg and re-run the connection derivation for that booking_record (this is the repair for the computed-then-discarded finding). Reader: roster/travel/tools/trips.py:_compute_trip_alerts and roster/travel/api/router.py:372 gain a `connection_broken`/`connection_tight` alert; frontend ButlerTravelTripsTab week-ahead panel renders the verdict inline. Insight: a new category 'connection-integrity' via propose_insight_candidate. Door: a broken connection raises a pending_actions row through the approvals spine (src/butlers/modules/approvals) offering 'notify carrier / rebook / accept risk' rather than a terminal alert.
moves.manifesto: roster/travel/MANIFESTO.md:21-23 — served; this is the promise being kept for the first time. No amendment needed. The rebooking door touches nothing another manifesto owns because it proposes, and the owner decides on the existing approval spine.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy: two legs of one booking_record 65 minutes apart at PEK with an 90-minute international minimum → verdict='broken', one alert, one approval door. Failure: PEK absent from airport_minimum_connect → verdict='unknown' with evidence.reason='no_minimum_on_file' and an expected_signals row saying so; the UI shows 'unknown', never 'holds'. Concurrency: derivation is keyed on (inbound_leg_id, outbound_leg_id) with ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE and a computed_at fence, so the 30-minute poll and a manual update_itinerary cannot interleave into a stale verdict. Idempotence: re-derivation with identical inputs writes the same row and does not re-propose the insight (dedup_key includes the verdict and the rounded delta, mirroring flight_status.py:376). Rollback: table is additive and derived; dropping it restores today's silence. Reversal: when a later poll shows the delay recovered, verdict flips back to 'holds' and the approval door is withdrawn rather than left dangling.
moves.verification: (1) Unit tests over the derivation: holds / tight / broken / unknown / terminal-change, including a same-carrier vs interline distinction. (2) A test that feeding parse_flight_status a 40-minute delay on the inbound leg flips a previously-holding connection to 'broken' and that legs.departure_at and updated_at both move (today _write_leg_status touches neither). (3) A test that verdict='unknown' emits an expected_signals row and never an alert claiming safety. (4) A test that the approval door is created once per verdict transition and withdrawn on recovery. (5) Live seam after slice 2: GET /api/travel/trips/{id} on the DD94XR journey returns a connections[] block (that journey has no connection, so assert an empty array with a stated reason rather than an omitted key).
moves.slice_plan: Slice 1: derivation + travel.connections + alerts on trip_summary and /upcoming, minimum table seeded with the airports actually present in travel.legs and 'unknown' elsewhere. Slice 2: live recompute wired into flight_status, including the departure_at/updated_at repair. Slice 3: approval door + insight category. Slice 4: dashboard rendering and the spec requirement in openspec/specs/butler-travel.

moves.title: Destination admissibility gate: passport as a first-class document, validity math against entry rules, and a hard door before departure
moves.why: The document CHECK at roster/travel/migrations/001_travel_tables.py:142 cannot store a passport, while openspec/specs/butler-travel/spec.md's memory taxonomy defines a `passport_expiry` predicate and MANIFESTO.md:24 promises 'Know which documents are valid and which need renewal before you travel'. Nothing compares any document to a departure date plus a destination rule, so the highest-consequence travel failure — denied boarding for insufficient passport validity — is entirely outside the system, and the expiry scan instead watches boarding passes, whose expiry is meaningless. Owner-visible immediately: 'China requires 6 months validity beyond entry; your passport expires 2027-01-10 and you enter 2026-10-16 — you are 12 days short. Renew before 2026-09-20 to be safe.'
moves.integration_points: Migration widens `travel.documents.type` to include 'passport','vaccination','entry_permit' and adds `issuing_country`, `document_number_last4`, `holder_traveller_id`, `valid_from`; new `travel.entry_requirements` (destination_country, nationality, min_passport_validity_months, visa_required text, vaccination_required text[], source_url, asserted_by, asserted_at, confidence) as an owner-asserted, evidence-cited reference table — not a scraped feed, so it stays inside the connectors-as-cost-boundary doctrine in about/heart-and-soul/architecture.md. Derivation in roster/travel/tools/documents.py plus a new `admissibility_check(trip_id)` MCP tool in roster/travel/modules/tools.py. Job: replace the dead run_trip_document_expiry (roster/travel/jobs/travel_jobs.py:232) with a registered deterministic handler in src/butlers/scheduled_jobs.py that scores admissibility per traveller per trip, and flip butler.toml's trip-document-expiry schedule from dispatch_mode='prompt' to 'job'. Honest absence: a trip whose destination country has no entry_requirements row emits a public.expected_signals row with unmeasurable semantics (RFC 0029) rather than a green verdict. Door: an admissibility gap inside 60 days of departure raises an approval-spine decision with 'renew / accept risk / cancel trip' options.
moves.manifesto: roster/travel/MANIFESTO.md:24 and the 'Prepare with peace of mind' clause — served. Implies a small amendment to openspec/specs/butler-travel/spec.md: the document-expiry requirement must name passport and must be expressed as validity-against-departure, not days-until-expiry.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy: passport on file for the owner and for Chloe, destination CN, 6-month rule → per-traveller verdict; the short one produces one alert and one door. Failure: no passport on file → verdict='unknown' + expected_signals row + an insight asking the owner to add it; never 'valid'. No entry_requirements row for the country → same honest-unknown path, with the destination named so the owner can assert the rule once. Concurrency: derivation is a pure read plus an upsert on (trip_id, traveller_id) with a computed_at fence; two schedules cannot produce contradictory verdicts. Idempotence: dedup_key 'travel:admissibility:{trip_id}:{traveller_id}:{verdict}' so a re-scan at the same verdict is silent and a verdict change re-notifies. Rollback: additive tables plus a widened CHECK; downgrade narrows the CHECK only after asserting no passport/vaccination rows exist, so a revert cannot orphan data.
moves.verification: (1) Unit tests: 6-month rule short by 12 days → 'insufficient'; exactly 6 months → 'marginal'; 8 months → 'ok'; no passport → 'unknown'; no requirement row → 'unknown' with the reason distinguishable from the no-passport case. (2) A test that the widened CHECK accepts type='passport' and that the migration's downgrade refuses when passport rows exist. (3) A test asserting the deterministic handler is reachable through src/butlers/scheduled_jobs.py's travel handler map (this is also the regression test for the dead-job finding). (4) A test that 'unknown' writes an expected_signals row and produces no admissibility alert. (5) Live seam: GET /api/travel/documents/expiring stops returning [] for a trip with a passport whose validity is short — today it returns [] even with two insurance documents on file, because both have expiry_date NULL.
moves.slice_plan: Slice 1: widen the document type CHECK, add holder/issuing-country columns, add passport to the expiry-relevant set and drop boarding_pass from it. Slice 2: entry_requirements table + admissibility derivation + admissibility_check tool. Slice 3: register the deterministic job, flip butler.toml to dispatch_mode='job', retire the prompt. Slice 4: approval door + expected_signals wiring + spec amendment.

moves.title: Destination-local time spine: every travel instant carries the timezone it is lived in
moves.why: There is no timezone column anywhere in travel (roster/travel/migrations/001_travel_tables.py has none), the API stringifies raw UTC (roster/travel/api/router.py:97 `str(r["departure_at"])`), _build_timeline sorts on UTC strings (roster/travel/tools/_helpers.py:39-118), and the briefing renders 'in {hours_until:.0f}h' with no local anchor (src/butlers/jobs/briefing.py:977-983) — yet MANIFESTO.md:26 promises 'time-zone adjustments' and the daily schedule is authored in SGT. The live SIN→PEK leg reads '2026-10-15 17:10 UTC' where the owner boards at 01:10 on the 16th Singapore time — which is also why the trip container says 16 Oct while the leg says 15 Oct. Owner-visible on day one: the itinerary reads in the time the owner will actually be standing in, and check-in windows stop being off by the offset.
moves.integration_points: Add `departure_tz`/`arrival_tz` (IANA) to travel.legs, `tz` to travel.accommodations and travel.reservations, and `home_tz`/`destination_tz` to travel.trips; a small `public.airport_tz` reference (iata, iana_tz, city, country) seeded from the airports present in travel.legs, extended by owner assertion, with NULL meaning unknown rather than UTC. Derivation at write time in roster/travel/tools/bookings.py (station code → tz) and a backfill for existing rows. Readers: roster/travel/api/models.py gains `departure_at_local`/`departure_tz` alongside the UTC instant (never replacing it); roster/travel/tools/_helpers.py:_build_timeline sorts on the UTC instant and labels in local; src/butlers/jobs/briefing.py:977 and src/butlers/jobs/calendar_overlay.py:369 render local; frontend ButlerTravelTripsTab uses the existing <Time> primitive with an explicit zone. Cross-butler: the tz delta is what makes Health's travel.trip_active medication wake (roster/health/AGENTS.md 'Domain-Event Wake') able to shift a dosing schedule instead of merely reminding about supply — so travel.trip_active gains optional home_tz/destination_tz fields in roster/travel/domain_events.toml.
moves.manifesto: roster/travel/MANIFESTO.md:26 ('time-zone adjustments') — served. The dosing-shift half is roster/health/MANIFESTO.md's to decide; Travel supplies the offset as reference data and asserts nothing clinical, matching the existing reaction_contract discipline in domain_events.toml.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy: SIN→PEK renders 'departs 01:10 Fri 16 Oct SGT · arrives 07:15 CST (+0 h shift)'. Failure: unknown station code → tz NULL, the UI shows the UTC instant with an explicit 'timezone unknown' marker and never silently labels it local; the trip's tz-shift figure is omitted rather than shown as zero. Concurrency: tz derivation is a pure function of the station code, so a re-derivation is byte-identical and safe to run concurrently with any other writer. Idempotence: the backfill is a WHERE tz IS NULL update. Rollback: additive nullable columns; dropping them returns to UTC-only rendering with no data loss. Ordering invariant: all sorting and window arithmetic continues to use the UTC instant, so a tz bug can mislabel but can never reorder an itinerary or shift a check-in window.
moves.verification: (1) A test asserting the 17:10Z SIN departure renders 01:10 SGT on 16 Oct and that trips.start_date derived from it is 2026-10-16, not 2026-10-15 (the live off-by-one). (2) A test that an unknown station yields tz NULL and a rendering path that says 'unknown' rather than assuming UTC. (3) A property test that _build_timeline's ordering is identical with and without tz populated. (4) A test that the 24-hour check-in window in roster/travel/tools/trips.py:264-282 opens at the right local moment across a DST boundary. (5) Live seam: /api/travel/trips/{id} returns departure_at plus departure_at_local plus departure_tz for the DD94XR legs.
moves.slice_plan: Slice 1: airport_tz reference + columns + write-time derivation + backfill. Slice 2: API model fields and the frontend <Time> zone wiring. Slice 3: briefing and calendar-overlay local rendering; correct trips.start_date derivation from local departure date. Slice 4: tz fields on travel.trip_active for Health.

moves.title: Execution truth: reconcile the itinerary against observed reality, and let trips close themselves with evidence
moves.why: src/butlers/jobs/context_producers.py:330-341 asserts `traveling` with confidence=1.0 purely because today falls inside a date range typed from an email, and nothing auto-advances travel.trips.status — all four live trips are still 'planned', including ones from April and July. So the fleet can believe the owner is in Beijing when the booking was quietly cancelled, Health's once-only medication wake fires on that belief with no retraction, and the owner's travel history never closes. The system already receives the two signals that would settle it: the OwnTracks connector (src/butlers/connectors/owntracks.py normalizes location and region transitions) and the flight-status poll. Owner-visible within a week: trips move themselves through planned → active → completed with a receipt naming the evidence, past trips stop cluttering 'planned', and the fleet's travelling signal stops being date-fiction.
moves.integration_points: New `travel.trip_observations` (id, trip_id, kind CHECK (kind IN ('departed','arrived','at_destination','back_home','divergence')), observed_at, source CHECK (source IN ('owntracks','flight_status','owner')), evidence jsonb, confidence numeric) — a perception ledger for Travel, the sibling of the deferred home.observations ledger. Reader: a new deterministic reconciliation job registered in src/butlers/scheduled_jobs.py that (a) advances status planned→active only on an observation, not a date, (b) advances active→completed on a back_home observation plus end_date elapsed, (c) raises a 'divergence' observation when the itinerary says in-transit and location says home. Rewrite src/butlers/jobs/context_producers.py:330-355 to key on status plus the latest observation and to carry a real confidence (1.0 observed, 0.5 date-only) in the context metadata instead of a hardcoded 1.0. Domain event: travel.trip_active gains a `basis` field ('observed'|'scheduled') in roster/travel/domain_events.toml and a companion travel.trip_abandoned so Health's once-only wake becomes retractable. Location source: consume OwnTracks region/location through the existing ingestion path, never by reaching into another schema (vision.md rule 3).
moves.manifesto: roster/travel/MANIFESTO.md ('synced, real-time', 'waiting for you when you return home') — served. Neighbour, not overlap: the ledger's owner-absent operation, absence plans and homecoming review are the *actions* taken while away; this move is only the perception and lifecycle truth that any of them would need, and it is Travel-side rather than Home-side. The at_home owner-scope work (run 11 item 11) is the Home-clock counterpart.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy: an owntracks region-leave at SIN plus flight_status='active' writes 'departed', status → active, travel.trip_active published with basis='observed'. Failure: OwnTracks silent (connector down) → no observation, status stays 'planned', the context signal is written with basis='scheduled' and confidence 0.5, and an expected_signals row states that departure confirmation is unmeasurable — the signal never claims observation it does not have. Divergence: itinerary in-transit + at_home for 6+ hours past departure → a 'divergence' observation, an insight, and travel.trip_abandoned so Health can retract. Concurrency: observations are append-only with a unique (trip_id, kind, source, observed_at) key; the status advance is a single conditional UPDATE ... WHERE status = expected, so two schedules cannot double-advance or move backward (the forward-only rule at roster/travel/tools/bookings.py:24-29 is enforced in SQL, not just in the tool). Idempotence: re-running the reconciliation with no new observation is a no-op returning zeros. Rollback: append-only ledger plus a feature flag on the auto-advance; disabling it returns to manual update_itinerary with the ledger intact as evidence.
moves.verification: (1) Tests for each transition, including that a date inside the trip window with zero observations does NOT advance status (today's date-fiction, asserted as a regression). (2) A test that context_producers writes basis='scheduled' + confidence 0.5 with no observation and basis='observed' + 1.0 with one. (3) A test that the divergence path publishes travel.trip_abandoned exactly once and that Health's subscription admits it (roster/travel/domain_events.toml permitted_subscribers). (4) A concurrency test firing the reconciliation twice under gather and asserting a single transition. (5) A test that the three long-past 'planned' live trips reach 'completed' or 'cancelled' under the backfill and that none moves backward. (6) Live seam: /api/butlers context signal for travel carries a basis field.
moves.slice_plan: Slice 1: trip_observations ledger + owner-asserted observations only (an MCP verb the owner can trigger from Telegram: 'I'm at the airport'), plus the honest confidence/basis rewrite of context_producers — this alone kills the date-fiction. Slice 2: flight_status-derived departed/arrived observations. Slice 3: OwnTracks-derived observations and auto-advance behind a flag. moves.title: Trip intentions: a dreaming-stage ledger with party and calendar feasibility, so the lifecycle starts before the confirmation email
moves.why: The pursuit question names six stages and the system implements four-and-a-half: nothing exists before a confirmation email arrives. There is no place to say 'Japan, April, two weeks, with Chloe, under S$6,000' — no table, no tool, no insight category — so the highest-leverage travel moment (the one where a decision is still open) is entirely unserved, and MANIFESTO.md's 'Prepare with peace of mind' begins only after the money is spent. Owner-visible within a week of shipping: an intention the owner typed once starts producing unprompted, specific observations — 'Your Japan-in-April intention: the only two-week window clear of calendar commitments starts 4 Apr, and it closes on 11 Apr when the offsite lands. Chloe's leave is not booked.'
moves.integration_points: New `travel.trip_intentions` (id, title, destination_hint, target_window_start, target_window_end, flex_days, duration_days, party_traveller_ids uuid[], budget_ceiling numeric, currency text, status CHECK (status IN ('dreaming','researching','ready_to_book','booked','abandoned')), booked_trip_id, created_at, updated_at) and `travel.intention_conditions` (intention_id, kind CHECK (kind IN ('calendar_clear','party_available','budget_available','document_ready','price_below')), state, evidence jsonb, evaluated_at). Tools: `intention_record`, `intention_list`, `intention_promote` in roster/travel/modules/tools.py. Deterministic evaluator registered in src/butlers/scheduled_jobs.py: calendar_clear resolves against the calendar module's own event reads; document_ready reuses the admissibility gate from move 3; budget_available is asked of Finance through delegate_ask (roster/travel/.agents/skills/cross-butler-delegation) — never by reading finance.* (vision.md rule 3); party_available reads relationship availability only through Switchboard MCP. Closure: when record_booking creates a trip whose destination and dates fall inside an intention's window, the intention transitions to 'booked' with booked_trip_id set, which is what makes the ledger a lifecycle rather than a wishlist. Insight category 'trip-intention' with a window-closing dedup key. API: GET/POST-free read routes in roster/travel/api/router.py plus a dashboard panel on the Trips tab.
moves.manifesto: roster/travel/MANIFESTO.md — implies an amendment: the manifesto today scopes Travel to 'booking chaos' and reading confirmation email ('Your trips are not complicated; your inboxes are'), which does not authorize a pre-booking planning surface. Amendment text: Travel owns the whole trip lifecycle including intentions that have not yet been booked, holding destination, window, party and budget ceiling as owner-asserted intent — while price discovery, vendor selection and booking execution remain out of scope. Ownership boundaries respected: Finance answers budget, Relationship answers party availability, Lifestyle keeps taste; Travel only asks and records.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy: an intention with a 4-week target window and a 14-day duration yields a ranked list of feasible sub-windows with the constraint that closes each one named. Failure: the calendar module unavailable → condition state='unknown' with evidence.reason, and the intention shows 'feasibility unknown' rather than 'clear'; a delegate_ask to Finance that times out sets budget_available='unknown', never 'available'. Concurrency: conditions are upserted on (intention_id, kind) with an evaluated_at fence; the evaluator is idempotent per cycle. Idempotence: intention_record is keyed on a caller-supplied idempotency title+window so a repeated Telegram message does not create a duplicate intention. Rollback: additive tables and a nightly evaluator; dropping both leaves no residue. Abandonment: an intention whose target window has fully elapsed with no booking auto-transitions to 'abandoned' with a reason, so the ledger cannot silently accumulate stale dreams — and that transition is itself a notice, not a deletion.
moves.verification: (1) Unit tests for the window solver: fully clear window, partially blocked, no feasible window, window shorter than duration. (2) A test that every condition failure path yields 'unknown' with a reason and never a false 'clear' — asserted per condition kind. (3) A test that record_booking of a matching trip flips the intention to 'booked' with booked_trip_id and that a non-matching booking does not. (4) A test that a Finance delegate_ask failure degrades the intention envelope rather than raising. (5) A test that an elapsed window transitions to 'abandoned' exactly once and emits one notice. (6) Live seam: GET /api/travel/intentions returns the ledger with per-condition state and evidence.
moves.slice_plan: Slice 1: the manifesto amendment (this move cannot ship without it) plus trip_intentions + intention_record/list tools + Telegram capture. Slice 2: calendar_clear evaluator and the window solver — the first thing the owner notices. Slice 3: document_ready via move 3's gate, and budget_available via delegate_ask. Slice 4: booking closure, abandonment, party_available, dashboard panel.

moves.title: Travel surface honesty: a degraded envelope on the KPI strip and disclosure of fragmented or duplicated journeys
moves.why: The north star says failure never impersonates health, and the Travel tab does exactly that today: with /api/travel/upcoming?within_days=90 returning 400 (live-confirmed), the KPI strip at ButlerTravelTripsTab.tsx:669 receives no error prop and renders '0 active trips', '0 planned trips', '0 open actions' and '—' next departure while four planned trips and a 16-Oct departure sit in the database — and two panels one row apart disagree, with the authoritative-looking one wrong. moves.behavior_matrix: Happy: endpoint 200 → strip renders real counts, no banner. Failure: endpoint error → each cell renders 'unavailable', the banner names the endpoint and the retry, and no numeral is shown; a screenshot of the failed state is not mistakable for an empty calendar. (2) A component test for the partial case: one unreadable trip, counts disclose the exclusion. (3) An API test that a single unconvertible metadata row yields a degraded envelope naming that trip rather than a 400 for the whole request. (4) An API test for the data_quality flags against the live-shaped DD94XR fixture (two 1-day trips, four legs, one PNR). (5) Live seam: after the fix, /api/travel/upcoming?within_days=90 returns 200 with a degraded or complete envelope — never 400.

Slice 2: server-side per-row degraded envelope on /upcoming and /trips/{id}.
