audits.jarvis_gap: Today the fleet's proactivity is a *sentence pipeline*: deterministic scans propose `insight_candidates` whose payload is `message TEXT NOT NULL` and nothing else (`roster/switchboard/tools/insight/broker.py:85-100`; `roster/switchboard/tools/insight/models.py:31-83`), a broker ranks/dedups/budgets them, and Messenger reads them out. Every consequential clause therefore terminates in prose — the owner is told, then does the work by hand. The substrate for the next step already exists and is unused for this purpose: `park_pending_action` is a single sanctioned choke point any producer can call (`src/butlers/modules/approvals/park.py:32-90`), the decision dossier carries `blast_radius`/`reversibility`, and relationship even manufactures message drafts — but stores them as inert facts whose own endpoint docstring says turning one into a send is something it "does not perform and cannot trigger" (`roster/relationship/api/router.py:3462-3467`; `roster/relationship/tools/reach_out.py:100`). Context is likewise half-wired: the bus knows *when* the owner is unavailable and is read only as a mute button, with the signal's own producer-set end instant (`expires_at` = the meeting's `ends_at`, `src/butlers/jobs/context_producers.py:153`) discarded in favour of a hardcoded `set_at + max_hold` (`broker.py:1081-1086, 1110-1125, 1186-1196`). Honest absence shipped as a primitive but is, on this live instance, 100% unmeasurable and denominates nothing: the only row is `producer:"unknown"` / `producer_unknown` (`GET /api/finance/expected-signals`, live), the ledger is last-write-wins with no `measurability_since` or transition history (`src/butlers/core/expected_signals.py:168-193`), and no read applies a staleness guard to `evaluated_at`. Forward time is the largest hole: `public.owner_conditions` is a level-triggered "is it still true" ledger with no `due_at`, no prerequisite edges, no measurability (`alembic/versions/core/core_184_owner_conditions.py:86-115`), and the only forward-dated mechanism — deadline tasks — judges its day boundary in UTC while the cron pass resolves owner-local time (`src/butlers/core/temporal/deadlines.py:59,139` vs `src/butlers/core/scheduler.py:398,452`) and expires with `logger.info` and nothing else (`scheduler.py:1205-1215`). And the vision's own promise to "automatically reduce frequency when the owner disengages" is honoured by exactly one knob inside one staffer's schema: `insight_engagement` / `attention_daily_rollup` are read nowhere outside `broker.py`, so 200+ scheduled LLM jobs keep firing at full cadence at a disengaged owner.
audits.ideal: A JARVIS-grade proactive layer would treat every proactive utterance as a *door on a prepared consequence*, not a sentence. Each domain scan would produce a typed forward item — an obligation with a due instant in owner-local time, the precondition that unblocks it, the evidence chain behind it, its measurability (present/absent/unmeasurable, inherited from `public.expected_signals`), and, where the act is knowable, an already-prepared executable action parked on the approval spine with its blast radius and reversibility computed — so a morning digest reads "Reply to the landlord drafted · approve to send" and a Wednesday panel reads "Before Thursday: 3 items, 1 blocked on you, 1 unmeasurable." The fleet would carry one shared statistical baseline primitive with an honest denominator (n observations, coverage, robust dispersion) so "unusual for you" is sayable in health, home, education and infra rather than only in finance's bespoke stddev facts. It would ask as well as tell: one typed `owner_questions` lane, one question at a time, each with an answer schema and a deterministic write-back, so the owner's own knowledge becomes an ingestible stream. It would speak at moments derived from the context bus's real end instants rather than hardcoded holds, and it would tell the owner when its senses fail — a sustained `unmeasurable` transition is itself news, with a repair door — while a single fleet-wide engagement state throttles every non-safety producer's cadence and spend when the owner stops looking, with a visible receipt and an explicit resume.
audits.live_verification: Live (READ-ONLY, http://127.0.0.1:42200): `/api/butlers` (all butlers up); `/api/switchboard/insights` → `{"data":[],"meta":{}}` (no live candidates); `/api/system/insights/delivery-state` → `{queued:0, delivered:97, failed:0, last_delivery_at:"2026-09-04T23:52:51Z"}`; `/api/attention/ledger/summary` → 7-day per-butler outcomes (finance 31 delivered/1 deferred, home 18/3 suppressed, chronicler 7/6 deferred, relationship 13, general 7, health 4, decision_review 1, lifestyle 1); `/api/finance/expected-signals` → exactly one signal, `producer:"unknown"`, `measurability:"unmeasurable"`, `unmeasurable_reason:"producer_unknown"`, `available:true`; `/api/health/measurements/expected-signals` → `signals:[]`, `available:true`; `/api/preferences` → `{"data":[]}` (no owner timezone row set); `/api/butlers/travel/schedules` → 18 cron schedules, no deadline task_type surfaced. Statically confirmed (exact decisive mechanism read): deadline UTC-date arithmetic and silent expiry; `find_unfired_threshold` one-per-tick ordering; broker `_CONTEXT_MAX_HOLD` vs `ContextEntry.expires_at`; `insight_candidates` DDL (message-only); `park_pending_action` choke point; `reach_out_draft` single-status dead end; `owner_conditions` DDL; `upsert_expected_signals` last-write-wins; finance-only baselines; `briefing_reads_total` counter-only. Not verified live: deadline behaviour (no deadline tasks exist on this instance), engagement ratchet behaviour over a 14-day window. Docker stack reachable; no Postgres container exposed locally, so all data checks went through the JSON API.

findings.title: Deadline day arithmetic judges the owner's day boundary in UTC while the cron pass is owner-local
findings.evidence: src/butlers/core/temporal/deadlines.py:59 (compute_days_remaining → datetime.now(UTC).date()), :139 (compute_expiry_transition), src/butlers/core/temporal/deadlines_db.py:113; contrast src/butlers/core/scheduler.py:398 (_effective_schedule_timezone) and :452 (_next_run, DST-correct per-timezone)
findings.taxonomy_shape: writer's clock impersonating the world's clock
findings.detail: The whole deadline lane — days_remaining, threshold firing, and expiry/disable — is computed against the server's UTC calendar date. The scheduler deliberately resolves an owner/schedule timezone for cron (`_effective_schedule_timezone`, DST-correct anchoring), and chronicler day-close reuses it, but deadlines never do. Effect: for an owner west of UTC a deadline flips to `expired` and the task is disabled hours before the owner's day ends (America/Los_Angeles: 17:00 the previous local afternoon); east of UTC, 'tomorrow' alerts fire mid-morning of the wrong local day. There is no per-deadline timezone column either, so the concept 'due Thursday' has no owner-local representation anywhere in the system.
findings.failure_scenario: Owner timezone America/Los_Angeles; deadline target_date = 2026-09-05. At 2026-09-06T00:05Z (2026-09-05 17:05 local, owner still at work with the deadline live), compute_expiry_transition returns ('expired', True); scheduler.py:1206-1214 sets deadline_status='expired', enabled=false. The owner's Thursday deadline is retired seven hours before Thursday ends, with no alert.

findings.title: Deadline expiry disables the task with only a log line — the one moment absence matters produces no owner signal
findings.evidence: src/butlers/core/scheduler.py:1205-1215 (UPDATE scheduled_tasks SET deadline_status, enabled=false; then logger.info and `continue`); no notify(), no propose_insight_candidate, no record_attention_event on this path
findings.taxonomy_shape: the last hop has no door
findings.detail: A deadline that passes without ever being marked `completed` is the highest-signal proactive event the system can observe: a tracked obligation went by unhandled. The expiry branch writes state, flips `enabled=false`, logs at INFO, and continues. Nothing reaches the attention ledger, the insight broker, `public.owner_conditions`, or notify(). The row is also now `enabled=false`, so no later pass will ever revisit it. The owner learns nothing, and the fleet's own 'what did I miss' surfaces cannot see it because attention_ledger has no row.
findings.failure_scenario: A 'renew passport' deadline (target_date 2026-09-04, alert_thresholds [{days_before:30},{days_before:7}]) fires its 30-day and 7-day alerts, the owner never acts, and on 2026-09-05 the pass sets status='expired', enabled=false and logs. /api/attention/ledger/summary shows no event; the digest never mentions it; the task is permanently disabled. The passport lapses in silence.

findings.title: After any scheduler gap, superseded deadline thresholds fire in reverse-urgency order, each spending a full LLM session
findings.evidence: src/butlers/core/temporal/deadlines.py:66-89 (find_unfired_threshold returns min(eligible) and only ever one threshold per call); src/butlers/core/scheduler.py:1226-1298 (one dispatch + one fired_thresholds append per task per tick)
findings.taxonomy_shape: staleness wearing current-data authority (obsolete alert impersonates current urgency)
findings.detail: Eligibility is `days_remaining <= threshold.days_before`, unfired thresholds are never marked superseded, and exactly one threshold is fired per tick. After an outage that skips several thresholds, the pass fires the most urgent one first and then, on subsequent ticks, the *less* urgent ones — 'T-30' arriving after 'T-1'. Each firing is a real `dispatch_fn` LLM session (metrics.record_task_dispatched), so a three-threshold gap costs three sessions and produces two owner-visible messages whose framing contradicts reality. Nothing prunes thresholds the clock has already overtaken.
findings.failure_scenario: alert_thresholds [{days_before:30},{days_before:7},{days_before:1}], daemon down for 35 days, target_date 1 day out on recovery. Tick 1 fires days_before=1 (correct, status→escalated). Tick 2 fires days_before=7. Tick 3 fires days_before=30. Owner receives three notifications, two of which announce a week or a month of lead time they no longer have, and three LLM sessions are billed for one real event.

findings.title: The insight broker reads each context signal's producer-set end instant and then discards it for a hardcoded max-hold
findings.evidence: roster/switchboard/tools/insight/broker.py:1081-1086 (_CONTEXT_MAX_HOLD), :1110-1125 (filter and return carry only set_at), :1186-1196 (_compute_catchup_deliver_at = context_signal_set_at + _CONTEXT_MAX_HOLD[signal]); src/butlers/context_bus.py:45 (ContextEntry.expires_at) and src/butlers/jobs/context_producers.py:153 (expires_at = the event's own ends_at), :435 (health producer sets the wake time)
findings.taxonomy_shape: computed-then-discarded value / wrong wake anchor
findings.detail: `get_active_context()` returns ContextEntry rows that already carry the truth: the meeting signal's `expires_at` is the calendar event's own end time, the sleeping signal's is the owner's wake time, the travel signal's is trip end. The broker's suppression filter and its catch-up scheduler use only `set_at` plus a per-type constant. Two symmetric failures follow. (a) Under-hold: a 3-hour meeting stops suppressing at the 2-hour mark, so a routine insight lands mid-meeting the system knows is still running. (b) Over-hold: a 25-minute meeting schedules the catch-up delivery 2 hours after set_at, long after the owner was free — the very latency the catch-up mechanism was built to remove. The correct anchor is min(expires_at, set_at + max_hold), and the data to compute it is already in hand.
findings.failure_scenario: Calendar producer sets signal_type='meeting' at 14:00 with expires_at=14:25 (a 25-minute standup). At 14:05 delivery_cycle finds the signal suppressing, and _compute_catchup_deliver_at schedules the catch-up for 16:00 (14:00 + 2h). The owner is free at 14:25 and gets nothing for 95 minutes. Inverse case: a 14:00-17:30 board meeting; at 16:01 the max-hold has elapsed, the signal no longer suppresses, and the digest is pushed while the owner is still in the room.

findings.title: expected_signals is last-write-wins with no measurability_since or transition history, so 'how long have we been blind' is unanswerable
findings.evidence: src/butlers/core/expected_signals.py:168-193 (ON CONFLICT (signal_key) DO UPDATE SET measurability = EXCLUDED.measurability, ... updated_at = now()); alembic/versions/core/core_210_expected_signals.py; openspec/specs/expected-signals/spec.md ('Expected-signal reads degrade honestly')
findings.taxonomy_shape: NEW: state overwritten in place so the transition — the thing that is actually news — is unobservable
findings.detail: Every evaluation overwrites the row. There is no `measurability_since`, no episode/append history, and no transition hook. Consequences: (1) nobody can detect present→unmeasurable, which is precisely the event worth telling the owner about ('I have stopped being able to see your sleep data'); (2) nobody can say 'unmeasurable for 9 days' vs 'unmeasurable since the last tick'; (3) the spec's promised client message ('signal health is unavailable and nudges are paused') can only ever be instantaneous, so a permanently dead instrument reads identically to a momentary blip. The condition-ledger pattern the repo already hardened for exactly this shape (append-per-episode, first_detected_at, escalation) was not applied here.
findings.failure_scenario: Google Health connector token expires. On the next health job the sleep signal flips present→unmeasurable; the row is overwritten. Six weeks later the owner asks why they got no sleep nudges: the row says measurability='unmeasurable', evaluated_at=now, and nothing anywhere records that the blindness began six weeks ago or that it ever changed state.

findings.title: expected_signals reads apply no staleness guard to evaluated_at, so a stalled detector serves a frozen verdict as current
findings.evidence: roster/finance/api/router.py:186-228 (returns available=true with whatever evaluated_at the row holds; degraded envelope covers only query failure); roster/health/api/router.py same shape; src/butlers/core/expected_signals.py:130-145 (evaluated_at is the detector's own clock)
findings.taxonomy_shape: writer's clock impersonating the world's clock
findings.detail: `evaluated_at` is when the producer job last ran, not when the world was last observed. The read path has a well-built degraded envelope for an unavailable *query* but none for an unavailable *evaluation*: if the finance pattern-recognition job or the health job stops, every row keeps its last verdict and the API keeps answering available=true. A `present` verdict frozen three weeks ago is served with the same authority as one computed a minute ago — exactly the failure mode RFC 0029 exists to prevent, one level up.
findings.failure_scenario: Live now: /api/finance/expected-signals returns evaluated_at 2026-09-05T08:05:55Z, available=true. Disable the finance insight/pattern schedule; a month later the same call still returns available=true with a month-old evaluated_at and the same measurability, and no client field distinguishes it from a fresh evaluation.

findings.title: Live: 100% of this instance's expected signals are unmeasurable via producer_unknown, and no surface denominates that coverage
findings.evidence: live GET http://127.0.0.1:42200/api/finance/expected-signals → 1 signal, producer:"unknown", unmeasurable_reason:"producer_unknown"; GET /api/health/measurements/expected-signals → signals:[]; root cause roster/finance/tools/pattern_recognition.py:379-387 (producer = source.producer if source is not None else "unknown") with roster/finance/tools/expected_signals.py:67-77 (resolve_complete_signal_source fails closed when any contributing row lacks the provenance stamp)
findings.taxonomy_shape: an aggregate that denominates nothing
findings.detail: The honest-absence spine is correct and fails closed as designed, but on the real instance it yields zero measurable signals: recurrence groups built from transactions written before the provenance key existed can never resolve a producer, and there is no backfill or attribution path to repair them. Worse, nothing anywhere reports the coverage — no surface says 'of N expected signals, M are unmeasurable and here is why', so the owner cannot distinguish 'the fleet is watching and saw nothing' from 'the fleet cannot watch at all'. Every consumer therefore silently withholds nudges forever with no visible reason.
findings.failure_scenario: Owner cancels a recurring payment. The finance recurrence signal for that merchant would be `absent` if measurable, but resolve_complete_signal_source returns None on the historical charge set, so the row is permanently `unmeasurable` and no candidate is emitted. The dashboard shows no missing-payment concern and no explanation; the owner reasonably infers everything is fine.

findings.title: Relationship reach-out drafts are a write-only dead end: prepared content with no send door, no expiry, and no lifecycle
findings.evidence: roster/relationship/api/router.py:3451-3480 (POST creates an inert fact; docstring: 'Turning a draft into a sent message is a separate, deliberate act that this endpoint does not perform and cannot trigger'); roster/relationship/tools/reach_out.py:100,124 (metadata status is always DRAFT_STATUS — no 'sent'/'discarded' transition exists anywhere in the repo); frontend/src/pages/EntityDetailPage.tsx:839-848 (list-only rendering)
findings.taxonomy_shape: the last hop has no door
findings.detail: The system already prepares the exact artefact proactive drafting needs — a per-entity message body with an intended channel — and then strands it. There is no approve-and-send verb, no link to `pending_actions`, no expiry, and no discard, so drafts accumulate as permanent facts in the entity graph and slowly pollute recall. Grepping the repo for any `sent` status on this predicate returns nothing.
findings.failure_scenario: Owner (or the relationship butler) drafts 'Hey, been a while — coffee this week?' for a Dunbar-tier-2 contact. The draft renders on the entity page as text. There is no control that sends it, no reminder that it exists, and no expiry; three months later it is still an active fact and the contact is still stale.

findings.title: Briefing reads are observed only as an unlabelled Prometheus counter, so the briefing can never learn its own shape
findings.evidence: src/butlers/api/routers/dashboard_briefing.py:98-99 (briefing_reads_total counter), :896 (briefing_reads_total.inc()); no durable per-section read record anywhere; section producers are fixed functions run_{health,finance,relationship,travel,education,home,lifestyle}_briefing_contribution (src/butlers/jobs/briefing.py:236,392,704,933,1072,1225,1592)
findings.taxonomy_shape: computed-then-discarded value
findings.detail: The one durable signal about what the owner actually cares about — which briefing sections they read, expand, or act on — is incremented into an ops counter with no section label and never persisted. `insight_engagement` measures only whole-digest engagement (any owner message within 60 minutes). So the briefing's section set and ordering are permanently static and the fleet cannot demote a section the owner has never once opened.
findings.failure_scenario: The owner reads the finance and calendar sections every morning and has never expanded the education section in 90 days. briefing_reads_total is at 90; no row anywhere attributes any of those reads to a section; tomorrow's briefing leads with education exactly as it did on day one.

findings.title: Insight candidates are structurally message-only: the delivery contract has no field for a door
findings.evidence: roster/switchboard/tools/insight/broker.py:85-100 (insight_candidates DDL: message TEXT NOT NULL, channel, metadata JSONB — no action/target/door column); alembic/versions/core/core_010_insight_tables.py:118; roster/switchboard/tools/insight/models.py:31-83 (InsightCandidate fields); openspec/specs/insight-delivery/spec.md ('Standalone Delivery' — the message is the payload)
findings.taxonomy_shape: the last hop has no door
findings.detail: Every proactive utterance in the system is typed as prose. The approval spine already has the complementary half — `park_pending_action` (src/butlers/modules/approvals/park.py:32-90) is a single sanctioned choke point that any producer can call with why/evidence/blast_radius/reversibility, and executor.execute_approved_action replays by tool_name+tool_args (src/butlers/modules/approvals/executor.py:155-193) — but no insight producer uses it, and the candidate row has nowhere to reference a parked action even if one existed. The result is that the moment of highest owner attention (the digest) is the moment with the fewest available verbs.
findings.failure_scenario: The relationship scan emits 'You haven't replied to the landlord's lease email (11 days).' The owner reads it on Telegram, has no verb, and must open Gmail, find the thread, and compose — the labour the system exists to absorb. Every one of the 97 delivered insights on this instance had this shape.

moves.title: Prepared Actions: proactive drafts parked on the approval spine and bound to the insight that motivated them
moves.why: vision.md 'What Success Looks Like' — 'the measure is not feature count, it is the amount of mental labor the system reliably absorbs'; architecture.md's daemon-deterministic doctrine (the preparation is a deterministic park, the drafting is one already-budgeted scan session). Today every proactive utterance is prose (broker.py:85-100 insight_candidates DDL, message TEXT only) and the one place the fleet already prepares content strands it with no send door (roster/relationship/api/router.py:3462-3467). Owner-visible payoff within a week: the morning digest and Telegram push stop being a to-do list and become a decision list — 'Reply to the landlord drafted · Approve / Edit / Never', 'Cancel Spotify (unused 94 days) · Approve', 'Move Thursday 15:00 to Friday 11:00 · Approve' — each one already carrying its blast radius, reversibility, and evidence.

Specs touched: module-approvals, insight-delivery, proactive-insight-engine, autonomy-tracker (a prepared action approved N times must feed the same promotion fingerprint).
moves.manifesto: Messenger owns delivery of the door (roster/messenger/MANIFESTO.md 'Outbound delivery ownership'); each domain butler owns preparation within its own manifesto scope. Requires one amendment to roster/relationship/MANIFESTO.md (reach-out drafting moves from an inert fact to a prepared action with a send door) and one to roster/switchboard/MANIFESTO.md SLAs (the insight delivery cycle now carries decision affordances, not only text).
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy: scan prepares draft → park_prepared_action inserts pending_actions(origin='prepared', status='pending', expires_at) → candidate rows with prepared_action_id → broker selects → digest renders door → owner approves → executor replays tool → outcome written to execution_result and decision memory. Failure: (a) preparation succeeds but candidate insert fails → the parked action is orphaned; a nightly sweep expires origin='prepared' rows with no live candidate (never executes them). (b) action already terminal at selection time (expired/denied) → candidate is delivered with the door removed and a factual line ('prepared reply expired'), never with a dead button. (c) executor fails at approve time → existing demotion-suggestion path plus an attention_ledger row. Concurrency: pending_actions.deduplication_key (already supported, park.py:87) keyed on the insight dedup_key gives DB-level one-active-prepared-action-per-concern; two scans racing produce one row. Idempotence: re-running a scan re-derives the same dedup key and no-ops; a re-prepared draft with changed content supersedes (cancel prior pending, insert new) exactly like the deferred-notification supersede rule in time-aware-delivery. Rollback: prepared actions are never auto-executed, so disabling preparation is a config flip; existing rows expire on their own expires_at; the migration's new columns are additive and nullable.
moves.verification: tests/modules/approvals/test_prepared_actions.py — park_prepared_action inserts origin='prepared' AND does not call emit_approval_push (assert on a spy runtime); dedup key collision leaves exactly one active row. tests/switchboard/insight/test_prepared_action_door.py — a candidate whose prepared action is terminal renders without a door and with the honest line; a candidate whose action is live renders the verb set. tests/modules/approvals/test_prepared_execution.py — approve on an origin='prepared' row calls tool_fn with the exact stored args and writes execution_result. S2 insight_candidates columns + broker validation + digest rendering with the door, one producer: relationship reach-out (replacing reach_out_draft). S3 finance subscription-cancellation prepared action (rides the already-shipped cancellation door fields) and email reply preparation in the email-owning butler. moves.title: Forward horizon: give the owner-condition ledger a due instant, a prerequisite, and a measurability — 'what needs doing before Thursday'
moves.why: docs/frontend/purpose-and-single-pane.md's five-second verification and the north star's 'unbroken signal-to-session-to-evidence spine': the fleet has no forward-ordered view at all. public.owner_conditions (alembic/versions/core/core_184_owner_conditions.py:86-115) is level-triggered with first_detected_at/escalation_level and NO due_at, no blocker, no measurability; the only forward mechanism, deadline tasks, is UTC-dated (deadlines.py:59) and expires silently (scheduler.py:1205-1215); calendar_prep precomputes attendee context per event but nothing about unmet preconditions (src/butlers/jobs/calendar_prep.py:1-56). Owner-visible payoff within a week: one keyboard-first 'Before Thursday' panel and one briefing section that says, in owner-local days, every dated obligation across finance/travel/home/health/education, which of them are blocked on the owner, which are blocked on someone else, and which the fleet cannot currently see — replacing seven per-domain notification streams that never sort against each other.
moves.integration_points: EXTEND public.owner_conditions (core migration; backward compat waived) with due_at TIMESTAMPTZ NULL, due_precision TEXT ('instant'|'day'), owner_timezone TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT resolved-owner-tz, blocked_on TEXT ('owner'|'counterparty'|'system'|null), unblocks_via JSONB (typed prepared-action ref or route), expected_signal_key TEXT NULL FK-by-convention to public.expected_signals(signal_key). src/butlers/core/condition_ledger.py + src/butlers/core/owner_conditions.py:reconcile_snapshot — accept and validate the new fields; owner-local day bucketing helper reusing scheduler.py:398 _effective_schedule_timezone (single owner-timezone authority, no new resolver). RETIRE the parallel deadline lane: src/butlers/core/temporal/deadlines.py + deadlines_db.py + scheduler.py _tick_deadline_pass become producers into owner_conditions instead of a second forward mechanism — fixing findings 1/2/3 by construction (owner-local dates, an expiry that reconciles a terminal condition episode that IS an owner-visible event, and thresholds derived from due_at rather than a fired_thresholds bag). API: extend GET /api/system/conditions with horizon=<days>&order=due_at and a degraded envelope; new briefing contribution section. Producers: finance bills/subscriptions, travel document expiry + trip legs, home maintenance, health medication refills, education review-due. Specs: deadline-tracking (rewrite as a producer contract), generalize-owner-condition-ledger (amend), dashboard-overview, cross-butler-briefing-contribution.
moves.manifesto: Switchboard's staffer contract already owns 'shared situational awareness' brokerage and needs a Responsibilities amendment naming the forward horizon as brokered state (roster/switchboard/MANIFESTO.md:15-24). Each domain butler's manifesto already claims its own dated obligations (finance bills, travel documents, home maintenance, health medications) — no domain amendment needed.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy: producer reconciles a complete snapshot with due_at in owner-local terms → horizon read returns items bucketed by owner-local day, ordered by due_at, each with blocked_on and measurability → owner clears one via unblocks_via → next snapshot resolves the episode. Failure: (a) producer job stalls → items keep last_confirmed_at; the read marks any bucket whose producer's last_confirmed_at exceeds its declared cadence as stale-by-producer and refuses to present it as current (this is the guard finding 6 shows is missing today). (b) expected_signal_key resolves to unmeasurable → the item renders as 'cannot verify' and is never rendered as satisfied. (c) due_at in the past and unresolved → a terminal 'missed' episode with an attention_ledger row and a notify — the door finding 2 is missing. Concurrency: the existing per-(source,fingerprint) advisory lock and uq_owner_conditions_active_episode partial unique index already give one active episode per identity; due_at is a column on that episode, so no new contention. Idempotence: reconcile_snapshot is already level-triggered and idempotent; due_at changes update the open episode rather than opening a new one. Rollback: additive nullable columns; the deadline retirement is the only breaking step and is a separate slice with a one-time migration of live deadline rows into owner_conditions.
moves.verification: tests/core/test_owner_conditions_horizon.py — owner-local day bucketing across a DST boundary and across a UTC-vs-local date flip (the exact America/Los_Angeles 17:05-local case in finding 1); an item whose expected_signal_key is unmeasurable never reports satisfied; a past-due unresolved item opens a terminal episode AND writes an attention_ledger row. tests/api/test_system_conditions_horizon.py — horizon ordering, stale-by-producer refusal, degraded envelope on query failure. tests/migrations/test_deadline_to_condition_migration.py — every live deadline row lands as one condition episode with due_at = its target_date at owner-local end-of-day and its fired thresholds preserved as escalation history. moves.slice_plan: S1 columns + condition_ledger/owner_conditions validation + owner-local bucketing helper (no producers, no UI). S2 GET /api/system/conditions horizon params + stale-by-producer guard + degraded envelope. S3 two producers with real live data: finance upcoming bills, travel document expiry. S4 briefing section + 'Before Thursday' panel (Dispatch, j/k, palette verb). S5 retire the deadline lane: migrate rows, make _tick_deadline_pass a producer, delete deadlines.py's UTC date arithmetic, add the missed-deadline notify.

moves.title: One shared baseline primitive with an honest denominator — 'unusual for you' becomes sayable outside finance
moves.why: vision.md non-negotiable #2 (capability that needs core belongs in core) and the north star's 'nothing fabricated / every aggregate denominates something'. Today the only anomaly baseline in the fleet is finance's, computed with plain stddev over a 180-day window, stored as memory facts with predicate='spending_baseline', with no measurability and no coverage denominator (roster/finance/tools/anomaly_detection.py:1-7,29-39,121-165). Health, home energy, education study time, lifestyle playtime and infra latency/spend all have dense time series and can say nothing about them. Owner-visible payoff within a week: 'Your resting HR is 2.6 MAD above your 60-day baseline (n=54 of 60 days observed)' and 'Home energy is 41% above your Tuesday baseline (n=11 Tuesdays)' — statements that carry their own sample size and refuse to speak when the instrument is dead.
moves.integration_points: NEW src/butlers/core/baselines.py + public.metric_baselines (core migration): metric_key, owner_timezone, window_days, bucket ('day'|'dow'|'hour_of_week'), center NUMERIC (median), dispersion NUMERIC (MAD), n_observations INT, n_expected INT, coverage NUMERIC, unit TEXT, expected_signal_key TEXT NULL, computed_at, producer TEXT, producer_endpoint_identity TEXT NULL. Reuses src/butlers/core/expected_signals.py:78 evaluate_expected_signal verbatim for measurability so a baseline built on a dead instrument is unmeasurable, never 'normal'. New core helper score_against_baseline() returning (deviation_in_mad, direction, n, coverage, measurability) — the only sanctioned way to claim an anomaly. RETIRE finance's bespoke path: roster/finance/tools/anomaly_detection.py:121 compute_baselines becomes a thin producer into metric_baselines; predicate='spending_baseline' facts are dropped (backward compat waived). Consumers: roster/health/jobs/health_jobs.py (weight/sleep/resting HR), src/butlers/jobs/home.py energy, education mastery velocity, src/butlers/jobs/spend.py session cost. Insight producers gate on measurability + a minimum coverage. Specs: NEW openspec/specs/metric-baselines; amend finance-anomaly-detection, expected-signals (baselines as a consumer), module-metrics.
moves.manifesto: Serves roster/health, roster/home, roster/finance, roster/education manifestos as a shared instrument — each butler keeps ownership of which metrics matter in its domain and what threshold is worth speaking about. No amendment needed; the primitive is core infrastructure under non-negotiable #2, not a module.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy: producer job computes median/MAD over the owner-local window, writes one row per metric_key+bucket with n/coverage, and evaluates measurability from its own producer identity → consumers score new observations and only propose a candidate above both the deviation and coverage floors. Failure: (a) n < minimum → row written with center/dispersion NULL and a reason; score_against_baseline returns 'insufficient_history' and no claim is made. (b) dispersion = 0 (a perfectly regular series) → deviation is expressed as an absolute delta with an explicit note, never as a divide-by-zero z-score (today's _safe_stddev returns 0.0 and the caller's multiplier comparison silently never fires). (c) producer unmeasurable → the baseline is served as unmeasurable and every consumer withholds. Concurrency: single-writer per metric_key by producer convention plus a keyed upsert (the expected_signals convergence pattern) — concurrent recomputes converge on one complete row, never a partial merge. Idempotence: recompute over the same window and clock yields the same row (the existing as_of parameter keeps bucketing deterministic). Rollback: the table is new; dropping it degrades every consumer to 'no baseline', which is the honest pre-state, not a wrong claim.
moves.verification: tests/core/test_baselines.py — median/MAD against a fixture series; zero-dispersion series produces an absolute-delta claim, not a z-score; n below floor returns insufficient_history and score_against_baseline refuses; a dead producer endpoint makes the baseline unmeasurable (reusing the killed-heartbeat fixture from tests/core/test_expected_signals.py); coverage denominates n_observations/n_expected exactly. tests/contracts/test_no_anomaly_claim_without_baseline.py — a repo-wide check that no insight producer emits an anomaly category without going through score_against_baseline. tests/migrations/test_spending_baseline_retirement.py — finance baselines land in metric_baselines and no predicate='spending_baseline' fact is written. Live seam: after one finance anomaly-insight-scan tick on the dev stack, the health/finance expected-signals endpoints and a new GET /api/system/baselines agree on measurability for the same producer.
moves.slice_plan: S1 table + core/baselines.py + score_against_baseline with the measurability and coverage contract (no producers). S2 re-point finance compute_baselines/anomaly_scan onto it and delete the fact-based path. S3 health producer (weight, sleep duration, resting HR) with dow bucketing — first new owner-visible capability. S4 home energy + education velocity. S5 contract test forbidding baseline-free anomaly claims; retire _safe_stddev/_severity_from_zscore.

moves.title: The fleet asks: one typed owner-question lane with a deterministic answer write-back
moves.why: vision.md 'The owner's health data, relationship context, financial signals and calendar are maintained without manual entry' has an unstated dual — the one data stream no connector can ingest is the owner's own knowledge, and the fleet currently has no way to elicit it. The pattern is already built five times inside one butler as prose insights with no answer channel (roster/relationship/jobs/relationship_jobs.py:2203 pending_actions_curation, :2489 fact_retraction_curation, :3018 entity_dedup_curation, :3551 email_identity_enrichment, :3949 episodic_predicate_curation) and once bespokely in chronicler (GET/POST /api/chronicler/gap-interview/resolve, /api/chronicler/correction-prompts). Distinct from the deferred 'insight feedback verbs' (which rate an insight the fleet produced); this elicits knowledge the fleet lacks. Owner-visible payoff within a week: one question a day, answerable in one tap from Telegram or the dashboard — 'Is finance@acme.com Alice Chen? [Yes / No / Skip]', 'Are these two contacts the same person?', 'Did you take the 20:00 dose?' — each answer landing as a typed fact with owner provenance instead of a message the owner has to compose an answer to and a butler has to re-parse.
moves.integration_points: NEW public.owner_questions (core migration): id, asking_butler, category, dedup_key, question TEXT, answer_schema JSONB (kind: bool|choice|value|date|free_text + choices/unit), why TEXT NOT NULL, evidence JSONB (typed refs, reusing the pending_actions evidence shape), cost_of_not_knowing TEXT, expires_at, status (open|answered|expired|withdrawn), answered_at, answer JSONB, answer_provenance JSONB. NEW public.owner_question_answers is unnecessary — one answer per question, superseding by withdraw+reask. NEW switchboard broker module roster/switchboard/modules/owner_questions_broker.py exposing ask_owner_question / withdraw_owner_question MCP tools (mirrors roster/switchboard/modules/owner_conditions_broker.py exactly) plus a direct-import path for dispatch_mode='job' handlers. Delivery: the broker's existing selection/budget/quiet-hours machinery in roster/switchboard/tools/insight/broker.py — questions compete in the SAME budget as insights (no second unmetered channel; this is the run-09 'one attention budget' discipline honoured, not re-proposed), with a hard cap of one open question at a time. Answer intake: Telegram inline keyboard callback (the callback_query handler that openspec/changes/decision-loop-one-tap-approvals already specifies for approvals — same signed single-purpose token, same owner verification), plus POST /api/owner-questions/{id}/answer for the dashboard. Write-back: the asking butler declares a deterministic writer callback at ask time (predicate + subject) so the answer becomes a fact/row with owner provenance and no second LLM session. RETIRE the five relationship curation insight producers' prose form and chronicler's bespoke correction-prompts endpoint (backward compat waived). Specs: NEW openspec/specs/owner-questions; amend proactive-insight-engine (budget sharing), insight-delivery, module-telegram, relationship-curation, chronicler-api.
moves.manifesto: Switchboard brokers it (needs a Responsibilities amendment for 'owner elicitation brokerage', roster/switchboard/MANIFESTO.md:15-24, exactly parallel to the insight brokerage it already carries). Messenger delivers and collects (no amendment — it is a notify.v1 intent). Each asking butler stays inside its own manifesto's knowledge scope; relationship's curation and chronicler's gap interview are already manifesto-sanctioned.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy: producer calls ask_owner_question with a schema and a writer declaration → broker admits at most one open question, competing in the daily budget → delivered with typed affordances → owner taps → answer validated against answer_schema → writer callback writes the fact deterministically → status answered, an attention_ledger row records the outcome. Failure: (a) answer fails schema validation → rejected with the valid set restated, question stays open (the notify priority-enum pattern). (b) writer callback fails → status stays answered with the answer preserved and a retry episode opened in public.owner_conditions, so the owner's input is never lost even if the write is. (c) expiry with no answer → status expired plus an expired-unanswered count (the honest denominator: the fleet must know how often it asked and got nothing, or it cannot back off). (d) the fact the question was about becomes knowable from a connector before the owner answers → producer withdraws the question and the owner is not asked a question that answered itself. Concurrency: partial unique index on (asking_butler, dedup_key) WHERE status='open' plus a global one-open-question guard enforced in the broker's selection step under its existing advisory lock. Idempotence: re-asking the same dedup_key while open is a no-op; after answered, re-asking requires an explicit reask reason. Rollback: no producer is required to use it; disabling the broker module leaves the fleet exactly as it is today.
moves.verification: tests/switchboard/test_owner_questions_broker.py — one-open-question invariant under concurrent asks; dedup_key no-op; withdraw on connector-derived answer. tests/core/test_owner_question_answer_writeback.py — a bool answer writes the declared fact with owner provenance and no LLM session; a writer failure preserves the answer and opens a retry condition. tests/api/test_owner_questions_api.py — schema validation rejection restates the valid set; expired-unanswered accounting is non-null and denominates asks. tests/switchboard/insight/test_shared_attention_budget.py — a question and an insight compete in one effective_budget and the total delivered never exceeds it. Live seam: POST is out of scope for read-only verification, so verify by GET /api/owner-questions after one relationship curation tick and confirm exactly one open question with a populated answer_schema and why.
moves.slice_plan: S1 table + broker module + ask/withdraw with the one-open-question invariant (no delivery). S2 shared-budget admission in the insight delivery cycle + digest rendering of a question with typed affordances. S3 dashboard answer route + write-back for one producer: relationship email_identity_enrichment (a real live queue). S4 Telegram inline-keyboard intake reusing the approvals callback token. S5 migrate the other four relationship curation producers and chronicler's correction prompts; delete the bespoke chronicler endpoint; add expired-unanswered accounting to the attention surfaces.

moves.title: Sensory outage lane: measurability transitions become an owner-visible event with a repair door and a coverage denominator
moves.why: RFC 0029's whole point is that failure must never impersonate health — but the current implementation makes instrument failure *silent* instead of *false*, which is only half the promise. upsert_expected_signal overwrites measurability in place (src/butlers/core/expected_signals.py:168-193) so the present→unmeasurable transition is unobservable and 'blind since when' is unanswerable; the read paths apply no staleness guard to evaluated_at (roster/finance/api/router.py:186-228); and live, 100% of this instance's expected signals are unmeasurable via producer_unknown with no surface reporting that coverage. Owner-visible payoff within a week: 'The fleet has been unable to see your sleep data for 9 days — Google Health needs reauth [Reconnect]' and one honest coverage line on the fleet board: 'Expected signals: 14 tracked · 9 measurable · 5 blind (3 producer unresolved, 2 connector stale)'. Nudges paused for a fixable reason stop being invisible.
moves.integration_points: EXTEND public.expected_signals (core migration): measurability_since TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL, previous_measurability TEXT NULL, evaluation_cadence_seconds INT NOT NULL (the producer's declared re-evaluation cadence, so a reader can judge whether evaluated_at is fresh enough to be authoritative). src/butlers/core/expected_signals.py:148 upsert_expected_signal — set measurability_since only on an actual state change (CASE in the ON CONFLICT clause, keeping the keyed-upsert convergence property RFC 0029 requires) and return the transition to the caller. NEW producer into public.owner_conditions with source='fleet:sensory-outage' — reuses the shipped condition ledger's open/aging/escalate/auto-resolve machinery verbatim (src/butlers/core/owner_conditions.py) rather than a new lane; opens an episode when a signal has been unmeasurable beyond a grace window, resolves it on recovery, and carries unblocks_via pointing at the exact connector repair route (/api/ingestion/connectors/{type}/{endpoint}/reauth or the finance provenance-backfill route). NEW GET /api/system/expected-signals — fleet-wide roll-up with the denominator (tracked / measurable / absent / unmeasurable-by-reason) and a stale-by-cadence flag per row; the per-butler reads (finance, health) gain the same staleness guard. Frontend: one coverage line on the fleet board plus the standing-conditions panel already renders source-grouped conditions. Specs: amend expected-signals (transition semantics, cadence-bound freshness, coverage read), core-notify (the outage intent), generalize-owner-condition-ledger.
moves.manifesto: No butler owns the fleet's own senses, so this sits with the Switchboard staffer contract and needs one Responsibilities amendment: 'Sensory coverage brokerage — maintain and surface the fleet-wide measurability roll-up and escalate sustained instrument blindness.' Domain butlers remain the producers of their own signals; they gain no new responsibility.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy: signal flips present→unmeasurable; measurability_since is stamped once; the outage producer opens a condition after the grace window; the owner gets one notify with the reason and a repair door; the connector is reauthed; the next evaluation flips back and the condition auto-resolves with recovered_after_s. Failure: (a) the producer job itself stops → rows freeze; the new cadence-bound guard makes every read mark them stale-by-cadence and refuse current-data authority, and a second-order 'evaluator stalled' condition opens (the guard finding 6 shows is entirely absent today). (b) reason is producer_unknown and unfixable by reauth (the live finance case) → the door is the provenance-backfill route, and the condition summary says so instead of offering a reconnect that cannot help. (c) flapping instrument → measurability_since only moves on a real change, and the condition ledger's existing aging/re-escalate semantics already debounce; the owner gets one episode, not one message per flap. Concurrency: the keyed upsert's convergence property is preserved (the CASE is evaluated inside the single ON CONFLICT statement, so concurrent evaluations still leave one complete row, never a partial merge) — this is the exact scenario the expected-signals spec already tests. Idempotence: re-evaluating with an unchanged state touches evaluated_at only; the condition producer is level-triggered and snapshot-complete. Rollback: additive columns with a backfill of measurability_since = updated_at; the outage producer is a schedule that can be disabled, returning to today's silence.
moves.verification: tests/core/test_expected_signals.py (extend) — measurability_since moves only on a state change and is stable across repeated identical evaluations; concurrent upserts converge with a single measurability_since; previous_measurability records the prior state. tests/core/test_sensory_outage_producer.py — a signal unmeasurable past the grace window opens exactly one condition episode with the correct unblocks_via per reason; recovery auto-resolves with recovered_after_s; a flapping signal produces one episode. tests/api/test_expected_signals_staleness.py — a row whose evaluated_at exceeds evaluation_cadence_seconds is flagged stale-by-cadence and is not presented as current; the fleet roll-up's denominator equals the row count and its buckets sum to it. Live seam: GET /api/system/expected-signals against the dev stack must today report tracked=1, measurable=0, unmeasurable=1 with reason producer_unknown — the honest version of what /api/finance/expected-signals currently reports without a denominator.
moves.slice_plan: S1 columns + transition-aware upsert + backfill (no owner-visible change). S2 cadence-bound staleness guard on all expected-signal reads + GET /api/system/expected-signals with the denominator. S3 sensory-outage condition producer with the per-reason repair door. S4 notify on sustained blindness through the existing insight/condition delivery path (shared budget). S5 fleet-board coverage line and a resolution of the live producer_unknown case (finance provenance backfill route).

moves.title: Owner engagement as a fleet-wide signal that actually throttles cadence and spend
moves.why: vision.md 'What Success Looks Like' states the requirement literally — 'Butlers surface timely, relevant insights without being asked — and automatically reduce frequency when the owner disengages' — and it is honoured by exactly one knob inside one staffer's schema: insight verbosity auto-off after 14 days of zero engagement (roster/switchboard/tools/insight/broker.py:653-745). public.insight_engagement and attention_daily_rollup are read nowhere outside broker.py (repo-wide grep), so the scheduler keeps dispatching every prompt-mode LLM task at full cadence at an owner who has stopped looking (src/butlers/core/scheduler.py has no engagement input at all). Owner-visible payoff within a week: a visible fleet posture — 'Engagement: drifting (4 of last 14 days). Non-essential cadence reduced; safety producers unchanged. [Resume full cadence]' — plus a real drop in daily spend during a holiday or a hospital stay, without the owner having to touch a single schedule.
moves.integration_points: NEW public.owner_engagement_state (core migration, singleton like atmosphere_feed_status): state TEXT ('engaged'|'drifting'|'disengaged'), computed_at, window_days, days_engaged INT, days_delivered INT, evidence JSONB, measurability TEXT, owner_override TEXT NULL, override_expires_at. Producer: a deterministic switchboard job reading public.attention_daily_rollup (already the durable, purge-surviving history — broker.py:584-621) plus src/butlers/core/attention_ledger.py:285 record_owner_ingress_rollup, so the state is grounded in the fleet's own delivery/ingress evidence and is `unmeasurable` (never 'disengaged') when the rollup is unavailable or the window has no deliveries to denominate. Consumers: (1) src/butlers/core/scheduler.py cron pass — a per-task cadence class declared in roster/{butler}/butler.toml (safety|routine|discretionary) and a deterministic skip rule (discretionary tasks skip N of M ticks while drifting, all but safety while disengaged), each skip writing a receipt so the reduction is auditable and never looks like a failure to fire. (2) The insight broker's compute_effective_budget (broker.py:407-425) reads the shared state instead of recomputing its own rate. (3) Prepared actions (move 1) hold rather than expire while disengaged. (4) src/butlers/jobs/spend.py surfaces the saved spend. API: GET /api/system/engagement (state + evidence + denominator), POST /api/system/engagement/override (explicit resume, TTL-bounded). Specs: amend proactive-insight-engine (adaptive delivery reads the shared state), core-scheduler (cadence classes and the skip receipt), NEW openspec/specs/owner-engagement-state.
moves.manifesto: Switchboard staffer contract — one Responsibilities amendment ('Owner engagement posture: compute and publish the fleet-wide engagement state'), which is a natural extension of the insight brokerage and eligibility-sweep duties it already owns (roster/switchboard/MANIFESTO.md:15-24, SLAs table). No domain manifesto changes; each butler declares cadence classes for its own schedules, which is operational tuning and belongs in the DB per non-negotiable #5 — so the class lives in runtime_config, seeded from butler.toml.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy: producer computes state from the rollup each day → scheduler's cron pass consults it, skips discretionary ticks per the deterministic rule, writes a skip receipt per skipped tick → broker's budget follows the same state → the dashboard shows the posture and the spend delta → owner returns, engagement recovers, cadence restores automatically. Failure: (a) rollup unavailable or window has zero deliveries → state is unmeasurable and NO throttling is applied (fail open to full cadence: the system must never go quiet because it cannot tell whether the owner is looking). (b) a safety-class producer (backup health, secrets expiry, model breaker, medication) is never throttled regardless of state — enforced by a contract test over the class assignments, not by reviewer diligence. (c) throttled-away work that is genuinely due (a bill deadline) still surfaces because it is a horizon item (move 2) whose due_at is class-independent. Concurrency: singleton row with a keyed upsert; the scheduler reads it once per tick and passes it down, so a mid-tick state change cannot half-apply. Idempotence: the skip rule is a deterministic function of (state, task cadence class, tick index derived from next_run_at) — replaying a tick makes the same decision, and skipped ticks advance next_run_at exactly as a fired tick would, so no backlog accumulates. Rollback: state defaults to 'engaged'; an owner override with a TTL forces full cadence immediately; deleting the table degrades every consumer to today's behaviour.
moves.verification: tests/core/test_owner_engagement_state.py — state derives from attention_daily_rollup with a non-null denominator; zero-delivery window and unavailable rollup both yield unmeasurable, not disengaged. tests/core/test_scheduler_engagement_throttle.py — a discretionary task skips deterministically and writes a receipt; next_run_at advances identically on a skipped and a fired tick (no backlog); a safety-class task fires in every state. tests/contracts/test_cadence_class_coverage.py — every enabled schedule in every roster butler.toml has a declared cadence class, and every schedule whose job is in the safety set is classed safety (the guard that keeps a future schedule from being silently throttled). tests/switchboard/insight/test_budget_reads_shared_state.py — compute_effective_budget's reduction matches the shared state and no longer recomputes a second engagement rate. Live seam: GET /api/system/engagement on the dev stack returns state with days_engaged/days_delivered and, cross-checked against /api/attention/ledger/summary and /api/system/insights/delivery-state (delivered=97), the denominator reconciles.
moves.slice_plan: S1 table + producer + GET /api/system/engagement with the honest denominator and unmeasurable fail-open (read-only, no throttling). S2 re-point the broker's compute_effective_budget onto the shared state and delete its local rate computation. S3 cadence classes in runtime_config seeded from butler.toml + the contract test asserting full coverage and safety-class immunity. S4 scheduler skip rule with per-skip receipts. S5 dashboard posture card with the spend delta and the TTL-bounded resume door.

moves.title: Briefing section attribution: let the briefing learn its own shape from what the owner actually opens
moves.why: docs/frontend/purpose-and-single-pane.md's five-second verification and the design-language rule that the pane must lead with what matters. The briefing's section set and order are hardcoded across seven producer functions (src/butlers/jobs/briefing.py:236,392,704,933,1072,1225,1592) and the only observation of owner reading is an unlabelled Prometheus counter (dashboard_briefing.py:98-99, :896). insight_engagement measures whole-digest engagement only ('any owner message within 60 minutes', openspec/specs/insight-delivery/spec.md), so the fleet cannot tell a section the owner reads daily from one they have never expanded. Owner-visible payoff within a week: the briefing leads with the two sections the owner actually opens, demotes the ones they never do, and says so honestly ('education demoted — not opened in 30 days [restore]') rather than silently reordering.
moves.integration_points: NEW public.briefing_section_engagement (core migration): day (owner-local), section_key, presented BOOLEAN, opened_at TIMESTAMPTZ NULL, acted_at TIMESTAMPTZ NULL, surface TEXT ('dashboard'|'telegram'|'email'). Writers: src/butlers/api/routers/dashboard_briefing.py:896 (replace the bare counter.inc() with a per-section presented write plus an opened write from a section-open read route), and the Messenger digest's per-section link/tap. Reader: a deterministic ordering pass in src/butlers/jobs/briefing.py:1428 collect_briefing_contributions that orders sections by a decayed open rate with an explicit floor (a section is demoted, never dropped — the honest-absence discipline applied to the owner's own attention), and a per-section 'demoted, not opened in N days' line with a restore door. API: GET /api/dashboard/briefing gains section order + demotion reasons; POST /api/dashboard/briefing/sections/{key}/restore. Specs: amend dashboard-briefing, cross-butler-briefing-aggregation, insight-delivery (per-section engagement is distinct from digest engagement).
moves.manifesto: Switchboard aggregates the briefing (roster/switchboard/MANIFESTO.md briefing brokerage) and Messenger delivers it — no amendment needed, since section ordering is presentation of already-contributed content, not a change to any butler's contribution scope. Each domain butler keeps full authority over its own section's content per its manifesto.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy: briefing renders → one presented row per section per day → owner expands two sections → opened_at written → the next ordering pass promotes those two and demotes an unopened one with a visible reason and a restore door. Failure: (a) engagement table unavailable → ordering falls back to the declared static order and the briefing says nothing about adaptation (never silently reorders on missing data). (b) fewer than a minimum number of presented days → no demotion at all (an aggregate that would not denominate makes no claim). (c) a section is empty on a given day → presented=false, so 'never opened' cannot be manufactured by a section the owner was never shown — the exact denominator error this move exists to avoid. Concurrency: upsert on (day, section_key, surface); a double render writes one row. Idempotence: the ordering pass is a pure function of the engagement window and the owner-local day, so two runs produce the same order. Rollback: drop the table and the static declared order resumes; no contribution content changes.
moves.verification: tests/api/test_briefing_section_engagement.py — presented rows are written per rendered section and not for suppressed/empty sections; a double render upserts one row. tests/jobs/test_briefing_section_ordering.py — ordering is deterministic for a fixed window; a section below the open-rate floor is demoted with a reason and never dropped; below the minimum presented days nothing is demoted; an unavailable engagement read falls back to the static order and sets no adaptation claim. Live seam: GET /api/dashboard/briefing on the dev stack returns section_order plus per-section demotion reasons, and the sum of presented rows for a day equals the number of sections that day's response actually rendered.
moves.slice_plan: S1 table + presented/opened writes from the dashboard briefing route, replacing the unlabelled counter (observation only, no behaviour change). S2 GET exposes the raw per-section rates so the owner can see the data before it moves anything. S3 deterministic ordering pass with the floor, the minimum-days guard, and the visible demotion reason + restore door. S4 Messenger digest per-section tap attribution. S5 feed the same signal into the insight broker's category ranking (one attention model, not two).

audits.jarvis_gap: Today the Health butler is a well-built filing cabinet wired to a live sensor stream it cannot read. Perception arrives nightly and richly — live dev stack shows 10 measurement types with data (weight 128, resting_hr 91, hrv 83, breathing_rate 82, spo2 76, active_minutes 71, steps 68, BP systolic/diastolic 3, heart_rate 5) plus real sleep sessions with stage breakdowns, 323 google_health samples and 123 home_assistant samples — and an active, serious cardiac condition on file ("Bicuspid aortic valve disease with severe aortic regurgitation"). Almost none of it becomes perception. All eight vital-sign tools the butler is spec'd to have (`health_sleep_latest/history`, `health_hr_history`, `health_hrv_history`, `health_spo2_history`, `health_breathing_rate_history`, `health_activity_summary`, `health_vo2_max_latest`) compute nothing: each returns a dict whose payload is an English instruction telling the LLM to go call `memory_search` and average things itself (src/butlers/modules/google_health.py:262-520; zero pool reads in any tool body). The two deterministic report tools the weekly-summary prompt is told to use hardcode five measurement types from 2025 and are blind to six of the ten live ones, including a blood-pressure predicate that no writer produces any more (roster/health/tools/reports.py:18). The daily briefing carries missed doses and weight, nothing else (src/butlers/jobs/briefing.py:236-380). The `sleeping` context signal is derived from an owner-declared quiet-hours policy window rather than from the measured sleep sitting in `facts` (src/butlers/jobs/context_producers.py:38-40). Conditions are inert name/status labels that drive no watch, no band, no cadence; the one place the fleet encodes a real care constraint ("obtain cardiology clearance before a treadmill stress test") is free prose in `health.rules`, consulted by nobody at decision time; and the one derived advisory Health does publish, `health.recovery_state`, declares `permitted_subscribers = []` against a bus that rejects any unlisted subscriber — a broadcast into a sealed room. Where the butler does speak, it can fabricate: the refill insight invents a 30-day supply nobody recorded, so a perfectly adherent owner is told at priority 90 that a medication "runs out in 0 day(s)". And the record leaks: every health fact writes to the fleet-shared `public.memory_catalog` at sensitivity 'normal' — live search returns the aortic-valve diagnosis, intimate symptom rows, and a third party's rectal-bleeding note — even though the write-time confidential/pii exclusion has been built and sits unused for exactly this domain.
audits.live_verification: Live (read-only, http://127.0.0.1:42200): GET /api/butlers (health ok, 19 sessions/24h); GET /api/health/measurements/types (10 types, counts and latest_at above); GET /api/health/measurements/sleep/latest (real session with rem/deep/awake/light stages, 355 min); GET /api/health/conditions (1 active: bicuspid aortic valve disease with severe aortic regurgitation); GET /api/health/symptoms (3 rows incl. a "Passive ingestion from chat" flatulence entry and a hedged "not a confirmed self-report" snoring entry); GET /api/health/medications (empty); GET /api/health/measurements/sources (google_health 323 samples last 2026-09-04, home_assistant 123 last 2026-09-05); GET /api/memory/catalog/search?query=aortic+valve+regurgitation and ?query=diarrhea+symptom (returned the health condition fact, the health cardiology-clearance rule, a switchboard medical_condition fact, health symptom facts with confidence 1.0 / sensitivity normal, and relationship's Chloe Wong health_concern about rectal bleeding); GET /api/system/conditions (only infra + no health-sourced owner_conditions). No writes issued. Everything else is source-confirmed by reading the decisive mechanism: google_health module tool bodies, reports.py, health_jobs.py refill/adherence math, diet.py nutrition_summary, memory storage.py catalog sensitivity exclusion, domain_event_contracts.py subscriber gate, context_producers.py, calendar_overlay.py, 002_seed_predicates.py.
audits.ideal: A world-class health butler treats the body as a continuously observed system and itself as the owner's honest witness. Every signal it ingests is rolled up deterministically by the daemon into a dated vitals ledger with per-metric baselines, so "resting HR ran 6 bpm above your 60-day baseline four nights running, and HRV is at its 10th percentile" is a fact the daemon computed, not a number an LLM improvised — and the same rollup feeds the briefing, the weekly summary, the insight scan, the dashboard, and a measured (not policy-guessed) recovery/sleep context signal the rest of the fleet can subscribe to. Conditions and owner goals are standing intents, not labels: each names the metrics it watches, the band that matters, the review cadence, and where the band came from (owner, provider, or default), and every claim the butler makes is anchored to one of them, so nothing is watched for no reason and nothing that matters goes unwatched. Every health fact carries who asserted it and how strongly — device-measured, owner-reported, provider-reported, or inferred from conversation — with a real confidence, so a hedge overheard in chat can never harden into a trend line; and every health fact carries a privacy class, so intimate content is structurally excluded from the fleet-shared catalog while aggregate-safe metrics stay discoverable. When a claim cannot be made honestly the butler says why: a refill estimate exists only when a dispensed quantity was recorded, an adherence rate only over a window the medication actually existed in, a nutrition average only against a stated coverage denominator. The butler's forward face is continuity made operational: an upcoming clinical appointment arrives already prepared — deltas since the last visit, the interval's symptom log, adherence, the owner's accumulated questions, the relevant saved research — on the same prep rail the calendar workspace already reads. And the owner's care constraints leave the health schema as narrow, privacy-minimized verdicts the rest of the fleet must check before proposing anything consequential, so Travel, Lifestyle and General cannot suggest what the owner's cardiologist ruled out, while the diagnosis behind the verdict never crosses the bus. Throughout, it stays a companion and not a doctor: it computes, remembers, and asks better questions; it never diagnoses.

findings.title: All eight vital-sign tools return English instructions instead of data; docstrings and spec present them as computed aggregates
findings.evidence: src/butlers/modules/google_health.py:262-288 (health_sleep_latest returns {"query","predicate","scope","instruction": "Call memory_search with ... Return session_start, duration_minutes, efficiency, stages"}), :289-320 (health_sleep_history: "Compute aggregate: avg_duration_minutes, avg_efficiency, avg_deep_minutes, avg_rem_minutes" as an instruction string), :329-520 (health_hr_history / health_hrv_history / health_spo2_history / health_breathing_rate_history / health_activity_summary / health_vo2_max_latest — same shape; grep -c 'instruction' == 8, and no tool body touches db.pool for a read); openspec/specs/butler-health/spec.md:32 asserts the butler 'SHALL additionally have access to sleep_latest, sleep_history, hr_history, hrv_history, spo2_history, breathing_rate_history, activity_summary, vo2_max_latest'
findings.taxonomy_shape: NEW: tool-as-prompt — a registered MCP tool whose entire return value is a natural-language instruction for the caller to fetch and compute the advertised result itself, so the advertised computation exists nowhere, is untestable, and differs run to run
findings.detail: The doctrine that the daemon is deterministic infrastructure and intelligence lives in sessions (about/heart-and-soul/vision.md rule 4) is inverted here: min/max/avg/'linear trend slope' over the owner's heart-rate history are pushed into the LLM. Consequences compound outward — because no deterministic code path ever computes sleep, HRV, SpO2 or breathing-rate aggregates, nothing else in the fleet can consume them: not the briefing, not the insight scan, not a context signal, not the dashboard. The spec makes the stubs look like a shipped tool inventory, so reconciliation passes. This is the root cause of most of the lens's other gaps.

findings.title: health_summary and trend_report hardcode a five-type measurement vocabulary and are blind to 6 of 10 live types, including a blood-pressure predicate nothing writes any more
findings.evidence: roster/health/tools/reports.py:18 (VALID_MEASUREMENT_TYPES = {weight, blood_pressure, heart_rate, blood_sugar, temperature}), :22-45 (health_summary loops that set), :122 (trend_report loops the same set); live GET /api/health/measurements/types returns active_minutes, blood_pressure_diastolic, blood_pressure_systolic, breathing_rate, heart_rate, hrv, resting_hr, spo2, steps, weight; src/butlers/connectors/home_assistant_wellness.py:76-79 writes blood_pressure_systolic / blood_pressure_diastolic, never blood_pressure; roster/health/butler.toml weekly-health-summary prompt instructs 'Use the health_summary and trend_report tools to compile this data'
findings.taxonomy_shape: NEW: frozen vocabulary — a hardcoded enum silently narrows a live, growing data surface, so the overview tool reports on a subset while presenting itself as the whole
findings.detail: 481 of 570 samples across resting_hr, hrv, spo2, breathing_rate, steps, active_minutes are invisible to the butler's own overview and trend tools, and therefore to the Sunday Telegram summary those tools back. Worse, `measurement_blood_pressure` has no producer (HA wellness fans out to _systolic/_diastolic per its ADR-6 note), so the overview reports BP as absent while three real readings sit in facts — failure impersonating absence.

findings.title: Medication refill insight fabricates a 30-day supply nobody recorded, so a perfectly adherent owner is told at priority 90 that supply runs out in 0 days — on an insight that expires the moment it is created
findings.evidence: roster/health/jobs/health_jobs.py:522-537 (comment 'Without an explicit supply quantity in the schema ... Assume a standard refill is 30 days'), :531-537 (days_consumed = doses_logged / doses_per_day; supply_days = 30; days_remaining = max(0.0, 30 - days_consumed)), :541-546 (days_remaining <= 3 → priority 90), :549-556 (expires_at = depletion_date = now + days_remaining; message 'supply estimated to run out in {days_remaining:.0f} day(s) (~{date})'); window is the last 30 days at :495
findings.taxonomy_shape: 3 (fabricated claim presented as measurement) + NEW: self-expiring alarm — the critical branch sets expires_at to now, so the highest-priority candidate is dead on arrival
findings.detail: For any daily medication logged faithfully for 30+ days, doses_logged/doses_per_day ≈ 30, so days_remaining ≈ 0 → the critical branch fires every scan with a made-up date, and expires_at == now means the insight broker gets a candidate that is already expired. Adherence is punished with a false emergency, and the one genuinely actionable health nudge in the system (a refill door) is the one built entirely on an invented number. Live medications count is currently 0, so this is dormant rather than firing today — but it is the first thing that fires when the owner registers a medication.

findings.title: Three different medication-adherence denominators disagree, under a module that documents itself as the single source of truth
findings.evidence: roster/health/tools/reports.py:180-188 (trend_report: rate = taken / total_logged — always 100% when the owner only logs doses taken); roster/health/api/router.py:806-818 (expected = round(doses_per_day * window) where window is the full requested lookback, never clipped to when the medication fact was created or activated); roster/health/jobs/health_jobs.py:806-812 (expected_doses = doses_per_day * dip window, ratio vs non-skipped doses); roster/health/tools/_medication_utils.py:8-14 ('Having one module ensures that the adherence route and the insight-scan job always agree on the expected-dose denominator (spec requirement: "Shared denominator with insight job")')
findings.taxonomy_shape: NEW: unified helper, divergent denominators — a shared units helper is treated as proof of a shared metric, while the three call sites each pick a different numerator/denominator pair, and one call site was never enrolled at all
findings.detail: The Sunday Telegram summary (trend_report) can report 100% adherence for the same medication and week that the dashboard adherence endpoint reports 40% — and a medication added three days ago is reported at 10% adherence over a 30-day window because the denominator is not clipped to the medication's own existence. Each surface is individually plausible, which is what makes it a trust defect rather than a bug.

findings.title: Every health fact is written to the fleet-shared public.memory_catalog at sensitivity 'normal'; the confidential/pii write-time exclusion built for exactly this case is never invoked by any health write path
findings.evidence: src/butlers/modules/memory/storage.py:61-100 (CATALOG_WRITE_EXCLUDED_SENSITIVITIES = {pii, confidential}; _is_catalog_write_excluded treats NULL as 'normal' → never excluded), :2003 and :2175 (catalog write-behind when enable_shared_catalog and source_schema); src/butlers/modules/memory/__init__.py:250 (enable_shared_catalog default True) with roster/health/butler.toml [modules.memory] setting only `groups`; grep shows the only sensitivity= in all of roster/health/tools/ is wellness_ingest.py:519 and :692, both hardcoding 'normal' — condition_add, symptom_log, measurement_log, meal_log, medication_add and research_save pass none; live GET /api/memory/catalog/search?query=aortic+valve+regurgitation returns source_schema health / sensitivity normal for the diagnosis and for the cardiology-clearance rule, and ?query=diarrhea+symptom returns health symptom facts plus relationship's 'Chloe Wong health_concern: rectal bleeding' at sensitivity normal
findings.taxonomy_shape: 5 (gate exists as metadata, never enforced) — the classification field is honored by the mechanism but never populated by the domain that needs it
findings.detail: The catalog is deliberately fleet-readable ('Fleet-knowledge search across all butlers', src/butlers/api/routers/memory.py:1412) and the dashboard exposes it unauthenticated on the local API. So the owner's cardiac diagnosis, symptom notes naming other people, and a third party's disclosed bleeding are one keyword search away from every butler and every dashboard reader. The manifesto's Agency clause ('You decide what to log, what to share, and what to keep private') has no mechanism behind it.

findings.title: Conversationally inferred symptoms are stored with confidence 1.0 and no assertion provenance; the hedge survives only as prose in notes, while the structured row feeds trends and a fleet advisory
findings.evidence: live GET /api/health/symptoms returns severity 1 'snoring' with notes 'Possible snoring/sleep symptom mention from Telegram chat ... Context suggests a sleep-related issue but not a confirmed self-report' and severity 2 'flatulence' with notes 'Passive ingestion from chat'; live catalog search shows the same symptom facts at confidence 1.0; roster/health/modules/tools.py:203-219 (symptom_log signature: name, severity, condition_id, notes, occurred_at — no confidence, no assertion/source parameter); roster/health/jobs/health_jobs.py:568-586 (symptom-trend query filters only on severity and window, counts every row equally) and :124-152 + :155-203 (compute_recovery_state → health.recovery_state domain event derived from the same rows)
findings.taxonomy_shape: NEW: hedge demoted to prose — uncertainty captured by the writer is stored only in free text while the structured fields carry full authority, so every downstream aggregate reads an inference as a self-report
findings.detail: An overheard 'possible' becomes an equal vote in symptom frequency, in the average-severity line the owner reads on Sunday, and in the depleted/recovering state the domain-event bus is meant to carry to other butlers' scheduling decisions. The manifesto explicitly promises 'no judgment in the butler's memory, only honesty' — honesty here requires the row to know how it learned what it claims.

findings.title: health.recovery_state is published to a sealed room: permitted_subscribers is empty and the bus rejects any subscriber not listed
findings.evidence: roster/health/domain_events.toml:16 (permitted_subscribers = []); src/butlers/core/domain_event_contracts.py:358-359 (if subscriber not in contract.permitted_subscribers: permitted = ', '.join(...) or '(none)' → rejection), :56 ('a subscription request from a butler outside permitted_subscribers is ...'); roster/health/jobs/health_jobs.py:155-203 (_publish_recovery_state_event docstring: 'other butlers (e.g. General/Lifestyle) may subscribe to defer non-essential scheduling while recovery state is depleted'); grep across src/ roster/ finds no consumer of 'health.recovery_state' other than doc mentions
findings.taxonomy_shape: 6 (the last hop has no door) — a producer, a contract, a dedup key and a TTL, all ending at a subscriber list that structurally forbids subscription
findings.detail: The most JARVIS-like thing Health currently does — telling the fleet 'the owner is depleted, defer non-essential load' — cannot reach any butler. The code, the declaration and the test coverage all exist; the one field that makes it consequential is empty, and there is no owner-visible signal that the advisory goes nowhere.

findings.title: The health calendar-overlay contribution reads an 'appointment' predicate that no tool, API, or registry seed ever writes
findings.evidence: src/butlers/jobs/calendar_overlay.py:876-889 (SELECT ... WHERE predicate = 'appointment' AND scope = 'health'), :851-853 (docstring claims the facts table is 'the butler's memory-backed store of record for medications and appointments'); grep for 'appointment' across src/ and roster/ finds only these read sites — no writer; src/butlers/modules/memory/migrations/002_seed_predicates.py:871-990 seeds the health predicates (measurement_*, symptom, took_dose, medication, condition, research) with no 'appointment'; roster/health/AGENTS.md:84 instructs 'Use calendar tools for medical appointments' — i.e. appointments live in Google Calendar, not in facts
findings.taxonomy_shape: NEW: dead read lane — a deterministic producer queries a predicate with no writer, so one of its two advertised lanes is permanently empty while its log line reports 'appointments=0' as though it had looked
findings.detail: The overlay job's appointment_count is structurally always 0; only medication_reminder entries can ever be produced. This matters beyond tidiness because it is the seam where a clinical-appointment lane would naturally live (see the consultation-dossier move) — today the overlay silently promises it.
