moves.why: `roster/chronicler/MANIFESTO.md` states "Episodes overlap freely; your life is not a Gantt chart" and commits to answering retrospective questions — and it is already sitting on the join: live `/api/chronicler/episodes` returns 12,467 episodes spanning `listening_episode`, `play_episode`, `social_episode`, `place_episode`, `movement_episode`, `sleep_episode`, `work`, each with exact or day precision and full source provenance. Nothing computes the overlap. This is the highest emotional value per line of code in the entire lens, and it is one deterministic pass over data that already exists. Owner-visible payoff inside a week: "the album you had on during the dinner at Koya", "the game you played through the week you were sick", "you always put that playlist on when you're moving" — each with both episode rows as doors.
moves.integration_points: New `roster/chronicler/migrations/0xx_episode_cooccurrence.py`: `chronicler.episode_cooccurrence` (episode_a_id, episode_b_id ordered canonically to avoid duplicate pairs, overlap_seconds, containment ∈ {a_in_b,b_in_a,partial}, worst_precision derived from both episodes' `precision`, computed_at), unique on the ordered pair. New deterministic projector in `src/butlers/chronicler/jobs.py` (zero-LLM, Tier-0 per RFC 0014 §D5, same discipline as `src/butlers/chronicler/adapters/owntracks_place_cluster.py`), watermarked like every other adapter. Read surface: `GET /api/chronicler/episodes/{id}/cooccurrence` on the existing `roster/chronicler/api/router.py`. Lifestyle consumes it by storing `context_episode_id` on `lifestyle.taste_signals` (Move 1) at projection time, and a `taste_recall(with_context=true)` verb narrates it. Spec: new requirement in `openspec/specs/chronicler-intent-evidence-activity/spec.md` for co-occurrence semantics, explicitly stating that a `day`-precision episode's overlap is advisory and must be labelled as such.
moves.manifesto: Chronicler (owns the table and the projection — "I do not write another butler's schema", so co-occurrence is Chronicler-owned and Lifestyle reads it over the API/MCP) and Lifestyle ("Taste is autobiography... they're the texture of a life" — the manifesto's opening claim, currently unsupported by any mechanism). No amendment needed; both manifestos already authorize their halves.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: a `listening_episode` overlapping a `social_episode` yields one pair row with overlap seconds and containment; the Lifestyle signal gains a context episode id. Failure/precision honesty: when either episode has `precision = 'day'`, `worst_precision = 'day'` and consumers must render "probably" language — staleness and coarseness never wear exact-boundary authority, which is precisely the `precision` discipline the steam adapter already documents for its day-anchored bars. Missing episode types degrade to no pairs, never fabricated ones. Concurrency: watermarked projector with the ordered-pair unique constraint, so an overlapping run converges. Idempotence: `ON CONFLICT (episode_a_id, episode_b_id) DO UPDATE` on overlap seconds only — a re-run over a widened episode updates rather than duplicates; a Chronicler override that shifts a boundary triggers recomputation of that episode's pairs. Rollback: derived table, additive route, additive nullable column; drop and the system returns to today.
moves.verification: (1) `roster/chronicler/tests/test_episode_cooccurrence.py` — three seeded episodes with known overlaps produce exactly the expected pair set with exact overlap seconds, and a second projector run produces zero new rows. (2) A precision test: a `day`-precision `play_episode` overlapping an `exact` `social_episode` yields `worst_precision = 'day'`, and an API test asserts the response carries that field so no consumer can render it as exact. (3) An override test: correcting an episode boundary through the existing override layer recomputes that episode's pairs and leaves others untouched. (4) A pathological-overlap test (one long `work` episode spanning 40 short episodes) asserting bounded row growth and no O(n²) blowup across the full 12k-episode corpus.
moves.slice_plan: S1 — table, ordered-pair constraint, and the deterministic projector with watermark; verified by the exact-overlap and idempotence tests. S2 — `worst_precision` derivation and the API read surface with the precision field mandatory. S3 — `lifestyle.taste_signals.context_episode_id` populated at projection, plus `taste_recall(with_context=true)`. S4 — surface it: episode-detail cross-links and a "heard during" line on the work detail page. S5 — override-driven recomputation.

moves.title: Verdicts from any channel + the digest of record (retire the panel that can never fill)
moves.why: Two defects and one missing verb are the same hole. There is no rating or annotation verb anywhere in the system — `importance` on a fact is an LLM-assigned memory weight, not the owner's opinion — so the manifesto's core promise ("Tell it you loved a restaurant... and it holds that") is served only by prose. Meanwhile the tab's fourth KPI hard-codes `value="—" / sub="no digest history"` (`ButlerLifestyleTasteTab.tsx:158-163`) and `WeeklyDigestArchivePanel` (:335-340) is a propless function that always renders "No weekly digests yet." occupying a quarter of the layout — decorative chrome presenting as a live-but-empty archive. The weekly digest genuinely goes out (`roster/lifestyle/butler.toml` `weekly-taste-digest` → `notify(channel="telegram")`) and is then unrecoverable. Owner-visible payoff inside a week: say "that was fantastic" or "3/5" or "dnf" in Telegram and it becomes a durable verdict on the work in the owner's own words; and every weekly digest becomes a page the owner can go back to.
moves.integration_points: Verdict capture: `taste_verdict_set(work, verdict_scale, verdict_text)` from Move 1's tool set, reachable from Telegram (via the existing routed-message path), dashboard chat (the shipped propose-then-act confirm loop), and email — with a compact grammar parsed in-session, the raw quote always preserved in `verdict_text` and never normalized away. Digest of record: new `lifestyle.digests` (period_start, period_end, generated_at, body_markdown, cited_signal_ids UUID[], delivery_receipt_id linking the `notify()` outbound) written by the `weekly-taste-digest` schedule before delivery, plus `GET /api/lifestyle/digests` and `/digests/{id}`. Frontend: delete `WeeklyDigestArchivePanel` and the hard-coded KPI cell now, replace with the digest read once S2 lands; the KPI becomes "last digest" with a real timestamp and a door onto the digest page. Spec: amend `openspec/specs/butler-lifestyle/spec.md` § Scheduled Task Shape to require digest persistence before delivery, and add a Verdict Capture requirement stating that the owner's words are preserved verbatim and never superseded destructively.
moves.manifesto: Lifestyle (Memory: "Tell it you loved a restaurant... and it holds that"; Discovery: "a small ritual that makes the week feel examined"). No amendment needed — this is the manifesto's two most concrete promises, currently unimplemented and, in the digest's case, actively misrepresented on screen.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: owner sends "Severance S2 was incredible, 5/5" from any channel → work resolved → one verdict row with scale 5 and the sentence verbatim → the taste ledger and `tonight` immediately weight it. Failure: an unresolvable work returns a clarifying question naming what it could not resolve, never a verdict on a guessed work; an ambiguous scale ("pretty good") stores `verdict_scale = NULL` with the text intact rather than inventing a number. Digest failure: if persistence succeeds and `notify()` fails, the digest row exists with a null delivery receipt and the existing delivery-evidence machinery owns retry — the archive never claims a delivery that did not happen; if persistence fails, delivery is skipped rather than sending an unrecorded digest. Concurrency: verdict supersession is per (work, owner) with `supersedes_id` chaining, so a revised opinion is history, not an overwrite; `lifestyle.digests` unique on (period_start, period_end) so a re-run of the schedule updates one row. Idempotence: verdict capture keyed on the source message id; digest keyed on the period. Rollback: dropping `lifestyle.digests` restores today's Telegram-only behavior; verdict rows are the owner's own data and are exported before any revert.
moves.verification: (1) `roster/lifestyle/tests/test_verdict_capture.py` — three phrasings ("5/5", "loved it", "dnf") produce the expected (scale, text) pairs including the deliberate NULL scale, and a revision produces a chained supersession with both rows readable. (2) A digest test asserting the row is written before the `notify()` call, proved by a failing-notify fixture that still yields a persisted digest with a null receipt. (3) A frontend test asserting the taste tab renders no digest-archive card and no em-dash KPI while no digest data source exists — i.e. the decorative element is gone, not hidden. (4) After S2, a test asserting the "last digest" KPI renders a real timestamp from `/api/lifestyle/digests` and links to the digest page.
moves.slice_plan: S1 — delete the stub archive panel and the hard-coded KPI cell immediately; the layout reflows to what is real (this alone closes finding 7). S2 — `lifestyle.digests` + persist-before-deliver in the weekly schedule + read routes. S3 — `taste_verdict_set` with the multi-channel grammar and the ambiguous-scale NULL branch. S4 — restore the archive panel and a real "last digest" KPI, both ledger-backed with doors. S5 — verdict revision history surfaced on the work detail page.

moves.title: Completion, abandonment, and a priced backlog for games (revive the dead pollers on purpose, and close the spec contradiction)
moves.why: `src/butlers/connectors/steam.py:86-95` drops achievement, library, and friend polling as "noise" against a game-session goal, and `openspec/specs/connector-steam/spec.md` still normatively requires all three — so `_poll_achievements`, `_poll_friends`, `_poll_game_library` (:900-904, :1511) and `build_game_purchase_envelope` (:656) are unreachable code satisfying unimplementable SHALL clauses. Those signals were noise for a session connector and are the two best signals a taste butler could have: achievement progress is the completion/abandonment signal, and library additions are the purchase signal that lets Finance price the backlog. `roster/finance/MANIFESTO.md` promises to know "where your money went"; nothing today connects a game purchase to whether it was ever played. Owner-visible payoff inside a week: "these seven games cost you $214 and you played three of them for under an hour", and "you're 40% through that one and haven't touched it in six weeks".
moves.integration_points: `src/butlers/connectors/steam.py`: re-enable `game_library` (daily) and `achievements` on a **scoped** interval — achievements polled only for apps with a `taste_signals` row in the last 60 days, capped by the existing `_DEFAULT_MAX_TRACKED_GAMES = 10`; add both to `_DEFAULT_INTERVALS` so `_filtered_bufs` (:847) and the spawn loop (:865) cover them. Route unlock and library events into `lifestyle.taste_signals` as `progress`/`completion`/`purchase` (Move 1), explicitly non-interactive per `openspec/specs/butler-lifestyle/spec.md` § "Spotify connector events are non-interactive" — extend that scenario to cover Steam so no unlock ever produces a Telegram message. New `roster/lifestyle/tools/backlog.py`: `taste_backlog()` returning bought-not-played, started-not-finished, and last-touched, each with the purchase evidence; the price comes from Finance over the Switchboard (`openspec/specs/cross-butler-delegation/spec.md`), never a cross-schema read. Spec surgery: rewrite `openspec/specs/connector-steam/spec.md` § Delta Detection so the achievement/library/friend scenarios state the real scoped behavior and the friend-list scenario is removed rather than left unsatisfiable.
moves.manifesto: Lifestyle (Pattern; "the show you watched three times" / "the game you've been playing") and Finance ("we record it, and we remember it... where your money went"). No amendment: both promises exist. The Lifestyle spec's non-interactive-connector-events requirement needs extending from Spotify to Steam, which is a spec amendment, not a manifesto one.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: an unlock delta produces one `progress` signal with the unlock timestamp; a new owned app produces one `purchase` signal; `taste_backlog` joins those against playtime and Finance's transaction to price it. Failure: Steam privacy settings hiding achievements returns the existing `_privacy_error` path and the poller marks that app unmeasurable rather than reporting zero progress — a private profile must not read as "never played". Finance unreachable yields backlog rows with `price = null` and a degraded envelope naming the missing input, never a fabricated total or a mixed-currency sum (the currency-honest aggregate discipline already shipped for Finance applies here). Concurrency: per-app poll state in `connectors.steam_cursors` as today; independent per-data-type backoff already exists (:865-880). Idempotence: unlock signals keyed `steam:<steamid>:<app>:<achievement>`; library signals keyed `steam:purchase:<steamid>:<app>` — the format `build_game_purchase_envelope` (:667) already defines. First library poll establishes the baseline without emitting, per the existing spec scenario, so no purchase flood. Rollback: remove the two keys from `_DEFAULT_INTERVALS` and the pollers go dormant again with no data loss.
moves.verification: (1) `tests/connectors/test_steam_scoped_pollers.py` — a fixture with 25 recently-signalled apps spawns achievement polling for exactly 10, and an app with no recent taste signal is not polled; asserted on issued API calls, not on config. (2) A privacy test asserting a hidden-achievements response marks the app unmeasurable and emits no zero-progress signal. (3) A baseline test asserting the first `game_library` poll emits zero purchase events and the second emits exactly one per genuinely new app. (4) `roster/lifestyle/tests/test_taste_backlog.py` — a seeded purchase with 12 minutes of playtime appears in bought-not-played with the Finance price, and with `price = null` plus a degraded envelope when the delegation is stubbed unavailable. (5) A non-interactivity test asserting no unlock or purchase event produces an outbound notify.
moves.slice_plan: S1 — spec surgery on `openspec/specs/connector-steam/spec.md` so the normative text matches intended behavior and the unsatisfiable friend-list scenario is removed (closes finding 8 before any code moves). S2 — re-enable `game_library` daily with the baseline-suppression proof; purchases become `taste_signals`. S3 — scoped achievement polling gated on recent taste signals, with the unmeasurable branch. S4 — `taste_backlog` read verb, Finance price via delegation with the degraded envelope. S5 — a backlog block on the Lifestyle dashboard surface from Move 1.

audits.live_verification: Dev stack UP and used read-side throughout. Live-confirmed via JSON API (http://127.0.0.1:42200): /api/butlers, /api/spend/summary?period=today|7d|30d, /api/spend/daily?period=month, /api/spend/breakdown, /api/spend/by-schedule, /api/spend/rules, /api/settings/models, /api/butlers/{name}/mcp/tools. audits.jarvis_gap: Today the fleet buys ~140.0M prompt tokens a week to emit 743,872 output tokens — a 188:1 ratio — and its own cost surface reports 39.9M of them. The four token buckets on `public.token_usage_ledger` are priced correctly and then thrown away at the API boundary (`spend.py:279`, `spend.py:834` destructure `_, _`), so $28.31 of a ~$54.19 weekly bill (52.2%) arrives on the Spend page with no row, no rate, and no name. Nothing in the system reasons about what the prompt is *made of*: `_compose_system_prompt` (`spawner_context.py:137-146`) claims a layering "stable for token-cache efficiency" and then places the per-spawn context-bus preamble (:141) above the settings-derived routing instructions (:143), which on a longest-common-prefix cache poisons every byte that follows; the routing score's cost term is a fictional 2000/500-token profile (`model_routing.py:689-690`) while a real per-model profile sits unread in the ledger; and the measured consequence is a 49.2% cache-hit rate on the highest-volume model (qwen3.7-plus, 615 calls, 28.7M uncached) against 97.0% on gpt-5.6-sol and 76.1% on gpt-5.6-luna in the same fleet. Meanwhile the one surface that should be pointing the owner at this — /api/spend/by-schedule — ranks a schedule that was *deleted from butler.toml and is asserted-absent by a test* at #1 with a $496.20/month forecast, because `schedule_costs` joins `scheduled_tasks` with no `st.enabled` filter (`sessions.py:997`) and the endpoint sorts by `projected_monthly_usd` (`spend.py:1424`). The cost spine is not merely uninstrumented; its loudest number is a ghost, and that is very likely why the real economics have never been worked.
audits.ideal: A JARVIS-grade inference economy treats the prompt, not the answer, as the product being purchased, and can say in one line what each layer of it cost and what it bought. Every spawn records — prompt-free, as digests and integers alongside the tokens it already logs — the size of each system-prompt layer, the size of the tool projection, a digest of the stable prefix head, and then the realized cached/uncached split the provider reported for that exact prefix; from that single joined row the fleet derives a true per-(butler, tier) token profile that replaces the synthetic cost term in routing, a per-model cache-hit rate the owner can read, and a yield figure for every injected layer. Composition is ordered by monotonically increasing volatility so that the static instruction body and the ~25k-token tool projection sit inside one long cacheable prefix and only the per-request tail is ever re-bought; the ordering is normative in `core-spawner`, locked by an invariant test, and switchable in one auditable row so the change can be measured against its own before-baseline rather than asserted. The Spend page shows four buckets, not two, names any model whose cached tokens are billed at the full input rate because no discount is configured, forecasts only schedules that are live, and marks locally-served inference as local rather than as metered-and-free. Capabilities the receipt advertises are either reachable by some enabled entry or shown as unmeetable: `session_resume` is either proven with hit/miss telemetry or retired, never left as a silent preference no catalog row can satisfy. Nothing here classifies a prompt to pick a model — every input is a measured integer or a trigger-derived scalar, so the daemon stays deterministic infrastructure while becoming, for the first time, an instrument that can see its own largest line item.

moves.title: Slice 2 — Volatility-ordered prompt prefix, switched in one auditable row and judged against its own before-baseline
moves.why: architecture.md's connectors-as-cost-boundary doctrine says the expensive thing is crossing a paid boundary; the fleet crosses it 140.0M tokens a week and half of that crossing is already discounted 10x by provider prefix caching, so prefix length is now a first-class cost variable that nothing in the codebase owns. `_compose_system_prompt` asserts it is ordered 'stable for token-cache efficiency' (spawner_context.py:125-129) and then puts the most volatile layer above two more stable ones (:141 vs :143). Closing qwen to luna's rate moves 15.2M tokens/week from $0.40/1M to $0.04/1M = $5.47/week = $23.75/month = $285/year; closing it to sol's rate = $42/month = $504/year. Against a measured ~$235/month fleet bill that is a 10-18% cut, taken from the largest and least-examined line item.
moves.manifesto: Doctrine non-negotiable 4 (vision.md:80-84): nothing here reads a prompt or classifies a task — layer order is a static policy, the digest is a hash, the decision to flip is the owner's. The owner payoff is the sentence, not just the dollar: 'you paid N tokens for Fleet Knowledge last month; it was referenced in X% of sessions' — and a budget the owner can shrink where X is zero, with the before/after on the page. audits.jarvis_gap: Today the fleet has three unconnected write-only knowledge stores and no capture verb. General is not a second brain; it is the switchboard's landfill — 399 items in 121 collections (3.3 items each), invented one free-text collection name at a time by whichever ephemeral session happened to run (roster/general/tools/items.py:35-44), and dominated by machine "informational, no action taken" residue rather than owner thought; the owner's actual brain inside it is `career_decisions` (6), `note` (5), `freeform-thought` (2). Nothing captured there can be found by keyword (item_search is JSONB containment only, unbounded, roster/general/tools/items.py:106-155) and nothing is registered in the shared discovery catalog, so every other butler is blind to it. Education's entire mastery apparatus — 571 lines of SM-2, review cron, quiz evaluation — has scheduled zero cards in its lifetime because the only door into it is a full curriculum flow, and the one curriculum ever requested settled "completed" against a mind map with no nodes and no root. Chronicler cannot accept owner testimony at all: corrections require an episode a machine adapter already witnessed, so a decision made on a walk simply never happened. Owner-authored behavioural rules are born `candidate` and stay there forever (226/226, applied_count 0), and every one is injected into every session prompt stamped "maturity: candidate, effectiveness: 0.00" — the system teaches its own agents to distrust everything it learned. And the sovereignty promise is hollow: the export the dashboard labels "all data" covers three memory tables plus audit and config, and queries a `memory` schema that does not exist in production. The ideal is the opposite of all six: one verb, typed routing, a receipt, one searchable spine, review for anything, owner testimony admissible, and an export that names what it contains.
audits.ideal: One capture verb from any channel — text, photo, screenshot, URL, voice — lands in an append-only `public.captures` ledger before anything else happens, and returns a receipt the owner can see: what was captured, which typed home it was routed to (note, fact, preference, review card, task, decision, chronicle), the exact row id it became, or `held`/`refused` with a reason. Nothing is ever "saved" without a durable row id behind that word. The typed homes are the existing specialists — General for freeform shape, memory for facts and preferences, Education for retrieval practice over any anchored knowledge object, Relationship for commitments, Chronicler for owner-witnessed time as a first-class source adapter with `precision=owner_stated` — and General names what it refuses to hold, routing bank alerts to Finance, message interactions to Relationship, listening to Lifestyle, presence to Home instead of hoarding shadow copies. Collection names come from a server-derived vocabulary with aliases and declared shapes, not from an LLM's spelling that day; unknown names are refused unless the owner declares one. Every capture is full-text and semantically searchable, carries a row in the shared discovery catalog so the whole fleet can find it, and photos and voice notes carry extracted text with extraction provenance so they are findable at all. Decisions are a typed object with the reasoning, the falsifiable expectation, and a revisit date that becomes attention when it arrives. What the owner already knows resurfaces at the moment of relevance — when a calendar event, a thread, or a chat turn resolves to the same entity — as one bounded, cited recall card on the existing insight spine, not as invisible prompt stuffing. And the whole brain exports as a round-trippable archive with a manifest that names every table, every row count, and every table it could not reach, so the sovereignty claim is measured rather than asserted.

findings.title: `item_create` auto-vivifies a collection from any free string; the second brain has fragmented into 121 collections for 399 items

findings.taxonomy_shape: NEW: vocabulary-free write authority — a durable namespace whose keys are minted by ephemeral LLM sessions with no catalog read, no canonicalization, and no refusal, so the store fragments faster than it accumulates
findings.detail: There is no vocabulary, alias table, trigram match, or shape contract behind `collection_name`. Every session invents a name. Live: 121 collections / 399 items (mean 3.3), 112 collections hold 1-10 items, 3 hold zero, and ~40 names are hyphen/underscore/singular/plural variants of another live name (email-records 20 vs email_records 16 is the worst — the same concept split across two collections, each with a plausible claim to be the real one). The owner's own freeform thought is scattered across `note`(5), `freeform-thought`(2), `home-note`(2), `telegram-note`(6), `inbox`(4), `telegram-inbox`(1). No search that names one collection can be trusted to be complete, which voids the manifesto's Reliability promise (roster/general/MANIFESTO.md:13, 'Once you tell us something, it's safe... We never lose what matters').

findings.title: General's only search is JSONB containment — the manifesto promises keyword search that does not exist, and the query is unbounded
findings.evidence: roster/general/tools/items.py:106-155 (conditions are `c.name = $n`, `e.data @> $n`, `e.tags @> $n`; no tsvector, no ILIKE, no LIMIT, no cursor); roster/general/MANIFESTO.md:19 ('Find what you need: Search by keywords, dates, or the shape of the data itself'); live /api/general/entities showing free-prose values under ad-hoc keys (`notes`, `summary`, `relevance_assessment`)
findings.taxonomy_shape: NEW: promise-without-mechanism — a manifesto clause (binding per vision.md rule 6) whose named capability has no implementation anywhere in the tool surface
findings.detail: `item_search` can only match exact JSONB subtrees. The captured content is prose living under keys the writer invented, so the owner must already know both the key and the exact value to retrieve anything. There is no date filter either, despite the manifesto naming one. Compounding it: the SELECT has no LIMIT and no pagination, so the tool's cost grows with the store it is supposed to make navigable.

So a note the owner captured under General is unreachable from Health, Finance, Relationship, or the dashboard chat — the catch-all butler is the one butler whose knowledge the fleet cannot discover, which is the inverse of what a catch-all is for.

findings.evidence: src/butlers/modules/memory/tools/writing.py:521-534 (memory_store_rule births candidates only; no maturity parameter); src/butlers/modules/memory/storage.py:2760-2827 (candidate->established requires success_count>=5 via mark_helpful); src/butlers/modules/memory/tools/feedback.py:31-56 (the only increment path); src/butlers/modules/memory/tools/context.py:186-190 (_format_rule_line prints maturity + effectiveness into every session prompt); src/butlers/modules/memory/migrations/006_drop_rule_applications.py:1-21 (the application-audit table was dropped as write-orphaned); no skill, prompt, or doc instructs mark_helpful (grep across *.md finds only the tool table in docs/modules/memory.md:82-83); live /api/memory/stats + /api/memory/rules

The frontend RulesRegister sorts and filters by a maturity dimension that has exactly one value (frontend/src/components/memory/RulesRegister.tsx:87-95, 58-59), and memory_context ranks rules by that same dead dimension (_MATURITY_RANK, context.py:27-32). Secondary defect in the same evidence: the consolidated rules are fleet engineering lessons (Codex failover classification, teaching_flow_advance call sequencing) written into a domain butler's life-memory under scope 'travel' because a travel session happened to hit the error — the fleet's operating knowledge has no home, so it contaminates owner knowledge with a misattributed scope.

findings.taxonomy_shape: 1 (aggregate that denominates nothing) + NEW: verification at a fabricated seam — the integration test creates the schema layout the code assumes instead of the layout production has, so the check is green precisely where the code is dead
findings.detail: Three compounding defects on the one surface that backs vision.md non-negotiable 1 (sovereignty). (a) Scope: 'all'/'full' is memory facts/rules/episodes + audit_log + three config tables. It contains no general.collections or collection_items, no education mind maps or quiz history, no chronicler episodes/point_events/overrides, no relationship contacts or entity_facts, no finance, health, home, no public.entities, entity_graph_edges, fleet_cases, or captures. The owner is told 'all data'. (b) Binding: there is no `memory` schema — the memory chain migrates into each butler's own schema — so every memory query resolves against nothing, and since the fetch is fail-fast, scopes memory/all/full return HTTP 500 rather than a partial archive. (c) The pool is switchboard's, whose role sees only the switchboard schema plus public, so even a correctly-qualified per-butler query would be denied from there. The single real-Postgres test asserts the qualification is present while itself provisioning the schema production lacks, which is why (b) has survived.

findings.title: General is the routing landfill: the catch-all butler hoards shadow copies of data four specialists own, and never refuses anything
