findings.taxonomy_shape: NEW: refusal-free catch-all — a store with no ownership boundary becomes the default sink for every un-actionable routed event, so the owner's own knowledge is buried under machine residue and specialist schemas silently lose their canonical claim
findings.detail: The largest live collection is `music-history` (22) — Lifestyle's domain. Bank alerts, message interactions, presence pings, and HA device status all have specialist owners with real schemas, yet General holds partial, unnormalized, unlinked copies because 'no judgment, no limitations' is read by every routing session as 'dump it here'. The result is two harms at once: the owner's actual second brain (career_decisions 6, note 5, freeform-thought 2) is a rounding error inside 399 rows of machine noise, and the specialists' schemas are missing evidence that exists in the fleet. Vision.md non-negotiable 6 makes the manifesto binding, so the fix is an amendment plus an ownership map, not a convention.

moves.title: `capture()` — one owner capture verb, typed routing, and a receipt that names the row it became
moves.why: vision.md 'What Success Looks Like': 'The owner sends a message from any channel and the right butler handles it without manual routing.' Today there is no capture verb anywhere in core (grep: only capture_tool_call, capture_commitment, capture_to_dead_letter) and General's item_create is the de-facto capture, requiring the session to invent a collection name (roster/general/tools/items.py:35-44). Owner-visible payoff within a week: send a thought, a link, a photo, or a voice note from any channel and get back one line — 'captured -> note in general/reading (id 4f2…)' or 'held: I could not decide where this belongs, tell me' — instead of the current silence over a store that fragments per write. The north star's unbroken signal-to-session-to-evidence spine starts at capture; right now capture has no signal row at all.
moves.manifesto: Serves roster/general/MANIFESTO.md:9-21 (the second-brain promise) and vision.md non-negotiable 7 (transport stays in connectors — capture is channel-blind). Implies a General manifesto amendment: General becomes the *default* home and the router of last resort, and gains a 'What We Refuse to Hold' section naming specialist-owned kinds. Also a small Switchboard classification amendment: `capture` joins the classification vocabulary at roster/switchboard/tools/routing/classify.py as a first-class outcome distinct from 'informational, no action taken'.
moves.integration_points: New core group `capture` and new module src/butlers/core_tools/_captures.py registered via register_all_core_tools (src/butlers/daemon.py:1335-1397, src/butlers/core_tools/__init__.py). New migration alembic/versions/core/core_220_captures.py creating public.captures (capture_id UUID pk, received_at, channel, source_request_id, raw_text, attachment_refs JSONB (s3:// BlobRefs, see src/butlers/tools/attachments.py), extracted_text, extraction_source, owner_stated BOOL, routed_kind TEXT CHECK (note|fact|preference|card|task|decision|chronicle|refused|held), target_schema, target_table, target_row_id, receipt_state TEXT CHECK (held|routed|refused), refusal_reason, routed_at, session_id) plus a partial index on receipt_state='held'. Read surface src/butlers/api/routers/captures.py -> /api/captures (cursor pagination per docs/api_and_protocols/response-conventions.md) and /api/captures/{id}. Typed routing calls existing verbs only: roster/general/tools/items.py item_create, src/butlers/modules/memory/tools/writing.py memory_store_fact, .../preferences.py set_preference, roster/relationship/tools/commitments.py capture_commitment, plus the two new homes from moves 4 and 5. Spec: new openspec/specs/owner-capture/spec.md; amend openspec/specs/butler-general/spec.md tool inventory.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: capture() writes a `held` row synchronously and returns capture_id before any routing runs; the routing session then sets routed_kind/target_*/receipt_state='routed' in one UPDATE and the owner receipt cites the target row id. Failure: routing session dies -> the row stays `held`, surfaces on /api/captures?state=held, and nothing was lost or claimed (contrast today, where a dead session loses the thought entirely). Target write fails -> receipt_state stays `held` with refusal_reason='target_write_failed:<detail>'; never 'routed' without a row id (the education-003 and curriculum-completion class of defect). Concurrency: two channels capturing the same content produce two rows — capture is a ledger, not a dedupe engine; dedupe is a later reconciliation proposal, never a silent drop. Idempotence: capture() accepts an optional `mutation_id` UUID derived from the originating MCP request exactly as roster/general/modules/tools.py:24-38 does for DND, uniquely indexed, so a transport retry returns the same capture_id. Rollback: routing is additive — un-route by setting receipt_state='held' and nulling target_*; the created target row is retired by its own butler's verb, and the capture row is never deleted.
moves.verification: tests/integration/test_capture_ledger_real_pg.py against a real migrated DB: (1) capture() with a fabricated target write that raises leaves receipt_state='held' with a refusal_reason and no target_row_id — asserts 'routed' is unreachable without a row id; (2) two concurrent capture() calls with the same mutation_id yield one row (unique index enforced at the backend, not mocked); (3) a routed capture's target_row_id actually SELECTs in its named target_schema.target_table (proves the receipt is not a label). tests/api/test_captures_router.py asserts /api/captures?state=held returns the orphan and the degraded envelope is used when a butler pool is missing. Frontend: a capture-inbox lane test asserting a `held` capture renders as held, never as saved.
moves.slice_plan: S1 migration + public.captures + capture() writing `held` rows only, with the receipt returning capture_id and state (immediately useful: nothing is ever lost). S2 typed routing to the three homes that already exist (note/fact/preference) with the target_row_id contract and the /api/captures read surface. S3 Switchboard `capture` classification + Telegram/dashboard entry points so any channel reaches it. S4 attachment + extracted_text path (photo/screenshot/voice) with extraction provenance. S5 the held-capture lane on Dispatch with keyboard verbs to route or refuse.

moves.title: Collection vocabulary authority + ownership refusal map — end the 121-collection rot and stop General hoarding specialist data
moves.why: Live: 121 collections for 399 items with ~40 near-duplicate names, and the largest is `music-history` (22) which Lifestyle owns. roster/general/tools/items.py:35-44 mints a durable namespace key from any string an ephemeral session types, which directly voids the manifesto's Reliability promise (roster/general/MANIFESTO.md:13) — a search that names one collection can never be known to be complete. This is the same defect class the fleet already solved for memory with server-derived catalog read authority (ledger #1); General never got it. Owner-visible payoff in a week: `email-records` and `email_records` are one collection, a search over 'notes' returns all of the owner's notes, and a bank alert lands in Finance where the owner can act on it instead of in a General bag nobody reads.
moves.manifesto: Requires a roster/general/MANIFESTO.md amendment. 'No judgment, no limitations' (line 11) must narrow to 'no judgment about shape; a firm boundary about ownership', and 'Organization' (line 13) must acknowledge a canonical vocabulary rather than unlimited free naming. The ownership map serves the *other* butlers' manifestos — Finance, Lifestyle, Relationship, Home each claim these kinds — and vision.md non-negotiable 6, which makes those claims binding.
moves.integration_points: New migration roster/general/migrations/003_collection_vocabulary.py: general.collection_vocabulary (canonical_name PK, description NOT NULL, shape JSONB key contract, owner_declared BOOL, created_at), general.collection_aliases (alias PK, canonical_name FK), and a `merged_into` column on general.collections so consolidation is additive and reversible (never DROP — matches chronicler's corrections doctrine). item_create (roster/general/tools/items.py) resolves collection_name: exact -> alias -> pg_trgm nearest above threshold (needs the trgm index the GIN data index does not provide) -> refuse with the three nearest candidates and the `collection_declare` verb to use instead. New core-side ownership map in src/butlers/core_tools/_captures.py: kind/tag patterns -> owning butler (bank/card alert -> finance, whatsapp|telegram|whatsapp_user_client interaction -> relationship, listening/track -> lifestyle, device_status|presence|owntracks -> home), consulted by capture() before General is offered. New API /api/general/vocabulary (read) and /api/general/collections/{id}/merge-proposal (owner-gated). Spec: amend openspec/specs/butler-general/spec.md 'General Butler Tool Surface' and add a 'Collection Vocabulary Authority' requirement.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: item_create('email_records') resolves through the alias table to canonical `email-records` and the item joins the 20 already there. Failure: an unrecognized name with no near match raises with the nearest candidates plus the explicit declare verb — the session cannot create a namespace key by accident. Refusal: item_create for a bank alert returns a typed refusal naming Finance and the tool to use, and capture() routes there instead. Concurrency: two sessions declaring the same canonical name race safely on the PK with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING; two items racing into a new alias both resolve to one canonical row. Idempotence: alias resolution is a pure function of the vocabulary tables, so a retried item_create with the same mutation_id is a no-op. Rollback: consolidation sets merged_into and repoints collection_id; the inverse UPDATE restores the split, and no row is deleted — an owner who disagrees with a merge can undo it. Migration of the live 121: generate merge proposals, never auto-apply; the owner approves each cluster.
moves.verification: roster/general/tests/test_collection_vocabulary.py: item_create with an off-by-punctuation name lands in the canonical collection (not a new one); an unknown name raises and creates zero rows in collections (assert the count, since today's bug is exactly a silent create); a declared collection with no shape is rejected. tests/integration/test_general_vocabulary_real_pg.py against real Postgres for the trigram threshold and the ON CONFLICT race (two concurrent declares -> one row). roster/general/tests/test_ownership_refusal.py: a bank-alert payload is refused with Finance named, and the refusal text names an actual Finance tool that exists. A repo guard test asserting no live collection name has both a hyphen and underscore variant, so the rot cannot silently return.
moves.slice_plan: S1 vocabulary + alias tables seeded from the live 121 with a generated canonical/alias mapping, read-only (nothing enforced yet) plus /api/general/vocabulary so the owner can see the mess. S2 item_create resolves through aliases (fixes new writes immediately, no data moved). S3 refusal for unknown names + collection_declare. S4 merge proposals + owner approval + merged_into repointing of the live duplicates. S5 the ownership refusal map wired into capture().

moves.title: Retrieval that works: full-text + semantic recall over captures, and catalog membership so the fleet can find them
moves.why: roster/general/MANIFESTO.md:19 promises keyword and date search; roster/general/tools/items.py:106-155 implements neither, has no LIMIT, and cannot match prose. And nothing General holds is registered in public.memory_catalog (live: catalog search returns only source_table=facts), so memory_context's Fleet Knowledge section (src/butlers/modules/memory/tools/context.py:99-132) is structurally blind to the second brain. Distinct from the ledger's conversation_recall + message FTS (PR #4012), which indexes *messages*; this indexes *captures* and joins them to the shared discovery catalog. Owner-visible payoff in a week: 'what was that thing about the structured note' returns the captured item, from any butler, including the screenshot whose text was extracted at capture time.
moves.manifesto: Serves roster/general/MANIFESTO.md:19-21 as written (delivers a promise already made, so no amendment needed) and vision.md 'the amount of mental labor the system reliably absorbs'.
moves.integration_points: Migration roster/general/migrations/004_capture_search.py: a `content_text` TEXT column on collection_items populated from the text-bearing leaves of `data` plus extracted_text, a generated `search_vector tsvector` with a GIN index (mirroring the pattern already proven in src/butlers/modules/memory/search_vector.py), and a created_at btree for the date filter the manifesto promises. New verb `capture_search(query, kind=None, collection=None, since=None, until=None, limit=50, cursor=None)` in roster/general/tools/items.py replacing the unbounded item_search, with cursor pagination per docs/api_and_protocols/response-conventions.md. Catalog membership: item_create/capture() writes a public.memory_catalog row (source_schema='general', source_table='collection_items', memory_type='capture', title, summary) through the same path memory writes use (src/butlers/modules/memory/tools/writing.py:521-570 enable_shared_catalog), which makes captures visible to _fetch_fleet_knowledge with no change to memory_context. Extraction: the routing session reads attachments via src/butlers/tools/attachments.py get_attachment and writes extracted_text + extraction_source ('vision'|'stt'|'html_readability') onto the capture — model work stays in the session per vision.md non-negotiable 4. API: /api/general/entities gains q/since/until; new /api/captures/search. Spec: amend openspec/specs/butler-general/spec.md and openspec/specs/memory-discovery-catalog/spec.md to admit non-fact catalog members.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: capture_search('structured note') returns the Arta item and the screenshot whose extracted_text mentions it, each citing collection, created_at, and capture_id. Failure: the tsvector column is absent (pre-migration butler) -> the tool degrades to the containment path and says so in the response envelope rather than returning an empty set that looks like 'nothing captured'. Extraction failure (blob missing, 5MB cap at src/butlers/tools/attachments.py:20) -> extracted_text stays NULL with extraction_source='failed:<reason>' and the capture is still searchable by its text, never silently 'indexed'. Concurrency: the generated column is maintained by Postgres, so concurrent item_update cannot leave the index stale. Idempotence: catalog writes upsert on (source_schema, source_table, source_id). Rollback: dropping the catalog rows and the generated column restores the prior behavior; no owner content is transformed in place.
moves.verification: roster/general/tests/test_capture_search.py: a prose value under an invented key is found by keyword (today's containment path cannot); the date window filters; the limit and cursor are honoured and the tool never returns an unbounded set. tests/integration/test_general_search_vector_real_pg.py against real Postgres: the generated tsvector updates on item_update, and the GIN index is actually used (EXPLAIN assertion) — the mocked-pool class of bug that hid education_003 and the export schema defect. tests/modules/memory/test_catalog_admits_captures.py: a captured note appears in _fetch_fleet_knowledge for a butler that is not general. A degraded-envelope contract case in tests/contracts/test_degraded_envelope.py for the pre-migration path.
moves.slice_plan: S1 content_text + search_vector + GIN and capture_search with keyword and date (the manifesto promise, delivered). S2 bounded pagination and retirement of the unbounded item_search. S3 catalog membership so other butlers can find captures. S4 extraction of text from image/PDF/voice attachments with provenance. S5 semantic recall by reusing the existing embedding engine over content_text.

moves.title: Retention requests — spaced review for anything the owner anchors, not only curriculum concepts
moves.why: Live: 5 mind maps, 0 nodes, 0 pending reviews, 0 quiz responses — 571 lines of SM-2 (roster/education/tools/spaced_repetition.py) has scheduled zero cards in the system's lifetime, because retention state lives as columns on education.mind_map_nodes (roster/education/migrations/001_education_tables.py:38-58) and a node needs a curriculum. The manifesto's central promise — 'we come back, at exactly the right moment' (roster/education/MANIFESTO.md:24-27) — has never once been kept. Owner-visible payoff in a week: capture a term, a name, a lesson from a decision, or a fact you want to hold, and a two-line quiz arrives on the SM-2 schedule; the fleet's most complete unused engine starts producing.
moves.manifesto: Requires a roster/education/MANIFESTO.md amendment. The mind map stays the curriculum territory, but retrieval practice extends to owner-anchored knowledge objects outside a syllabus. The amendment must preserve the existing 'What We Do Not Do' boundaries verbatim — still no external LMS/Anki import, still no source fetching (which keeps it clear of bu-istke source-grounded education), still one person, still no certification. Serves roster/general/MANIFESTO.md:9-21 as the capture side and vision.md 'progressively more autonomy'.
moves.integration_points: New migration roster/education/migrations/006_retention_items.py: education.retention_items (id, subject_prompt, subject_answer, entity_id UUID FK public.entities ON DELETE SET NULL — the same anchoring pattern education_003 established for nodes, source_schema/source_table/source_id provenance triple, capture_id, ease_factor, repetitions, next_review_at, last_reviewed_at, retired_at) plus the partial index on next_review_at that mirrors idx_mmn_next_review. The SM-2 core is reused unchanged: sm2_update (roster/education/tools/spaced_repetition.py:57-113) is already a pure function and needs no edit; only the row-loading and cron-naming helpers gain a retention_items branch, and the existing per-map batch cap generalizes to a per-owner cap. New verbs education_retain(prompt, answer, source_ref, entity_id) and education_review_answer(retention_item_id, quality) in roster/education/modules/tools.py. Review delivery uses the existing one-shot cron + notify() path already used for node reviews. API: /api/education/retention (list, due, history) in roster/education/api/router.py; the capture kind `card` from move 1 routes here. Spec: new openspec/specs/module-education-retention/spec.md; amend openspec/specs/module-education-spaced-repetition/spec.md to name two subject kinds.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: capture 'the SM-2 ease floor is 1.3' as kind=card -> a retention_item with next_review_at = now+6h; the review arrives, the owner answers, sm2_update advances the interval, quiz history records it. Failure: notify() delivery fails -> next_review_at is NOT advanced and the item stays due (the review must not be consumed by a delivery that never landed); a delivered-but-unanswered review decays into the existing pending state rather than silently rescheduling. Concurrency: two answers for the same item serialize on a SELECT ... FOR UPDATE of the row inside the SM-2 transaction, so a Telegram double-tap cannot double-advance the interval (the pattern already proven at src/butlers/chronicler/gap_interview.py:462-472). Idempotence: education_review_answer keyed on (retention_item_id, delivery_id) is a no-op on retry and returns the already-recorded quality. Rollback: retired_at is a soft retire; the schedule row is deleted by the existing schedule_delete, and clearing retired_at restores the item with its history intact. Batch cap: a per-owner ceiling on due items prevents a capture spree from producing a review avalanche — over-cap items wait rather than being dropped.
moves.verification: roster/education/tests/test_retention_items.py: a retention item created from a capture schedules a review with the exact SM-2 interval sm2_update returns for repetitions=0 (asserts the reused engine, not a reimplementation); a failed notify leaves next_review_at unchanged and the item due; two concurrent answers produce one interval advance. tests/integration/test_retention_real_pg.py: the entity_id FK and the next_review_at partial index exist and bind (this is precisely the education_003 UndefinedColumn class that mocked pools missed). An API test that /api/education/retention/due is non-empty after one capture — the first non-zero review count this subsystem will ever have. Plus a manifesto-alignment test alongside roster/education/tests/test_manifesto.py asserting the amendment text and the preserved boundaries.
moves.slice_plan: S1 table + education_retain + due list (a card exists at all). S2 review delivery on the existing cron/notify path with the delivery-evidence gate on interval advance. S3 education_review_answer + quiz history + the concurrency lock. S4 capture kind `card` wired through move 1, plus 'remember this' doors on a memory fact and a chronicler episode. S5 the per-owner batch cap and the due-items lane on the Education surface.

moves.title: Decision records — the choice, the reasoning, the falsifiable expectation, and a revisit door
moves.why: Live: the owner is already keeping a decision journal by hand — general collection `career_decisions`, 6 items, freeform JSONB with no revisit, no outcome, no entity links, unsearchable by keyword. Distinct from the Owner Decision Desk (bu-ckkpz) and openspec/specs/dashboard-decisions, which govern *pending* decisions and approvals; this is the record of a decision already made and what it was expected to produce. Owner-visible payoff in a week: 'why did I choose that' answers in five seconds with the reasoning as written at the time, and the revisit date arrives as attention instead of being forgotten. Serves the north star's 'every consequential clause is a door': a decision with a revisit_at and no door is the last hop with no door.
moves.manifesto: No current manifesto claims judgment records — General's claims storage (roster/general/MANIFESTO.md:9-21), Chronicler explicitly does not plan or interpret forward (roster/chronicler/MANIFESTO.md 'What I Am Not'). Cheapest honest path: a General manifesto amendment naming decisions as a typed kind General holds with a shape, not a freeform bag. The alternative, if the owner wants reasoning *quality* engaged rather than merely stored, is a new small butler (working name Counsel) owning decision framing, expectation calibration, and outcome scoring — which would need a fresh MANIFESTO.md and a port, so propose the amendment first and let usage justify the butler.
moves.integration_points: New migration alembic/versions/core/core_221_decision_records.py: public.decision_records (id, decided_at, question, chosen_option, options_considered JSONB, reasoning TEXT, expectation TEXT, expectation_horizon, confidence NUMERIC, revisit_at TIMESTAMPTZ, entity_ids UUID[] -> public.entities, capture_id -> public.captures, superseded_by) and public.decision_outcomes (decision_id, observed_at, what_happened, expectation_met BOOL NULL, note) — append-only, additive corrections, no in-place rewrite (chronicler's doctrine). Public schema because it is cross-butler by nature (a career decision touches finance, relationship, and time) and because public is the sanctioned home for cross-butler tables per CLAUDE.md. Core verbs decision_record(...) / decision_outcome(...) in a new src/butlers/core_tools/_decisions.py under a `decisions` core group. Revisit delivery rides the existing insight-broker attention spine (roster/switchboard/modules/insight_broker.py) rather than a new notifier. Chronicler gains a `decisions.records` source adapter entry in src/butlers/chronicler/contracts.py (read_surface public.decision_records, boundary_semantics 'one decision point event at decided_at', precision exact) so decisions appear in lived time. Links use the shipped public.entity_graph_edges substrate. API: /api/decisions + /api/decisions/{id} (record + outcomes). Spec: new openspec/specs/decision-records/spec.md.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: capture kind=decision -> a decision_record with reasoning and a revisit_at 90 days out; at revisit_at one insight card arrives citing the record; the owner records an outcome and expectation_met. Failure: revisit_at passes while the insight broker is suppressed -> the catch-up path already shipped (insight-broker suppression catch-up) delivers it late and the card says it is late; a revisit is never silently dropped and never marked reviewed without a delivery receipt. Missing expectation: a record with reasoning but no falsifiable expectation is accepted but flagged `unfalsifiable` and its revisit asks only 'what happened', never 'were you right' — the system does not fabricate a scoreable claim. Concurrency: two revisit deliveries for the same record are deduped on (decision_id, revisit_at) in the attention ledger. Idempotence: decision_record accepts a mutation_id so a retried capture routing does not create a second record; decision_outcome is append-only so retries add a row only under a distinct observed_at + mutation_id. Rollback: superseded_by chains a revised decision to the original; nothing is edited or deleted, so the reasoning as written at the time survives a later change of mind.
moves.verification: tests/integration/test_decision_records_real_pg.py: a record with revisit_at in the past produces exactly one attention row and, on retry, still one; expectation_met stays NULL for an unfalsifiable record and the revisit prompt omits the scoring question (assert the rendered prompt, so the flag is enforcement and not metadata); superseding preserves both rows. tests/api/test_decisions_router.py for the read surface and the degraded envelope. A chronicler adapter test asserting a decision appears as a point event at decided_at with precision exact, alongside the existing contracts tests. Plus a one-off migration test that the 6 live career_decisions items map into decision_records without losing any JSONB key (reported, not silently dropped).
moves.slice_plan: S1 tables + decision_record verb + /api/decisions (the owner can write one and read it back). S2 revisit_at on the insight-broker spine with the catch-up and dedupe contract. S3 decision_outcomes + expectation scoring + the unfalsifiable flag. S4 chronicler source adapter so decisions land in lived time. S5 entity-graph edges linking a decision to the people, accounts, and topics it touched; migrate the 6 live career_decisions items with a reported mapping.

moves.title: Sovereignty export that contains the brain, reports its own completeness, and imports back
moves.why: vision.md non-negotiable 1 is sovereignty: 'The user owns the database, the credentials, the LLM API keys, and all data.' The one surface backing that claim is dead and mislabelled: /api/data/export scope 'all' (frontend/src/pages/SettingsPermissionsPage.tsx:488-493 labels it 'all data') resolves to three memory tables plus audit and three config tables (src/butlers/api/routers/data_ops.py:113-127), queries a `memory` schema that does not exist in production, and runs on the switchboard pool that could not read another butler's schema even if the qualification were right (data_ops.py:513-517). It fails fast (data_ops.py:471-484), so the owner's 'export all data' returns HTTP 500. Distinct from the nightly pg_dump defect (bu-e1410) and openspec/specs/backup-coverage-boundary: that is operational restore, this is owner portability. Owner-visible payoff: an archive that actually contains the notes, decisions, mind maps, chronicles, contacts, and facts, with a manifest that names every table it holds and every table it could not reach.
moves.manifesto: Serves vision.md non-negotiable 1 directly and roster/general/MANIFESTO.md:21 ('Export and share. Take your data with you.') — currently the manifesto's most straightforwardly false clause. No amendment needed; the promise exists and the mechanism does not.
moves.integration_points: Rewrite src/butlers/api/routers/data_ops.py: replace the hardcoded _SCOPE_MAP with schema discovery over the butler roster (src/butlers/migrations.py get_all_chains / the DatabaseManager's per-butler pools at src/butlers/api/db.py) so each butler's tables are read through *its own* pool, plus the public cross-butler set (entities, entity_facts-bearing schemas, entity_graph_edges, fleet_cases, memory_catalog, audit_log, and the new captures/decision_records). Memory tables are read unqualified per butler schema, which is where they actually live (src/butlers/lifecycle.py:160-173, src/butlers/modules/memory/migrations/001_memory_schema.py:33-567), including chronicler_mem (roster/chronicler/butler.toml:46). Add MANIFEST.json to the archive: every table, row count, byte size, and every skipped table with a machine-readable reason (pool_unavailable | permission_denied | empty), so completeness is reported and the 'all' label is earned or contradicted in the same file. Add a human-legible rendering (Markdown per collection/decision/chronicle) beside the NDJSON. Add /api/data/import validating a MANIFEST and replaying NDJSON through each butler's own verbs so the export is a round trip. Retire the misleading 'all data' label in favour of a scope picker that shows the manifest preview before download. Spec: new openspec/specs/owner-data-portability/spec.md superseding the export requirements currently in openspec/specs/dashboard-settings-console.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: request scope=brain -> a manifest naming ~N tables with row counts, an encrypted archive whose contents match those counts, and a Markdown rendering the owner can read without tooling. Failure: one butler's pool is down -> the export still completes and the manifest names that butler's tables as skipped with reason pool_unavailable; the current fail-fast 500 is replaced by an archive that is honest about its holes (a partial export that says so beats a clear error the owner cannot act on, provided the manifest is authoritative). Permission denied on a schema -> same treatment, never a silent omission. Concurrency: the export is a read snapshot per pool; the manifest records each table's read timestamp so an archive taken during a write is self-describing rather than claiming a single instant. Idempotence: the signed-URL design is already stateless (data_ops.py:17-28) and a repeated download rebuilds from live data — the manifest timestamps make the two archives distinguishable rather than falsely identical. Rollback: export is read-only. Import is the risky direction and is gated: it replays through butler verbs into a named target, refuses to overwrite a non-empty target without an explicit phrase, and writes an import receipt with per-table applied/skipped counts.
moves.verification: Replace tests/integration/test_data_ops_memory_export_schema_faithful.py — which provisions the fictional `memory` schema it is meant to be testing (its own docstring at lines 41-51 says so) — with tests/integration/test_owner_export_production_layout.py that provisions the *production* layout (core into public, the memory chain into each butler schema, chronicler's into chronicler_mem, butler chains into their own schemas) and asserts: (1) the export succeeds and the manifest names general.collection_items, education.mind_map_nodes, chronicler.episodes, relationship contacts, public.entities, public.captures and public.decision_records; (2) every manifest row count equals the NDJSON line count for that table; (3) a deliberately-unavailable butler pool yields a skipped entry with reason pool_unavailable and a 200, not a 500; (4) no table present in the discovered schema set is absent from the manifest without a reason (the anti-silent-omission assertion). Plus a round-trip test: export -> import into a fresh DB -> row counts match per table. Plus a frontend test that the scope label is not 'all data' unless the manifest preview says every discovered table is included.
moves.slice_plan: S1 fix the fatal binding: per-butler pools and unqualified memory reads, so the existing scopes stop 500ing, and replace the fabricated-seam integration test. S2 MANIFEST.json with row counts and skipped-with-reason, and retire the 'all data' label in favour of a manifest preview. S3 schema discovery widening the scope to the whole knowledge layer (general, education, chronicler, relationship, public identity/graph/captures/decisions). S4 the human-legible Markdown rendering. S5 /api/data/import + import receipts, making it a round trip.

moves.title: Recall at the moment of relevance — 'you already know something about this', cited and owner-visible
moves.why: Everything the fleet knows about an entity is currently either invisible to the owner (memory_context injects it into a session prompt the owner never sees, src/butlers/modules/memory/tools/context.py:217+) or unreachable (General is not in the catalog; captures have no keyword search). Distinct from meeting-prep commitment context (bu-bb9gz), which surfaces *commitments*, and from the deferred proactivity producers in the ledger (waiting-on-them, watch registry, rhythm deviation, expiry harvest, seasonal recurrence). Owner-visible payoff in a week: a calendar event with a person you captured a note about, or an inbound thread on a topic you already decided, arrives with one line — 'you captured 2 things and made 1 decision about this' — citing the exact rows. This is what makes three silos feel like one brain, and it is the read half that justifies capturing at all.
moves.manifesto: Serves vision.md 'Butlers surface timely, relevant insights without being asked --- and automatically reduce frequency when the owner disengages', and rides the existing attention budget rather than opening a second unmetered channel (a named run-09 theme). Respects roster/chronicler/MANIFESTO.md's no-proactive-notification promise by never routing recall through Chronicler — Chronicler is a read source here, and the card is delivered by the insight broker.
moves.integration_points: A deterministic producer in core (daemon-side, no LLM per event, per vision.md non-negotiable 4): on a calendar event materializing, an ingestion_event resolving a sender entity, or a dashboard chat turn declaring a visible_resource (the page-context v2 typed visible_resource shipped in #4008), look up prior knowledge anchored to the same entity_ids across public.memory_catalog (now including captures after move 3), public.captures, public.decision_records, and chronicler episodes via public.episode_entities, walking one hop of the shipped public.entity_graph_edges substrate. Emit one bounded card through roster/switchboard/modules/insight_broker.py with the source rows cited as links, subject to the existing suppression, clustering, and catch-up behavior. Feedback verbs reuse the shipped insight feedback path so a useless recall reduces future recall for that shape. Read surface: /api/insights already exists; the card carries a `recall` kind and its citations. Spec: amend openspec/specs/proactive-insight-engine/spec.md with a recall producer requirement; no new table beyond an idempotence key.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: a calendar event with an attendee resolving to an entity that has 2 captures and 1 decision produces one card at event materialization citing all three rows, and the citations resolve. Failure: an anchor entity resolves to nothing, or the catalog read fails -> no card is emitted; recall stays silent rather than emitting an empty or fabricated 'nothing found' nudge (honest absence, not a false negative dressed as a signal). Under DND or an exhausted attention budget -> the broker's existing suppression holds it and the shipped catch-up delivers it when suppression ends, labelled late. Concurrency: the idempotence key is (trigger_kind, trigger_row_id, entity_id_set hash) so a re-materialized calendar event or a retried ingestion does not produce a second card. Idempotence: the producer is a pure read plus one keyed insert. Rollback: disable the producer in runtime_config; no owner data is written, so there is nothing to unwind. Disengagement: repeated dismissals feed the existing frequency reduction rather than a bespoke counter.
moves.verification: tests/integration/test_recall_producer_real_pg.py: an entity with captures + a decision + a chronicler episode yields exactly one card whose citations SELECT successfully in their named tables (proves the citations are doors, not decoration); the same trigger fired twice yields one card; an entity with no prior knowledge yields zero cards and zero attention rows. tests/modules/test_insight_broker_recall_suppression.py: under DND the card is held and arrives via catch-up marked late. A frontend test that a recall card's citation links navigate to the cited capture/decision (the inert-strip defect class the ledger flags repeatedly).
moves.slice_plan: S1 the producer over calendar-event materialization only, one entity hop, citing captures and decisions (narrowest trigger, clearest payoff). S2 broaden the trigger to ingestion_event sender resolution. S3 add chronicler episodes and the entity_graph_edges hop. S4 wire it to the dashboard chat's visible_resource so recall follows what the owner is looking at. S5 feedback-driven frequency reduction per recall shape.

audits.jarvis_gap: Today the fleet has no way for one butler to tell Finance about money, and the one place real cross-domain money already lives is the weakest ledger in the repo. Relationship's loans are no longer a table — migration 010 dropped `relationship.loans` (roster/relationship/migrations/010_drop_legacy_contact_tables.py:248,267) and money now lives as memory `facts` rows with `predicate='loan'` and `{amount_cents, currency, direction, settled}` in JSONB metadata (roster/relationship/tools/loans.py:1-20). That means: no CHECK constraint on direction or amount, a currency silently fabricated as `"USD"` whenever the metadata lacks one (loans.py:55,96,234,289-290), a settle path that supersedes the old fact with a bare UPDATE and then inserts the replacement in a separate round-trip with no transaction (loans.py:209-231) so a mid-flight failure erases the loan from every read, and a dashboard route that reads the same JSONB with *no* default so the API and the MCP tool disagree about the same loan's currency (roster/relationship/api/router.py:3553 vs loans.py:289-290). Finance, meanwhile, cannot see any of it — Rule 3 forbids the cross-schema read — and its own manifesto only ever promises outbound money ("Knowing what you owe and when. Knowing what you spent and where.", roster/finance/MANIFESTO.md §Why It Matters); money owed *to* the owner appears nowhere in the document. Finance's `domain_events.toml` declares exactly one outbound advisory (roster/finance/domain_events.toml:4-27) and Relationship has neither a `domain_events` core group nor a declaration file at all (roster/relationship/butler.toml:11-20), so the run-11 sketch of "relationship.loan_outstanding on the bus" is not even buildable as written. The consequence for the owner is that "who owes me money?" and "did Alex pay me back?" are unanswerable in one hop, and the one number that would answer them is stamped with a currency nobody asserted. Everything needed to fix this already exists and is unwired: the RLS-fenced shared-ledger pattern (`producer_role = current_user`, alembic/versions/core/core_210_expected_signals.py:101-107; `current_user = 'butler_switchboard_rw'`, core_217_fleet_case_file.py:124-138), a deterministic payee/amount/window matcher with an ambiguity rule that already refuses to auto-apply (roster/finance/tools/reconciliation.py:49-188, openspec/specs/butler-finance/spec.md:145,152,156), honest per-account feed staleness that refuses to fabricate health (roster/finance/tools/feed_reconciliation.py:171-214), the owner-condition snapshot reconciler (roster/finance/jobs/finance_jobs.py:753-786), the insight broker `_propose` path (finance_jobs.py:726-751), and a live currency-honest response envelope already shipping `by_currency` + `legacy_aggregate_degraded` on /api/finance/spending-summary.
audits.ideal: A cost claim is a first-class, typed, durable object in `public` — not an event, not a JSONB blob, not a view. Any butler may assert one about money it legitimately knows of (a loan Relationship recorded, a trip Travel booked, a co-pay Health saw, a contractor Home hired), stating amount, an explicitly required currency with no default anywhere in the stack, a counterparty anchored on `public.entities`, an expected date, and its own evidence reference — under a readable natural key that makes re-assertion a database-level no-op rather than an application-level dedup. The database itself enforces manifesto ownership: row-level security keyed on `current_user` lets the asserting butler write only its own assertion and lets only `butler_finance_rw` write the reconciliation verdict, so nobody can edit anybody else's truth and no cross-schema read is ever needed. Finance runs one deterministic sweep — zero LLM sessions, reusing the payee/amount/window matcher and the ambiguity rule the bill reconciler already proved — that binds a claim to real transactions, refuses to bind one transaction to two claims, refuses to settle across currencies, and, crucially, distinguishes three different kinds of "no": *no candidate found while I had fresh coverage*, *two candidates and I will not guess*, and *I cannot see, because the account feed for this currency is stale or never synced* — the last carrying a named reason and the exact timestamp of the newest evidence Finance actually holds. Every claim, and every "I cannot see", is a door: a row on the Finance page and a chip on the Relationship entity with settle / dispute / write-off verbs, a standing owner condition that resolves itself the moment the money lands, an insight candidate on the existing broker, and a one-session answer to "who owes me money?" from the chat lane. Aggregates are never blended across currencies. The claim is a projection, never the only copy — the asserter's own schema stays the source of truth, so the whole ledger can be dropped without losing a single fact.
audits.live_verification: Live-confirmed against the dev stack (read-only GETs on http://127.0.0.1:42200): the fleet is up and finance is healthy (`/api/butlers` → finance status ok, port 41105, 10 sessions/24h). `/api/finance/spending-summary` returns the shipped currency-honest envelope — `{"currency":null,"total_spend":"726.15","by_currency":[{"currency":"SGD",...},{"currency":"USD",...}],"legacy_aggregate_degraded":true,"degraded_reason":"multiple_currencies_unconverted"}` — confirming the owner genuinely holds two currencies live and confirming the exact response shape the cost-claim read API must copy. `/api/finance/accounts?limit=3` returns `{"data":[],"meta":{"total":0,...}}` — zero accounts, i.e. today every claim would reconcile to `unverifiable`, which is precisely why that state must exist before the feature can be honest. `/openapi.json` confirms the mount boundary (`/api/finance/*`, `/api/relationship/entities/{entity_id}/loans`) and that no cost-claim route exists. Everything else is source-confirmed: I read the decisive mechanisms (RLS policies in core_210/core_217, the loans fact-store path, `account_feed_freshness`, `_payee_match`, `_propose`/`_reconcile_owner_conditions`, the domain-event contract loader and its Switchboard-routed delivery, both butler.toml core-group lists, both manifestos). A repo-wide grep for `cost_claim|expected_outflow|cost_committed|loan_outstanding` outside docs/redesigns returns nothing, and neither `openspec/specs/` nor `openspec/changes/` contains a finance cost-claim or cross-butler-money spec — the contract does not exist in any form. No writes of any kind were issued.

findings.title: Relationship fabricates USD on every loan whose metadata omits a currency
findings.evidence: roster/relationship/tools/loans.py:55 (`currency = meta.get("currency", "USD")`), :96 (`currency: str = "USD"` parameter default), :234, :289-290 (`if "currency" not in r: r["currency"] = "USD"`)
findings.taxonomy_shape: run-11 theme: aggregates that denominate nothing (mixed currency) — here at the single-record level: a unit is invented rather than blended
findings.detail: Four independent sites stamp USD onto a loan whose currency was never asserted. The finance side of the house was made currency-honest in #3973 (live-confirmed `by_currency`/`legacy_aggregate_degraded` on /api/finance/spending-summary), but the fleet's only real cross-domain money ledger still manufactures a denomination. For an owner whose live data is SGD-majority, an unlabelled 300 loan reads as $300. The cost-claim contract must make `currency` NOT NULL with no DEFAULT at the column, and required-with-no-default at the tool signature, and slice 2 must delete these four defaults rather than carry them into the public table.

findings.title: loan_settle supersedes the old loan fact and inserts the replacement outside a transaction — a mid-flight failure erases the loan
findings.evidence: roster/relationship/tools/loans.py:207-231: `await pool.execute("UPDATE facts SET validity = 'superseded', invalid_at = $2 WHERE id = $1", ...)` followed by a separate `await store_fact(pool, ...)`, with no `async with pool.acquire() ... transaction()` around the pair
findings.taxonomy_shape: NEW: two-step state transition on money with no atomicity — the intermediate state is 'this obligation does not exist'
findings.detail: Both statements take their own pool connection. If `store_fact` raises (embedding engine unavailable, DB blip, session kill), the original loan is already `validity='superseded'` and no settled snapshot exists, so `loan_list` (which filters `validity='active'`) and `GET /entities/{id}/loans` (router.py:3532-3540, same filter) both return nothing: the money silently disappears with no error surface. This is the strongest argument for the claim ledger being constraint-enforced and trigger-audited rather than application-sequenced, and for the claim being a projection whose asserter-side source can be repaired.

findings.title: Money state lives in memory-module JSONB with no constraints — the exact anti-pattern Finance's own AGENTS.md forbids
findings.evidence: roster/relationship/tools/loans.py:1-20 (metadata contract) and :133-147 (metadata assembled as a free dict, stored via `store_fact`); contrast roster/finance/AGENTS.md:34-36 ("Integrity rule: NEVER write settlement state (e.g. status=\"paid\") into a metadata prose field without the structured status column change")
findings.taxonomy_shape: run-09 theme: primitives built once and generalized nowhere — finance's settlement-integrity rule was never applied to the fleet's other money store
findings.detail: `amount_cents`, `direction`, `settled`, `currency` and both counterparty ids are unvalidated JSONB keys on a `facts` row. Nothing rejects `direction='lend'`, a negative amount, a settled-without-settled_at pair, or a missing currency. Finance enforces exactly the opposite discipline on its own bills. The public claim table is where the two are reconciled: typed columns, CHECK constraints on direction/kind/amount/currency, and a trigger-written append-only event log so a state change cannot be made without an audit row.

findings.title: The relationship butler cannot publish domain events at all — the run-11 'relationship.loan_outstanding on the bus' slice is not buildable as sketched
findings.evidence: roster/relationship/butler.toml:11-20 core_groups list omits `domain_events` (finance has it, roster/finance/butler.toml:11-20); no roster/relationship/domain_events.toml exists (only finance/health/home/travel declare one); src/butlers/core/domain_event_contracts.py:47-52 refuses any publish of an undeclared type
findings.taxonomy_shape: NEW: a proposal's named first slice depends on a capability the proposed butler does not hold
findings.detail: Slice 1 as originally written would have required adding a core group, authoring a declaration file, standing up a subscription, and accepting one Switchboard-routed LLM session per delivery (src/butlers/core_tools/_domain_events.py:138-206) before a single loan reached Finance. The public-table carrier needs none of that: an INSERT by the relationship role and a deterministic SELECT by the finance role, zero sessions. This is decisive evidence for the carrier choice, not a defect to fix.

findings.title: The same loan's currency is USD to the MCP tool and null to the dashboard
findings.evidence: roster/relationship/api/router.py:3553 `currency=(r["metadata"] or {}).get("currency")` (no default) vs roster/relationship/tools/loans.py:289-290 (defaults to "USD")
findings.taxonomy_shape: run-11 theme: built twice, unified never — two readers of one row disagree about its denomination
findings.detail: An LLM session asking `loan_list` and an owner reading the entity page get different answers about the same fact. Collapsing both onto one typed claim row with a NOT NULL currency removes the divergence by construction.

findings.title: dropped: the domain-event bus as the claim's carrier of record
findings.evidence: src/butlers/core/domain_event_contracts.py:33-71 (append-only declarations, no lifecycle); src/butlers/core_tools/_domain_events.py:138-206 (every delivery is a Switchboard route() into a subscriber LLM session); about/legends-and-lore/rfcs/0032-fleet-case-file.md §Alternatives rejected (candidates are cycle-scoped and expire; a situation needs a lifecycle they were never designed to carry)
findings.taxonomy_shape: n/a (rejected alternative)
findings.detail: Run 11 proposed the bus as the carrier. Rejected on four grounds: (1) an event is an immutable fact, a claim has states, amendments, partial settlement and voiding; (2) idempotence would be application-level, where RFC 0032 established that it must be a table constraint; (3) every delivery costs an LLM session, against the connectors-as-cost-boundary/daemon-deterministic doctrine for what is pure SQL matching; (4) there is nowhere to write the verdict back. The bus is retained in the design for exactly one job it is good at — an optional `finance.cost_claim_settled` wake so the asserting butler can tell the owner in its own voice — declared minimized (claim_key, state) with `permitted_subscribers` naming only the asserters.

findings.title: dropped: keeping the claim in finance's own schema with an RFC 0010-style cross-schema read view
findings.evidence: about/legends-and-lore/rfcs/0010-cross-butler-briefing-exception.md §Five Guardrails (read-only UNION view, date-filtered, general reads from specialists, no writes cross schema)
findings.taxonomy_shape: n/a (rejected alternative)
findings.detail: RFC 0010's exception is one-directional and read-only by construction (PostgreSQL refuses writes on a UNION view). A cost claim needs a write in each direction — the asserter writes the assertion, Finance writes the verdict — so the view pattern cannot carry it, and widening RFC 0010 to permit cross-schema writes would gut Rule 3. `public` with per-role RLS is the sanctioned shape and already has two precedents (core_210, core_217).

findings.title: dropped: extending public.fleet_cases as the claim carrier
findings.evidence: alembic/versions/core/core_217_fleet_case_file.py:141-146 (INSERT/UPDATE fenced to butler_switchboard_rw); RFC 0032 §Write authority
findings.taxonomy_shape: n/a (rejected alternative)
findings.detail: Tempting because the substrate just landed, but fleet_cases is arbitrated solely by the Switchboard — a claim must be arbitrated by Finance, whose manifesto owns money. Bending fleet_cases would either give Finance switchboard write authority or route every money verdict through the Switchboard, both worse than a sibling table. The right relationship is a link, not a merge: when a claim goes `unverifiable` or overdue alongside other signals, it becomes `fleet_case_links` row with `link_kind='cost_claim'` in RFC 0032's S7 three-ledger binding.

findings.title: dropped: integer minor units (amount_cents) on the public contract
findings.evidence: roster/relationship/tools/loans.py:7,55-70 (amount_cents, /100) vs roster/finance/migrations/001_finance_tables.py:57 (`amount NUMERIC(14,2)`)
findings.taxonomy_shape: n/a (rejected alternative)
findings.detail: The two existing money stores disagree on representation. `amount_cents` bakes a 2-decimal exponent into a currency-agnostic field (wrong for JPY at 0, KWD at 3) and would require carrying an exponent column to be honest. The public claim adopts `NUMERIC(14,2)` to match `finance.transactions`, so the reconciler's tolerance arithmetic (`max($1.00, 1%)`, roster/finance/tools/reconciliation.py:38,166-188) compares like with like and no conversion sits between the claim and the transaction it is matched against.

findings.title: dropped: converting currency at settlement time via an FX table
findings.evidence: live /api/finance/spending-summary returns `legacy_aggregate_degraded:true, degraded_reason:"multiple_currencies_unconverted"` rather than converting
findings.taxonomy_shape: n/a (rejected alternative)
findings.detail: An SGD claim settled by a USD transaction is a real case (a friend repays in a different currency). Auto-converting would let a rate the owner never saw decide whether an obligation is closed. The design instead refuses: a currency mismatch yields state `ambiguous` with `unmatched_reason='currency_mismatch'`, surfaced as a door the owner resolves with an explicit rate on `cost_claim_settle`. Consistent with the shipped aggregate behavior, which degrades rather than converts.

findings.title: dropped: a delegate_ask round trip per claim instead of a ledger
findings.evidence: openspec/specs/cross-butler-delegation/spec.md:12-31 (ledger of record), :84 (answering is asynchronous and guarded); roster/relationship/butler.toml:19 (relationship holds the delegation group)
findings.taxonomy_shape: n/a (rejected alternative)
findings.detail: Relationship could ask Finance 'did a 300 SGD credit from Alex land?' via delegation. Rejected: it is a question, not a standing obligation — nothing persists, nothing reconciles on its own, the owner gets no door, and every check costs two sessions. Delegation stays the right tool for a one-off owner-initiated question; the ledger is for the standing claim that must survive both butlers restarting.

findings.title: dropped: shared-expense splitting (Splitwise-shaped multi-party settlement)
findings.evidence: roster/finance/AGENTS.md:24 ("Do not offer investment advice, payment initiation, tax filing, or accounting double-entry")
findings.taxonomy_shape: n/a (rejected alternative)
findings.detail: N-party split with netting is double-entry bookkeeping by another name and is explicitly out of Finance's scope. `kind='shared_expense'` is retained in the contract as a single owner-side claim (what one counterparty owes the owner, or vice versa) with no netting graph, keeping the AGENTS.md boundary intact without an amendment.

moves.title: Slice 1 — public.cost_claims / cost_claim_resolutions / cost_claim_events: the typed money claim, fenced by RLS
moves.why: Vision non-negotiable 3 forbids Finance reading relationship's schema and non-negotiable 6 makes each manifesto binding, so the only doctrinally clean carrier for cross-butler money is a `public` table whose write authority is split by role at the database. Both precedents exist: `producer_role = current_user` (alembic/versions/core/core_210_expected_signals.py:101-107) and `current_user = 'butler_switchboard_rw'` (core_217_fleet_case_file.py:124-138). RFC 0032's rule that 'idempotence is a table constraint, not application logic' is adopted verbatim. Owner payoff at the end of the arc: one honest answer to 'who owes me money, and what can you actually see?'
moves.manifesto: Finance MANIFESTO.md §Our Promise/§Why It Matters is outbound-only ("Knowing what you owe and when. Knowing what you spent and where.") — money owed TO the owner and claims asserted by siblings are absent, so slice 5 carries the amendment. Relationship needs none: MANIFESTO.md:32 already states "**Financial clarity:** Track loans, shared expenses, or money you've lent so no awkwardness lingers."
moves.integration_points: New `alembic/versions/core/core_221_cost_claims.py` (re-verify the head against alembic/versions/core/ at merge; core_220 is current). `public.cost_claims`: id UUID PK; claim_key TEXT NOT NULL; asserted_by TEXT NOT NULL; asserted_by_role TEXT NOT NULL; kind TEXT CHECK IN ('receivable','payable','shared_expense','committed_cost','expected_refund'); direction TEXT CHECK IN ('inbound','outbound'); amount NUMERIC(14,2) CHECK (amount > 0); currency CHAR(3) NOT NULL CHECK (currency ~ '^[A-Z]{3}$') **and no DEFAULT**; counterparty_entity_id UUID REFERENCES public.entities(id) ON DELETE SET NULL; counterparty_label TEXT; expected_on DATE; description TEXT NOT NULL; evidence_kind/evidence_ref TEXT; asserted_at; superseded_at; retracted_at; retraction_reason; CHECK (counterparty_entity_id IS NOT NULL OR counterparty_label IS NOT NULL); CHECK (asserted_by_role = 'butler_' || asserted_by || '_rw'); partial UNIQUE (asserted_by, claim_key) WHERE superseded_at IS NULL AND retracted_at IS NULL. `public.cost_claim_resolutions`: claim_id UUID PK FK ON DELETE CASCADE; state TEXT CHECK IN ('unreconciled','matched','ambiguous','partially_settled','settled','unverifiable','disputed','written_off'); matched_amount NUMERIC(14,2); matched_currency CHAR(3); match_refs JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]'; unmatched_reason; unverifiable_reason; evidence_horizon_at TIMESTAMPTZ; decided_at; decided_by; CHECK ((state='unverifiable') = (unverifiable_reason IS NOT NULL)). `public.cost_claim_events`: append-only, written by BEFORE/AFTER triggers on both tables so no code path can change money state without an audit row (the fleet-wide generalization of roster/finance/AGENTS.md:34-36); UNIQUE (claim_id, actor_role, action, idempotency_key). RLS on all three, FORCE, SELECT USING (true) for every role; cost_claims INSERT/UPDATE WITH CHECK (asserted_by_role = current_user); cost_claim_resolutions INSERT/UPDATE WITH CHECK (current_user = 'butler_finance_rw'); grants via core_217's `_grant_best_effort` helper over `_ALL_RUNTIME_ROLES`. New core group `cost_claims` in `src/butlers/core_tools/_cost_claims.py::register_cost_claim_tools`, hung into `src/butlers/core_tools/_dispatcher.py:56-72` and gated with `@_core_tool("cost_claims")` (pattern: src/butlers/core_tools/_temporal.py:20-29). Core, not a module — Rule 2 forbids a module adding cross-butler infrastructure. Tools: `cost_claim_assert` (currency required, no default; upsert on (asserted_by, claim_key); identical re-assert is a no-op returning the existing id; changed values create a superseding row), `cost_claim_amend`, `cost_claim_retract`, `cost_claim_list_mine`. Finance-only verdict tools (`cost_claim_resolve`, `cost_claim_settle`, `cost_claim_dispute`, `cost_claim_write_off`) are registered in the same group but fenced by RLS, so a second butler holding the group still cannot write a verdict — authority is in the database, not the tool list.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy: relationship asserts claim_key `loan:{fact_id}` → one row, one 'asserted' event, resolution row seeded 'unreconciled'. Duplicate: identical re-assert returns the existing id (partial unique index, not application dedup). Amend: superseding row + old `superseded_at`; the old resolution is retained, the new one restarts at 'unreconciled'. Retract: `retracted_at` set, sweep skips it, last verdict frozen, UI shows it struck through with the reason rather than vanishing. Forgery: a butler inserting `asserted_by='finance'` is refused by the RLS WITH CHECK and again by the asserted_by/role CHECK. Cross-write: `butler_finance_rw` UPDATE of a claim's amount is refused; `butler_relationship_rw` INSERT into resolutions is refused. Concurrency: two asserters race → one wins the unique index, the loser's identical payload returns the winner's id. Rollback: downgrade drops all three CASCADE; nothing is lost because the claim is a projection and the asserter's schema stays the source of truth.
moves.verification: `tests/test_cost_claims_rls.py` connecting as real roles: butler_relationship_rw CAN insert its own claim, CANNOT insert/update a resolution, CANNOT update another butler's claim; butler_finance_rw CAN write a resolution, CANNOT change an asserted amount — behavior executed against the fenced tables, mirroring the existing expected-signals/fleet-cases RLS tests. Concurrent double-assert test expecting exactly one live row (the constraint is what is under test). Trigger test: a direct UPDATE of resolutions.state with no tool involvement still produces an event row. Migration replay test on a DB seeded with `scripts/init-db.sql` twice, proving the RLS fence survives init-db re-widening default privileges (the AGENTS.md "Fencing a `public` table to one runtime role" trap).
moves.slice_plan: This is slice 1 of 6: schema, RLS, core tool group, tools, tests. No reconciler, no API, no UI, no manifesto change — nothing owner-visible ships here, exactly as RFC 0032 S1 did.

moves.title: Slice 2 — relationship.loan_outstanding: every loan becomes a claim, and the USD fabrication dies
moves.why: This is the smallest real case with real owner money, and it is currently the fleet's least trustworthy record: currency invented at four sites (roster/relationship/tools/loans.py:55,96,234,289-290), a non-transactional settle that can erase the loan (loans.py:207-231), and no constraint on direction or amount because the state is memory-module JSONB. Relationship's manifesto already owns this ("Track loans, shared expenses, or money you've lent so no awkwardness lingers", MANIFESTO.md:32) — asserting a claim is exposure of what it holds, not new scope. Owner payoff: the loan you recorded stops being denominated in a currency nobody chose, and stops being able to disappear.
moves.manifesto: Relationship MANIFESTO.md:32 covers this without amendment. The Finance-side amendment is deferred to slice 5 because nothing owner-facing from Finance ships until then.
moves.integration_points: `roster/relationship/tools/loans.py`: (a) `currency` becomes a required argument on `loan_create` with no default, and the three read-side defaults at :55, :234, :289-290 are deleted — a loan with no currency reads back as `currency: null` and is rendered as unknown, never as USD; (b) `loan_settle`'s UPDATE+store_fact pair (:207-231) is wrapped in `async with pool.acquire() as conn, conn.transaction():`; (c) `loan_create`/`loan_settle`/`loan_retract` additionally call `cost_claim_assert`/`cost_claim_retract` with `claim_key=f"loan:{fact_id}"`, `kind='receivable'|'payable'`, `direction` derived from lent/borrowed, `counterparty_entity_id` from the already-resolved `contact_entity_id` (loans.py:129-133), `counterparty_label` from the entity's canonical_name, `evidence_kind='fact'`, `evidence_ref=fact_id`. moves.title: Slice 3 — Finance reconciliation sweep with three honest kinds of 'no'
moves.why: North star: 'failure never impersonates health, staleness never wears current-data authority.' Finance already computes per-account `never_synced`/`stale` and deliberately refuses to fabricate health from an absent timestamp (roster/finance/tools/feed_reconciliation.py:171-214) — and today, live, the owner has zero accounts (`/api/finance/accounts` returns an empty set), so a naive reconciler would report every claim as 'not repaid' when the truth is 'I have no transaction source at all.' The `unverifiable` state is the whole point of the feature: a butler that says 'I cannot see' is trusted; one that says 'nothing arrived' when it is blind is not. Owner payoff: 'Alex has not repaid you' and 'I cannot tell whether Alex repaid you' become two visibly different sentences.

moves.behavior_matrix: One matching credit in window → settled + event + binding row. Two → ambiguous, nothing bound, both candidates carried in match_refs for the owner to pick. Debit offered against an inbound claim → never matched. Transfer-category credit → never matched. USD credit against an SGD claim → ambiguous/currency_mismatch, never converted. No candidate with a fresh feed → unreconciled/no_candidate_in_window. No fresh feed (today's live state: zero accounts) → unverifiable/no_account with evidence_horizon_at NULL. Same transaction already bound → ambiguous/transaction_already_bound. Sweep crashes → previous verdict retained with its original `decided_at`, so the surface renders 'last checked {decided_at}' and never a fresh-looking verdict from a dead sweep. Two sweeps race → advisory lock; the loser exits without writing. Amended claim → binding released, resolution restarts unreconciled. Rollback: drop the binding table and reset resolutions to 'unreconciled'; no transaction or claim is mutated.

audits.jarvis_gap: Butlers has built, one at a time, most of the *mechanisms* a JARVIS-grade interaction-speed layer needs: a named poll-policy token file with an ESLint gate (`frontend/src/lib/poll-policy.ts`, `frontend/eslint.config.js:217-237`), a bus-aware refetch cadence (`use-bus-aware-poll-interval.ts`), a declarative event→cache-patch registry with a coverage manifest and test (`hooks/event-cache-registry.ts`, `event-cache-manifest.ts`), a typed shell-capability manifest projecting route chunks and query warmups (`lib/shell-capability.ts`), hover/focus intent prefetch (`use-prefetch-on-intent.ts`, `use-route-chunk-prefetch-on-intent.ts`), a never-blank `FetchingDim` + `placeholderData` idiom, a shared optimistic-mutation primitive, a stable `RouteSuspense` frame, and hand-tuned `manualChunks`. Every one of these is well-reasoned and documented. And every single one stopped at partial adoption: warmups exist for 8 of 46 capabilities and two of them warm the wrong (non-hero) query; chunk prefetch fires only from the rail and the palette while every table row warms data only; `placeholderData` covers the telemetry half of the app and none of the butler-domain half; the "bus-covered" 5-minute cadence is adopted by four hooks with zero bus coverage (including Fleet Halt) because the coverage test explicitly declines to check that direction; two flagship surfaces (Approvals, Settings Console) still hold a flat 5-minute poll that never degrades when the bus dies; and there is no work-in-progress primitive at all, so the chat composer and sixteen textarea dialogs destroy typed input on close. On top of that, a genuinely new defect appeared under the bus itself: the 200-event snapshot is replayed one event at a time through the full patch registry on every connect and reconnect — live-measured at 598 `invalidateQueries` calls in a single synchronous tick at first paint, on a stack that is otherwise idle. The gap to JARVIS is not invention; it is that no seam forces a new surface onto the mechanism that already exists, so each generation of pages re-enters the app at the pre-mechanism baseline.
audits.live_verification: Dev stack reachable and healthy. Read-only HTTP GETs against http://127.0.0.1:42200 (no writes issued). Steady-state timings, 3 runs each: /api/ingestion/events?limit=20 = 0.559/0.547/0.585s; /api/audit-log?limit=20 = 0.447/0.417/0.412s; /api/issues?limit=20 = 0.080/0.065/0.059s; /api/butlers/board = 0.176s; /api/decisions = 0.141s; /api/qa/patrols = 0.112s; /api/notifications = 0.110s; /api/timeline?limit=50 = 0.118s; /api/approvals = 0.022s; /api/sessions = 0.031s; /api/spend/summary = 0.017s; /api/butlers = 0.037s. First (cold) hit of /api/audit-log was 7.15s and /api/issues 4.89s before warming — cause not isolated, reported as inferred. Fleet WS bus probed read-only (`ws://127.0.0.1:42200/api/events/stream`): connect 0.060s, snapshot delivered immediately with exactly 200 events spanning 227 seconds, composition 199×`ingestion` + 1×`chronicles`; replaying that snapshot through `applyFleetEvent` costs 598 `invalidateQueries` calls (computed from the per-type invalidation counts in `hooks/event-cache-registry.ts`). Two live `ingestion` events arrived within 0.9s of connect. Everything else in this report is source-confirmed by reading the decisive mechanism; nothing is asserted from behavior I could have read but did not.

findings.title: Fleet-bus snapshot is replayed event-by-event through the full patch registry — 598 cache invalidations in one tick at first paint, measured live
findings.detail: `useEventStream`'s onmessage loops the entire snapshot and calls `applyFleetEvent(qc, replayed)` plus `onEventRef.current?.(...)` once per event (frontend/src/hooks/use-event-stream.ts:216-224). The server ring buffer is 200 events (src/butlers/api/routers/events.py:79) and is replayed on EVERY connect — including the first one at app mount, where no events can have been missed — and on every reconnect (exponential backoff at use-event-stream.ts:243-250, plus the 45s half-open watchdog at use-event-stream.ts:277-294). Each replayed event runs the full patch: `sessionPatch` issues 8 `invalidateQueries`, `calendarPatch` 10, `spendPatch` 7, `approvalPatch` 5, `ingestionPatch` 3 (hooks/event-cache-registry.ts, 40 invalidation statements total). I probed the live socket: the snapshot is 200 events, 199 of them identical-shaped `ingestion` events, costing 598 `invalidateQueries` calls synchronously — 597 of them redundant re-invalidations of the same three ingestion keys. `EventBusProvider.dispatch` additionally fans all 200 events to every subscribed component (frontend/src/lib/event-bus.tsx:96-100). This lands exactly during the shell's own first-paint fetches, so the app's most latency-sensitive moment is also its heaviest cache-churn moment. Secondary measurement: the 200-event ring covered only 227 seconds of wall clock, i.e. less than the 300s `POLL_BUS_RECONCILE_MS` safety net it is supposed to backstop.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/hooks/use-event-stream.ts:216-224; frontend/src/hooks/event-cache-registry.ts:118-215 (40 invalidateQueries); frontend/src/lib/event-bus.tsx:96-100; src/butlers/api/routers/events.py:79; live: ws://127.0.0.1:42200/api/events/stream snapshot = 200 events / 227s / 199 ingestion → 598 invalidations
findings.taxonomy_shape: NEW: replay amplification — a correctness mechanism (snapshot-on-connect so the client is never blank) re-enters the system through a per-event hot path with no coalescing, converting a 'never miss an event' guarantee into an O(ring × keys) burst at the exact moment the UI is most latency-sensitive

findings.title: Four hooks adopt the "bus-covered" 5-minute cadence with no bus event that invalidates their key — Fleet Halt among them
findings.detail: `useBusAwarePollInterval()` returns `POLL_BUS_RECONCILE_MS` (5 min) while the bus is healthy, on the explicit premise that live invalidation is doing the real work (frontend/src/hooks/use-bus-aware-poll-interval.ts:14-18). Five query keys take that cadence with zero registry coverage: `["dispatch-attempts"]` (use-fleet-halt.ts:42,94 — the FLEET HALT surface), `["domain-event-subscriptions"]` and `["domain-event-deliveries"]` (use-domain-events.ts:19,28), `["delegation-ledger"]` (use-delegation.ts:17), `["healing-dispatch-events"]` (use-healing.ts:18). Grepping all four strings across `hooks/event-cache-registry.ts` and `hooks/event-cache-manifest.ts` returns nothing. The coverage test is aware of the hole and declares it out of scope in its own header: "Adding a new bus-covered surface without a matching manifest entry is invisible to this test by design — the manifest is the opt-in list, not a static-analysis sweep of every hook in the app." Owner-visible consequence: the fleet-halt banner (spend ceiling has stopped the fleet) can be up to five minutes behind reality while the Live indicator reads healthy — the exact inversion of the five-second-fleet-verification north star.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/hooks/use-fleet-halt.ts:42,94; frontend/src/hooks/use-domain-events.ts:19,28; frontend/src/hooks/use-delegation.ts:17; frontend/src/hooks/use-healing.ts:18; frontend/src/hooks/event-cache-registry.coverage.test.ts:16-19; absent from frontend/src/hooks/event-cache-manifest.ts:37-104
findings.taxonomy_shape: gates as metadata not enforcement (run 11 theme) — new instance: a *cadence* claims a coverage guarantee, and the test that exists to catch exactly this drift opts out of the direction that would catch it

findings.title: Same page, two cadences: Approvals and Settings Console hold a flat 5-minute poll that never degrades when the bus dies
findings.detail: `POLL_BUS_DOWN_FALLBACK_MS` (30s) exists precisely so a bus-covered surface degrades to honest polling instead of silently sitting stale for the full reconciliation window (frontend/src/lib/poll-policy.ts:36-56). Fourteen hooks route through `useBusAwarePollInterval` to get that. Two flagship surfaces do not: `ApprovalsPage.tsx:1652` sets `refetchInterval: POLL_BUS_RECONCILE_MS` flat on the page's primary pending/stalled list query, while `use-approvals.ts:100` (the metrics on the same page) is bus-aware — the Approvals page therefore runs at two different cadences in the same viewport whenever the socket drops. `SettingsConsolePage.tsx:572` does the same for `["settings-console"]`. `use-ingestion-events.ts:82` documents a third variant: a fixed 30s that was left alone because reclassifying it was "outside this coverage pass's scope". The existing ESLint rule enforces only that the value is a *named token*, not that it is the *right* token, so all three pass lint.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/ApprovalsPage.tsx:1652 vs frontend/src/hooks/use-approvals.ts:100; frontend/src/pages/SettingsConsolePage.tsx:572; frontend/src/hooks/use-ingestion-events.ts:74-82; frontend/eslint.config.js:217-237 (rule checks token-ness, not token identity)
findings.taxonomy_shape: built once, generalized never — the lint seam was built at the wrong altitude (bans literals, permits the wrong constant)

findings.title: Query warmup covers 8 of 46 shell capabilities; every un-warmed rail destination pays its full server latency behind a generic skeleton
findings.detail: `ShellCapability.queryWarmup` is optional (frontend/src/lib/shell-capability.ts:52-53). Only eight capabilities declare one: /timeline, /sessions, /spend, /health and five dynamic detail routes (:name, :id, :entityId, :factId, :ruleId, :episodeId, :beadId, /approvals/:id). Every other navigable destination resolves to `null` in `resolveShellWarmup` (shell-capability.ts:216-222) — /approvals, /decisions, /memory, /entities, /notifications, /issues, /qa, /audit-log, /system, /ingestion, /ingestion/connectors, /ingestion/filters, /calendar, /chronicles, /education, all six /health/* subpages, both /settings/* subpages, and all four context-only detail routes. Measured steady-state cost of the resulting cold first paint: /api/ingestion/events 0.55s, /api/audit-log 0.42s, /api/butlers/board 0.18s, /api/decisions 0.14s, /api/notifications 0.11s, /api/qa/patrols 0.11s. Because the rail DOES warm the route chunk (Sidebar.tsx:250,394,770,917), the page shell renders instantly and then sits on `RouteSuspense`'s identical generic skeleton for 100-550ms — the worst of both: fast enough to look loaded, empty long enough to feel broken.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/lib/shell-capability.ts:52-53,129-196,216-222; frontend/src/components/layout/RouteSuspense.tsx:19-41; live timings against http://127.0.0.1:42200 (3 runs each)
findings.taxonomy_shape: primitives built once, generalized nowhere (run 09 theme) — new instance at the manifest level: the field is optional, so absence is invisible

findings.title: Two of the four static warmups warm a query the destination does not paint first
findings.detail: Nothing binds a capability's `queryWarmup` to the page's actual first-paint cache key. /spend warms `["spend-forecast"]` (shell-capability.ts:158) but SpendPage's above-the-fold hero is `useSpendSummary` twice — key `["cost-summary", period, fromStr, toStr, butler]` (use-spend.ts:81, called at SpendPage.tsx:2828 and :2839); the forecast query it warms lives at SpendPage.tsx:2619 inside a lower panel. /health warms `["health-measurement-types"]` (shell-capability.ts:141) but HealthOverviewPage's first paint is the briefing and insight-candidate queries (HealthOverviewPage.tsx:283,322), which deliberately carry no interval. So hovering those two rail items spends a network request warming a slot the owner does not see, and the slot they do see stays cold. (Distinct from the deferred bu-zs4at, which is about query-string filters on /timeline links; this is hero-key mismatch on unfiltered static routes and has an observable consumer today — the rail itself.)
findings.evidence: frontend/src/lib/shell-capability.ts:141,158; frontend/src/hooks/use-spend.ts:81; frontend/src/pages/SpendPage.tsx:2619,2828,2839; frontend/src/pages/HealthOverviewPage.tsx:283,322
findings.taxonomy_shape: NEW: warm-the-wrong-slot — a prefetch contract that names a cache key but is never bound to the key the destination's first frame actually reads, so the mechanism reports success while paying cost for nothing

findings.title: Intent prefetch is split in two: rows warm data but never the chunk; the rail warms both; nothing enforces parity
findings.detail: There are two near-identical intent hooks with the same 120ms debounce, deliberately not shared (use-prefetch-on-intent.ts:30 `PREFETCH_INTENT_DELAY_MS = 120`; use-route-chunk-prefetch-on-intent.ts:26 `ROUTE_CHUNK_PREFETCH_INTENT_DELAY_MS = 120`; the rationale is documented at use-route-chunk-prefetch-on-intent.ts:10-16). The consequence is uneven adoption nobody can see: Sidebar calls both (Sidebar.tsx:250-251, 394-395, 770-771, 917-918); EntityFinder calls the data hook and then reaches around it to `resolveRouteChunkLoader` inline (EntityFinder.tsx:457-466); RowLink (RowLink.tsx:72), DisclosureRow (DisclosureRow.tsx:88) and SessionTable (SessionTable.tsx:94) call the data hook ONLY. So the dominant in-page navigation gesture — hovering or focusing a table row on Sessions, Timeline, Notifications, Audit Log, Memory, Entities — warms the query and leaves the route chunk to a cold network round trip after the click. The inverse also holds for rail items whose capability has no warmup (finding 4): chunk warm, data cold. No test or lint asserts that a site attaching one hook attaches the other.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/hooks/use-prefetch-on-intent.ts:30,82-91; frontend/src/hooks/use-route-chunk-prefetch-on-intent.ts:10-16,26; frontend/src/components/ui/RowLink.tsx:72; frontend/src/components/ui/DisclosureRow.tsx:88; frontend/src/components/sessions/SessionTable.tsx:94; frontend/src/components/layout/Sidebar.tsx:250-251; frontend/src/components/layout/EntityFinder.tsx:457-466
findings.taxonomy_shape: built twice, unified never (run 11 theme) — new instance: two halves of one gesture (warm the code, warm the data) split across two registries with no parity seam

findings.title: Stale-while-revalidate is a telemetry-only convention: every butler-domain list blanks to a skeleton on each filter change
