findings.detail: `placeholderData: (prev) => prev` plus `FetchingDim` is the codebase's documented never-blank contract (components/ui/fetching-dim.tsx:1-13, extracted by the same audit that built the primitive). It appears in 17 files, all on the telemetry/ops side: sessions, timeline, audit-log, notifications, approvals, ingestion, entities, contacts, qa, calendar, search, butler-logs, chronicles-briefing, finance (partial). It appears in none of the butler-domain hooks: `use-health.ts` has 13 `["health-*", params]`-keyed queries with no placeholder (e.g. useMeasurements at :88-93, useMeasurementTrend at :106-113), and neither do `use-memory.ts` (useEpisodes :89-94), `use-education.ts`, `use-travel.ts`, `use-owntracks.ts`, `use-home.ts`, `use-system.ts`, `use-schedules.ts`. `use-issues.ts:45-48` keys on `{ window }`, so flipping the Issues page's window toggle re-keys the query, drives `isLoading` true, and `QueryBoundary` (priority loading > error > empty) swaps the whole populated list for a skeleton and back — a full blank cycle on a control the owner uses to compare two windows. `FetchingDim` itself is used in only 6 pages.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/ui/fetching-dim.tsx:1-13; 17 files contain placeholderData, 0 of them in the domain hooks; frontend/src/hooks/use-health.ts:88-93,106-113; frontend/src/hooks/use-memory.ts:89-94; frontend/src/hooks/use-issues.ts:44-50; frontend/src/components/ui/query-boundary.tsx:11-21 (loading beats data)
findings.taxonomy_shape: primitives built once, generalized nowhere — split along the telemetry/domain seam, which is also the seam the run-11 dossier keeps finding

findings.title: No work-in-progress primitive exists: the chat composer and 16 textarea dialogs destroy typed input on close, and only one dialog in the app guards dismissal
findings.detail: The interaction-speed bar names this the top-severity class: "Context survives: navigation, refresh, and failure preserve typed input... Destroying work-in-progress is a top-severity defect — worse than any latency finding." ChatPanel holds the composer text in plain component state (`const [inputValue, setInputValue] = useState("")`, ChatPanel.tsx:92) with no persistence anywhere in the file. FloatingChatWidget mounts its panel only while open (`{open && <WidgetPanel onClose={closeWidget} />}`, FloatingChatWidget.tsx:856) and documents the unmount-on-close lifecycle at :25-29 — so Esc, the close button, or navigating away silently deletes whatever the owner had typed but not sent. Sixteen files render a `<Textarea>` (health MeasurementForm/MedicationForm/ConditionForm/SymptomForm/MealForm/ResearchForm, ScheduleForm, create-rule-dialog, EntityVerbRail, EpisodeDrawer, ButlerStateTab, ButlerMcpTab, StateBrowser, SettingsModelsPage, CalendarWorkspacePage, MessageInput); none persists a draft, and grepping the whole tree for `onInteractOutside` / `onPointerDownOutside` / `onEscapeKeyDown` returns exactly one hit (MergeCompareDialog.tsx:429), so every other form dialog dismisses on a stray backdrop click and takes the content with it. Send *failure* is handled well by comparison (the failed text is retained as `failedText`, ChatPanel.tsx:551-556) — which shows the team knows the rule and simply has no primitive to apply it with.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/chat/ChatPanel.tsx:92,569-572; frontend/src/components/chat/FloatingChatWidget.tsx:25-29,856; 16 files matching `<Textarea`; only frontend/src/components/relationship/MergeCompareDialog.tsx:429 guards dismissal; frontend/src/components/ui/dialog.tsx (no dirty-state guard); th-design/subskills/interaction-speed §Input integrity
findings.taxonomy_shape: NEW: no-draft-spine — the system has a durable ledger for everything the *butler* produces and no persistence at all for what the *owner* is midway through typing

findings.title: No token home for interaction latency: the debounce constant is copy-pasted three times and the intent delay twice
findings.detail: `lib/poll-policy.ts` exists precisely because a bare numeric interval hides intent, and `eslint.config.js:217-237` enforces it. There is no equivalent for the other half of interaction timing. `const FREE_TEXT_DEBOUNCE_MS = 300` is declared verbatim three separate times (AuditLogPage.tsx:22, SessionsPage.tsx:37, NotificationsPage.tsx:43); the 120ms intent debounce is declared twice under two names (use-prefetch-on-intent.ts:30, use-route-chunk-prefetch-on-intent.ts:26); and ad-hoc literals live at ConversationList.tsx:135 (300), CalendarWorkspacePage.tsx:2930 (400), use-entities.ts:281 (200), use-search.ts:10 (300), plus bare `setTimeout(..., 1500)` for the chat interrupt handoff (ChatPanel.tsx:542). Whether a filter feels instant is therefore a per-page accident with no reviewable rule and no seam to change it fleet-wide.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/AuditLogPage.tsx:22; frontend/src/pages/SessionsPage.tsx:37; frontend/src/pages/NotificationsPage.tsx:43; frontend/src/hooks/use-prefetch-on-intent.ts:30; frontend/src/hooks/use-route-chunk-prefetch-on-intent.ts:26; frontend/src/hooks/use-entities.ts:281; frontend/src/hooks/use-search.ts:10; frontend/src/lib/poll-policy.ts (the pattern that exists for the other half)
findings.taxonomy_shape: built once, generalized never — the token+lint pattern was proven for polling and never extended to the interaction timings the owner actually feels

findings.title: Cold-path first request on two rail destinations measured 4.9s and 7.1s against an idle dev stack
findings.detail: The very first GET of /api/audit-log?limit=20 after an idle period returned in 7.15s and /api/issues?limit=20 in 4.89s; repeat requests settled at 0.41-0.45s and 0.06-0.08s respectively. Both routes are keyboard chords in the shell (`a` and `i`, shell-capability.ts:152,150), both have no `queryWarmup`, and both land on the generic `RouteSuspense` skeleton with no elapsed-time or honest-progress affordance — so a first visit after a quiet period can present as a multi-second blank with nothing distinguishing it from a hang. I did not isolate the cause (plan cache, connection warm, or a genuinely unbounded scan), so the mechanism is inferred; the measurement itself is live.
findings.evidence: live: first-hit http://127.0.0.1:42200/api/audit-log?limit=20 = 7.147s, /api/issues?limit=20 = 4.892s; steady state 0.412-0.447s / 0.059-0.080s; frontend/src/lib/shell-capability.ts:150,152 (chords, no warmup); frontend/src/components/layout/RouteSuspense.tsx:19-41
findings.taxonomy_shape: NEW: cold-path invisibility — latency budgets are reasoned about at steady state only, and the >1s branch of the budget table ("progress is visible, say what's happening") has no implementation anywhere in the route frame

moves.title: Coalesced snapshot replay + a replay budget the test suite enforces
moves.why: vision.md non-negotiable 4 (the daemon is deterministic infrastructure) and the north star's five-second fleet verification both die at first paint if the shell spends its opening tick issuing 598 cache invalidations. Owner-visible payoff: the dashboard's first frame and every reconnect stop competing with themselves; a reconnect after a network blip becomes a single reconciling refresh instead of a several-hundred-call storm plus 200 subscriber callbacks.
moves.manifesto: Serves the fleet-wide honesty doctrine in about/heart-and-soul/architecture.md (daemon-deterministic, connectors as cost boundary) applied to the client: a liveness mechanism must not itself be the dominant cost. Implies a `dashboard-shell` spec amendment adding a replay-coalescing clause next to the existing bus-aware-polling clause (openspec/specs/dashboard-shell/spec.md:711-717).
moves.integration_points: Mechanism home: `frontend/src/hooks/event-cache-registry.ts` gains `applyFleetEventBatch(qc, events)` — reduce the batch to a per-type set (carrying the union of `approval_id` / `butler`+`session_id` keys seen) and run each patch exactly once. `frontend/src/hooks/use-event-stream.ts:216-224` calls it for the snapshot branch instead of looping; `frontend/src/lib/event-bus.tsx` gains a `dispatchBatch` so subscribers receive one replayed batch rather than N calls. Server side, `src/butlers/api/routers/events.py:79` gets a per-type cap on the replayed slice (the 200-event ring is 199 duplicates of one type today). Spec: openspec/specs/dashboard-shell/spec.md §fleet event bus.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: connect → one coalesced apply, ≤ (#distinct types × keys-per-type) invalidations regardless of ring size. Failure: a malformed event in the batch is skipped without aborting the batch (same tolerance as today's `isFleetEvent` guard). Concurrency: a live event arriving mid-replay is applied after the batch, never before, so ordering is preserved. Idempotence: invalidation is idempotent by construction; coalescing changes only the count. Rollback: keep `applyFleetEvent` exported and unchanged for the live-event path, so reverting is a one-line swap in use-event-stream.ts.
moves.slice_plan: Slice 1: `applyFleetEventBatch` + unit test asserting a synthetic 200×ingestion snapshot yields exactly 3 invalidations. Slice 2: wire the snapshot branch and `dispatchBatch`. Slice 3: server-side per-type ring cap + a first-connect flag so the very first connect (nothing can have been missed) skips replay entirely and only seeds `lastEventAt`.
moves.verification: New test in `frontend/src/hooks/event-cache-registry.coverage.test.ts`: build a 200-event snapshot with the live composition (199 ingestion + 1 chronicles), run the batch, assert `invalidateQueries` call count ≤ 5 (currently 598) — a behavior-executing budget assertion at the real seam, not a snapshot. Second test: a snapshot mixing all 8 cache-affecting types invalidates every key the manifest says it must (reuse EVENT_CACHE_COVERAGE_MANIFEST). Re-probe the live socket after landing and confirm the measured call count.

moves.title: Bus coverage becomes a declared token, and the coverage test closes the direction it currently disclaims
moves.why: `use-bus-aware-poll-interval.ts:14-18` grants a 10× cadence relaxation on the strength of a claim no seam checks, and five keys — including Fleet Halt's `["dispatch-attempts"]` — took it without coverage. The north star's 'failure never impersonates health' applies to freshness: a surface that reads Live and is five minutes stale is health impersonating itself. Owner-visible payoff: the halt banner, delegation ledger, healing dispatches and domain-event panel become as fresh as they look, or visibly admit their own cadence.
moves.manifesto: Directly serves the run-11 theme the dossier already named (writer's clock impersonating world's clock) and the dashboard-shell spec's own bus-aware-polling requirement (openspec/specs/dashboard-shell/spec.md:711-717), which today is satisfiable by cadence alone. The spec clause needs the coverage precondition written into it.
moves.integration_points: Mechanism home: `frontend/src/hooks/event-cache-manifest.ts` exports a `BusCoverage` token per manifest row; `frontend/src/hooks/use-bus-aware-poll-interval.ts` changes signature to `useBusAwarePollInterval(coverage: BusCoverage)` so the call site must name the row that justifies it. Affected call sites: use-fleet-halt.ts:94, use-domain-events.ts:19,28, use-delegation.ts:17, use-healing.ts:18 (uncovered — must either gain a bus event or drop to an honest own-cadence constant) plus the 14 covered sites which simply name their existing row. Enforcement seam: `frontend/src/hooks/event-cache-registry.coverage.test.ts` (whose header at :16-19 currently declines this) gains a source-scanning test; `frontend/eslint.config.js` bans the zero-arg call.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: a covered hook names its row and behaves identically. Failure: an uncovered hook fails to typecheck, forcing an explicit decision. Concurrency: none — this is a compile/lint-time contract. Idempotence: n/a. Rollback: the token is a phantom type over the existing number; reverting is deleting the parameter.
moves.slice_plan: Slice 1: token type + manifest row ids, migrate the 14 already-covered call sites (mechanical). Slice 2: source-scan test that every `useBusAwarePollInterval(` argument resolves to a manifest row whose queryKey prefixes the call site's key. Slice 3: resolve the five uncovered keys — `dispatch-attempts` and `healing-dispatch-events` ride the existing `spend`/`issue` patches with added registry lines and manifest rows; `delegation-ledger` and the two domain-event keys drop to a named local constant until move 3 gives them a real event.
moves.verification: Extend event-cache-registry.coverage.test.ts with a parse-and-assert sweep over `frontend/src/hooks/*.ts` + `pages/*.tsx`: every `useBusAwarePollInterval` call site's owning `queryKey` must be prefix-covered by its named manifest row. A deliberately-uncovered fixture hook must make the test fail. Plus a rendering test that `useFleetHaltStatus` refetches within one tick of a synthetic `spend` bus event.

moves.title: Domain rows on the fleet bus: bridge public.domain_events into the dashboard socket so butler surfaces stop polling blind
moves.why: This is the feature half. Today the fleet bus carries only infrastructure (session, spend, approval, notification, issue, ingestion) plus calendar and chronicles (src/butlers/api/routers/events.py:60-74); every butler DOMAIN surface — health, memory, education, travel, finance, home, entities, decisions — is poll-only on nine differently-valued local constants (HEALTH_POLL_MS 30s, FINANCE_POLL_MS 60s, TRAVEL_POLL_MS 60s, EDUCATION_POLL_MS 30s, MEMORY_POLL_MS 30s, SYSTEM_POLL_MS 60s, …). The substrate to fix this already shipped: `public.domain_events` is an append-only publish log with a namespaced `<butler>.<event>` vocabulary and exactly one insert choke point. Owner-visible payoff: a measurement the Health butler records, a fact Memory writes, a trip Travel books appears on the open dashboard in the same beat it happens, instead of up to a minute later — the fleet becomes something you can watch, not something you refresh.
moves.manifesto: Serves vision.md's 'shared situational awareness' and non-negotiable 7 (transport is not the butler's business — the butler already publishes a domain event; only the dashboard's transport changes). Distinct from bu-d3k9e (domain-event contracts lack an *operator* surface) — this is domain events as a *freshness* transport for existing surfaces. Needs an amendment to openspec/specs/dashboard-shell/spec.md's bus clause and a delta on openspec/changes/domain-event-bus.
moves.integration_points: Producer: `src/butlers/core/domain_events.py:95-110` (the single INSERT) also calls `publish_fleet_event(pool, "domain", {"event_type": ..., "source_butler": ...})` — same LISTEN/NOTIFY bridge every daemon-side producer already uses (src/butlers/fleet_events.py:41, src/butlers/api/fleet_events_bridge.py). Registry: `src/butlers/api/routers/events.py:60` adds `"domain"` to EVENT_TYPES. Consumer: `frontend/src/hooks/event-cache-registry.ts` gains a `domainPatch` driven by a namespaced map `{ "health.*": [["health-measurements"], …], "memory.*": [["memory-episodes"], …] }`; `frontend/src/hooks/event-cache-manifest.ts` gains one row per domain event type. Hooks in use-health.ts / use-memory.ts / use-education.ts / use-travel.ts / use-finance.ts / use-home.ts move from their bespoke `*_POLL_MS` onto the (now-tokened, per move 2) bus-aware cadence.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: butler publishes → NOTIFY → WS `domain` envelope → namespaced patch invalidates only that domain's keys → the open page updates without a poll. Failure: NOTIFY drop is non-fatal (existing convention at fleet_events.py:94) and the bus-aware fallback returns the surface to 30s polling, so a dead bridge degrades to today's behavior, never to silence. Concurrency: many butlers publishing at once coalesce through move 1's batch path. Idempotence: invalidation only; no client state is derived from the payload. Rollback: remove `"domain"` from EVENT_TYPES and the hooks fall back to their own constants (keep them, do not delete).
moves.slice_plan: Slice 1: emit `domain` from the single insert choke point + EVENT_TYPES entry, no consumer (safe, inert). Slice 2: namespaced patch map + manifest rows for one butler (Health) and migrate use-health.ts's 13 queries; measure. Slice 3: Memory, Education, Travel, Finance, Home. Slice 4: retire the per-domain `*_POLL_MS` constants that are now redundant, leaving the bus-aware fallback as the only cadence.
moves.verification: Backend: a test asserting `publish_domain_event_once` produces exactly one `domain` fleet envelope carrying `event_type` and `source_butler`, and that a failed NOTIFY does not fail the insert. Frontend: manifest-driven coverage rows (`health.measurement_recorded` → `["health-measurements"]`) executed by the existing coverage test, so drift is caught the same way it is for session/spend. End-to-end: with the dev stack up, publish a domain event and confirm the WS envelope arrives (read-side probe, same method used to measure the 200-event snapshot).

moves.title: One navigation-intent primitive: warm the chunk and the data from a single gesture, everywhere
moves.why: The two halves of 'the owner is about to go there' were built separately and adopted unevenly: rows warm data only, the rail warms both, the palette reaches around the abstraction to do it by hand. The doctrine bar (interaction-speed §Optimism and caching, 'preload what the user will probably want next') is met by neither half alone. Owner-visible payoff: hovering or arrow-keying to any row, rail item, or palette result makes the destination's first frame real content rather than a skeleton — the keyboard-first path in particular stops paying a chunk round-trip after Enter.
moves.manifesto: Serves docs/frontend/purpose-and-single-pane.md's single-pane promise and the north star's 'every consequential clause is a door': a door that takes 500ms to open is a door the owner learns not to use. No manifesto amendment needed.
moves.integration_points: Mechanism home: new `frontend/src/hooks/use-nav-intent.ts` returning one handler bundle that, on intent, calls both `resolveRouteChunkLoader` (lib/route-chunk-registry.ts) and `resolvePrefetchTarget` (lib/prefetch-registry.ts) — both already project from the same `lib/shell-capability.ts` manifest, so this is unifying two projections of one source, not inventing a third. Call sites migrated: components/ui/RowLink.tsx:72, components/ui/DisclosureRow.tsx:88, components/sessions/SessionTable.tsx:94, components/layout/Sidebar.tsx:250-251/394-395/770-771/917-918, components/layout/EntityFinder.tsx:457-466 (deleting its inline loader call). Enforcement seam: `frontend/eslint.config.js` `no-restricted-imports` forbidding `use-prefetch-on-intent` / `use-route-chunk-prefetch-on-intent` outside `use-nav-intent.ts`.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: pointer pause ≥ intent delay, or focus, warms both resources; click/Enter calls `warmNow` first so a pending timer cannot be cancelled by activation (preserve the existing guarantee at use-prefetch-on-intent.ts:95-101). Failure: chunk-load rejection stays swallowed (never surfaces near navigation, per use-route-chunk-prefetch-on-intent.ts:12-15); query prefetch failure is ignored, and the page's own query re-fetches normally. Concurrency: a pointer sweep across a dense list fires nothing — one shared timer, cancelled on leave and on unmount. Idempotence: `prefetchQuery` and dynamic `import()` are both natively deduped. Rollback: the two old hooks stay as thin re-exports for one release.
moves.slice_plan: Slice 1: `use-nav-intent.ts` + tests, both old hooks re-implemented on top of it. Slice 2: migrate RowLink / DisclosureRow / SessionTable (the biggest win — every table row). Slice 3: migrate Sidebar and EntityFinder, delete EntityFinder's inline loader call. Slice 4: lint rule + delete the old hooks.
moves.verification: Component test: render a RowLink to `/sessions/abc`, fire pointerenter, advance 120ms fake timers, assert BOTH the capability's loader was invoked AND `queryClient.prefetchQuery` was called with the capability's warmup key. Second test: pointerenter+pointerleave inside the debounce fires neither. Third: the lint rule fails a fixture importing the retired hook directly.

moves.title: Warmup becomes a required, hero-bound clause of every shell capability
moves.why: 38 of 46 destinations declare no warmup and two of the eight that do warm a key their page never paints first. Because the field is optional, absence is invisible in review and no one can tell whether a route was considered and refused or simply forgotten. Owner-visible payoff: with move 4's unified intent gesture in place, every rail item, row and palette result the owner touches arrives with its hero data already in cache — a 100-550ms skeleton (measured) becomes content.
moves.manifesto: Serves the Dispatch 'as if built by one hand' clause: today a destination's responsiveness depends on whether someone remembered it. Implies a normative clause in openspec/specs/dashboard-shell/spec.md alongside the existing staleTime/poll clauses (:53-56, :711-717): every capability declares a first-paint warmup or a recorded refusal.
moves.integration_points: Mechanism home: `frontend/src/lib/shell-capability.ts` — make `queryWarmup` non-optional, typed as `WarmupResolver | NoWarmup`, where `NO_WARMUP(reason: string)` is the explicit refusal. Bind hero keys by extracting each page's initial query params to a shared module (the pattern `lib/entity-detail-query.ts` already establishes and shell-capability.ts:14 already imports) so the page and the capability import the SAME constant — `lib/spend-query.ts` (`cost-summary` initial window), `lib/health-overview-query.ts`, `lib/approvals-query.ts`, `lib/decisions-query.ts`, `lib/notifications-query.ts`, `lib/issues-query.ts`, `lib/audit-log-query.ts`, `lib/ingestion-query.ts`, `lib/qa-query.ts`. `DEFAULT_QUERY_STALE_TIME_MS` (shell-capability.ts:76) should import from `lib/query-client.ts` rather than restate 30_000. Enforcement seam: new `frontend/src/lib/shell-capability.warmup.test.ts`.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: hovering a rail item pre-seeds the destination's hero key at the same staleTime the page uses, so the page's own `useQuery` resolves from cache with zero network on first paint. Failure: a warmup fetch that rejects is swallowed; the page's query runs normally. Concurrency: a warmup racing the page's own mount is deduped by react-query on the identical key — which is exactly what the hero-binding guarantees. Idempotence: prefetch is idempotent. Rollback: `NO_WARMUP` on every capability restores today's behavior exactly.
moves.slice_plan: Slice 1: make the field required, fill every existing gap with `NO_WARMUP("not yet audited")`, add the completeness test — the debt becomes visible in one commit with zero behavior change. Slice 2: fix the two mis-bound warmups (/spend → cost-summary via a shared window constant; /health → the briefing key) and add the first-paint identity test. Slice 3: warm the six measured-slow rail destinations (/ingestion 0.55s, /audit-log 0.42s, /butlers-board 0.18s, /decisions 0.14s, /notifications 0.11s, /qa 0.11s). Slice 4: the remainder; delete every `NO_WARMUP("not yet audited")` or convert it to a real recorded reason.
moves.verification: `shell-capability.warmup.test.ts`: (a) every capability has a resolver or a `NO_WARMUP` carrying a non-empty reason; (b) for each warmed static route, render the page inside a QueryClient pre-seeded with ONLY the warmup's key+value and assert zero fetches fire for that key on first paint — a behavior-executing hero-identity check that would fail today for /spend and /health; (c) `DEFAULT_QUERY_STALE_TIME_MS` equals the query-client default by import, not by coincidence.

moves.title: Never-blank as an enforced list contract, not a telemetry convention
moves.why: The bar is explicit: 'A blank screen that could have shown yesterday's data is a defect.' The codebase agrees and built the primitive; it then applied it to the ops half and skipped the butler-domain half entirely, so flipping a window toggle on Issues or a type filter on Measurements throws away a populated table and shows a skeleton. Owner-visible payoff: comparison — the single most common thing an owner does with a filter — stops destroying the thing being compared.
moves.manifesto: Serves the north star clause that staleness never wears current-data authority *in both directions*: the honest answer to 'refetching' is dimmed previous data plus an `aria-busy` marker (which `FetchingDim` already renders), not a blank. Fits openspec/specs/dashboard-shell/spec.md §loading states (:32).
moves.integration_points: Mechanism home: new `frontend/src/hooks/use-list-query.ts` — a thin `useQuery` wrapper that forces `placeholderData: (prev) => prev` and returns `{ ...query, isRefreshing }` (isFetching && !isLoading) for direct hand-off to `components/ui/fetching-dim.tsx`. Migrate: hooks/use-health.ts (13 queries), use-memory.ts, use-education.ts, use-travel.ts, use-owntracks.ts, use-home.ts, use-system.ts, use-schedules.ts, use-issues.ts:44-50, use-decisions.ts. Enforcement seam: `frontend/eslint.config.js`, a new `no-restricted-syntax` block modelled on the poll-policy rule at :217-237 — a `useQuery` whose `queryKey` array references an identifier named `params`/`filters`/`window` must also set `placeholderData`.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: filter change keeps the previous rows, dims them, swaps in new rows when they land — no layout shift, no skeleton. Failure: an errored refetch must still reach `QueryBoundary`'s error branch and must NOT render stale rows as current — so the wrapper surfaces `isError` unchanged and callers keep the error > data priority (components/ui/query-boundary.tsx:11-21). Never apply to a value where stale misleads: any balance/permission read opts out explicitly (the bar's own exception). Concurrency: react-query already discards a superseded key's response. Idempotence: n/a. Rollback: per-hook, one option.
moves.slice_plan: Slice 1: `use-list-query.ts` + the ESLint rule in warn mode, so the gap is enumerated. Slice 2: migrate use-issues.ts (the proven window-toggle blank) and wire FetchingDim on IssuesPage. Slice 3: use-health.ts's 13 queries + the six /health/* trackers. Slice 4: memory / education / travel / home / system / schedules; flip the rule to error.
moves.verification: Behavior test per migrated surface: render with filter A, wait for rows, change to filter B, assert the A rows are still in the DOM with `aria-busy="true"` on the wrapper and that no skeleton testid appears — run first against use-issues.ts's window toggle, where it fails today. Plus `poll-policy-eslint.test.ts`-style fixture tests for the new rule (a param-keyed useQuery without placeholderData errors; one with it passes; a balance-style opt-out with the documented disable comment passes).

moves.title: A draft spine: the owner's unsent words survive close, navigation and reload
moves.why: The interaction-speed bar puts this above every latency finding, and the app has no primitive for it at all — the chat composer lives in state that unmounts on close (ChatPanel.tsx:92 / FloatingChatWidget.tsx:856), sixteen textarea dialogs persist nothing, and exactly one dialog in the tree guards outside-click dismissal. Owner-visible payoff: half-typed messages to a butler, half-filled medication and meal entries, half-written rule descriptions stop vanishing on a stray backdrop click, an Esc, or a navigation — the single most consequential trust repair in this lens.
moves.manifesto: Serves vision.md's sovereignty framing (the owner's data includes what they are midway through writing) and the north star's 'nothing fabricated' read in reverse: silently discarding owner input is the destructive twin of fabricating it. Implies a clause in openspec/specs/dashboard-shell/spec.md and openspec/specs/dashboard-chat-ui/spec.md: composers and form dialogs preserve unsent input across unmount.
moves.integration_points: Mechanism home: new `frontend/src/lib/draft-store.ts` (namespaced, debounced localStorage with TTL and quota-safe try/catch, following the exact conventions in `lib/local-settings.ts` and `lib/recents-store.ts`) plus `frontend/src/hooks/use-draft.ts` returning `[value, setValue, { restored, discard }]`. Wire into `components/chat/ChatPanel.tsx:92` keyed by conversation id (fixing a second latent bug: today one `inputValue` follows the owner across conversation switches, so text typed for conversation A can be sent to B), `components/chat/FloatingChatWidget.tsx`, and every `<Textarea>`-bearing dialog. `components/ui/dialog.tsx` gains an opt-in `dirty` prop that attaches `onInteractOutside`/`onEscapeKeyDown` guards — today only components/relationship/MergeCompareDialog.tsx:429 does this by hand. Enforcement seam: `frontend/eslint.config.js` — a `<Textarea>` inside a `DialogContent` must be bound to a `useDraft` value or carry an explicit documented disable.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: type, close, reopen → the text is back with a quiet 'draft restored' affordance and a one-click discard. Send success → draft cleared. Send failure → draft retained (aligning with the already-correct `failedText` path at ChatPanel.tsx:551-556, which this subsumes). Concurrency: two tabs writing the same key — last-write-wins with a timestamp, and a restored draft is always shown as restorable rather than silently merged. Idempotence: writes are debounced and keyed; re-restoring the same draft is a no-op. Rollback: `use-draft` degrades to plain useState when storage throws (private browsing, quota) — never a thrown error, never a lost keystroke in the happy case. Never persist a secret: `components/secrets/*` and any password-typed input are excluded by an explicit denylist in draft-store.ts.
moves.slice_plan: Slice 1: draft-store + use-draft + the dialog `dirty` guard, with tests. Slice 2: the chat composer, keyed per conversation (fixes cross-conversation bleed at the same time). Slice 3: the six health forms + ScheduleForm + create-rule-dialog. Slice 4: EntityVerbRail, EpisodeDrawer, ButlerStateTab, StateBrowser, CalendarWorkspacePage; then the ESLint rule to error, with the secrets denylist asserted by test.
moves.verification: Behavior tests at the real seam: (a) type into FloatingChatWidget, close (unmount), remount, assert the text is present and the restore affordance is announced; (b) type into MeasurementForm, fire a backdrop pointerdown, assert the dialog stays open and prompts; (c) successful submit clears the stored key; (d) a storage-throwing environment still renders and accepts input (no throw); (e) a fixture component storing a secrets-page field fails the denylist test.

moves.title: Interaction-timing tokens with the same lint seam polling already has
moves.why: `lib/poll-policy.ts` + the ESLint rule at eslint.config.js:217-237 proved the pattern: name the number, state the intent, enforce it repo-wide. The other half of interaction timing — debounces, intent delays, handoff timeouts — has neither, so `FREE_TEXT_DEBOUNCE_MS = 300` is copy-pasted three times and the 120ms intent delay twice under two names. Owner-visible payoff: how responsive a filter feels becomes one reviewable decision instead of a per-page accident, and tuning it is one edit.
moves.manifesto: Serves the Dispatch 'as if built by one hand' clause and the engineering bar's single-source-of-truth expectation. No manifesto amendment; a short clause in openspec/specs/dashboard-design-language/spec.md naming the token file as the source of interaction timings.
moves.integration_points: Mechanism home: new `frontend/src/lib/interaction-timing.ts`, sibling of `lib/poll-policy.ts`, exporting `FREE_TEXT_DEBOUNCE_MS`, `SEARCH_DEBOUNCE_MS`, `NAV_INTENT_DELAY_MS` (subsuming both 120ms constants once move 4 unifies the hooks), and `TRANSIENT_HANDOFF_MS` (ChatPanel.tsx:542's bare 1500). Call sites: AuditLogPage.tsx:22, SessionsPage.tsx:37, NotificationsPage.tsx:43, ConversationList.tsx:135, CalendarWorkspacePage.tsx:2930, use-entities.ts:281, use-search.ts:10, use-prefetch-on-intent.ts:30, use-route-chunk-prefetch-on-intent.ts:26. Enforcement seam: `frontend/eslint.config.js`, a `no-restricted-syntax` selector for `useDebounce(_, <numeric literal>)` and for numeric-literal `setTimeout` delays inside `src/components` and `src/pages`, worded like the existing poll-policy message.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: identical timing, one source. Failure: none — this is a naming/lint change with no runtime behavior delta unless a value is deliberately harmonized (call that out in the PR). Concurrency/idempotence: n/a. Rollback: revert the import.
moves.slice_plan: Slice 1: token file + migrate the three duplicate FREE_TEXT_DEBOUNCE_MS declarations. Slice 2: the remaining bespoke literals, harmonizing 200/300/400 into named tokens with a stated reason for any that stay distinct. Slice 3: the ESLint rule, with fixture tests mirroring `lib/poll-policy-eslint.test.ts`.
moves.verification: New `frontend/src/lib/interaction-timing-eslint.test.ts` in the shape of the existing `poll-policy-eslint.test.ts`: a fixture with `useDebounce(q, 300)` errors with the token message; one with `useDebounce(q, FREE_TEXT_DEBOUNCE_MS)` passes; a locally-declared named constant passes. Plus a grep-style test asserting no file outside interaction-timing.ts declares a `*_DEBOUNCE_MS` constant.

moves.title: Honest waiting above one second: an elapsed-aware route frame
moves.why: The budget table's >1s row ('progress is visible, completion is announced where the user is now') has no implementation anywhere: `RouteSuspense` renders one identical generic skeleton forever, with no elapsed cue and no distinction between a 100ms warm load and the 7.1s cold first hit of /api/audit-log I measured. A skeleton that never changes cannot tell the owner whether the system is working or wedged — which is the same failure mode as failure impersonating health, one layer down.
moves.manifesto: Serves the north star clause 'failure never impersonates health': an indefinite skeleton is health impersonating progress. Fits openspec/specs/dashboard-shell/spec.md §loading states (:32) as an added clause on long waits.
moves.integration_points: Mechanism home: `frontend/src/components/layout/RouteSuspense.tsx` — after a threshold (~1.2s) the frame adds an honest line naming the destination and the elapsed time, and after a second threshold offers a retry that remounts the boundary; it must never fabricate a progress bar. The destination's name comes free from `resolveShellCapability(pathname).label` (lib/shell-capability.ts:208), so this also gives the frame per-route identity without duplicating any registry. `frontend/src/lib/shell-announcer.ts` announces the long-wait transition once for assistive tech. Enforcement seam: `frontend/src/components/layout/RouteSuspense.test.tsx`.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path (<1.2s): pixel-identical to today, no flicker, no extra text. Slow path: at 1.2s the elapsed line appears; at ~8s a retry appears. Failure: a genuinely failed chunk load surfaces the retry rather than an eternal skeleton. Concurrency: a route change while the frame is showing resets the timers. Idempotence: retry remounts the lazy boundary; no duplicate fetch state survives. Rollback: one threshold constant set to Infinity restores today's behavior.
moves.slice_plan: Slice 1: elapsed threshold + destination label from the capability manifest, with fake-timer tests. Slice 2: retry affordance + announcer wiring. Slice 3: apply the same treatment to ButlerDetailPage's per-tab `Suspense` fallbacks (ButlerDetailPage.tsx:291-338), which today are bare skeletons with the same blind spot.
moves.verification: `RouteSuspense.test.tsx` with fake timers: under threshold renders exactly today's markup (snapshot-free assertion on absence of the elapsed node); past threshold renders the destination label and an elapsed value that advances; past the second threshold renders a retry whose activation remounts the child; the announcer is called exactly once per long wait, not per tick.

audits.jarvis_gap: Today the Dispatch language is a well-written spec (openspec/specs/dashboard-design-language/spec.md, 459 lines) whose *color-role* axis alone is genuinely governed — a typed registry (frontend/src/lib/visual-token-roles.ts), spec-parity tests, a contrast test suite (frontend/src/lib/contrast.test.ts), an eight-rule eslint guard, and a CI gate (.github/workflows/ci.yml frontend job). Everything else in the language is aspiration. The decisive mechanism is one file: `@theme inline` in frontend/src/index.css:374-489 registers Tailwind utilities for shadcn's vocabulary (background/foreground/card/muted/destructive/chart/sidebar/severity/permanence/categorical/tier) and for *zero* of the eleven core Dispatch tokens — `--red`, `--amber`, `--green`, `--red-text`, `--amber-text`, `--mfg`, `--dim`, `--border-soft`, `--border-strong`, `--bg-elev`, `--bg-deep` (verified: `grep -c "^\s*--color-$t:" index.css` returns 0 for all eleven). Likewise the registered type scale is a ratio-1.2 modular scale (index.css:280-286) with no member equal to four of the seven Dispatch type roles (Display 44px, Title 24px, Body 14px, Eyebrow 10px). Where the registry covers the role, drift is near zero — spacing is registered (index.css:354-365, 476-487) and there are only 15 arbitrary-px spacing sites fleet-wide. Where the registry omits the role, drift is enormous: 1,066 `text-[Npx]` sites across 21 distinct pixel values; 429 hand-rolled eyebrows across 10 distinct letter-spacings against one canonical `<Eyebrow>` used 83 times; 42 hand-rolled state-color background tints at 8 different alphas against `.attention-row` (index.css:735) used 9 times; 25+ distinct hover backgrounds against a spec that names one. The ideal is that the language is unreachable-by-accident: the token registry, not review discipline, makes the correct thing the shortest thing to type, and a generated visual inventory turns every remaining deviation into a reviewable CI diff. Today it is the opposite — the ergonomic path (`text-sm`, `text-destructive`, `<Badge variant="destructive">`, `rounded-md`, `hover:bg-muted`) is the non-Dispatch path, so every surface built by a different hand drifts by default, and the fleet-verification page paints its healthiest state in saturated green fills.
audits.live_verification: Dev stack read-side reachable: `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:42200/api/butlers` returned the butler roster (all `status: "ok"`), confirming the fleet API is up; `/api/connectors` 404s. No frontend dev server or preview is listening (probed 42201, 5173, 3000, 42210, 8080 — all connection-refused), so no rendered-DOM confirmation was possible. Every visual finding below is therefore source-confirmed by reading the decisive mechanism (index.css token definitions and the `@theme inline` registry, eslint.config.js selector lists, the component files themselves) plus reproducible grep counts, each with the command shown in the finding's detail. The one live-confirmed element is that the status vocabulary the API emits (`status` on /api/butlers) is a single string field with no presentational contract, which is what the five parallel status-badge dialects each re-interpret independently.

findings.title: @theme registers shadcn's vocabulary and none of Dispatch's — the token registry is the root cause of every type/color drift count in this report
findings.evidence: frontend/src/index.css:374-489 (@theme inline block); index.css:280-286 (--text-xs..3xl modular scale); index.css:462-468 (--font-size-* aliases); index.css:354-365 + 476-487 (spacing scale, the control case)
findings.taxonomy_shape: NEW: the registry omits the role — the design system's token registry exposes the vendor vocabulary it was scaffolded from, so every consumer of the project's own language must escape into arbitrary-value syntax, and the escape hatch becomes the dialect
findings.detail: Verified with `for t in red amber green mfg dim red-text amber-text border-soft border-strong bg-elev bg-deep; do grep -c "^\s*--color-$t:" index.css; done` → 0 for all eleven. The @theme block registers --color-background/foreground/card/popover/primary/secondary/muted/accent/destructive/border/input/ring/chart-1..5/sidebar-*/bg/fg/severity-*/permanence-*/categorical-1..12/role-*/state-unidentified/tier-1..6. The three canonical state colors the spec calls the entire state vocabulary, both AA-safe text variants minted by bu-86c4c.16/bu-f310e, the muted and tertiary neutrals, both border softness variants, and both surface elevations have no utility. Type is the same shape: --text-xs=0.694rem (11.1px), sm=0.833rem (13.3px), base=1rem, lg=1.2rem, xl=1.44rem, 2xl=1.728rem, 3xl=2.074rem — a ratio-1.2 modular scale in which the spec's Display (44px), Title (24px), Body (14px) and Eyebrow (10px) roles have no member at all, and no registered role bundles its mandated tracking/leading/family. The control case proves causation: spacing IS registered on the 4px scale, and `grep -roh "p[xytblr]\?-\[[0-9]*px\]" --include=*.tsx .` finds only 15 arbitrary spacing sites, while the unregistered type role produces 1,066 `text-[Npx]` sites across 166 files and 21 distinct pixel values (496×10px, 341×11px, 47×9.5px, 40×9px, 32×13px, 21×15px, 21×12px, 14×22px, 9×12.5px, 7×13.5px, 6×28px, 6×14px, 6×10.5px, 5×8px, 4×17px, 3×44px, 3×24px, 2×32px, 2×11.5px, 1×20px, 1×16px) alongside 1,626 legacy Tailwind text-xs/sm/base/lg/xl sites. Radius repeats it: --radius=0.625rem yields shadcn's 6/8/10/14/18px ramp, so the Dispatch 3px pill is hand-typed as `rounded-[3px]` 42 times, `rounded-[4px]` 10, `rounded-[2px]` 7, `rounded-[1px]` 10, beside rounded (250), rounded-full (146), rounded-md (106), rounded-sm (74), rounded-lg (26) — 13 radius values fleet-wide against a spec naming two.

findings.title: 170 `text-destructive` sites render error text below the light-mode AA floor the repo's own doctrine sets, because the AA-safe token has no utility and the failing alias does
findings.evidence: frontend/src/index.css:52 and :508 (`--destructive: var(--red)` in both themes); index.css:97 (light `--red: oklch(0.627 0.257 29.2)`); index.css:141-147 (`--red-text` comment: "Base --red at 3.84:1 against --bg is below the 4.5:1 AA floor"); frontend/src/lib/contrast.test.ts:260; frontend/src/components/ui/error-state.tsx:36 (`text-destructive/80`)
findings.taxonomy_shape: NEW: the fix landed as a token nobody can reach — an accessibility repair shipped as a new token while the unfixed alias kept the ergonomic spelling, so the fix's own call-site count grew instead of shrinking
findings.detail: Counts: `grep -rn "text-destructive" --include=*.tsx src | grep -v '\.test\.' | wc -l` → 170; `[var(--red-text)]` → 97; `[var(--red)]` → 52. bu-f310e minted --red-text because base --red measures 3.84:1 as text in light mode and was in use at ~57 sites; it repointed those 57. But `--destructive` is aliased straight to `var(--red)` (not --red-text) in both :root and .dark, and --destructive IS a registered Tailwind color while --red-text is not — so `text-destructive` is the shortest legal spelling of a red word and it now outnumbers the AA-safe spelling nearly 2:1. The contrast suite asserts the token values are correct (contrast.test.ts:260 explicitly blesses --red as "below the text AA floor by design") but nothing asserts that the alias is never used as text, so the guard passes while 170 sites fail the light-mode WCAG AA floor that the design-language spec's Purpose section binds as settled doctrine. ErrorState — the canonical error surface — compounds it at 0.8 alpha (error-state.tsx:36).

findings.title: Five parallel status-badge dialects render the same fleet tri-state with five shapes and five word lists; two of them live in the same file and deliberately disagree on wording
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/ingestion/StatusBadge.tsx:47-100 (filled pills) and :142-206 (RowStatus dot+word, with the comment at :126-140 stating the two word lists are "intentionally decoupled"); frontend/src/components/sessions/StatusBadge.tsx:42-88; frontend/src/components/butler-detail/ButlerStatusBadge.tsx:26-70; frontend/src/components/ui/live-status-badge.tsx:56-70; frontend/src/components/ui/StateDot.tsx (canonical, 18 usages)
findings.taxonomy_shape: built twice unified never
findings.detail: One canonical StateDot exists (ok/degraded/error/waiting, 18 `<StateDot` sites). Around it: (a) ingestion/StatusBadge renders 8 lifecycle states as filled/outline shadcn pills including `bg-[var(--green)] text-white` for 'ingested'; (b) ingestion/RowStatus renders the SAME 8 states as a 6px dot + mono word, with its own header comment acknowledging the design language forbids the fills its file-mate uses, and with ROW_STATUS_WORDS deliberately saying 'replay complete' where STATUS_LABELS says 'replayed' — the same event reads as two different words on two surfaces; (c) sessions/StatusBadge renders a rounded-md bordered chip with a dot for Success/Running/Cancelled but drops to a filled destructive Badge for Failed, so it is internally inconsistent; (d) ButlerStatusBadge says Up/Degraded/Down as filled-green / outline-amber / filled-red; (e) LiveStatusBadge says Live/Idle/Down/checking. Five shapes, five word lists, one concept. The API side offers no presentational contract to unify against — `curl http://127.0.0.1:42200/api/butlers` returns a bare `status` string (live-confirmed all 'ok').

findings.title: `.attention-row` — the single sanctioned exception to the no-background-fill rule — was built once and generalized never; 42 sites hand-roll their own tint at 8 alphas, only 1 pairs the mandated rail
findings.evidence: frontend/src/index.css:735-741 (.attention-row[data-tone] with 6%/5% tint + 2px rail); openspec/specs/dashboard-design-language/spec.md § State Color Discipline (4-7% red / 4-6% amber, "tint + rail travel together as a single signal unit"); frontend/src/pages/ApprovalsPage.tsx:404, :762; frontend/src/components/relationship/OwnerSetupBanner.tsx:244; frontend/src/components/ingestion/filters/PipelineGateDiagram.tsx:156,164
findings.taxonomy_shape: primitives built once generalized nowhere
findings.detail: `grep -rn "attention-row" --include=*.tsx src | grep -v test | wc -l` → 9 sites in 4 files (SettingsConsolePage, SpendPage, SettingsPermissionsPage, SpendVerdictOpener). Meanwhile `grep -rn "bg-\[var(--\(red\|amber\|green\)[^]]*)\]/" --include=*.tsx src | grep -v test | wc -l` → 42, at eight distinct alphas: /[0.04], /5, /10, /20, /30, /60, /90, plus a full-opacity `bg-[var(--amber)]` panel background at OwnerSetupBanner.tsx:244. None of the 42 is inside the spec's 4-7%/4-6% bounds except by accident; `grep -rn "border-l-2 border-l-\[var(--" src` finds exactly 1 paired rail (ApprovalsPage.tsx:404). PipelineGateDiagram paints 60%-alpha amber and red bars as chart geometry. The result is that the one visual signal the language reserves for 'a human must decide this now' is diluted across dozens of routine surfaces at arbitrary intensity, and the guard cannot see it: eslint.config.js:64 bans the *Tailwind-shade spelling* of a state color but not the *semantic* of a state color on a background.

findings.title: Eleven saturated-green filled pills announce healthy states across eight surfaces — the fleet-verification page is loudest when nothing is wrong
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/system/DriftTile.tsx:112, BackupTile.tsx:129, DeploymentTile.tsx:172, SecurityPostureTile.tsx:82; components/butler-detail/ButlerConfigTab.tsx:191, ButlerStatusBadge.tsx:33, ButlerModelOverridesTab.tsx:331, ButlerQaInvestigationsTab.tsx:195; components/schedules/ScheduleTable.tsx:194; components/notifications/notification-feed.tsx:83; components/ingestion/StatusBadge.tsx:51
findings.taxonomy_shape: NEW: calm is not the quiet state — the healthy branch of a status renderer is given the loudest treatment in the palette, inverting the composure doctrine exactly where five-second verification happens
findings.detail: `grep -rn "bg-\[var(--green)\][^\"']*text-white" --include=*.tsx src | grep -v test | wc -l` → 11. Four of them are the /system page's own tiles (Drift, Backup, Deployment, SecurityPosture) — the surface the north star designates for five-second fleet verification. Each violates three separate clauses simultaneously: § State Color Discipline ("never on background fills — foreground or border only", one exception which these are not), § Composure Doctrine rule 5 ("one affordance per signal"; a filled green pill is color + word), and § Interface Copy ("no celebration... no green-check moments — quiet success is the success state"). A healthy fleet therefore renders with more saturated color than a degraded one, since degraded states use outline-amber (ButlerStatusBadge.tsx:41).

findings.title: 429 hand-rolled eyebrows at 10 distinct letter-spacings; the eslint guard bans the named fork and misses the anonymous one — including inside the design system's own Section primitive
findings.evidence: frontend/eslint.config.js:132-152 (PRIMITIVE_REDECLARATION_SELECTORS matches only `FunctionDeclaration[id.name=/^(?:Eyebrow|Voice)$/]`); frontend/src/components/overview/Section.tsx:19-29 (inline eyebrow style object, not the canonical Eyebrow); frontend/src/components/ui/Eyebrow.tsx (canonical, 83 usages)
findings.taxonomy_shape: gates as metadata not enforcement
findings.detail: `grep -rn "uppercase" --include=*.tsx src | grep -v test | grep "tracking-" | wc -l` → 429 sites. Distinct trackings on those lines: tracking-[0.14em] 122 (the spec value), tracking-wide 66, tracking-widest 63, tracking-wider 44, tracking-[0.12em] 41, tracking-[0.08em] 31, tracking-[0.06em] 19, tracking-[0.10em] 18, tracking-[0.1em] 14, tracking-[0.04em] 11. Against `<Eyebrow` at 83 sites. The spec's most-repeated signature element ("Sections SHALL be titled with eyebrows — 10px / mono / uppercase / 0.14em") is therefore rendered at ten different letter-spacings across the fleet. bu-86c4c.6's guard closed the 7 named `function Eyebrow` forks but a hand-typed `text-[10px] font-mono uppercase tracking-[0.14em] text-muted-foreground` span is invisible to it — and components/overview/Section.tsx, itself a design-system primitive imported by 6 surfaces including DashboardPage and HealthOverviewPage, reimplements the eyebrow as an inline style object rather than importing Eyebrow. The type-role primitives that would fix this are effectively unadopted: `<Title` 3 usages, `<Display` 8, against 1,626 legacy text-xs/sm sites.

findings.title: Three icon dialects and no stroke-weight default: lucide ships at strokeWidth 2 everywhere, inline SVG uses six different weights, and 20 sites use Unicode text glyphs as icons — Sidebar.tsx mixes two of them in one rail
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/layout/NavIcon.tsx:152 (strokeWidth 1.25, 16-viewBox) vs frontend/src/components/layout/Sidebar.tsx:336, :691, :872 (strokeWidth 2, 24-viewBox chevrons, same file, same rail); frontend/src/components/layout/PageHeader.tsx:164,166 (inline 24-viewBox strokeWidth 2); openspec/specs/dashboard-design-language/spec.md § Iconography ("stroke-only at a single 1.25–1.5px weight, 16×16 viewBox... No emoji, ever")
findings.taxonomy_shape: NEW: no default at the vendor boundary — a third-party icon set is imported per-file with its own defaults intact, so the project's stated weight applies only where someone remembered to override it
findings.detail: 57 files import lucide-react (47 distinct icons); `grep -rn "lucide" index.css main.tsx App.tsx` finds no global stroke default, and only 5 call sites pass an explicit strokeWidth, so the overwhelming majority render at Lucide's default 2 — outside the spec's 1.25–1.5 band. `grep -rhoP 'strokeWidth=\{?"?[0-9.]+' --include=*.tsx src` over inline SVG returns six values: 2 (×11), 1.5 (×10), 1 (×5), 4 (×2), 3 (×1), 1.25 (×1). Sidebar.tsx — the one chrome element present on every surface — renders NavIcon at 1.25/16-viewBox next to hand-inlined chevrons at 2/24-viewBox. A third dialect: `grep -rnP "[\x{1F300}-\x{1FAFF}\x{2600}-\x{27BF}]" --include=*.tsx src | grep -v test | wc -l` → 20 sites using ✓ ✗ ✕ ⚠ ⚡ ⚙ ★ ◦ • ∅ ↗ ✎ as icons (SettingsModelsPage.tsx:1465,1473; EntityDetailPage.tsx:616,622; ConflictRadarBanner.tsx:217,245; EntityFinder.tsx:694,851,939; Provenance.tsx:167; secrets/passport/atoms.tsx:677; WhatBreaks.tsx:127). ⚠ and ⚡ carry emoji-presentation variants and render as color emoji on several platforms, which the spec forbids outright; ✓ is also a green-check moment the copy doctrine bans.

findings.title: The motion vocabulary has four entries; the codebase ships bouncing chat dots, a 2,200ms flash, 29 spinners and Radix zoom/slide, and the lint guard covers exactly one forbidden token
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/chat/TypingIndicator.tsx:9,14,19 (three `animate-bounce` dots with 0/150/300ms staggers); frontend/src/index.css:751-763 (@keyframes calendar-entry-flash, 2.2s); frontend/eslint.config.js:198-214 (ANIMATE_PULSE_SELECTORS — animate-pulse only); openspec/specs/dashboard-design-language/spec.md § Motion Vocabulary (four entries; "Forbidden: spring physics, bounce, parallax, scale-in, scale-on-hover, shimmer, skeleton-pulse, count-up animations, 'delight' of any kind")
findings.taxonomy_shape: gates as metadata not enforcement
findings.detail: `grep -roh "\banimate-[a-z-]*" --include=*.tsx --include=*.css src | sort | uniq -c` → animate-spin 29, animate-out 9, animate-in 9, animate-bounce 4 (3 real + 1 test assertion), animate-pulse 2 (both in comments — the ban held). Only animate-pulse is linted; bounce, which the spec forbids *by name*, ships in the chat surface's TypingIndicator inside a `rounded-2xl rounded-bl-sm bg-muted` speech bubble — the generic-chat-app idiom the spec's own thesis rejects ("a butler announcing, not a chatbot reporting"), and a radius (rounded-2xl = 18px) outside the fleet vocabulary. .calendar-entry-flash runs 2,200ms, eleven times the spec's longest budgeted transition. index.css:663-700 additionally defines a general-purpose three-step motion scale (--duration-fast/base/slow at 150/200/250ms with transition-fast/base/slow utilities) that the spec's four-entry table does not contain and does not authorize; 200 `transition-colors` sites consume it.

findings.title: Four `var(--…)` references in shipped components resolve to nothing, silently disabling a hover, a file-input background and a severity color
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/calendar/CalendarAgendaView.tsx:79,87 (`hover:bg-[var(--surface)]`); frontend/src/components/calendar/CalendarPortabilityDialog.tsx:228 (`file:bg-[var(--surface)]`); frontend/src/pages/CalendarWorkspacePage.tsx:1199 (`text-[var(--yellow)]`); frontend/src/index.css (neither --surface nor --yellow is defined; 205 tokens enumerated)
findings.taxonomy_shape: NEW: dead token reference — an undefined custom property fails silently to inherited/transparent, so a missing affordance looks like a design decision rather than a bug
findings.detail: Reproduced by extracting all 205 `--x:` definitions from index.css and diffing against every `var(--x)` reference in src/**/*.{ts,tsx}: the only non-test, non-Radix unresolved names are --surface (3 real sites) and --yellow (1). `background-color: var(--surface)` with --surface undefined is an invalid declaration, so CalendarAgendaView's two row hovers produce no visual change at all and the portability dialog's file button has no background. `--yellow` is a fourth state-color name that never existed; CalendarWorkspacePage.tsx:1199 returns `text-[var(--yellow)]` from what reads as a severity branch, so that branch renders in the inherited foreground and is indistinguishable from the neutral case. Nothing in the existing guard chain checks reference→definition resolution: scripts/visual-role-css-guard.mjs validates role *namespaces*, not existence.

findings.title: The Page shell is adopted by half the fleet; the other half loses breadcrumbs, the loading/error/empty triad and the route announcement, and re-invents the hover treatment 25 ways
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/ui/page.tsx:1-12 (imports Breadcrumbs, EmptyState, skeletons, `announce` from shell-announcer); 20 of 40 non-test pages import it (ApprovalsPage, CalendarWorkspacePage, DecisionsPage, EducationPage, HealthOverviewPage, IngestionConnectorsPage, IngestionFiltersPage, IngestionTimelinePage, MealsPage, MeasurementsPage, MedicationsPage, MemoryPage, QaInvestigationDetailPage, QaOverviewPage, QaPatrolDetailPage, SecretsPage, SettingsConsolePage, SettingsModelsPage, SettingsPermissionsPage, TimelinePage do not)
findings.taxonomy_shape: primitives built once generalized nowhere
findings.detail: Classified every non-test file in src/pages by whether it imports components/ui/page: 20 PAGE-SHELL, 20 OWN-SHELL. The shell owns four things nobody re-implements consistently: breadcrumb chrome, the archetype layout, the loading/error/empty triad, and `announce()` for route changes — `grep -rln shell-announcer src` shows only 5 files touch the announcer at all, so the 20 own-shell pages announce nothing on navigation. Downstream, the shared async-state primitives are barely adopted: EmptyState 15 files, ErrorState 4 files, against 80 hand-rolled `font-serif italic` empty lines across 57 files and 59 literal "No …"/"Nothing …" strings. Hover is the same story — the spec pins exactly one value (6% white / 5% black, no transform) and `grep -roh "hover:bg-[a-z0-9/.\[\]()-]*"` returns 25+ distinct treatments led by hover:bg-muted (24), hover:bg-muted/50 (15), /40 (9), /30 (9), hover:bg-foreground/5 (9), hover:bg-foreground/[0.06] (8), hover:bg-accent (7), hover:bg-foreground/[0.03] (5), hover:bg-foreground/[0.025] (2), plus a raw hover:bg-blue-700 that survives because the blue/purple guard is scoped to a 16-file allowlist (eslint.config.js BLUE_PURPLE_STATUS_AUDIT_FILES).

findings.title: Composure rule 4 — "if nothing is happening, the section drops its borders" — has no mechanism anywhere in the codebase
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/overview/Section.tsx:17-33 (renders eyebrow + children unconditionally; no emptiness branch despite the docstring citing the editorial archetype doctrine); openspec/specs/dashboard-design-language/spec.md § Composure Doctrine scenario "Quiet state removes chrome"
findings.taxonomy_shape: NEW: the doctrine clause with no primitive — a normative visual behavior is specified with a testable scenario but has no component that can express it, so conformance depends on each author hand-writing the branch
findings.detail: The spec has a scenario for it ("WHEN a section has no active content THEN the section renders either without borders or as a single serif-italic sentence"). The only Section primitive takes `{ eyebrow, children }` and always renders the eyebrow and a container, and is imported by DashboardPage, HealthOverviewPage, ChroniclesPage, RecentDaysIndex, ChroniclesDrilldownPanel and HealthLedgerIndex. Nothing in components/ui exposes a quiet-state variant. This is the clause that most directly implements 'earned calm' at the fleet-verification glance, and it is the one clause with no executable home — which is why the 80 hand-rolled serif-italic empty lines exist as one-off spans rather than as a primitive's quiet branch.

audits.ideal: A JARVIS-grade Dispatch is a language you cannot accidentally leave. Its token registry — one `@theme` block — exposes the project's own vocabulary as first-class utilities, so `text-body`, `text-eyebrow`, `text-title`, `text-red`, `text-dim`, `border-soft`, `radius-pill` are shorter to type than the shadcn or Tailwind spellings, and each type role carries its size, weight, tracking, leading and family as one indivisible unit. Roles that must never be composed freely (a state color on a background, an eyebrow's letter-spacing, an icon's stroke weight) are simply not expressible: the state palette exposes `attention-tint-red` at exactly 6% and nothing else, so the sanctioned exception is the only reachable fill. Every fleet concept has exactly one presentation registry — one status renderer reading one word list beside the API enum it renders, one icon component with the stroke weight baked in, one Page shell that owns breadcrumbs, the loading/error/empty triad and route announcement, one Section that drops its own chrome when nothing is happening, so a calm fleet literally renders calmer. Enforcement is layered the way this repo already knows how: a typed role registry with spec-parity tests (the pattern of `visual-token-roles.ts`), eslint selectors that ban the escape hatches once the correct path exists, a resolution guard that fails on any `var(--x)` with no definition, contrast tests that assert *call sites* rather than only token values, and — the missing keystone — a generated, committed, CI-diff-gated visual inventory that is the exact twin of `about/lay-and-land/frontend-copy-inventory.md`: every distinct font size, letter-spacing, radius, hover tint, state-color fill, icon stroke and motion class in the fleet, with counts and file:line, so drift arrives as a reviewable diff on the PR that introduces it instead of as an audit finding once a quarter. And because the system reports honestly on its own process everywhere else (the Process Status Pill requirement already establishes the register), that inventory feeds a /system tile: the fleet can say how far it has drifted from its own language, in numbers, without anyone running a grep.

moves.title: Make @theme speak Dispatch: register the seven type roles, the eleven missing semantic colors, and the two-value radius vocabulary as first-class utilities, then ban the escape hatches
moves.why: Root cause of every count in this report. openspec/specs/dashboard-design-language/spec.md § Type System, § Surface Palette and § State Color Discipline are normative and index.css is declared normative for values — but the registry that turns values into ergonomics omits four of seven type roles and eleven of the core color tokens, so the correct spelling is always longer than the wrong one. The control case is decisive: spacing IS registered and has 15 drift sites; type is not and has 1,066. Owner-visible payoff: one hierarchy instead of two, one red instead of four spellings, and every future page inherits conformance instead of earning it.
moves.manifesto: Dashboard Design Language (Dispatch) spec § Type System, § Surface Palette, § State Color Discipline, § Page Conformance check (3) 'no new colors' and (4) 'numbers are tabular and mono' — this move is what makes those checks mechanically satisfiable rather than reviewer-enforced.
moves.integration_points: Home: frontend/src/index.css `@theme inline` (lines 374-489) — add `--text-display/title/body/body-sm/voice/eyebrow/mono` as bundled font-size roles (Tailwind v4 accepts `--text-<name>` with `--text-<name>--font-weight`, `--text-<name>--letter-spacing`, `--text-<name>--line-height` companions, so each role ships its tracking and leading), add `--color-red/amber/green/red-text/amber-text/mfg/dim/border-soft/border-strong/bg-elev/bg-deep`, add `--radius-pill: 3px` and `--radius-mark: 4px`. Retire `--text-xs..3xl` (index.css:280-286) and the `--font-size-*` aliases (462-468). Enforcement seam: frontend/eslint.config.js — new selector groups banning `text-[Npx]`, `tracking-[Xem]`, `rounded-[Npx]`, and `[var(--red|amber|green|mfg|dim|border-soft|border-strong|red-text|amber-text)]` bracket escapes once utilities exist; plus frontend/src/lib/visual-token-roles.ts extended with `typography` and `radius` role entries and frontend/src/lib/visual-token-roles.test.ts extended to assert spec-table parity for them. Spec: amend § Type System to name the utility per role so the table and the registry are checkable against each other.
moves.slice_plan: Slice 1: add the new @theme entries additively (nothing breaks; both spellings work) and extend visual-token-roles.ts + its parity test. Slice 2: codemod the 1,066 `text-[Npx]` sites onto the nearest role, reporting any site whose pixel value has no role as a design decision to make (the 21-value inventory says roughly 9.5/12.5/13.5/10.5/11.5/8/17/15/22/28/20px need adjudication). Slice 3: codemod the 1,626 legacy text-xs/sm/lg/xl sites and delete the modular scale. Slice 4: codemod the ~430 `[var(--token)]` bracket escapes onto utilities. Slice 5: turn on the eslint bans. Each slice is independently mergeable and independently revertible.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: a new page typing `text-body text-dim` gets the spec's 14px/1.5 Inter Tight and the tertiary neutral with no bracket syntax. Failure: a codemod site whose px value maps to no role fails the build at slice 5 rather than silently rounding — the ban is the forcing function. Concurrency: none (build-time only). Idempotence: codemods are pure text transforms with a fixed point; re-running is a no-op. Rollback: slices 1-4 are additive or mechanical and revert cleanly; slice 5 is a single eslint config revert.
moves.verification: Extend frontend/src/lib/visual-token-roles.test.ts with a parity test that every row of the spec's Type System table has a registered `--text-*` role whose companion weight/tracking/leading match the table (mirrors the existing color-role parity test). Add a build-time assertion test that `grep -c 'text-\[[0-9.]*px\]'` over src is 0. Extend frontend/src/lib/contrast.test.ts to assert every registered `--color-*` used as a text utility clears 4.5:1 in both themes. Run `npm run lint && npm run test` in frontend/ (the CI frontend job's exact commands).

moves.title: One status presentation registry: collapse five status-badge dialects onto StateDot + one word list bound to the API enum
moves.why: § Status Indicators says status renders through StateDot with four canonical states, and § Composure Doctrine rule 5 says one affordance per signal. Five independent renderers exist instead, two of them in the same file with deliberately divergent wording ('replayed' vs 'replay complete'), and the healthy branch of three of them is a filled saturated pill. Owner-visible payoff: the same fleet event reads with the same word and the same mark on every surface, which is a precondition for five-second verification — today the owner must learn five vocabularies.
moves.manifesto: Dispatch spec § Status Indicators, § Composure Doctrine rule 5 ('one affordance per signal'), § Kind Tags ('mono, uppercase, muted, no background fill'), § Interface Copy ('no celebration'). Implies a spec amendment naming the registry as the executable source, exactly as § Semantic Visual Role Matrix already does for color roles.
moves.integration_points: Home: new `frontend/src/components/ui/status.tsx` exporting `<StatusMark state kind />` built on components/ui/StateDot.tsx's existing TONE_COLORS, plus one exported word map per domain enum co-located with its API type in frontend/src/api/. Retire: components/ingestion/StatusBadge.tsx (both StatusBadge and RowStatus, keeping RowStatus's shape as the single form and its word list as the single vocabulary), components/sessions/StatusBadge.tsx, components/butler-detail/ButlerStatusBadge.tsx; keep components/ui/live-status-badge.tsx's freshness *logic* but have it render through StatusMark. Enforcement seam: frontend/eslint.config.js — a selector banning `<Badge` in any file that also imports a status enum, and a repo-wide ban on `bg-[var(--green)]`/`bg-[var(--red)]`/`bg-[var(--amber)]` outside components/ui/attention.tsx (see next move). Spec: amend § Status Indicators to name components/ui/status.tsx as the executable source with a parity requirement.
moves.slice_plan: Slice 1: build StatusMark + move the four state tones and the word maps in, with tests. Slice 2: migrate ingestion (both renderers) — largest blast radius, has existing tests asserting the two divergent word lists, so the vocabulary decision surfaces here. Slice 3: migrate sessions + butler-detail + notifications + schedules + system tiles (the 11 green fills die here). Slice 4: turn on the eslint bans and delete the retired files.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: every surface showing butler health renders a 6px dot plus one mono word from one map. Failure: an unrecognized status string renders the neutral 'waiting' tone plus the raw string, never a green 'ok' — failure never impersonates health. Concurrency: none. Idempotence: pure render. Rollback: per-slice file revert; slices 2-3 are independent.
moves.verification: A registry test asserting every member of each status enum has exactly one word and one tone, and that no tone maps to a background fill. Update the existing ingestion StatusBadge/RowStatus tests to assert one vocabulary rather than two (the divergence is currently test-locked at components/ingestion/StatusBadge.tsx:126-140). An a11y test asserting role=status + accessible name on StatusMark. Reuse the existing `*.a11y.test.tsx` lane run by `npm run story:test`.

moves.title: Generalize the attention tint into an <Attention> primitive and make every other state-color background unspellable
moves.why: § State Color Discipline grants exactly one exception to the no-background-fill rule, tint+rail as a single signal unit within 4-7%/4-6% alpha. The implementation exists (index.css:735) and is used at 9 sites, while 42 sites hand-roll tints at eight alphas up to 90% and only one pairs a rail. The signal that means 'a human must decide this now' is currently indistinguishable from decoration. Owner-visible payoff: a tinted row on any surface means the same thing, so the eye can be trained on it — this is the visual half of 'every consequential clause is a door'.
moves.manifesto: Dispatch spec § State Color Discipline (attention-tint exception and its two scenarios), § Composure Doctrine rule 1 ('color and motion appear only when state demands'); doctrine about/heart-and-soul/design-language.md § Attention-tint exception.
moves.integration_points: Home: new `frontend/src/components/ui/attention.tsx` wrapping the existing `.attention-row` class as `<AttentionRow tone="red"|"amber">` and exposing nothing else; frontend/src/index.css:735-741 stays the value source. Enforcement seam: frontend/eslint.config.js — extend the existing STATUS_COLOR_SELECTORS group (line 64) from banning Tailwind *shades* to also banning the *semantic*: `bg-[var(--red|amber|green|severity-*)]` with or without an alpha modifier, and `bg-destructive`, outside components/ui/attention.tsx and components/ui/status.tsx. Call sites to migrate or delete: the 42 alpha-tint sites, the 11 green celebration fills, OwnerSetupBanner.tsx:244's full-opacity amber panel, PipelineGateDiagram.tsx:156,164's 60% bars (these are chart geometry and belong on --chart-* per § Non-butler Categorical and Decorative Hue Ramp).
moves.slice_plan: Slice 1: ship <AttentionRow> and migrate the 9 existing .attention-row sites onto it. Slice 2: adjudicate the 42 hand-rolled tints — each is either a real attention state (→ AttentionRow), a chart mark (→ --chart-*), or decoration (→ deleted); land as one PR per owning surface. Slice 3: delete the 11 green fills, replacing with StatusMark from the previous move. Slice 4: turn on the extended eslint ban.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: an open approval renders 6% red tint + 2px rail and carries no second affordance. Failure: a row that already shows a Sev glyph and requests a tint is a lint error, not a double signal. Concurrency: none. Idempotence: pure render. Rollback: the eslint extension is one config revert; the component migrations are per-surface.
moves.verification: A test asserting AttentionRow emits only the two sanctioned data-tone values and no inline background. A DOM test asserting a row carrying a Sev glyph and AttentionRow together fails (or that the component refuses the combination). A grep-assertion test that `bg-[var(--red|amber|green)]` appears zero times outside components/ui/. Run in the frontend CI job's `npm run test`.

moves.title: Generated visual inventory with a CI diff gate — the twin of the frontend copy inventory — and a /system tile that reports the fleet's own drift
moves.why: The repo already proved this mechanism works for copy: about/lay-and-land/frontend-copy-inventory.md is generated by scripts/extract-frontend-copy.py, committed, and diff-gated in .github/workflows/ci.yml:322-334 with the explicit rationale that 'committing the inventory only pays off if it is guaranteed current'. Visual drift has no such twin, which is why this audit had to be run by hand and why run 09's counts were still true today. Feature half: § Process Status Pill already establishes that the system reports honestly on its own process — extend that to the language itself, so the owner can see drift as a number instead of commissioning an audit.
moves.manifesto: Dispatch spec § Page Conformance ('the dispatch-kit review checklist operationalizes them') — this makes the checklist executable; § Process Status Pill ('always honest about what is rendering') extended from data provenance to visual provenance. Vision § What Success Looks Like: 'the system is boring, it works' — drift that reports itself needs no vigilance.
moves.integration_points: Home: new `scripts/extract-frontend-visual-inventory.py` (parses frontend/src/**/*.tsx directly, no node_modules, pure function of the files — the exact non-flaky contract extract-frontend-copy.py already satisfies) emitting `about/lay-and-land/frontend-visual-inventory.md`: every distinct font-size, letter-spacing, radius, hover treatment, state-color fill, icon stroke width, motion class and `var(--x)` reference, with counts and file:line, plus a resolution section listing any `var(--x)` with no definition in index.css. Gate: .github/workflows/ci.yml, a regenerate+`git diff --exit-code` step immediately after the existing frontend-copy pair. Feature surface: a Dispatch-conformance tile on frontend/src/pages/SystemPage.tsx reading a JSON sibling of the inventory, rendered through StatusMark (degraded when any category exceeds its budget), served by the existing dashboard API pattern. Also subsumes finding 9: the resolution section fails CI on --surface/--yellow today.
moves.slice_plan: Slice 1: the generator + committed inventory, no gate (establishes the baseline and immediately documents today's 21 font sizes / 10 trackings / 13 radii / 25 hovers / 6 stroke widths). Slice 2: the CI diff gate. Slice 3: the unresolved-`var()` assertion promoted from advisory to failing (fix the 4 dead references first). Slice 4: per-category budgets that ratchet down as the earlier moves land. Slice 5: the /system tile.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: a PR that adds a new letter-spacing shows it as a one-line inventory diff in review. Failure: a stale inventory fails CI with the regenerate command in the error message (same ergonomics as the copy gate). Concurrency: none — generation is a pure function of the checked-out tree, so merge_group and PR runs agree. Idempotence: regeneration is deterministic with no timestamp field, the property that makes the copy gate non-flappy. Rollback: delete the CI step; the inventory becomes advisory.
moves.verification: A generator unit test on a fixture tree asserting exact counts. A determinism test running the generator twice and diffing. Assert the gate catches a seeded drift (add a `text-[7px]` in a fixture, expect non-zero exit). For the tile, an a11y test plus a degraded-envelope test asserting the tile renders 'unavailable' rather than 'conformant' when the inventory JSON is missing — staleness must never wear current-data authority.

moves.title: One icon contract: a single <Icon> with the stroke weight baked in, and no Unicode glyph icons
moves.why: § Iconography is unambiguous — stroke-only, single 1.25–1.5px weight, 16×16, currentColor, no emoji — and it is the one requirement with no implementation at all: 57 files import lucide-react with its default strokeWidth 2 intact, inline SVG uses six weights, 20 sites use text glyphs, and Sidebar.tsx (present on every surface) mixes two weights in one rail. Owner-visible payoff: icon weight is the single loudest carrier of 'built by one hand' at a glance, and today the persistent chrome contradicts itself.
moves.manifesto: Dispatch spec § Iconography and its conformance scenario; § Anti-Pattern Prohibitions ('emoji in interface chrome'); § Page Conformance check (10) 'the page reads calm at 3am during an outage'.
moves.integration_points: Home: new `frontend/src/components/ui/icon.tsx` — the only module permitted to import lucide-react, re-exporting a fixed named set wrapped at strokeWidth 1.25 / size 16 / currentColor / aria-hidden, and absorbing components/layout/NavIcon.tsx's hand-drawn 16-viewBox path set so there is one source rather than two. Migrate: 57 lucide-importing files, the 11 files with inline <svg> (notably components/layout/Sidebar.tsx:336,691,872 and components/layout/PageHeader.tsx:164,166), and the 20 Unicode-glyph sites. Enforcement seam: frontend/eslint.config.js — ban `from "lucide-react"` outside components/ui/icon.tsx, ban `strokeWidth` literals outside it, and add a Unicode-glyph selector for the ✓✗✕⚠⚡⚙★◦•∅↗✎ range (the existing HEX_COLOR_SELECTORS group at line 102 is the pattern to copy).
moves.slice_plan: Slice 1: build components/ui/icon.tsx and fold NavIcon into it; migrate components/layout/* first since that is the chrome on every page and gives the largest visible win per line changed. Slice 2: migrate the remaining lucide importers by directory. Slice 3: adjudicate the 20 glyph sites — each becomes a named icon or plain text. Slice 4: turn on the three eslint bans.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: every icon on every surface is 16px, 1.25 stroke, currentColor, and inherits the state color of its row rather than carrying one. Failure: an icon name not in the fixed set is a type error at build time, not a runtime fallback. Concurrency: none. Idempotence: pure render. Rollback: per-slice; the eslint bans are one config revert.
moves.verification: A snapshot test over the exported icon set asserting strokeWidth 1.25, 16 viewBox, fill=none, stroke=currentColor on every member. A grep-assertion test that lucide-react is imported in exactly one file and that no `strokeWidth` literal exists outside it. An a11y test asserting every Icon is aria-hidden unless given a label. Run under `npm run test` in the frontend CI job.

moves.title: Give Composure rule 4 a primitive: a <Section> that drops its own chrome when nothing is happening
moves.why: The spec has a testable scenario for quiet-state chrome removal and no component can express it; the only Section primitive (components/overview/Section.tsx) always renders its eyebrow and container, and additionally reimplements the eyebrow as an inline style object rather than importing the canonical Eyebrow, so it is itself a drift site. This is the clause that most directly produces 'earned calm' at the five-second glance.
