audits.jarvis_gap: Today the command-control spine (Overview -> Butlers board -> Butler detail -> Approvals -> Decisions -> Bead -> System) is unusually honest for its maturity: the board endpoint (GET /api/butlers/board, confirmed live) carries explicit heartbeat_unavailable/schema_unreachable/stripe_source_error flags rather than silently defaulting, DecisionsPage documents its own read-only scope in its docstring instead of faking action buttons, and keyboard triage (useListTriage, j/k + verb keys) is wired on Dashboard, Approvals, and System already. The gap to JARVIS-grade is now almost entirely on the 'act' and 'perceive-something-new' axes rather than the 'don't lie' axis: decisions surfaced to the owner still cannot be closed or delegated from the console (by the page's own admission), a butler with zero configured cron schedules is visually indistinguishable from a busy one until you open it, and there is no fleet-wide correlation for the one moment a 12-butler personal fleet actually needs one -- a shared-cause incident (DB blip, breaker trip) that turns several rows amber at once currently reads as N separate unrelated signals rather than one diagnosable event. The ideal version closes every one of those doors: the decision desk gets a real close/delegate verb wired to bd, the board or overview computes and displays a same-cause cluster when multiple butlers degrade together, and every numeric field the API emits is either wired to a real source or removed rather than left as a plausible-looking zero.

audits.jarvis_gap: Today, once a notification actually carries a session_id or trace_id, the trace spine is genuinely good: SessionDossier surfaces tool calls, cost, token usage, error + root evidence (stderr/exit code), trace_id, request_id, and parent_session_id as real backend-filtered links (frontend/src/components/sessions/SessionDossier.tsx:159-320). But live data on the running dev stack shows that for an entire, frequent, safety-relevant producer class -- the home butler's scheduled `device-health-check` and `environment-report` skills, which fire every 4 hours / daily and are exactly the kind of thing that pings the owner overnight -- no session is ever recorded at all: 100/100 sampled notifications have session_id=null, and home butler's own session history (/api/sessions?butler=home) shows zero `schedule:device-health-check` or `schedule:environment-report` entries across its visible history (last real session 2026-08-21), even though other named schedules (`schedule:daily-spaced-repetition-nudge`, `schedule:chronicler_day_close`, etc.) show up correctly. The ideal JARVIS-grade version guarantees that every consequential notification is the output of a provable, logged unit of work: either a real session row (LLM skill run, with tool calls/cost/trace) or an explicit, honestly-labeled deterministic producer (job name, schedule id) -- never a silent absence that looks identical to 'nothing to show here.' Getting there closes the single biggest hole in the signal-to-session-to-evidence spine for this surface, ahead of any cosmetic polish on the pages that already do their job well once evidence exists to show.

findings.title: Scheduled home-butler skills that produce owner-facing alerts leave zero session evidence trail -- the 'walk to the session' step of the journey is structurally impossible for this producer class
findings.evidence: Live: GET /api/notifications?limit=100 -> 0/100 rows have session_id set (all null); trace_id present on only 13/100, and for one such trace (0ba28048b0f42b8a56b779ed1e1c63fa, the 'Device Health Check ... Synology backup offline' notification at 2026-09-05T12:05), GET /api/timeline?trace=<id> returns exactly one event -- the notification itself -- no session. GET /api/sessions?butler=home&limit=20 shows only trigger_source in {route, schedule:consolidation}, most recent 2026-08-21, with zero schedule:device-health-check or schedule:environment-report rows, despite roster/home/butler.toml:48-57 defining named schedules `environment-report`/job_name `environment_report` and `device-health-check`/job_name `device_health_check` (cron `0 */4 * * *` per roster/home/.agents/skills/device-health-check/SKILL.md:24-25). Contrast: GET /api/sessions?limit=100 shows other named schedules (schedule:daily-spaced-repetition-nudge, schedule:chronicler_day_close, schedule:upcoming-travel-check, etc.) DO appear as real session rows with that exact trigger_source shape -- so session logging for named schedules works in general; these two home-butler producers specifically escape it.
findings.failure_scenario: Owner is pinged overnight by 'Bedroom STYRBAR controls: offline (state: unavailable)' (a Critical device alert) or 'Scheduled Synology backup: offline'. Following the assigned journey -- notification -> session -> tool calls -> cost -> error -- there is no session to open (session_id null), the Trace link (when present) resolves to a one-item timeline containing only the notification itself, and NotificationFeed.tsx (frontend/src/components/notifications/notification-feed.tsx:249-267) simply omits both links when neither id is set, with no note that anything is missing. The owner cannot forensically verify what actually checked the device, when, using what HA data, at what cost, or whether the check itself half-failed -- the notification's own claim ("331 devices checked") is unverifiable evidence dressed as a routine alert.
findings.taxonomy_shape: NEW: silent producer-class evidence gap -- an entire class of real, consequential events is missing its logged unit-of-work, and the UI renders this identically to genuine 'nothing more to show,' so the gap is invisible rather than flagged.

audits.jarvis_gap: Today the owner can widen a permission or set the global spend ceiling and get a gated, audited, reason-carrying change (permissions.py, spend.py ceiling/rules) -- that half of the journey is genuinely solid. But the journey's actual headline verb, 'change a butler's model tier this month within a spend ceiling,' hits a dead zone: there is no per-butler monthly ceiling primitive at all (only a fleet-wide singleton ceiling and a per-call cap rule), and the per-butler model-tier override endpoint is a bare CRUD with no reason field, no cost/consequence preview, and -- unlike every sibling mutation on this surface -- no audit_log entry at all, so the owner has no way to later see that the tier changed, who changed it, or what it cost since. The ideal JARVIS-grade version treats 'give this butler more autonomy within a ceiling' as one composed action: the owner picks a butler, sees its current tier and live per-token price next to the proposed tier's price and a projected MTD delta before confirming, sets a butler-scoped ceiling (not just a fleet one) with an explicit consequence clause ('this butler will hard-stop at $X, currently on pace for $Y'), confirms in the same flow that any credential the tier relies on survives the ceiling's window, and lands on one audit trail entry per sub-decision that a later click resolves into 'spend by this butler since this timestamp' -- no separate pages, no manual timestamp correlation, no un-audited consequential write.

audits.jarvis_gap: Today the life-graph surface is a set of well-built, honestly-empty rooms with no doors between them. Individually strong pieces exist -- a live linked_people resolver on calendar entries, a fully-designed MeetingPrepRail with commitment/note/message-context cards, a chronicler /episodes endpoint that already answers 'when did we last see this person' with real per-entity data, gift/loan/timeline panels on EntityDetailPage -- but the owner's named journey (event -> person -> facts -> chronicles -> what-they-like -> what-I-owe-them -> fix-a-wrong-fact) breaks at nearly every hop: the prep rail's attendee card never links to the person it names, EntityDetailPage never queries chronicler despite the exact filter it needs already existing and returning real rows for a live entity, and there is no entity-scoped door to commitments at all -- the one built commitment card only fires inside an unpopulated event-scoped cache. The ideal JARVIS version treats the person, not the event or the fact-store, as the hub: clicking any attendee anywhere (prep rail, timeline, gift list) lands on one entity page that itself proactively pulls last-met from chronicles, open commitments from wherever they are asserted, and gift/preference facts with one-key correction, so the owner never has to remember which specialist owns which fact type -- the graph substrate (core_215) that was supposed to make this possible has zero consumers yet, so the fleet still answers 'what do we know about this person' the expensive, ungraphed way the RFC was written to retire.
audits.live_verification: Live-confirmed against http://127.0.0.1:42200 (read-only GETs): (1) /api/calendar/workspace returned a real near-term event with a non-empty linked_people (Chloe Wong, entity d2521b5f-...); (2) /api/calendar/workspace/prep/{that event_id} returned has_prep_context:false, attendees:[] for that same event -- an honest empty, but it means the one journey door that would show commitments/notes/last-met for this real upcoming meeting is dark; (3) /api/relationship/entities/{id} for that entity returned a normal profile with no chronicle/last-met/commitment fields; (4) /api/chronicler/episodes?participant_entity_id={id} returned real populated episodes (email/message threads with Chloe Wong dated 2026-08-29) for the exact same entity -- proving the data the journey needs exists and is queryable today, just never queried from the entity or calendar surfaces. Static/source-confirmed: grep across src/ and roster/ for entity_graph_edges consumers (walk/path/dossier) returns nothing, matching RFC 0031's own 'only Slice 1 landed' statement; the OpenAPI schema (505 paths enumerated) has no entity-scoped commitments route; roster/relationship/api/router.py has no PATCH/DELETE for a generic entity_facts row (only a contact-channel triple edit-in-place at line ~4933).

audits.jarvis_gap: Today the connectors roster and detail page render honest, well-derived health/auth verdicts (deriveConnectorDispatchInfo correctly distinguishes offline/degraded/needs_reauth with no fabricated calm), and per-event filter reasons are shown inline — real engineering care went into truthful status. But the owner journey named in this audit breaks at its last two doors: there is no way to see whether QA has already investigated a specific quiet connector (QA cases carry only a `butler` field, never a connector identity, and the API silently ignores a connector_type filter), and there is no way to re-arm a paused/quiet connector from the UI at all — the backend's pause/run-now endpoints are fully implemented and ungated but have zero frontend callers. The ideal JARVIS-grade version closes the loop the owner actually walks: from a connector card showing 'quiet since 3am, last delivered X, filtered N for reason Y', one click to 'QA already opened case #482, PR merged 40 minutes ago' if it exists, and if not, one click to run-now/pause-resume with an audit receipt, ending in a fleet-whole confirmation — every clause a door, nothing requiring the owner to guess or retype context across a page boundary.

ranked_moves.non_goals: Voice-note speech-to-text (bu-r0dsz); receipt/OCR finance extraction; acoustic sensing; HA camera streams. This move carries pixels to a model, nothing more.

Concurrency: two channels capturing the same content produce two rows (a ledger, not a dedupe engine). Idempotence: optional mutation_id from the MCP request (as roster/general/modules/tools.py:24-38 does for DND), uniquely indexed, so a transport retry returns the same capture_id. Rollback: un-route by resetting receipt_state; the capture row is never deleted. Vocabulary — Happy: alias resolves to canonical. Concurrency: declares race safely on the PK with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING. Idempotence: alias resolution is pure. Rollback: consolidation sets merged_into and repoints collection_id; the inverse UPDATE restores the split, no row deleted. Retrieval — Failure: tsvector absent (pre-migration butler) → degrade to the containment path and say so in the envelope; extraction failure → extracted_text NULL with extraction_source='failed:<reason>', still searchable by its text. Concurrency: the generated column is maintained by Postgres. Idempotence: catalog upsert keyed. Rollback: drop the catalog rows and the generated column; no owner content transformed in place.

ranked_moves.title: Fleet cost-claim contract, slices 1–3: a typed money claim fenced by RLS, every loan becomes a claim and the USD fabrication dies, and a Finance reconciliation sweep with three honest kinds of 'no'
ranked_moves.why: roster/relationship/MANIFESTO.md:32 ('Track loans ... so no awkwardness lingers') and roster/finance/AGENTS.md:34-36 ('NEVER write settlement state ... in JSONB'). Relationship fabricates USD on every currency-less loan, settles a loan outside a transaction (the old fact can be superseded and the new one lost), and keeps money state in memory-module JSONB with no constraints. Finance cannot see a sibling's claim at all. The design is a six-slice contract; the first three make the assertion honest and give Finance a verdict that never impersonates a reconciliation it could not run.
ranked_moves.evidence: roster/relationship/tools/loans.py:55,96,234,289-290 (USD default), :207-231 (supersede + store_fact with no transaction), :1-20,133-147 (free-dict metadata); roster/relationship/api/router.py:3553 (currency null to the dashboard, USD to the tool); roster/finance/AGENTS.md:24,34-36; live /api/finance/accounts → [] (zero accounts, so every claim is unverifiable today).
ranked_moves.outcome: Creating a loan without a currency raises; a legacy currency-less loan reads null, never USD; a loan and its claim show on both GET /api/relationship/entities/{id}/loans and GET /api/finance/cost-claims on a database where finance holds no grant on the relationship schema; every claim on the current dev stack resolves unverifiable/no_account, not unreconciled; a forged asserted_by is refused by RLS.
ranked_moves.non_goals: Slices 4–6 (owner surface, Finance manifesto amendment, shared-expense splitting); FX conversion at settlement; integer minor units on the public contract; the domain-event bus as carrier; extending fleet_cases as the carrier (all dropped with citations).
ranked_moves.governing_intent: roster/finance/MANIFESTO.md 'Reconcile the evidence'; roster/finance/AGENTS.md integrity rule and no-double-entry boundary; RFC 0032 write-authority pattern; AGENTS.md 'Fencing a public table to one runtime role' trap.
ranked_moves.surface_map: public.cost_claims / cost_claim_resolutions / cost_claim_events (core migration, RLS: asserter role may INSERT its own claim, finance role may write resolutions only, partial unique index on live claim_key, superseded_at/retracted_at, event trigger); core tool group for assert/amend/retract; roster/relationship/tools/loans.py (claim_key loan:{fact_id}, required currency, settle inside one transaction, backfill skipping currency-less loans); Finance sweep job under an advisory lock with candidate matching over finance.transactions (credit only, non-transfer, same currency, window), binding table, verdicts settled / ambiguous(reason) / unreconciled(no_candidate_in_window) / unverifiable(no_account); GET /api/finance/cost-claims.
ranked_moves.behavior_matrix: Slice 1 — Happy: relationship asserts loan:{fact_id} → one row, one 'asserted' event, resolution seeded unreconciled. Duplicate re-assert returns the existing id (partial unique index). Amend: superseding row + old superseded_at; the new resolution restarts. Retract: retracted_at set, sweep skips it, last verdict frozen, UI shows it struck through with reason. Forgery: asserted_by='finance' from another role refused by RLS WITH CHECK and the role CHECK. Cross-write refused both ways. Concurrency: two asserters race → one wins, the loser's identical payload returns the winner's id. Rollback: downgrade drops all three; the asserter's schema stays the source of truth. Slice 2 — Loan without currency → refuse naming the field. Claim assert fails (public unreachable) → the loan fact is still written, the failure logged and retried by the next sweep. Settle mid-flight failure → transaction rolls back, loan stays active. Duplicate backfill → no-op. Slice 3 — One matching credit in window → settled + event + binding. Two → ambiguous, nothing bound, both candidates in match_refs. Debit, transfer-category, or different-currency candidate → never matched (currency_mismatch is ambiguous, never converted). Fresh feed, no candidate → unreconciled/no_candidate_in_window. No fresh feed (today) → unverifiable/no_account with evidence_horizon_at NULL. Already-bound transaction → ambiguous/transaction_already_bound. Sweep crash → previous verdict retained with its decided_at so the surface says 'last checked {decided_at}'. Two sweeps race → advisory lock, loser exits. Amended claim → binding released, resolution restarts.

ranked_moves.title: Blind-spot preamble and task continuity ledger: every session is told what it cannot see, and every recurring task remembers what it concluded last time
ranked_moves.why: roster/health/MANIFESTO.md honesty (a health butler reporting stale vitals as current is the sharpest violation) and every domain manifesto's honesty clause. The expected-signals primitive shipped (QC: as designed) but nothing tells a session at spawn which of its declared signals are absent or unmeasurable, so a session confidently reasons over data that is not there; and a recurring task starts every run from nothing, with the chronicler's day-close continuity a bespoke hook rather than a general layer.

ranked_moves.outcome: With every declared signal PRESENT the composed prompt is byte-identical to today; with a stale connector the health session's prompt carries a typed block naming the signal, its producer, last_observed_at and the evaluator's clock; if the blind-spot query itself errors the preamble says 'source health could not be evaluated' rather than omitting the layer; run N+1 of an opted-in recurring task carries run N's carry_forward block with its age, or an honest 'the last run recorded no carry-forward'.
ranked_moves.non_goals: Prefix reordering / cache volatility (dropped); consequence-gated verification; situational horizon; owner-question lane; retiring the chronicler hook before the general layer is proven equivalent (slice 4 only after the regression test).
ranked_moves.governing_intent: openspec/specs/expected-signals (amended: session-facing projection as a first-class consumer); vision.md Rule 4; roster/chronicler, roster/general, roster/finance manifestos (the mechanism they already assume).
ranked_moves.surface_map: core/expected_signals.py generalized to a per-butler evaluator with declared-dependency input; spawner_context.py new additive layer gated by runtime_config; GET /api/butlers/{name} exposes the same projection; public.task_continuity + sessions.continuation_of_session_id (core migration); carry_forward core tool (upsert by (butler, task, session_id), partial unique index for the live row); scheduler dispatch seam injecting the block; ScheduleConfig continuity=true opt-in; chronicler prompt_hooks migration.
ranked_moves.behavior_matrix: Preamble — Happy: all PRESENT → no preamble, byte-identical prompt (prefix cache preserved). Degraded: ABSENT/UNMEASURABLE → typed block per signal with the instruction that dependent claims be stated as unmeasured. Failure (deliberate inversion): the blind-spot query errors → emit the unevaluable wording; never silently omit, because omission is indistinguishable from all-clear. Concurrency: read-only per spawn against now(). Idempotence: pure function of (butler, declared signals, clock). Rollback: runtime_config flag off restores the four-layer composition exactly. Continuity — Happy: task calls carry_forward once; the row supersedes the previous live row; the next run's prompt carries the block with an explicit age. Failure: session ends without carry_forward → previous row NOT superseded and the next run is told the gap, never a stale block presented as fresh; a carry_forward older than N cadence periods is injected as historical with its age. Concurrency: the scheduler's atomic claim plus the partial unique index so two ticks cannot both supersede. Idempotence: upsert-by-(butler, task, session_id). Rollback: per-task opt-in; a task without continuity=true behaves exactly as today.
ranked_moves.doc_impact: openspec/specs/expected-signals amendment; scheduler spec: continuity opt-in and injection contract; docs/architecture/butler-daemon.md prompt layer list; roster/chronicler docs once the hook migrates.
ranked_moves.verification: (1) Composition test: _compose_system_prompt byte-identical when every declared signal is PRESENT. (2) Fail-closed test: the expected_signals query raises → the preamble carries the unevaluable wording. (3) A butler with no email module gets no Gmail blind-spot line (scoped by declared dependencies). (4) End-to-end spawner test with a stubbed stale connector asserting the string reaches invoke_kwargs['system_prompt'] at spawner.py:2033-2040. (5) GET /api/butlers/{name} and the injected preamble derive from the same evaluator call. (6) Scheduler test at the dispatch seam: run N+1's dispatched_prompt contains run N's carry_forward block and timestamp. (7) Gap test: run N records nothing → run N+1 names the gap. (8) Two ticks for one task against the atomic claim → exactly one live continuity row. (9) carry_forward twice in one session → one row. (10) Chronicler regression: the general layer's day-close prompt is equivalent to today's hook output.

S5 carry_forward tool; observe adoption. S6 injection for a briefing and a finance check behind the opt-in with age stamp and gap wording. S7 migrate the chronicler day-close hook onto the layer after the equivalence test; extend opt-in across the roster.
